Summary

“It is … with the consideration of the welfare of humanity, the protection of the United States Government and its people, that President Baker had signed an incarceration order for the stated below, Lena Kieran Luthor, on grounds of treason and crimes against humanity. Furthermore, it is the decision of the President of the United States that the Department of Extranormal Operations take into consideration the superhuman intelligence of Miss Luthor-“

“Superhuman?” Lena scathingly scoffed. “I’m human.”

“The superhuman intelligence of Miss Luthor, and, as such, convict her of her crimes in line with their punishment for all extranormal persons found guilty of possessing abilities deemed inhuman by the DEO. As such, a life sentence will be served at a secret DEO facility, at the discretion of Director Hank Henshaw. Dated this morning.”

The air was expelled from Lena’s lungs and she gripped the edge of the table, her eyes burning with the urge to cry as her heart hammered in her chest.

“Please. You can’t do this; I didn’t hurt anyone. I’m- I’m innocent. You haven’t even given me a- a trial. I mean-“

    Chapter 1

                They came in the middle of the night, bursting into her apartment with a sudden flurry of noise and activity and light. Lena was still in bed, bolting upright at the sound of breaking and entering as her heart hammered in her chest, reaching for the pistol in her nightstand. The sound of shouts and doors splintering beneath kicks made her panic and Lena stayed in her bedroom, blinking back sleep as her skin prickled with alarm.

     

                It was there that they found her, a gun held in her shaking hands as she stood her ground. Half a dozen agents in black tactical gear, sweeping into the bedroom as the sweeping beams of light attached to their rifles cut through the darkness.

     

                She winced at the brightness, pistol lowering and arm thrown up to blot out the blinding lights. They were the FBI, she assumed, or maybe the CIA. It was late and she was confused, still blinking the sleep out of her eyes as these agents broke into her apartment.

     

                “Lena Luthor?” a man said as he walked over to her, flashing a badge that she didn’t catch as she looked down, blinking back black spots as her vision adjusted. “You’re being detained on suspicion of treason and crimes against humanity. Somebody cuff her.”

     

                Straightening at the words, said lazily and somewhat smugly, a flash of disbelief crossed Lena’s face before horror bloomed in its place. Head whipping around as someone took her arm, Lena pulled away, brow crumpling.

     

                “I- what? No, there’s- this is a mistake, I-“

     

                Her words fell on deaf ears and she was rapidly escorted out of her apartment, barefoot and still wearing her pyjamas, watching as agents overturned tables, emptied out cupboards, and bagged up evidence. Mouth dry and eyes wide, Lena was left stammering and speechless as she was dragged into the elevator and down to the lobby. Her doorman watched with wide eyes as she was carried out in handcuffs, stumbling and frazzled, clueless to what was going on.

     

                Shoved into the back of an SUV, none too kindly, she was wedged in between two agents, their rifles exchanged for pistols they kept trained on her as she was driven through Metropolis in the early hours of the morning, the bulky car wedged between two sedans, while a fleet of motorbikes took the point and rear. Lena was jostled around in the back, her hands cuffed behind her back, shoulders awkwardly pulled together, and no amount of asking, her voice rasping and shaking, elicited an answer.

     

                Their destination ended up being a black site, some off-the-grid secret headquarters hidden in the basement of an abandoned warehouse down near the industrial district. Corrugated iron and crumbling brick provided a derelict veneer for the fortified site tucked away below ground and Lena’s mouth went dry as she was whisked away inside. 

     

                She went from car to elevator, rattling its way down the shaft, shivering in the cold emanating from the iron box and the rock they descended through. They spilled out into a dimly lit hallway, an open space of desks and computer monitors giving it a rather ordinary office feeling, and Lena was led straight into an interrogation room.

     

                Her cuffs were undone and she was pushed down onto the chair, despite her resistance, and her hands were cuffed to the table instead, a loop allowing her some small amount of freedom as the cold floor beneath her feet made her raise her knees to her chest, becoming a small ball on the chair.

     

                Lena didn’t know how long she was left alone for, watched by the blinking lights of two cameras, and she shivered, chin propped up on her knees, becoming stiff. Blinking owlishly as sleep nagged at the back of her mind, she thought perhaps they planned on leaving her there all night when the door eventually jerked open.

     

                The man who had spoken to her in her penthouse bustled in, a folder under his arm and a coffee cup in hand. He moved over to the desk and pressed play on the recording device, which clicked and whirred, a red line blinking as the tape started to wind. 

     

                “Miss Luthor, good evening. I’m Director Hank Henshaw, of the Department of Extranormal Operations. Is this organisation familiar to you?”

     

                Lena’s face crumpled with confusion as she softly cleared her throat. “I- no. I’ve- I’ve never heard of you before.”

     

                He smiled placidly as he set down his cup of coffee and his manila folder before shedding his black suit jacket. Hesitating, he walked behind her and settled it around her shoulders in an act of pity.

     

                “Coffee? Or perhaps water?”

     

                She sneered at Hank, who smiled faintly in return as he pulled a chair out across from her. He eased himself onto his seat, the steel legs grating along the floor, setting Lena on edge as she swallowed thickly.

     

                “No? It’s going to take a while.”

     

                She was silent for a long minute while the man sipped his coffee, slowly spreading out the contents of the manila folder he’d brought in with him, a disinterested look on his face. His pace was leisurely and he looked perfectly at ease, contrasting Lena’s tense posture. 

     

                “This is unlawful,” Lena eventually exclaimed, rigid and haughty in her seat, hands cuffed to the table before her. “I want my lawyer.”

     

                He let out a short chuckle, leaning back in his seat. “There’ll be no lawyers here. This here …” he said, rifling through the documents and picking up one before he set it down before her and tapped it with a finger. “This is a signed warrant for your arrest by President Baker.”

     

                “I haven’t done anything,” Lena ground out, her hands splayed helplessly as she hunched her shoulders, blanching at his words as her stomach lurched.

     

                There was an edge of desperation to her words as she leaned forward, her eyes wide and pleading. He watched her closely and was silent for a few minutes, idly twirling a pen with his fingers as he leaned back before he suddenly shifted forward and set the pen down.                 “As you’re aware, an arrest for your brother, Alexander Luthor, was made nine months ago.                 Lips parted as she listened, Lena shook her head as she frowned. “What’s that got to do with me?”

     

                He took a sip of his coffee and coolly appraised her from across the table. “At seven minutes past eleven last night, a DEO operation led by myself entered your laboratory at L-Corp headquarters, located at 1200 West Cordova, National City,” Henshaw recited from a page he held in his hand. “A search warrant was granted, based on the evidence provided in your brother’s personal items.”

     

                “You broke into L-Corp?” Lena spluttered, aghast at his audacity.

     

                “Upon entering the building, multiple items were confiscated as evidence to corroborate the DEOs suspicions on unlawful activity and gross misuse of power conducted by yourself-“

     

                “I-“ Lena started to protest, but found herself swiftly silenced as he held up a hand, forging onwards.

     

                “Which has been recognised as an act of terrorism against the United States of America. Kryptonite being the alien substance originating on planet Krypton, a weakness to a known alien species, but shown to be harmless against humans, and Anti-Kryptonite, meaning it has the opposite effect, with incapacitating effects on humans. Do you deny your involvement in the creation and manufacturing of said substances?”

     

                The blood drained from Lena’s face and it took her a moment to swallow before she replied, her voice trembling and halting. “I- yes, I mean no. I- I discovered a- a new form … it’s not- it was just a … personal project. I would never-“

     

                “And do you deny your brother, Alexander Luthor, had any knowledge of this creation and did not weaponise it against human populations?”

     

                Ducking her head, Lena curled her hands into fists as her mouth thinned. “He knew. He- he stole it from me.”

     

                There was a long pause of silence and she was silent and fuming, the tension so unbearable that she almost broke it several times. She didn’t have any defence though, didn’t have any excuse that would suffice. It seemed to drag on, the interrogation parsing through her research, with documents stolen from her computer, hacked into by agents just outside the room, photos of her creations in their varying statuses, bank transfers, and communications with her brother, all the way back to when she was eighteen. Hours seemed to pass by and Lena was stiff and pale as the Director tried to trap her in lies. She was too clever for that though, choosing her words carefully and biting her tongue on more than one occasion to stop herself from taking the bait.

     

                “May I ask about your interest in developing this substance?” Henshaw eventually asked, five hours after she’d been deposited into the room.

     

                With a quiet huff of laughter, Lena closed her eyes. She was thirsty and cold, wishing she’d taken the offered water, her eyelids burning with the urge to sleep. “I … like to know things. I was studying Kryptonite to understand its chemical compounds; I discovered Anti-Kryptonite … by accident.”

     

                He curtly nodded and gathered up his photographic evidence into a neat pile, setting it on top of the documents before him. Picking up another one, he cleared his throat.

     

                “It is … with the consideration of the welfare of humanity, the protection of the United States Government and its people, that President Baker had signed an incarceration order for the stated below, Lena Kieran Luthor, on grounds of treason and crimes against humanity. Furthermore, it is the decision of the President of the United States that the Department of Extranormal Operations take into consideration the superhuman intelligence of Miss Luthor-“

     

                “Superhuman?” Lena scathingly scoffed. “I’m human.”

     

                “The superhuman intelligence of Miss Luthor, and, as such, convict her of her crimes in line with their punishment for all extranormal persons found guilty of possessing abilities deemed inhuman by the DEO. As such, a life sentence will be served at a secret DEO facility, at the discretion of Director Hank Henshaw. Dated this morning.”

     

                The air was expelled from Lena’s lungs and she gripped the edge of the table, her eyes burning with the urge to cry as her heart hammered in her chest.

     

                “Please. You can’t do this; I didn’t hurt anyone. I’m- I’m innocent. You haven’t even given me a- a trial. I mean-“

     

                He set the page down and fixed her with a flat look. “There’ll be no trial, no jury, no escape. Your brother caused us trouble for years, outsmarting the FBI, CIA and police force, in what can only be described as some superhuman genius-“

     

                Snorting, Lena’s lip curled, “outwitting a bunch of idiots in uniform who can’t tell their ass from their elbow is hardly superhuman.”

     

                He surprised her by laughing quietly, his chair scraping as he pushed it back and climbed to his feet. “Your family are … interesting. Consider it a mercy that you’re allowed to keep your life.”

     

                Plucking his jacket from her shoulders, the cold shrouding her as she shivered, Henshaw pulled it back on and pressed stop on the recording before he drained his coffee.

     

                “It’s been … enlightening, Miss Luthor. I wish you the strength needed to endure what comes next.”

     

                “Fuck you,” she snarled, rising from her chair, although she was still chained to the table, which left her hunched as she strained against the handcuffs. “You can’t take me anywhere - I won’t let you. I can pay-”

     

                An agent stepped inside with another waiting outside the door and Hank gave her a faint smile as he arched an eyebrow. “You see, that’s where you're wrong. Money is where your justification ends; here is where mine begins.”

     

                He vanished out the doorway then and the agent unlocked the cuffs from her wrist to free her from the table. In a moment of panic, Lena seized the opportunity to fight back, elbowing the man in the stomach and darting around the other side of the table.

     

                His companion stepped inside and sighed, his face grim as he rounded the table to get to her. Penned in by them both, Lena shook her head, hands up as she was backed into the corner. Making an attempt to push past the one directly in front of her, blocking the door, Lena was caught and flung back, her head slamming against the wall behind her and making her wince.

     

                “Sedate her,” Henshaw softly called from outside.

     

                One agent managed to grab ahold of her arm, grounding her as the other approached and grabbed the other one. Caught between the two of them, Lena watched as another person entered the room, holding a syringe in hand, and crossed over to them. Twisting and shouting, Lena pleaded as she was held fast, and the bite of the needle plunged into her neck made her face ripple with pain before it went slack a moment later and she sagged between the two men.

     

                She was out cold for the duration of the helicopter ride out over the choppy ocean, stretched out and bound on the floor, wrists and ankles cuffed and chained together. That was for the best - she hated to fly and she doubted motion sickness would have helped if she’d been conscious - and hours later they circled an empty spot of the ocean for five minutes until something emerged from beneath the waves.

     

                A large raft of concrete and metal broke through the surface of the ocean, a grey landing pad for the helicopter emblazoned with a yellow H, and the chopper set down there and was secured in place before the doors were opened. Lena’s unconscious form was dragged out, sea spray soaking into the trio as guards came out to assist.

     

                The two agents handed her over into the custody of the guards and were left to refuel and fly back to land, while Lena was blissfully unaware of the prison she’d just been exiled to. Taken to an empty room, she was left on a low cot to wake up as the drugs wore off.

     

                By the time she came to, it was past lunchtime and she woke feeling groggy and off-balance as if something was amiss. There was the lingering unease and a stiffness to her muscles, and Lena was a little delayed in coming to the realisation that none of it had been a bad dream as she came to in that empty concrete room with a jolt of fear.

     

                Banging on the metal door didn’t summon anyone faster, although Lena spotted the camera up high in the corner of the room. There were no windows and she had no idea what time it was, only that she was hungry. She shouted and banged on the door for what felt like an hour before it opened to reveal a young woman, only a few years older than her, Lena thought, with reddish-brown hair cut to her chin and an undercut.

     

                “Prisoner LL93, welcome to Fort Rozz. Follow me; I’ll get you processed.”

     

                “Where the fuck am I?”

     

                “Your new home,” the woman drily replied. “Now, move it.”

                “Vasquez,” the woman said, turning slightly to call over her shoulder, although she didn’t take her eyes off Lena. “This one’s going to be a fighter.”

     

                Tensing, Lena watched as the other officer stepped inside, wearing a matching black polo shirt and the same cargo pants. She had dark cropped hair and was shorter, yet Lena wasn’t confident. Another two followed her shortly afterward and Lena scoffed at how excessive four guards were for an unarmed woman. Still, Lena wouldn’t make it easy for them.

     

                “It’ll be easier if you come quietly.”

     

                “Fuck you,” Lena snarled.

     

                Sighing, the woman nodded at the other officers, who stepped forward. The short one reached out for Lena, who pulled away, smacking her hand aside, affronted.

     

                “Don’t touch me.”

     

                “The easy way or hard way - your choice,” Vasquez warned her, hand straying down to her own baton as the others mirrored her action.

     

                She reached for Lena again and Lena reached up to grab her arm, using her momentum against her to fling her into a wall.                 It was composed of two manacles and a rotating length of metal connecting the two, allowing for a limited range of motion.                 Taken through to a room with grimy grey tiles and a row of empty shower heads, not a stall in sight, Lena was let go as the door was locked automatically as it hissed closed, leaving her alone with the guard she’d first encountered.

     

                “Your uniform has already been prepared for you. You have five minutes to shower.”

                She stared at the other woman for a long minute, disbelief written on her face. If she wasn’t so frightened and angry, she might have laughed.

     

                “And my clothes?” Lena haughtily asked. “Am I supposed to shower with them on too?”

                “You have four minutes; make it quick.”

                “There’s n-no shower gel. Or shampoo,” she stammered.

     

                “There are bars of soap.”

     

                Lena gagged at the sight of the communal lump of soap, worn away by frequent use. So far she’d been keeping it together remarkably well, she thought. She hadn’t cried in the interrogation room - although she’d come perilously close on more than one occasion - and she’d shouted herself almost hoarse in the cell after waking up, but the thought of using the sad, greyish lump of soap to wash herself clean was too much.

     

                A sob escaped her as she picked it up with a trembling hand, the harsh water so cold that it hurt, her skin turning red from the stinging impact of it, while her fingernails turned purple. Her tears mingled with the water and vanished down the drain and she stiffly washed, a shiver wracking her every few moments.

     

                “It’s … cold.”

     

                “Tough. One minute.”

     

                Letting out another pitiful sob, Lena washed the suds from her skin and fumbled for the knob, her hand shaking so badly that it took her a moment to turn the water off. Wrapping her arms around herself, Lena’s teeth chattered as she stood in the puddle of water, the drain emptying slowly, and looked at the guard with bloodshot eyes.

     

                “Can I get a towel or will I have to air dry?” she snidely asked, her voice thick with the evidence of her crying.

     

                Snorting, the woman walked over to a pile of folded clothes resting on the edge of a long row of sinks. A scummy layer clung to the metal basins and the mirrors were spotted with black as Lena looked at her ghostly reflection, shivering in the middle of the bathroom. The guard grabbed a towel and walked over to her, shoving it out. It was thin terry cloth and Lena hurriedly wrapped it around herself, shivering as she wiped her face with the corner of it and dripped onto the grey tiles.

     

                The uniform consisted of a pair of boxer shorts and a sports bra in heather grey, hastily pulled on as her bare skin prickled with goosebumps, followed by the grey scrubs, baggy and unflattering. She pulled on the socks and a pair of slip-on canvas shoes - no laces allowed - and raked a hand through her damp hair. Drying the ends with a towel, she cleared her throat.

     

                “Can I brush my teeth?”

     

                “You can in the morning. Hold out your arms.”

     

                Lena’s bottom lip wobbled and she pressed them together to stop it, her jaw aching with the effort of stifling her urge to cry. Her pale face was blotchy and she glared daggers at the woman as she held her arms out and the cuffs were clamped back around her wrists.

     

                “Let’s go.”

     

                She was dragged over to the door, her new shoes squeaking on the floor as she resisted slightly, and then they were back out in the hallway. It was just the two guards now, and Lena was held between them until the other one peeled off at an exit and left her alone with the one she assumed was in charge. They were both silent and the guard was stony-faced and tense, ready to beat the shit out of her at a moment’s notice, Lena was sure.

     

                The prison was a warren of concrete hallways and the occasional airlock as they went from one area to the other, as much a security containment device as it was to pressurise the air, as far underwater as they were. Lena was quickly lost, no manner of tracking turns allowing her to keep it straight in her memory as her body sagged and her head pounded with a headache.

     

                They came to a small, dank office where a man sat behind a desk, typing away on a computer as a small, boxy TV played a fuzzy soccer game. He removed his feet from the desk and straightened up at the arrival of them and Lena was made to stand against the wall, photos of her taken from every angle before her hands were pressed against a tablet and digital scans of her fingerprints were taken.

     

                There were forms quickly filled out, the woman typing away on the tablet and brusquely asking her a few questions, but they already had a pretty comprehensive dossier on her that chilled Lena. This hadn’t been something hastily carried out overnight - they’d been compiling evidence for weeks, months , scrounging up her Social Security Number, her address, her phone number.

     

                Once they were finished with her there, she was led down a different hallway and to another room, where the woman hesitated, casting her a sideways look. 

     

                “Behave yourself in here.”

     

                Lena snorted and didn’t offer any other response as the woman pressed her hand to the scanner and admitted them. She pushed Lena in ahead of her and the door slid closed, automatically locking them in. Blinking in surprise as she found herself in a familiar setting, Lena felt a pang of longing in her chest as she looked around at the medical equipment. The prickle of fear was quick to follow as she took in the sight of an older blonde woman. She might have looked kind under any other circumstance as she looked up, her face softening slightly.

     

                “The new prisoner for you.”

     

                Smiling slightly, the woman nodded, putting away a new box of gauze and dusting off her hands. “Ah, yes. Lena Luthor. I’m Doctor Danvers - it’s nice to meet you.”

                There was a brief moment of tension, and Lena’s eyes slid from the stern doctor to the impassive guard before the latter inhaled sharply and sighed. “Doctor Danvers, I-”

     

                “Don’t you Doctor Danvers me, Alexandra Danvers,” the blonde woman chastised her, a hard look on her face as her voice turned brittle. “I’m your mother and this is my patient. If they want me to do my job, they can keep their orders to themselves. Uncuff her. Now.”

     

                Mouth thinning as her cheeks flushed at her mother’s sharp rebuke, Alex pushed off the closed door and walked over to Lena. She pressed her thumb against the scanner on the side and the manacles clamped around Lena’s wrists unclicked. They were swiftly removed and she rubbed at her scraped skin, a hateful look in her green eyes as she looked at the guard, who stared back blankly.

     

                “Sit,” Doctor Danvers motioned her onto the padded leather bed, the paper crinkling beneath Lena’s weight as she sat down.

     

                “I’m just going to be doing a check-up to make sure everything’s okay,” she soothingly murmured, removing her stethoscope from around her neck and giving Lena a wan smile. “If you can just relax for me.”

     

                Lena involuntarily tensed at her words, a swooping, sickening feeling in her stomach as her insides tied themselves into knots. Her mouth was dry and her breaths were quick and panicked, heart hammering in her chest as the doctor put the ends of her stethoscope in her ears and held the chest piece up. The press of it was cold against Lena’s chest as she slipped it beneath the v of the prison uniform’s neck.

     

                “Are you on any medications?”

     

                “No,” Lena rasped.

     

                “Birth control? No? Any allergies? Take a deep breath for me, sweetie.”

     

                Tears pricked Lena’s eyes and her throat constricted, hot anger knifing through her at the woman’s kind words. She didn’t want her kindness, not when she was just as culpable as the guards who had manhandled her into the prison. Lena refused to breathe deeply and she saw the corners of the woman’s mouth tighten with dismay as she checked her breath sounds on the other side of her chest before rounding the table and pressing the stethoscope against Lena’s ribs.

     

                “It’s easier if you don’t fight me,” the woman murmured.

     

                Lena let out a listless huff of laughter, reaching up to rub a hand over her face. The cool touch of metal vanished a moment later and the doctor reappeared before her, draping the stethoscope around her neck and plucking a thin light from the breast pocket of her white coat. 

     

                “Look right here for me, please.”

     

                Glaring from beneath furrowed brows, Lena clenched her teeth as the bright light of the torch blinded her as the doctor checked her pupillary response. Reaching out, the woman gently cradled her chin as she hunched over.

     

                “Can you open your mouth for me?”

     

                Perhaps it was childish, but Lena clenched her teeth together as a tight-lipped smile graced her stony face, a challenge sparking in her green eyes as she looked up. Giving her a patient smile as she indulged her in her petulance, Doctor Danvers sighed softly as she straightened up, her light touch dropping from Lena’s chin. Lena’s eyes strayed to Alex a moment later as she watched the guard stalk towards her, tense and irate, only to be held back by her mother, who murmured some low warning too soft for Lena’s ears.

     

                Retreating back to the wall, Alex watched Lena closely, while Lena sagged on the bench, her shoulders curving in, and listened to the suffocating silence of the room. The doctor was quiet as she typed on the slim computer set up on a desk in the corner, the sound of the clacking keys filling the room while Lena breathed slowly, the clinical coldness and her waning adrenaline leaving her pale and uneasy.

     

                “Ready to continue?” Doctor Danvers asked after a few minutes, standing up from the desk chair.

     

                Squeezing her eyes shut, Lena swallowed thickly. “Why are you doing this to me?”

     

                “I … it’s my job to make sure you’re healthy. That’s all.”

     

                “I mean-”

     

                “I know,” she murmured, cutting Lena off as she gave her a grim look, full of guilt and weary resignation. “But I don’t know the answer to that.”

     

                There was a tremor in Lena’s chin before she pressed her lips into a flat line, shoulders dropping as she wilted. Opening her mouth, she closed her eyes and heard the scuff of shoes on the linoleum as the doctor crossed back over to her. She was silent for a moment before making a sound of agreement and telling Lena she could close her mouth again.

     

                There were dozens of questions as she felt Lena’s lymph nodes, made her lay on her back to press down gently on her abdomen, checked her reflexes and her range of motion. Had Lena ever been pregnant? Had she ever had surgery? Was there a family history of any medical conditions? Just the psychosis , Lena had thought, a glint in her eyes as she jerked her chin up in a stubborn manner, silent. She was made to stand on a scale and her height measured against the wall, her blood pressure measured with a cuff and sent into a small private toilet for a urine analysis, cameras blinking as they watched from the walls.

     

                “Are you up to date with all of your shots? When was your last flu vaccine?”

     

                Lena had hers annually, fastidious about making sure she had it every November, was up to date on her tetanus shot, considering all the work she did with metal, and Hep B too. Doctor Danvers pulled on blue latex gloves and filled a syringe from a small sealed bottle after her questioning was done, moving over to Lena as she flicked the side of it and pressed the plunger down slightly.

     

                “This is a shot of a contraceptive I administer monthly; it’ll help stop menstruation. It’s better that way.”

     

                “I’m not letting you put anything in me,” Lena said with a scathing scoff of laughter, her lips twisting derisively. 

     

                Doctor Danvers approached the bench, reaching out for her arm and Lena tore herself away from her grasp. Stumbling off the bed, she grabbed a fistful of the doctor’s white coat and slammed her against the wall, bristling as panic shot through her. The sound of the hammer of a pistol being pulled back made her freeze and her eyes slid sideways, but Alex was out of her line of sight. 

     

                “It’s alright,” Doctor Danvers said, her voice shaking slightly beneath her calm demeanour, holding up her hand with the needle to talk her daughter down before her blue eyes slid over to Lena.

     

                They were of a height, the doctor just a little taller, and she gave Lena a rueful smile. “I know you’re frightened, but I’m not your enemy, okay? My husband … he was killed for hiding an alien. I was brought here to offer my expertise instead. We’re prisoners, just as much as you are, just … on the other side of the cell.”

     

                Wavering for a moment, Lena quietly scoffed, “not just as much. ”

     

                Hesitating, the woman nodded slightly, “no, not just as much. But I don’t want to hurt you. Trust me.”

     

                Lena’s eyes flickered over to the tip of the needle, wariness curling up her spine as a cold sweat dampened her skin. “And if I say no?”

     

                Lips twitching with regret, the doctor sighed, her head cocking to the side slightly. “They’ll get someone else to do it, even if they have to hold you down or drug you. I’m sorry. Really, I am. But I don’t want you to suffer, I don’t want them to violate you so … it’s your choice.”

     

                Pushing her against the wall for a moment, Lena dropped her hand and stepped back, turning as she paced cagily. Her eyes were glassy as a muscle worked in her jaw as a strangled laugh built in her chest. “But it’s too late for that, and not much of a choice, is it?”

     

                “I’m afraid not.”

     

                Running a hand through her damp hair, Lena let out a broken laugh as she came to a stop, closing her eyes and tipping her head back. Climbing back up onto the padded bench, Lena pushed the short sleeve of her grey, baggy shirt up and the doctor tore open a new alcohol wipe and swiped it over her pale skin. She was as gentle as could be while poking a needle into her arm and Lena didn’t even flinch, staring blankly at the wall ahead as a small, circular band-aid was gently smoothed over it.

     

                “I’ll need to do a blood test, too.”

     

                Exhaling wearily, just wanting the nightmare to be over, Lena dipped her chin slightly in a nod - of acceptance, not agreement - and was limp as she let the woman tighten a strap around her bicep, swipe the crook of her elbow, and slip a cannula with a tube attached to it into a vein. Vivid red blood ran down the tube and into the vials the doctor held, and Lena felt light-headed and disjointed, her skull heavy as if it was sinking into her spine, and a pulsing ache behind her eyes as she stared numbly ahead. Her lips were set in a drawn, bloodless line and her pale cheeks looked positively ghostly.

     

                Afterward, she was given five minutes to sit there and recover, a cotton ball taped to the inside of her arm and a juice box sitting beside a snack packet of mini Oreos on the padded seat beside her. The sugar helped a little but Lena had to choke it down, her throat painfully tight and her mouth perpetually dry as she blinked, the burning in her eyes refusing to go away.

     

                Eventually, Alex cleared her throat and looked at her mother. “I need to take her.”

     

                Nodding, the doctor moved over to Lena, gently gripping her shoulders as she helped her off the bed, giving her daughter a severe look. “Be gentle with her; she’s lost a lot of blood and the shock-”

     

                “I know .”

     

                Raising her eyebrows in a reproachful look, the doctor peeled off her latex gloves and dumped them in the trash as Alex picked up the manacles and cuffed Lena again. The cuffs were heavy on her limp limbs and she felt like her arms were being pulled out of their sockets as her hands fell before her, shoulders slumped. Gripping her arm, not unnecessarily rough, Alex escorted her out of the doctor’s office and down a hallway.

     

                They passed through an airlock and down another concrete hallway before stopping at another room, accessed by Alex’s thumbprint. A man behind steel mesh sat on a stool, staring at a wall of monitors, each one showing the interior of a cell with a panel of green lights and numerous touchpads and buttons beneath it. He looked over and gave Lena a cursory once-over before reaching out to pick up a metal collar. Heavily setting it down on the counter, he slid it under the gap in the mesh and Alex picked it up, standing in front of Lena as she reached up to brush her dark hair out of the way and put the collar around her neck.

     

                With her thumb pressing into the small blue square light dimly glowing on the front, Alex held the collar in place and Lena’s hair in her other fist as the collar cinched in tightly around Lena’s neck. Its presence was immediately oppressive, so tight against her throat as she swallowed that Lena thought she might suffocate. She could feel the cold points of metal denting her skin - not hard enough to hurt, but enough for her to be aware of it.

     

                “Is it active?”

     

                The man leaned forward, flipping a switch, tapping a button on the panel, and watching as an amber light came on. It was a few minutes of silent waiting before it flashed green for a few seconds and then solidified.

     

                “She’s good to go.”

     

                Nodding, Alex grabbed Lena by her arm and towed her out of the room and back into the hallway, making for the airlock at the end. They waited inside while it pressurised and they were admitted to the similarly bleak hallway on the other side.

     

                They stopped at a guard checkpoint, a small antechamber off the main hallway, full of more monitors and machines, and Alex conversed with the woman Lena had bitten earlier. “Need a hand with her?”

     

                “She’s one human; how hard can it be to put her into her cell?”

     

                Lena stilled at the words, her hands curling into fists in front of her. The scoffing tone of Alex’s voice made cold anger burn inside her and when she’d finished confirming which cell Lena was to be locked in she grabbed her arm again and pulled. Only, this time Lena didn’t go willingly. They’d been lulled into a false sense of security after her initial outburst, her initial struggling as she’d cursed them out and been almost rabid. It resurfaced now as she twisted out of Alex’s grasp and backed away.

     

                Sighing, Alex gave her an exasperated look. “Don’t make it harder for yourself.”

     

                The other guard, Vasquez, pulled out her baton, flicking it out as it hummed with blue electricity. Lena sneered at her, backed up against the wall of the room, cold seeping into her shoulder blades as her eyes darted between the two guards. Closing her eyes, Alex exhaled softly and moved towards Lena, who skittered sideways - closer to Vasquez - and lashed out with a kick to the other guard’s knee. 

     

                Cursing, Vasquez slammed her baton into Lena’s side as she went down and Lena tensed at the voltage that coursed through her. She sagged on her feet, her vision dimming as her blood loss and recent beating left her woefully outmatched. Sinking to her knees, the concrete floor hard against her bones, she breathed heavily through gritted teeth.

     

                “That’s enough, now,” Alex murmured, hauling her back to her feet.

     

                Hands still clamped before her, Lena had no choice but to find her feet, her other arm grabbed by Vasquez. Between the two of them, they got her back out into the hallway and made for the wide doors, which hissed open at the swipe of a thumbprint and a retinal scan from the two women. 

     

                They dragged her inside and Lena twisted in their grasp, fighting them the entire time as her slip-on shoes squeaked against the floor, scrabbling for traction. Snarling as she hunched her shoulders and tried to tip one off-balance, tear her arm from the other’s hand, cursing them out, she was sweating and panting as they brought her to a stop before an empty cell. 

     

                “Hold her,” Alex ordered Vasquez.

     

                Lena promptly found herself in a chokehold, the guard’s other arm pinning her arms down in front of her, and she wasn’t strong enough to fight her off. No amount of pilates and spin class could outmatch the muscled physique of guards who had nothing better to do when off-duty except throw weights around in the gym. She made a pitiful sound at the back of her throat, eyes wide with terror at the sight of the cell, and watched as Alex pressed her hand to the panel set beside the cell.

     

                It was made of three grey concrete walls - the fourth was a flickering blue translucent forcefield. The forcefield was lowered by a series of taps and Lena was slowly led inside before Vasquez let her go and backed out, pulling her pistol from her belt and steadily pointing it at Lena. It didn’t stop her from trying to run, turning to find the guard blocking her way, the cold muzzle of the pistol pressing against her forehead.

     

                Lips trembling, Lena backed up and smacked into Alex, who grabbed her shoulder and held her fast. Pressing her thumb to the scanner on the manacles, they released and Alex tapped out the back of her knee and forced her to the floor.

     

                “Stay down.”

     

                Vasquez backed out, gun still trained on Lena, and Alex quickly followed, slamming her hand against the panel just in time. Never one to do what she was told, Lena leaped to her feet and ran full speed at the empty air before her, only to slam into something solid as the forcefield snapped into place.

     

                The warmth of blood ran over her lips and she blinked back the tears that sprang to her eyes, her nose throbbing from the impact. Doubling over with her hand clamped over her nose, Lena quietly gasped, a coppery taste in her mouth as her dark hair hid her face and she listened to the laughter, jeers and claps from some of the other prisoners. Face flushing pink with embarrassment, she strained up and flung herself at the forcefield again, a frenzied look in her eyes.

     

                “You fucking bastards,” Lena snarled, pounding a hand against the hard barrier as she bared her bloody teeth at Alex and Vasquez. “Let me out. You can’t do this to me.”

     

                “Prisoner LL93, back away from the forcefield.”

     

                Slamming her hand against it again, Lena let out a low sound of frustration. “This is illegal. Let me out, you piece of shit.”

     

                Sighing heavily, Alex shook her head and nudged the other woman and they both vanished, leaving Lena to pound at the forcefield. No doubt they assumed she’d wear herself out shortly, but they greatly underestimated the stubbornness of a Luthor. 

     

                She shouted so loud that her insults became unintelligible, scraping her throat until her words were rasping and her breathless sobs choked her. There was nothing in the cell to even try and breach the barrier so Lena used her body, flinging herself at it, bruising her shoulders from the impact.

     

                “You can’t leave me here!”

     

                “Can someone shut her the hell up,” someone called out.

     

                “Hey, hey, you need to stop,” another voice cautioned her, low and gentle, yet fraught with panic as it drifted up from the floor. “If you don’t they’ll-“

     

                As Lena rebounded off the barrier again, staggering backward, she suddenly stiffened, her whole body going taut, the tendons in her neck strained as her mouth opened in a silent scream. The effect was worse than being tasered, more painful, and more intense, and Lena crumpled to the floor, letting out a quiet gasp as her chest rose and fell quickly.

     

                There was a certain hush that descended over the prison then as she lay there, cheek pressed into the gritty concrete floor, breathing in the damp smell of it. Inhaling sharply, she dragged herself back to her feet after a moment, blinking rapidly as she got her bearings.

     

                It was a bare cell, with nothing but three grey concrete walls and a certain darkness to the prison. Squares of fluorescent lights illuminated the interior of each cell but otherwise, it was a dim place. The contents included an angle iron and steel mesh bed welded to a wall, the world’s thinned mattress on it with a scratchy grey blanket, and a lumpy pillow. Behind an opaque waist-high wall, offering minimal privacy, was a metal toilet and a sink screwed to the wall next to it. That was all they’d afforded her but it was all lost on Lena as she stood, hands clenched in fists as her chest heaved.

     

                She was sobbing then, breathless and quick as tears spilled over and cut through the wet blood smeared across the lower half of her face. Finding that she couldn’t manage much more than a strangled shout of anger, Lena threw herself at the barrier again, banging her head against it twice, hard.

     

                “We’ve got a fighter!” someone shouted from further down the row of cells. “Let’s go round two!”

     

                Slamming a palm against it once more, she recoiled and then stiffened again as the collar around her neck sent a second round of voltage through her. Teeth gritted against the pain as she hoarsely screamed, Lena’s vision dimmed as she collapsed to the ground, knees cracking hard against the floor as she bowed forward, hands clamped on either side of her head as she found herself clinging to consciousness.

     

                On the edge of hyperventilating, Lena tried to drag in deep breaths to calm herself, but every one felt like a buoy refusing to sink. The panic kept resurfacing as she curled in on herself, broken sobs wracking her as the muffled sounds of laughter and cheers fell on her ears, tinny and distant. She could taste sour bile coating the back of her tongue and let out a breathless sob, catching in her throat.

     

                “Hey.”

     

                That same voice from before came from Lena’s left, near a small vent set into the bottom of the wall, mirroring the one up near the ceiling to allow for some air circulation through the string of cells. 

     

                “Hey, it’s okay. It’ll be okay.”

     

                A loud sob escaped Lena and she squeezed her eyes shut, pain radiating from half a dozen spots as she grit her teeth and her lips trembled. Sinking onto her side, facing the wall as she curled into a fetal position, Lena cried into her arms as hot tears slid down her skin.

     

                “Can you tell me your name?”

     

                The voice was warm and soothing, a balm to the pain that consumed Lena at that moment. There was the faint accent and uncertainty to her words that made it hard for Lena to place where she was from. She ignored her for a long while, a hand clamping over her mouth as she lay on the cold, stained floor, the fluorescent light stuttering overhead every so often.

     

                At some point, the young woman next door started to hum. It was low and slow, a strange cadence to the tone as if there were words to go along with it, and slowly, Lena’s sobs subsided. The woman hummed for a minute longer, as Lena’s breaths came in hitching fits and starts, her face blotchy and an ache in her chest.

     

                “Lena,” she whispered after a minute, her voice scratchy and breaking as she drew in a shuddering breath. “My name’s Lena.”

     

                “A beautiful name. It reminds me of the golden hour - you know, just before sunset. It’s my favourite time of day.”

     

                Lena was quiet, a bewildered look crumpling her face as she lay there, catching her breath. The other woman sighed, the sound wistful and full of regret.

     

                “Ah, what I’d give for another golden hour,” she murmured, talking for the sake of it, but perhaps knowing that Lena needed the droning sound of chatter to calm her. “My name’s Kara.”

     

                “Kara,” Lena whispered, her eyelids fluttering closed.

     

                “Yes, like that.”

     

                “Blue.”

     

                “What?”

     

                Lena’s lips twitched with the barest ghost of a smile and she sniffed, her nose hurting, before letting out a shaky breath. “Your name, it’s blue.”

     

                “My favourite colour; how did you know?”

     

                Closing her eyes, Lena exhaled as her body went slack against the floor, her fingertips pressed into the grit and a gust of cold air sweeping through the ventilation low down, making her shiver. She made a rough sound of amusement at the back of her throat as tears slid down her temples and across the bridge of her nose. Quiet for a long minute as she tried to swallow, the lump not going down easily, she let out a choked sob as the hysterical urge to laugh built in her chest.

     

                It came out broken and halting, so robotic and monotone that it was sad . Wiping at her face, Lena screwed her eyes shut and tried to ignore all the places that it hurt as she huddled on the concrete.

     

                “I know everything.”

     

                “Ah,” Kara murmured, “well … then you know it’s going to be okay.”

     

                Choking on a quiet laugh as a heavy weight pressed down on her chest, Lena swiped her thumb over her eyelids as she sniffed. For perhaps the first time in her life, she found herself not knowing the answer, but to hear it from this stranger, who owed her nothing, yet sounded so sure, eased the pain a little. 

    Chapter 2

                Lena was roused by the sound of metal scraping against gritty concrete. Pushing herself up a fraction, she was momentarily confused, having fallen asleep on the bare floor, and then hurriedly climbed to her feet at the sight of open air.

     

                Running toward the forcefield it snapped into place before she could take more than a step. Still, she let her feet carry her the rest of the way and slapped her palms against the barrier before lashing out and kicking the tray. It slid across the floor, the cup of water spilling over into the mashed potatoes.

     

                Moving over to her cot, Lena huddled on the mattress and pulled the scratching blanket over herself. The lights were still on inside her cell and she found it glaringly bright, stewing in her bitter anger and her silent panic. Her nose hurt and there was a yawning pit of worry inside her as she reassessed her circumstances.

     

                She wasn’t sure how she’d managed to drift off, only that the woman in the cell next to her had kept talking. Kara, her mind supplied, a name that she felt ought to be whispered, in those early blue hours before dawn, when the world was still and peaceful. Lena wanted to call out to her not, that small gap at the bottom of the wall located under her cot, but she didn’t know this woman at all, wasn’t here to make friends but find a way for them to let her out.

     

                She drifted off again eventually, restless with the sound of other people around her. Lena had never slept anywhere where she could hear the sound of someone snoring, of loud breathing and sleep talking. Even with the few attempts at relationships she’d had, she’d always chosen to go home with them, not liking the idea of anyone in her space, not liking the idea of being forced to be around someone she couldn’t evict. She’d never slept beside anyone else, and yet she was in a prison with nine other people within hearing distance.

     

                But, eventually, she slept and her body gratefully sank into it, trying to catch up on the missed hours where she’d been dragged from her bed and roughly violated. Her food remained untouched and even though she was starving, Lena had gone to bed without her dinner, defiant and stubborn as ever. When she woke, it was with an aching stomach though.

     

                “Prisoners, up and against the back wall,” the guard called Alex shouted.

     

                The fluorescent lights, which had been shut off during the night, flared to life, blindingly bright, and Lena hissed as she threw an arm across her eyes. Groggy and foul-tempered, she curled up beneath the blankets again and let her heavy eyelids close. 

     

                There was a bang on the barrier to get her attention.

     

                “Prisoner LL93, up against the back wall.”

     

                Choosing to ignore them, Lena pulled the pillow over her head for good measure. They could keep her there as long as they wanted to but that didn’t mean she’d comply. It didn’t mean Lena would give an inch unless forced to.

     

                And force her they did, the barrier coming down and rough hands hauling her to her feet a moment later. Her cheek was pressed against the concrete wall as her eyes snapped open, any semblance of sleep vanishing from sight, and those manacles were clapped back around her wrists, this time behind her back so her shoulders were uncomfortably pulled back.

     

                She was prodded into motion and scowled at the guard who ushered her along as she almost tripped over her own feet. Lena watched as two other women were dragged from their cells - one blonde with some sort of headpiece on, the other with dark hair - similarly bound and dressed identically. 

     

                Turning to try and peer into the cell beside hers for a glimpse of her neighbour, Lena was roughly jerked back around and propelled forward by the back of her uniform. Scowling as she was pushed into line behind the other two women, Lena followed them out at gunpoint as more guards closed in.

     

                Four of them escorted the three women through the prison and nobody spoke a word until they came to a door. Alex unlocked it and glanced at the two men that made up their company.

     

                “Wait out here.”

     

                The door opened to that infernal bathroom again and Lena's mouth twisted with contempt as the door hissed shut behind them, sealing the five of them inside.

     

                “You know the drill; five minutes,” Alex stated as she unlocked their manacles one by one.

     

                The women made no complaints and didn’t object as they quickly stripped off their clothes. Lena was slower to follow, haughty and silently fuming the whole time. They couldn’t remove their collars and she was highly aware that both women were armed, which was the only driving force in her undressing and stepping beneath the harsh spray of freezing cold water.

     

                Swallowing as her gorge rose at the greyish lump of soap, Lena washed briskly, trying to be thorough as the rough soap and freezing water left her feeling like her skin was being flayed from her body. Blood circled down the drain from her nose, which throbbed, but she felt better for being clean, even if it felt an awful lot like being tortured. Teeth chattering, she shut off the water a moment later and shivered her way over to the towel held out to her.

     

                The other two women had likewise been quick, finishing just after her, and the three of them were handed a new pile of clothes.

     

                “There's a storm today; you’ve been issued sweatshirts as well. It’ll be cold.”

     

                Lena fumbled with her clothes, hastily pulling them on, glad for the layers as she found a long-sleeved white cotton shirt too to go underneath. She was handed a small stick of deodorant, mercifully brand new, one of those small travel ones, and a disposable toothbrush too, relishing the minty flavour of the toothpaste as she scrubbed her teeth in the mirror.

     

                “So, what’s your name?”

     

                The dark-haired woman spoke and Lena slowed as she held her hair back and spat into the sink.

     

                “Lena.”

     

                “I’m Andrea. That’s Gayle - or Psi.”

     

                “What’d you do to end up here? Rare that humans get a sentence to this shithole,” the blonde drawled.

     

                “Quiet,” Alex murmured, bored.

     

                Lena rinsed out her mouth and tossed her toothbrush into the small trash bag attached to the trolley containing their clothes and hygiene products. She wanted to ask for a hairbrush but was too proud to ask for something or be denied it. Raking a hand through her hair, she then held her wrists out before herself to be cuffed again.

     

                They were marched back out into the hallway, but instead of heading straight back to their cells, they were taken down a different route. Stopping at a small room with a long counter and a steel mesh barrier, a door behind leading into an even bigger room beyond, stocked with numerous little boxes and orange bottles, they were lined up. One by one, the three of them were given a little white cup with pills in them.

     

                “What’re these?” Lena asked, her voice rasping from her shouting tirade the night before.

     

                “Vitamins. From the Doctor,” Alex curtly replied. “Swallow them.”

     

                Lena held the little paper cup in her hand and stared at them for a moment. One clear yellow oval one, a green and white capsule and a round red one. A faint smile graced Lena’s mouth as she let the cup slip from her fingers, bouncing slightly on the floor as the three pills scattered.

     

                Immediately, one guard grabbed a fistful of her hair and jerked her head down, Lena’s face spasming with pain, while another picked up her pills off the floor and the third unholstered their gun, directing it at the other two prisoners, who silently shifted into the corner, away from the trouble.

     

                “Sawyer.”

     

                The short woman who’d dragged Lena from her cell held the three vitamins and she grabbed Lena’s chin, squeezing where her jaws met to try and force Lena’s mouth open. It was painful but Lena ground her teeth together.

     

                “Careful - she bites,” Alex warned her.

     

                After a minute of struggling, Sawyer managed to force Lena’s mouth open as the other guard held her in place, and she tipped all three pills into her mouth and clamped her jaw shut. Covering Lena’s mouth with her hand, she pinched her nose shut as well so Lena had no choice but to swallow them instead of spitting them in her face.

     

                As the pills went down her dry throat with agonising slowness, Lena aimed a vicious kick at the short woman, who swore loudly and raised a hand. Alex stepped in, blocking her before the strike could land.

     

                “We’re here to guard, Sawyer.”

     

                Giving her a sneer, she pulled her arm from Alex’s grasp. “You might want to set her up for a visit with your little girlfriend. See if she can’t do something about that infamous Luthor insanity.”

     

                “Oh, you haven’t seen crazy yet,” Lena muttered through her teeth, stiff-faced and fuming.

     

                “Get them back to their cells; make sure this one doesn’t bring them back up.”

     

                “Move it,” Sawyer snapped, pushing Lena forward.

     

                Alex just clicked her tongue and sighed but didn’t intervene again. Lena didn’t expect her to either; she didn’t expect sympathy from anyone on the other side of the cells, and perhaps not from within either. One moment of kindness from someone in a similar situation, who had been there longer than her - by how much Lena didn’t know - didn’t make them allies, by any means.

     

                Back in her cell, uncuffed and her breakfast waiting for her - a tray of oats, an apple and a slice of toast with another cup of water - Lena gave Sawyer a sneer from behind the barrier before making her way over to the toilet.

     

                “Don’t even fucking think about it,” the guard warned her.

     

                Her smile grew and Lena sank to her knees before the metal toilet bowl, nothing if not petty and stubborn. But she didn’t even get the chance to bring the pills back up and piss off the guards before she found herself going rigid and collapsing back onto the floor, writhing in pain as the collar shocked her.

     

                “That’s enough,” Sawyer said into the small radio clipped to the shoulder of her vest. 

     

                The voltage ceased and Lena stared up at the ceiling, blinking back black spots as she panted, her skin beading with sweat. She lay there for a second before picking herself up and staring straight ahead at the trio of guards outside, watching her closely.

     

                Brushing her damp hair out of her face, Lena slowly walked over to her breakfast and the guards seemed to relax slightly, hands moving away from their batons. But Lena picked up the tray and stared down at the food before she threw it against the wall. Oats splattered across it in an arc and water spilt onto the floor.  Slamming the metal tray toward the ground, the sound loud and ringing, she moved over to her bed and pulled the blanket off it, a fit of rage consuming her. She tore open the pillow, pulling out the stuffing, and then dragged the pitifully thin mattress off and did the same, shaking hands pulling out old wads of cotton and tossing it around the cell.

     

                In the midst of that, they shocked her again, bringing Lena to her knees as her vision dimmed momentarily. When she climbed back to her feet, she doubled over and promptly brought up what little was in her stomach, coughing and choking on sour bile before she resumed her destruction.

     

                She didn’t manage to continue for much longer than that though, still dragging out the stuffing and causing a mess when a hand grabbed a fistful of her dark hair and a steel-capped boot kicked her knees out. Driven to the floor, Lena snarled up at Sawyer, who was glaring at her with such hatred that Lena couldn’t help but sneer back at her.

     

                “You really aren’t making it any easier for yourself,” she clicked her tongue, almost pleased in a way that Lena was making her life so difficult.

     

                “Fuck you,” Lena bitingly replied, spitting in her face.

     

                Jerking back in surprise, revulsion crossing the guard’s face, her eyes slid sideways to one of the other guards. He was the biggest one there and moved forward without a word, his gloved hand smacking Lena across the mouth and cheek before she could even blink.  A small gasp escaped her and she blinked as she stared down at the ground, the taste of blood filling her mouth. Swallowing thickly, cold anger swept through Lena, so much worse than her fiery rages, and she was still for a moment before going wild.

     

                On her knees, she tackled Sawyer around her legs and brought the guard crashing down before she scrambled on top of her and wrapped a hand around her throat. Digging her thumb in hard, Lena watched surprise flash across the woman’s face - but not panic because a moment later a heavy kick sent Lena sprawling sideways off her, pain blossoming in her rib cage.

     

                As she struggled to catch her breath, a shaky hand cradling her ribs, the third guard lashed out with his baton. Tendons going taut in Lena’s neck as her back arched off the ground, she let out a hoarse sound of pain before slumping. The other guy grabbed her hair and dragged her up, her feet tripping over themselves as he wouldn’t let her catch her balance.

     

                “Clean it up,” he ordered as he tossed her toward the mess of strewn cotton lumps.

     

                On her knees, hands in her lap as pain consumed her, Lena just hunched her shoulders and pressed her lips into a flat line to stop her chin from wobbling. Blinking back the stinging feeling of tears, she swallowed.

     

                “No,” she whispered.

     

                “Are you fucking deaf? I said clean it up.”

     

                “No,” Lena shouted back, jerking her chin up defiantly.

     

                The next punch struck her fully on her cheek, just at the corner of her eye, and she let out a strangled laugh as she pitched sideways. She didn’t care what they did to her, she would never comply, not to make it easier and not to save herself. They wouldn’t let her out for keeping a tidy cell and sitting meekly in the corner, but she would get their attention, even if it bought her bruises and broken bones.

     

                “Hey! Jensen, that’s enough.”

     

                Laying on the floor, the concrete cool against her red cheek, her split lip smarting and the other side of her face numb from the punch, Lena smiled faintly. There were raised voices and a sharp exchange of words before she was hauled to her feet.

     

                Her legs wouldn’t support her and she collapsed back down, wincing as pain lanced through her already bruised knees. Dragging her back up again, Alex gripped her arm and dragged her out of the cell.

     

                “And clean this mess up,” she snapped as she pulled Lena towards the doors.

     

                They hissed closed behind them and Lena shivered in the cold of the open hallway. Alex didn’t speak as she towed Lena along, her pace slowing a little when she realised that her prisoner was struggling, a pain lancing through Lena’s ribs with each step and her face numb and swelling. Still, she could feel the guard’s anger radiating from her but Lena wasn’t deluded into thinking it was out of any concern for herself.

     

                Passing through an airlock, they continued down a hallway until Alex brought them to a stop outside a door identical to the rest. She pressed her hand to the panel to unlock it and the door hissed open to reveal that doctor’s clinic again and Lena winced at the sight. She would have preferred to nurse her wounds alone in her cell.

     

                “What happened?” Doctor Danvers exclaimed, rising to her feet as her eyes widened.

     

                “She was causing a disturbance.”

     

                “You-“

     

                “I wasn’t there,” Alex bristled as she uncuffed Lena, “I was handling Prisoner KZ64’s shower time.”

     

                Rolling her eyes as she crossed over to them, putting an arm around Lena’s shoulder and propelling her over to the leather bed, Doctor Danvers’s mouth thinned.

     

                “I don’t know why you don’t just use their names. Lay down for me sweetie.”

     

                Lena lay back, closing her eyes as Doctor Danvers pulled in the examination light on an adjustable arm, bright as it cut across her face. She heard the snap of latex gloves and a squeaky cart dragged a bit closer and Doctor Danvers took a seat on a wheeled stool beside her.

     

                Clicking her tongue as she gently pressed her fingers to Lena’s swelling cheek, eliciting a sharp hiss as Lena turned from her touch. 

     

                “Less than a day and you’ve already ended up back here. You’re not off to a good start,” Doctor Danvers murmured, giving Lena a grim look.

     

                Lena let out a quiet huff of laughter that shook her chest and made her wince at the ache in her ribs. Her hand moved up to cradle her side and Doctor Danvers frowned.

     

                “Where does it hurt?”

     

                Pressing her mouth into a flat line, Doctor Danvers hesitated and then reached out to pull up Lena’s layers. She was gentle, the sweatshirt, baggy prison scrubs and the white undershirt peeled back to reveal the fresh bluish tint of forming bruises on Lena’s stomach. A small sound of shock escaped Doctor Danvers and she continued to pull her shirts up, revealing the blackening side of her rib cage.

     

                “My God, couldn’t they have given her a break for a single day?” Doctor Danvers said, aghast as she looked over at her daughter, who had the decency to look embarrassed. “Look at this! Brutalising my patients isn’t going to help them adjust.”

     

                “I stopped them.”

     

                “A little too late for that. I’ll be speaking to the Deputy about this.”

     

                Lena wanted to laugh again but knew it would hurt. There was nothing this doctor could say that would make them any more sympathetic toward her; Lena had dealt with the police before, dealt with investigators and detectives and all sorts, and none of them was particularly concerned about those they deemed criminals. And they’d made that assumption about Lena based on nothing more than her brother’s actions and her intelligence that allowed her to develop things ordinary people didn’t have the ability to. Where was the crime in either of those?

     

                “I’ll need to do an x-ray. It’s already bruised; they’ve probably broken something. There could be internal damage,” Doctor Danvers noted.

     

                “How long will it take?”

     

                “You can go,” Doctor Danvers dismissively replied.

     

                Alex scoffed, rolling her eyes, “I’m not going to leave you alone with a prisoner.”

     

                “She’s been beaten to a pulp; remind me, who’s the threat here?”

     

                Silent for a moment as she stood rigidly, meeting her mother’s expectant gaze, Alex opened and closed her mouth before her lips flattened into a line.

     

                “Don’t forget why we’re here.”

     

                Scoffing, Alex looked away. “You shouldn’t talk like that. If someone hears-“

     

                “Who’s going to tell them? You.”

     

                “Stop it,” Alex muttered. “I’m trying to do my job.”

     

                “Then do your job and go and report the guard who did this.”

     

                Mouth flattening as she looked down, hands curling into fists, Alex sighed heavily and Lena was silent as she followed the conversation with interest. She was still as Doctor Danvers’s hands gently probed her bruised ribs. Anything they said could be used against them and Lena was too smart to waste the opportunity.

     

                “It was Maggie.”

     

                “Ah. Well, she’s already angry at you.”

     

                Alex left after a moment with promises of returning afterwards and Doctor Danvers moved to her tray, rummaging around. She reappeared at Lena’s side with a cotton ball dipped in an antiseptic liquid held in a pair of forceps. Lena kept still as Doctor Danvers dabbed at her cuts, the stinging making her face spasm with pain.

     

                “What did you do?” Doctor Danvers quietly asked after a long few minutes of silence.

     

                Lena let out a breathless laugh. “Threw my food. Pulled my stuffing out of my pillow and mattress. Vomited up those pills they gave me after they shocked me.”

     

                “Ah. You really should take your vitamins and eat your food.”

     

                Mouth twisting derisively as her eyelids fluttered and she breathed in shallowly, Lena made a sound of amusement at the back of her throat.

     

                “I don’t think so.”

     

                “Listen, I know this is all turning out … badly for you. But you need to pull your head in or you’re going to end up hurt. Worse than this.”

     

                Chin dimpling as her mouth turned down at the corners, Lena sniffed. “Can you help me?”

     

                Stilling, Doctor Danvers grimaced. “I can’t. There’s no way out of this place. If I could get my daughter off here, I would’ve done it a long time ago.”

     

                “I’m not supposed to be here. I’m- I’m not …”

     

                Hushing her as she pulled her layers back down, the other woman gave Lena a pitying look. “No one is supposed to be here. But we are. Now, I need to take you next door for an x-ray of those ribs.”

     

                She helped Lena sit up, a small gasp of pain escaping her patient as her ribs twinged, and unlocked a door to the adjoining room, where a bed occupied the middle of the space. Doctor Danvers made her lay down again and pulled the adjustable arm of the x-ray machine positioned above her. She was helped out of her three shirts and the collar around her neck, the leather bed stuck to her clammy lower back as Doctor Danvers set up the machine. 

     

                There was a small room with the controls and the doctor tucked herself away in there while the machine whirred, taking scans of Lena’s chest. Doctor Danvers had the results a few minutes later, attaching them to the light panel on the wall, revealing two cracked ribs.

     

                Listening to her breath sounds once she’d redressed, Doctor Danvers was confident that there was no internal bleeding and was gentle as she felt her stomach for any distension. Back in the medical room, the doctor fetched her a gel ice pack and let Lena sit on the edge of the bed with it pressed to one side of her face, alternating it.

     

                “Do you want some cookies? Juice?”

     

                “No.”

     

                “Your blood sugar will be low if you haven’t eaten breakfast. You didn’t eat lunch yesterday either. You were being flown here, drugged, at breakfast yesterday, and Alex said you didn’t eat your dinner. Your blood tests came back with low iron as well.”

     

                “It’s none of your concern.”

     

                Humming dubiously, Doctor Danvers walked over to the fridge and fetched the small packet of mini chocolate chip cookies and a juice box and set it down beside Lena. Taking a seat on her stool, she typed away on the tablet, making a note for Lena’s file.

     

                “You should take what you can get while you’re in here. It’s not usually a frequent occurrence with most prisoners, aside from the monthly check-up. Cookies and juice are usually the highlights of the month, so don’t let the other prisoners know you’ve been shown any favouritism.”

     

                “Favouritism?” Lena echoed with a breathless laugh, her mouth twisting wryly. “Lady, don’t act like you’re doing me any favours.”

     

                “I know I’m not. But I won’t let them strip my humanity from me while I’m here.”

     

                Lena scoffed quietly and ended up picking up the juice box, stabbing the straw into the hole and taking a sip. Her split lip stung but the apple juice washed away the coppery taste of blood. 

     

                It was almost an hour before Alex eventually returned, Lena’s face swollen and bruised despite the ice pack, and her neck free of the collar for a short while. It was a reprieve, she thought, but it didn’t give her any pause in her plans to escape. Whether it be tomorrow or in a decade, Lena wouldn’t sit and wait for her death to greet her inside a cell.

     

                For the most part, the doctor was quiet, turning on a little speaker and playing some music - for Lena’s benefit, she realised, denied any entertainment so far - and in her beaten state, Lena didn’t feel quite so bad. The shock of being there hadn’t worn off yet, and the anger was still raging inside, but it was a momentary pause that allowed her to catalogue and take stock, picking up on what little information she could. When she shook out some painkillers, Lena swallowed them gratefully.

     

                When the doors slid open and Alex stepped in, Doctor Danvers reached for her shock collar and attached it with a murmured apology. Setting the considerably warmer ice pack on the bench, Lena eased herself down and stared coldly at Alex.

     

                “If anything else happens to her-“

     

                “I spoke to Deputy Lane.”

     

                “I’ll keep her in one of the private medical rooms for a month if she ends up back here in this state.”

     

                “I’ll keep an extra eye on her.”

     

                Smiling softly, the doctor patted her daughter’s cheek and Alex grimaced faintly. Opening the door, Alex stepped outside and waited for Lena. She didn’t rush her and didn’t drag her back to her cell and didn’t cuff her again, perhaps sensing that Lena didn’t have the energy. 

     

                “I’m sorry, you know,” Alex said as they stood in the airlock, the air pressurising before the doors before them hissed open. “They shouldn’t have done that to you.”

     

                “I didn’t expect anything less.”

     

                “We’re not all-“

     

                “Yes, you are. You work here, for the government. You’re all exactly the same.”

     

                Conceding, despite the circumstances that had brought the officer to the prison, Alex nodded and they resumed their walk in silence. Another guard opened the doors to the prison, along with Alex, and Lena was silent as she made her way back to her cell.

     

                The mess had been cleaned up, the wall and floor scrubbed clean with bleach, the odour strong in the air as Lena was ushered over the threshold of the cell. Her cot was bare of a mattress and pillow though, nothing but the scratchy blanket on the hard steel mesh, and her eyes were bright with sharp anger as her lips twisted wryly.

     

                “You should take it easy for a bit,” Alex softly cautioned her as the forcefield was activated.

     

                Choking on a laugh, Lena moved over to the bed and gingerly sat down, her ribs hurting even through the mild numbing of the painkillers. Heaving a weary sigh, she ran a hand over her face and hissed at the pain. One eye was swollen shut, limiting her vision slightly, and her cheek was stiff and lips thick.

     

                Left alone, she sat on the edge of the cot, unable to even lay down because the thought of moving made her wince. Exhaling softly, she closed her eyes and listened to the sound in the silence of the prison. 

     

                “Lena.”

     

                She startled at the sound of her name being softly called from beneath her. Glancing down, she hesitated and then eased herself off the hard mesh of the cot, down onto the floor as she bared her teeth in pain.

     

                “Yes?”

     

                “Where’d you go?”

     

                “Ah … they took me to shower.”

     

                Kara let out a soft laugh, “took a long time. How generous of them.”

     

                “Yeah,” Lena mumbled, touching her thumb to her lip. “How come they didn’t bring you?”

     

                “Ah, well, the meta-humans go first. It’s only the three of you on this cell block. Then they take the aliens that aren’t as dangerous in pairs. The dangerous ones go alone.”

     

                “So … you’re an alien?”

     

                “Mm. To this planet, I suppose,” Kara haltingly replied. “And you’re a meta-human?”

     

                Swallowing thickly, Lena's lips twitched with frustration as she closed her eyes to the concrete wall separating the two of them.

     

                “No,” she eventually murmured. “No, I’m just- I’m human. I … I don’t have any powers.”

     

                Kara’s reply was long to come and her voice was quiet. “Then what the hell did you do to end up here?”

     

                With a quiet scoff of laughter, Lena smiled faintly. “Believe it or not, I’m so smart they thought it had to be inhuman.”

     

                “Hm.”

     

                Neither of them spoke for such a long while after that that Lena thought Kara might have fallen asleep - she hadn’t moved, that much she was sure of, but the cell was silent.
