                Kara started to question Alex’s suggestion but then pressed her lips into a flat line. As Alex retreated back to her corner, Kara’s eyes slid back to Lena and she gave her a searching look as Lena stared back, her expression blank and her posture feigning more nonchalance than she really felt. Still, it was a surprise that Kara saw straight through her, not knowing the first thing about Lena’s mannerisms but knowing Alex well enough to let out a small laugh as her face furrowed.

     

                “You haven’t asked her have you?”

     

                “Yes, I did.”

     

                It wasn’t a lie so Lena didn’t feel guilty about it. She idly tapped a finger on the table and Kara watched her, hesitating before replying. Her voice was soft and defeated as her shoulders slumped.

     

                “She said no.”

     

                Lena stopped tapping, straightening up as she quietly cleared her throat. “A small setback. She’ll come around, though.”

     

                Letting out a small huff, Kara’s mouth thinned with displeasure and Lena’s stomach jolted. Climbing to her feet, the alien frowned with a wounded look in her blue eyes as she stood over Lena and their drawings. 

     

                “You lied to me. Friends shouldn’t do that to each other.”

     

                Mouth opening and closing as she tried to protest, Lena’s face softened with dismay as she watched Kara walk away and take a seat beside J’onn. Folding her cuffed arms over her chest, she watched Jeopardy while Lena was left to her own devices. Her eyes darted over to Alex with annoyance and found the guard looking at her with a distinctly pleased air about her.

     

                Making a scathing sound at the back of her throat, Lena ducked her head down to hide her burning cheeks as embarrassment slammed into her. She wasn’t used to being chastened like that, and her pride made her bristle, but mostly she was ashamed that she’d so readily lied to the one person she genuinely liked inside the prison, the one person on her side, who was willing to help her reckless plan to escape. She shouldn’t have done that.

     

                Picking up the crayons, Lena continued her drawing until their time was up and they were all instructed to pack everything away. J’onn switched off the TV, Psi shuffled the cards back into a deck and Lena tossed the paper in the trash and put the checkerboard away with the crayons. They took Kara first and the rest afterwards until it was Lena and the two metahuman women left. 

     

                Distracted as she was taken back to her cell, Lena was wrapped up in her own thoughts, bringing up the rear of their procession. Alex walked behind her and chuckled quietly as they walked down the hallway.

     

                “What’d you do to piss her off?”

     

                “Who said I did anything?”

     

                “She’s the sweetest person I’ve ever met - not that it’s hard when this place is pretty much all I know - but she’s naïve as hell and believes the best in everyone. Until you prove her otherwise and then she has this whole … wounded puppy act.”

     

                Lena snorted, her mouth thinning as she kept her eyes trained forward. “You clearly know firsthand and she still trusts you; I’m not bothered.”

     

                “Fuck with her and I’ll have you transferred to the other side of the prison. She’s not yours to manipulate.”

     

                “I’m not manipulating her,” Lena scoffed, contempt hardening her features. “I’m the only one who gives a shit that she’s trapped in here. If you cared about her half as much as you pretend to, we wouldn’t even be having this conversation. She’d be far away, at a beach somewhere.”

     

                Alex let out a harsh laugh. “For someone so smart, you’re pretty clueless.”

     

                Scoffing, Lena didn’t reply and walked the rest of the way back without another word. The chained cuffs were unlocked and they were brought their lunch once everyone was settled back inside. Lena poked at the soggy sandwich and slowly peeled the orange instead, eating the segments piece by piece and setting her tray down near the forcefield after finishing off her water.

     

                Once she’d finished, she wriggled under the bed with her scratchy blanket, feeling the chill of the cell as she curled in on herself. Near the narrow gap bridging the cells, she slipped a folded-up piece of paper from her sleeve and nudged it through the gap. The paper was just long enough to go through and she gave it a quick push to help it along, the gritty dirt scraping. 

     

                Listening closely, after a moment she heard the sound of someone moving and the subsequent sound of unfolding paper. There was a pause and then the sound of the paper being folded again. Swallowing thickly, Lena winced slightly.

     

                “I’m sorry I lied.”

     

                “You should trust me more.”

     

                “I do trust you. I just- I didn’t want to upset you.”

     

                “I’m more upset about you lying than Alex not helping. But if you’d told me, I could’ve worked on her. She trusts me.”

     

                “Kara,” Lena started before sighing heavily. She squeezed her eyes shut and rubbed her fingers over her eyelids. “She hates me, so she’s not going to trust you when it’s directly related to me. She … well, she thinks I’m a bad influence, that I’m manipulating you.”

     

                “Isn’t that what you were just doing.”

     

                Cringing, Lena shifted beneath the bed. “No. If I was manipulating you, it would be for my own benefit. But I want to get you out too. We are friends.”

     

                There was coy amusement in Kara’s voice when she replied. “I know. Alex is all bark, no bite. Isn’t that the saying? I’ve heard the other guards say it before because she’s never cruel to me. She used to sneak me extra food when they weren’t feeding me enough. She’s always looked out for me like a sister would, I think. I think it used to be because she was lonely and we were about the same age, but I do trust her. I’ve been in here a long time; I know her better than I know anyone else.”

     

                Lena didn’t want to believe that the agent was even remotely good but she had to admit she didn’t know her that well. But she had to be somewhat trustworthy to not report Lena to the Deputy for talking about plotting an escape. Lena didn’t trust easily though, least of all anyone on the other side of the cell forcefield, no matter how much Kara put her faith in the guard.

     

                “Then you'll have to try your hardest to convince her - and the doctor. I can’t do this without you.”

     

                “I can’t do it without you either. But that means we have to trust each other, and you have to tell me things.”

     

                Hesitating, Lena was torn. Could she trust Kara? Or was this some elaborate scheme to coax information out of her with a pretty face and friendly words as the isolation and poor conditions made her let her guard down? Kara felt almost too good to be true, too sane to be believed. But after a moment of deliberation, Lena decided she had nothing to lose; if Kara could be trusted, then she had someone to help her fight her way out of the prison, and if she couldn’t, she wouldn’t mind that Lena wouldn’t tell her everything.

     

                “Okay.”

     

                “Okay.”

     

                There was a pause and Lena heard the scrape of unfolding paper, followed by Kara’s quiet laugh.

     

                “Is it supposed to be a hummingbird?”

     

                Wrinkling her nose as her cheeks warmed, Lena self-consciously laughed. “Yeah. I’m not known for my artistic skills.”

     

                “I guess that’s why you went into science. Thank you, though.”

     

                “I wish I could see you again,” Lena murmured, her back to the wall as she tugged the blanket tighter around herself. “It’s different, talking face-to-face, don’t you think?”

     

                “You get used to it. It’s been a long time since speaking to people face-to-face longer than a few minutes a day has felt normal.”

     

                Lena let out a hoarse laugh, strangled and bitter. “I don’t want to get used to it.”

     

                “You won’t have to. When we’re out of here … you’ll be so sick of looking at my face, you’ll wish you could stare at this wall instead.”

     

                A soft huff escaped Lena as her lips twitched with a smile, cheeks shallowly dimpling. “I don’t think I’d ever get sick of looking at your face. I mean … you’re very interesting to me.”

     

                “Why? Because I don’t have antennas?” Kara lightly teased.

     

                “Something like that.” 

     

                Even if she hadn’t known she was an alien, even if they’d been outside, Lena thought she would have noticed her and paid attention if she’d seen her on the street, at a coffee shop or at a conference. Closing her eyes, she tried to envision Kara’s smile, the way her face had gently crumpled, eyebrows and ears rising slightly, eyes creasing, cheeks rosy. She hadn’t seen the expression enough for her memory to do it justice though and she let out a soft sigh, her body relaxing against the cold concrete.

     

                “I feel like … I’d like to be alone with you. I don’t know. Maybe it’s the lack of social interaction - which, funnily enough, never used to bother me when I could seek it out on my own terms when I needed it - but … I think you understand me, and if we spent some time alone together, not stuck on opposite sides of a wall in a prison, we’d be able to help each other out. I like talking to you.”

     

                “I like talking to you too.”

     

                And if they were stuck in there, Lena was glad it was in adjoining cells. If she was locked away in a prison, she would gladly share a prison cell wall with Kara and plot their escape, because she listened and remembered and made the pain of being there just a little bit smaller. Hopefully, it wouldn’t be for too long, but she was an interesting distraction and Lena was oddly grateful for her company.

     

                “Well, soon enough we’ll have all the time in the world to talk. Away from here. I promise you, better days are coming.”

    Chapter 9

                Scratching another line into the row on the wall, a light powder of cement raining down as she held the scalpel delicately, Lena quietly conversed with Kara as she mined any information that could have been useful. 

     

                “What we need is a distraction,” Lena said, running her thumb over the shallow groove and blowing away the grit. “Something that’ll give me time.”

     

                “I can cause a distraction,” Kara said with amusement. “I’m actually quite good at it. Only because they’re all scared of me.”

     

                Lena hummed dubiously, “I don’t want them to hurt you.”

     

                “Wouldn’t it be better to experience a little bit of pain for eventual freedom as opposed to a placid life in here forever?”

     

                “That’s a matter of preference.”

     

                “Well, I know you’d pick the pain.”

     

                “Of course! Short-term pain, long-term gain.”

     

                Kara’s laugh made Lena’s lips twitch with a smile and she tucked the scalpel back into the metal frame of her cot, her eyes skipping along the row of tallied lines. 

     

                “You know-”

     

                “Prisoner LL93.”

     

                Lena ducked her head out from beneath the cot and saw Alex standing at her forcefield. Sighing, Lena scooted out and climbed to her feet, dusting grit from her hands as she walked over to the agent at a leisurely pace. Alex’s expression was unreadable and Lena raised her eyebrows, as haughty as ever.

     

                “Up against the wall,” Alex ordered her.

     

                Rolling her eyes as she turned around and strolled towards the back wall, Lena paused halfway and ducked down, hooking her finger in the back of her shoe as if she was adjusting it. Her eyes glanced under the bed and her lips twitched with a smile as she kept her voice low, knowing Kara’s sensitive hearing would pick up on it.

     

                “I think our distraction time is here already.”

     

                Straightening up and shaking her leg out as if she was just readjusting, Lena walked to the back wall and leaned against it, watching as Alex spoke into her radio and the forcefield vanished. Unlatching a set of manacles from her belt, Alex held them out and Lena offered up her wrists so she could be cuffed, the weight of them making her shoulders curve as her arms were dragged down. 

     

                “Walk.”

     

                Pushing off the wall, she crossed her cell and stepped outside, backtracking to the side as she craned her neck to catch a glimpse of Kara. She caught a fleeting snippet of a lanky figure stretched out on her cot, the soles of her shoes towards the forcefield and little else of her visible beyond the grey of her scrubs as Lena was jerked forward. Alex gave her a disgruntled look that made the corners of Lena’s mouth twitch. There was some satisfaction to be had knowing it annoyed Alex that she was so friendly with Kara.

     

                “Where are we going?” Lena asked. “Can’t be a doctor or shrink visit; it hasn’t been long enough yet.”

     

                Alex was silent as she led her to the doors accessing the hallway beyond the cell block and waited until they were through the other side before she finally spoke. “What’s that got to do with anything? If the doctor asks to see you, you go.”

     

                “Do you always do what your mom says or does she just have more power here?”

     

                “No one has any power here.”

     

                “I don’t know, I think the people with guns have some power.”

     

                “The people with guns aren’t criminals.”

     

                “Neither are the ones without them.”

     

                “Some of them are. Some of them have killed a lot of people.”

     

                “My hands are clean,” Lena said through thin lips, a muscle jumping in her jaw.

     

                “Your mind is not,” Alex countered.

     

                “What would you know? You’ve spent over half of your life inside here; you don’t have a clue who I am.”

     

                Alex made a disgruntled sound as she led Lena right down a hallway, “I know who you are. We still get news inside here so I know who you are.”

     

                “Then you know I was merely a scientist, an engineer, a businesswoman . I never hurt anybody. I’d wager you have a hell of a lot more blood on your hands than I do.”

     

                “A hazard of the job. A job I never wanted.”

     

                “Then why do you do it?”

     

                “There aren’t a lot of job opportunities here. For obvious reasons.”

     

                “Better a janitor than a government goon.”

     

                Alex let out a sharp laugh, “better to be higher on the hierarchy and try and make a difference than be one of the bottomfeeders exiled here as a step above a prisoner.”

     

                “So you agree, you have power.”

     

                “Not enough. But … enough to get you out of your cell to make yourself useful. A few of the circuits are shorting again; you’ll be helping Agent Schott do the repairs to speed things along.”

     

                A jolt of excitement shot through Lena and she forced herself to swallow as her heart lodged itself in her throat, her pulse racing as her mind quickly ran through a series of opportunities. 

     

                “Yes ma’am.”

     

                Scoffing, Alex shook her head as they walked side by side. “Just behave yourself.”

     

                Pressing her lips into a flat line, Lena didn’t respond. Escorted through to one of the tool stations, a cramped room with a metal grille partitioning the space and all manner of hand tools lining the shelves, Alex pointed Lena onto a metal folding chair while the mousy-haired man she’d seen on her first day pottered about behind the secured area.

     

                “Prisoner’s ready to go,” Alex called out, knocking on the grille.

     

                “I’m just looking for my … there it is! Wrench. Okay, that’s it. Let me just grab the toolbox.”

     

                Winn unlocked the door from the inside and stepped into the cramped area with the rusted and dented toolbox in tow. The three of them filed out of the room, Winn taking the lead and Alex penning Lena in as she brought up the rear. Enjoying the simple act of being out of her cell, Lena tried to walk as slowly as possible as she drank in the sight of cameras and doors, marking what was behind the open ones and trying to understand protocols. 

     

                They came to the same room the last time she’d lent her expertise and Lena idled in the corner as Alex helped shift a ladder and Winn scuttled up to remove the ceiling panel. Waiting as they got everything ready, Lena startled slightly at the crackling sound of the radio on Alex’s shoulder as she was uncuffed and gestured towards the ladder. Standing beside it as Winn slipped through the roof, his radio also transmitting a message, Lena listened intently. 

     

                “Agent Vasquez, calling for backup. We’ve got Prisoner KZ64 trying to break out of her cell. Over.”

     

                Lena knew Kara’s code by now and blinked, trying not to reveal any signs of recognition as she loitered at the bottom of the ladder. Alex stiffened, her face hardening and a shallow furrow of worry creasing her brow as she reached for her radio.

     

                “Copied. Agent Danvers, confirming backup is on the way. Don’t do anything rash. I’ll be there shortly. Over.”

     

                Alex glanced sideways at Lena and then up at Winn, who was halfway up the ladder. “I need to go and handle this. You’ll be alright with her?”

     

                Lena pretended to be oblivious to their conversation, glancing around the space as she rubbed her raw wrists. She felt both pairs of eyes land on her before a decision was made.

     

                “Lock the door behind you,” Winn said after a moment.

     

                “Radio if you need help,” Alex replied before her eyes slid to Lena. “Behave.”

     

                Giving her a lazy salute as she smiled thinly, Lena watched Alex leave and listened to the sound of the door locking. Glancing up through the hole in the ceiling, she took in the pale, meek face of the other agent. When he swallowed she could have sworn it was audible.

     

                “Pass the toolbox up,” Winn instructed her.

     

                “Copy that,” Lena mockingly replied, reaching down to heft it up as she ran through her options.

     

                He stuck an arm through the hole but Lena couldn’t pass it up without climbing halfway up the ladder first, and as she climbed, lugging the toolbox with her, it was only logical to her that she take advantage of her opportunity. She kept her eyes trained on Winn, following him up the ladder like a shadow, her pale face impassive as her mind ran through her plan without betraying a single thought. 

     

                Hefting the toolbox, Lena passed it up as she rose with it, her left hand reaching for Winn’s holstered gun. The metal was cool and Lena’s hands were quick as she yanked it free, shoving the toolbox at him at the same time so that he was forced back on his haunches, blinking in surprise as he clutched the toolbox to his chest.

     

                Forcing herself up through the hole quickly, Lena blinked at the darkness as she willed her eyes to adjust and heard the clang of the toolbox set aside. Blindly searching for Winn, she winced as a sharp beam of torchlight fell across her face, throwing an arm up in defence. 

     

                “What’re you playing at?” he asked, a little nervous to be alone with her, the wild card that was very contrary in her moods.

     

                Lowering her arm, Lena smiled slowly and he blanched, reaching for his radio to call for backup. Lena threw herself at him, knocking him backwards on one of the support beams, but despite his relatively short stature, only several inches taller than Lena herself, he was stronger than her, especially in her weakened state as a prisoner. Winn managed to roll her off him, pinning Lena to the beam and then freezing at the sound of a hammer clicking into place and the cold muzzle of a gun pressed under his jaw.

     

                Flinching back, Winn’s eyes were wide in the gloom as his hands scrambled at his waist. Realisation elicited a small sound of surprise at his blunder and he reached for his radio again in a last-ditch effort to call for help as Lena thumbed the hammer back up and swung her arm, catching him on the temple with the butt of the pistol. 

     

                He sprawled to the side into the insulation, his elbow striking the edge of another support beam as Winn hissed, his hand going to his head. Still conscious, he gave Lena a fearful look and she bit back a sigh as she struck him again without any relish.

     

                “Sorry,” she mumbled to the unconscious form, fumbling at his belt in the dark for the spare cuffs he carried. 

     

                She dragged him a short way off to the side, resting him gently on the insulation and hoping he wouldn’t fall through the ceiling before cuffing him and dragging the ladder up through the hole and replacing the ceiling panel. Tucking the gun into the waistband of her scrub pants, Lena picked up Winn’s lit torch and shone it around, closing her eyes as she recalled the steps she’d taken through each hallway and room to get up to that point. Confident in her mental recall, Lena squatted beside the toolbox and ferreted out a few useful tools to cause as much havoc and help for herself as possible before concluding she was as prepared as possible given the circumstances, and silently praising Kara for her on the fly distraction, although Lena hoped she hadn’t gotten herself hurt in the process.

     

                Putting those thoughts aside for now, envisioning the door of the room below, Lena precariously crawled over to the point it was situated below and then turned as if she’d just walked out. Quietly counting under her breath, she retraced her steps through the confined ceiling space, back to her cell as she tried to keep her bearings straight, the vents and wires and pipes making it hard for her to envision where she’d be located down below. 

     

                Once she was confident she was within the realms of her own cell, Lena carried on a few more steps to the adjoining cell, her throat constricted as panic settled in. This was her one chance to try and hash out the beginnings of her escape plan, knowing that any flimsy trust she’d accrued would be in the bin by the time they caught her again, if they didn’t put a bullet in her on sight. 

     

                Torch clamped between her teeth as sweat beaded on her forehead and she breathed in the dusty air, Lena clawed at the insulation, filling the close air with even more particles that made her throat itch. She burrowed through to the ceiling panel that she was sure was Kara’s cell and started carving out the rest of the square, clearing the space out so that the panel could be pried up at the edges. 

     

                Wiping her forehead on the dirty white sleeve of her undershirt, Lena sat back for a second and listened, wondering how long she’d have until Alex or another guard came to check on Winn and found his unconscious and manacled form just beside the open panel. If they didn’t find him soon, he’d wake up on his own and that would pose a similar problem. Lena hoped to be a few cell blocks over by then, lost in the warren of the prison without a digital trace to give her away. Even with the meagre food rations they were supplied with, Lena imagined she’d survive a few days of starvation for the sake of research purposes, and it wouldn’t have been unfamiliar grounds for her anyway. Only, there would be no medium-rare sirloin and bottle of Malbec as a victory dinner after she was done with her obsessive research this time. 

     

                Using a flat-head screwdriver, Lena prised the edge up a fraction and then was still as she waited a moment before continuing. Cautiously lowering herself down to her stomach, she had her head in the hole she’d made in the insulation and lifted the panel up another inch as she tried to see inside. It was the unmistakable design of a cell and her stomach jolted with relieved surprise, but as she lifted it up further, dust raining down and a wider swathe of the cell visible, she couldn’t see Kara within it. That didn’t mean it wasn’t her cell though and Lena cautiously lowered the panel back down and wriggled back up onto the support beam.

     

                Filling in the hole again with the loose insulation making her cough, Lena moved a few squares over and started the process of clearing the insulation off a different panel, this one revealing itself to be up against the wall, above the empty cot below. The ceilings were too high for anyone to be able to escape through the panels, which was probably why everyone was still imprisoned there, but she had a plan in mind to get Kara out and at least they had a shot this way.

     

                She left the panel uncovered for easy access from below, the grime that had the panel stuck fast now disturbed by Lena’s prising, and she was pleased with her efforts as she tucked away her screwdriver and shuffled off on hands and knees. The torch offered a narrow beam of light to see by but it was still awkward and slow as she crawled beneath pipes wider than she was, clambered over vents, feeling the damp chill of the metal above her, the knowledge of the ocean only feet away making her feel claustrophobic and nervous. Lena wasn’t sure how long she’d been up there yet - perhaps half an hour or more, and her time allowance running out. 

     

                In the end, she clicked the torch off, knowing it would give her away soon, and she went by touch alone, trying to be as quick as she could. Luckily, there were any number of hissing steam pipes or gurgling water ones, ones leaking and groaning, vents whirring and wires sparking as the old prison tried to keep itself running, and the noise covered the quiet scuffling of her movements through the roof of the place. Trying to mask the way she’d come, Lena didn’t so much as touch a wire to sabotage the systems, knowing that if the cameras or lights went down in one area, they’d know exactly which direction she’d been heading in.

     

                She must’ve crawled almost a mile by the time she heard voices, dim but angry and frantic, and Lena hurriedly wormed her way beneath a pipe and lay waiting, her breaths short and shallow as panic tightened her chest. Behind her, she caught sight of the cutting beam of a torch and swallowed dryly, her mouth filled with dust and an ache in her throat for clean water. She waited there for what must have been five minutes before continuing onwards, knowing that her time was borrowed now. However long it took for them to find her now was an added bonus.

     

                Carrying on, Lena crawled to the point of exhaustion, the cold of the place leaving her shivering and aching despite the sweat from her exertion. She had no clue where she was now, how far the prison even went on, but she kept going anyway until she reached an edge. Which direction it was, Lena couldn’t have said, but she’d hit the edge of the prison now and knew the only way to go was to follow the wall a while before backtracking and seeing where she came out. 

     

                Following her course, Lena didn’t account for the collar around her neck. When the jolt of electricity came, it was incapacitating as her whole body stiffened, tendons taut and teeth grit hard enough to draw blood as she involuntarily bit her tongue, there was nothing Lena could do but endure it as she swallowed a hoarse scream of agony. 

     

                The pain passed quickly and she was left gasping and limp, a lingering burning pain filling her body as she tried to overcome it. Once she’d managed to make her body move again, Lena pushed herself up and kept moving, crawling forward, foot by foot through the cramped space, every muscle burning and her lungs aching from disturbing the decades worth of accumulated dirt, her hands touching things she didn’t want to think about, drops of frigid water soaking into the back of her grey scrub top. Lena desperately needed a shower, she needed a cup of water, a bruised apple, and her shitty cot to sleep off her exhaustion. She’d be lucky if she saw her cell again.

     

                They shocked her twice more and she could hear the dim sound of an alarm below, and by the time the third one receded to a tingling pain, Lena couldn’t move any further. She was just so tired, her body stiff and locked up, her eyes raw and her hands and clothes and face filthy. Dragging herself over to the nearest panel, she prayed it was somewhere private and was rewarded with what looked like a supply closet. 

     

                Trying to covertly check for cameras, Lena didn’t find any blinking red lights in the corner and eased herself down onto the metal edge of a sink, her shoes squeaking on the linoleum as she came onto solid ground for the first time in hours. It was an effort to stay standing, gripping the cold edge of the metal as she breathed in clean air and then let out a hoarse sound of relief. 

     

                Hunching over the sink, she breathed for a few minutes until her heart rate settled and then turned on the tap. The water was baltic, so cold that it made Lena’s knuckles ache and her nails turn lavender as the filth was washed away and she splashed it over her face and hair, trying to rinse away as much of the dirt as she could. Then she bent her mouth to the tap and scooped handfuls of the freezing water to her lips, rinsing out the dust and grit coating her tongue and spitting it out before she drank until her stomach hurt. 

     

                Once she felt a little more refreshed, Lena glanced around the storage space, lit by a bare bulb and filled with mops and bottles of bleach and shelves of toilet paper. Tired from her efforts, she deemed it as safe a spot as any to have a nap, climbing back up into the ceiling to shift the panel back into place before she moved one situated above the steel shelving unit holding the packages of toilet paper. Slipping through, she stretched out as much as she could on the top shelf, using the packages as a screen against anyone searching for her there. As far as hiding places went, it wasn’t the best but it was all Lena could do given the circumstances and she hoped they wouldn’t think to look for her in a cupboard that was barely five feet wide.

     

                After sleeping perhaps a couple of hours, Lena woke up stiff and with a pain in the side of her neck from sleeping awkwardly. Listening carefully before she moved, Lena slunk down off the shelves and drank some more from the sink before climbing back up into the ceiling. She didn’t dare to move for a few minutes, straining her ears for the sound of any agents crawling around nearby, looking for the sweeping signs of a torch seeking her out but if they were searching for her they were a way off yet.

     

                Continuing her crawling, she carved a path upwards, wondering how big the prison was and how she was going to get back to her own cell block if it came to it, knowing even her memory wasn’t good enough for her to retrace her steps. It seemed to never end as she pushed onwards, covered in filth again soon enough, trying to stifle her coughs as she stirred up fresh dirt and dust, repulsed by a dead rat she found and the breath catching in her throat as she crawled through a spiderweb and was left with the sensation of things crawling all over her. Her stomach growled at missed meals and Lena was tasered once more, the shock collar leaving angry red welts on her neck beneath the metal. 

     

                She wondered how long they would look for her or if they were content to let her run loose until she starved to death up in the ceiling or gave herself away on purpose, knowing that Lena would never be stupid enough to slip up accidentally. Lena already knew she would push herself to the brink of death to uncover as much information as possible about the prison and feeling less urgent and hunted than she had earlier - or perhaps the day before, time blending together indecipherably - she risked opening a few more panels. 

     

                One of them was a close call, a guard station with a radio blasting the score for a baseball game, fortunately empty as she assumed all guards were called off to search for her, and she decided it wasn’t worth the risk to check for cameras so she could steal some snacks. Another was a room where a large amount of pipes congregated and Lena eased herself down into the steaming space, barely able to see in front of her as she scalded herself on numerous pipes trying to work her way through the room.

     

                She went to town on a few gauges and used a wrench to try and loosen some old, rusted knuts, turning the stiff mechanical wheel and fraying a few wires in a control panel on the wall before she scrambled back up into the ceiling, the soles of her shoes almost melting off at the heat of the pipes as she struggled back up. It wasn’t enough damage for her to be identified as being there but it would create problems slowly but surely and that was all she was aiming for.

     

                Repeating the tactic a couple more times as she went, finding a room with a boiler unit and another with a bunch of wiring, exacerbating the damage mice and rats had done to cables that left the lights flickering every so often and airlock doors getting stuck. Sabotage was thankless work, leaving Lena wondering if she’d loosened a bolt enough, if she’d turned a handle too much to allow her plan to come about slowly.

     

                It was slow work and a few times she watched as panels were lifted in the distance, a patch of light suddenly illuminating the near vicinity before a beam of torchlight swept around, trying to spot her. Lena was lucky she was relatively average in size and could hide behind any number of pipes and vents, and on one occasion almost burying herself in the insulation as she lay in wait. 

     

                Her day passed by with exhaustion creeping up on her, fatigue and skipped meals leaving her weaker than usual, which was saying something with her poor diet and inhumanly cruel bed, and she found an empty guard room by luck when she called it a day. She was sure the room was empty by the locked door, the stripped mattress and lack of personal items and was careless enough to stretch out on the mattress and sleep as deeply as possible in an underwater prison while on the run from her guards.

     

                Roused twice from sleep by her shock collar, looking grey with the toll it was taking on her, Lena eventually resumed her sabotage and came across the kitchens for whichever area she was in a few hours later. There would undoubtedly be cameras in the space where she assumed less dangerous prisoners helped out so she replaced the panel and continued onwards and came to a storage cupboard next door by some fortune. Ducking her head down and finding no blinking red lights, Lena eased herself down into the large industrial steel space and looked around.

     

                Finding a can of preserved peaches, she opened it and fished the slippery slices out with her fingers, wolfing down the entire can and drinking the nectar before she hid it with the unopened ones and moved on. Stuffing her pockets with ripe apples and bananas and bread rolls, she ate as much as she could stomach and then spent a few minutes with the packing slips from the delivery, memorising the date and trying to outline when the next one would be. If she could find some more information on the next one, she’d be able to outline a schedule and map out her escape better, counting the notches on her cell wall with the little scalpel she’d hidden away.

     

                She fell asleep in the ceiling later on and came the closest she’d come to discovery yet when she was electrocuted, waking with a jolt that sent a nearby guard sweeping his torch across where she lay beneath a large water pipe. A storm had started up a while before, Lena assumed from the sudden plummeting in temperature that left her shivering, and she’d crawled beneath the steaming vent for warmth. At the electricity coursing through her, waking her was a start, Lena headbutted the pipe and had to bite back a scream of pain at the burning touch of it against her hairline, not to mention the loud thud that resulted from it.

     

                Remaining still, she heard the guard speak into a radio and call for another round of electrocution, Lena writhing in agony as she clenched her teeth shut hard enough to make her teeth ache as she refused to give herself away. He must have assumed it was just the old pipes because he moved on shortly after, cursing her as he crawled through the cramped space with more difficulty than her.

     

                She stayed there a long while, waiting until she was sure he was far enough away to not hear her move again, and Lena carried on. Deciding it would be wise to find somewhere to bed down for the night, Lena shifted a few panels as she went until she found one she deemed suitable, illuminating the dark room with her torch and finding it bare. That was where she fucked up, getting her feet through the hole and starting to lower herself just as she was electrocuted again. 

     

                Her body went limp and her muscles stopped supporting her as she fell the distance to the floor, cursing the high ceilings as she struck the floor hard, feeling the sharp pain of one leg snapping beneath her before the rest of her body followed, collapsing into a heap. Her torch clattered to the floor, splaying a yellow spotlight on the concrete wall, and a small cry escaped Lena before she clapped a hand over her mouth, tears pricking her eyes. 

     

                Swallowing a sob, Lena lowered her hand, shaking so badly that she had to curl her fingers into a fist. Pushing herself up, she shifted her leg around, dragging it by the stained fabric of her pants and shuffled back to lean against the wall. Frozen fingers probing along the length of her leg, she felt a shooting pain as she ghosted over the site of the break, grateful that the bone hadn’t perforated the skin but cursing her stupidity that had now incapacitated her. Lena wouldn’t be able to walk on it. 

     

                Splayed limp and shivering, wishing for one of the pilled grey sweatshirts they handed out during storms, when the water temperature dropped and seeped through the prison, bringing coughs and pneumonia and tonsillitis, Lena couldn’t do anything but sit there. The pain was a constant throb and her hair was plastered to her clammy face as she stayed there on the floor, lips cracked and throat dry and her pockets full of snacks that would see her through a day at least before the gnawing hunger crept back in.

     

                It was three days before someone found her, the door unlocking and a torchlight sweeping around and then doing a double-take, taking in her sprawled form and the apple cores and banana peels scattered around her. Lena had the pistol in her hand, her fingers curled around the trigger, and raised it, her arm feeling leaden and shaking from the effort. 

     

                “Don’t move,” she threatened, using the wall to push herself up. “It’ll be better for you if you don’t.”

     

                The woman was a few inches shorter than her and was reaching for her radio as Lena balanced precariously on one leg, now slightly swollen and sending stabbing pains through the length of it as she moved. Running a hand over her grey, sweaty face, Lena sniffed and adjusted her grip on the gun, motioning the guard inside.

     

                “I don’t want to shoot you. Just come inside and lock the door.”

     

                The guard moved warily, fingers twitching as if to reach for her own gun, but she wasn’t stupid enough to risk it just yet, not when Lena’s own stolen one was trained on her. And Lena was a good shot too, target practice and self-defence lessons were a mandatory routine for herself, given her high profile status and family name. She wouldn’t miss, not this close, probably not even at a hundred yards.

     

                Shuffling in and fumbling for the lock on the door, the woman swallowed, looking pale in the darkness of the cramped room, her torch casting them in ghastly light. Gesturing for her to raise her hands, Lena hopped forward and told her to turn around. Moving slowly, the woman was stiff and quiet and Lena’s face crumpled with guilt as she drew her arm back and slammed it into the side of her head, knocking her out cold. 

     

                The guard dropped to the floor and Lena clicked the hammer back into place before awkwardly sinking down to the floor. Picking up the unconscious woman’s hand, Lena pressed her thumb to the square on the shock collar and went weak with relief as she heard a small click and it loosened from around her neck. It felt unnecessarily cruel to clamp it around the guard so she tossed it aside and quickly started to strip off the woman’s uniform. Once she was in her underwear, Lena used the manacles hanging at the belt to cuff her and then grit her teeth against the jostling pain as she undressed and then pulled on the guard uniform. It was too short and bulky, but was a decent disguise as she took the woman’s hair tie and braided her greasy hair quickly, covering it with the black cap and wiping her face as clean as she could with her discarded prison uniform.

     

                The sturdy combat boots provided some support for her leg, laced tightly around her shins and she was able to hobble out of the room, using the keys to lock the room from the outside with the unconscious guard inside. Limping down the hallway, feeling out of sorts with the weight of the kevlar vest, the two-way radio, the baton and gun and keys hanging from her, Lena dried to remain inconspicuous, aware that cameras would be watching her now. Luckily, the other woman was a brunette too, and she hoped with the same outfit on they’d look the same via the security cameras.

     

                She didn’t see anyone for a while as she walked around the hallways, following one to the next turning and then making a guess. When she hit an airlock, Lena thought she was done for, a thumb and retinal scan were required to move from one section to another, and she was positively green from leaning on her leg as she scrambled to think of a way through.

     

                “Need help?”

     

                Stiffening, Lena swallowed dryly, letting out a nervous laugh as she half-turned. “I think it hates me.”

     

                “It’s an old system,” the guy sighed, “gets a bit temperamental. Here.”

     

                He ducked down a little so it could scan his retina and then slapped his hand against the panel, rolling his eyes as the light turned green and the doors hissed open. They stepped into the airlock together and Lena could feel sweat beading at her hairline as her heart raced. The chamber pressurised with a hiss of air and they were spat out on the other side. 

     

                “Old injury?”

     

                “What’s that?” Lena murmured, glancing sideways at him.

     

                “Your leg. An old injury?”

     

                “Mhm. Ex-military. Shrapnel got me good. I think it’s the cold making it flare up.”

     

                “You new?”

     

                “Yes, sir. Fresh off the last delivery.”

     

                He clicked his tongue, “well, that’s something you’ll get used to. Nothing but damp and misery down here.”

     

                She nodded, trying to keep the pinched look of panic from her face as she walked down the hallway. When they came to an intersection, he started bearing left and Lena hesitated, looking around.

     

                “Where you heading?” he asked.

     

                “Oh, um, I was told to go and report to Agent Danvers.”

     

                “Danvers, huh? She’s a few blocks over.”

     

                “Oh.”

     

                “Come on, I’ll walk you there. Might be that your access hasn’t been set up right yet. You’ll need to see Schott for that but he’s been laid up in bed for the last few days.”

     

                Nodding, she followed after the agent as he walked off, continuing straight down the hallway as he chatted away animatedly. Lena made the occasional sound of agreement or hummed inquisitively and he filled her in on all the gossip as she pretended to know what he was talking about. When he brought up lunchtime, Lena made a scathing sound of disgust and rolled her eyes.

     

                “Do you get used to the food?” she asked, fishing for information.

     

                “Eventually. I warn you, it gets progressively worse as the month goes on though. Slightly better when the fresh deliveries come in.”

     

                “When’s the next one?” 

     

                He thought for a second, “two weeks I think. First Monday of every month. At least we eat better than the poor bastards behind bars. Better to be a prisoner on the right side of the cell.”

     

                Humming, Lena filed away the information and continued to follow him. He took her right to the airlock and opened the door as he gestured her inside. He remained on the other side as the doors started sliding shut, and Lena stared at him as he spoke into his radio, cold fear settling in her stomach like a stone as she realised her error too late.

     

                “Agent Taylor, opening airlock 374A to cell block D for Agent …” his eyes glanced down at the name badge on Lena’s chest. “Lane. Lane?”

     

                The double-take made the guard’s eyes widen with surprise and he was briefly obscured by the puffs of air as the doors shut and the airlock pressurised. Turning around, Lena was practically pressed up against the opposite door as she willed it to hurry up and open, which happened far too slowly for her likely. She could hear the agent - Taylor - shouting on the other side of the opposite door, banging against the glass and cursing her out as the door finally opened and Lena limped out.

     

                She went as quick as she could, knowing she was in deep shit now, each step sending a flaring pain through her leg, leaving her lurching and grey-faced as she hurried down a hallway. Making two turns, she barged into a storage closet and scrambled up a row of shelves to push a panel out of the way and drag herself up into the vents. Her vision blurred and she couldn’t see a thing as she crawled through the ceiling space, palms sweaty, chest tight with panic and a blinding pain making her want to give in.

     

                Knowing they’d be on the cameras now, tracking her movements to that storage closet, Lena shifted a few ceiling panels to find somewhere to hide and came out a few rooms over in a bathroom. Red cameras winked at her as she slipped on the toilet seat and went crashing down, her vision dimming at the edges as she exacerbated the pain in her leg. The floors were wet from being recently mopped and she slipped as she tried to climb to her feet and went back down.

     

                The door shrieked open and Lena quickly scuttled backwards on the floor, using her hands to drag herself as she watched Jensen stalk in. He was tall and threatening, every inch of him filled with violence, and she winced as he quickly crossed the room over to her, smiling with manic eyes.

     

                “There you are, you little bitch,” he said with relish, reaching down to wrap his fingers around her throat and lift her.

     

                His fingers bit in painfully and Lena let out a breathless choked sound as she clawed at his hand, nails leaving furrows, and fumbled for the gun with her other hand. Yanking it free, she forced the hammer back and jammed it against his hip, in the narrow gap between his kevlar vest and pants, and squeezed the trigger. The sound was loud in the tiled room and he looked surprised, dropping her hard onto the floor and pressing a hand to his side. Fingers came away red and his surprise darkened to anger.

     

                “You-” he snarled, fumbling for his gun before a sharp voice cut him off.

     

                “Jensen.”

     

                Yanking his gun free, he quickly thumbed the hammer and pointed it at Lena as he took a few steps forward. Shrinking in on herself, Lena squeezed her eyes shut and grit her teeth, expecting the bite of a bullet.

     

                “Jensen, down.”

     

                The shot of a gun cut through the raised voices and Lena flinched but felt nothing. Nothing except the gentle mist of warm blood splattering her cheeks as her eyes flew open and she watched the large, lifeless form of the agent drop to the bathroom floor with a hole in the back of his head. A frayed sound of horror escaped Lena as she blinked, her mouth floundering as she tried to process what had happened. 

     

                “Put it down.”

     

                Alex stepped inside as Lena let her stolen gun fall from limp fingers, pale as she holstered her own, her mouth a flat line. Lena shuffled backwards, dragging her leg with her as she knew it was game over. Her back hit the wall and she let out a ragged sigh, closing her eyes as she listened to the advancing footsteps.

     

                “You’re done,” Alex stiffly said, crouching beside her.

     

                Eyelids shuttering, Lena swallowed the bitter taste of regret and nodded. A moment later a pinch in the side of her neck filled her with the ice-cold feeling of a drug before she was out cold and none the wiser to what happened next.

     

                When she woke, it was in a hospital bed, only slightly more comfortable than her cot, with harsh fluorescents overhead that made her wince and two arms and one leg chained to the bed frame. The other leg was encased in plaster and Lena frowned as she blinked back the furry feeling of drugs that slowed her mind. A listless sigh escaped her and she let her head loll to the side on the pillow, taking stock of the private room.

     

                Cameras winked from two corners and Lena struggled to sit up a little as she felt the heavy weight of her shock collar back around her neck. The urge to cry built in her chest as she grit her teeth and pulled against the restraints, anger making her cheeks flush as she found herself trapped once more. Even the pleasant hum of whatever painkillers they’d given her wasn’t enough to dull the despair in her chest.

     

                The door opened a few minutes later and Lena caught sight of a guard outside past the white coat of Doctor Danvers. Hands on her hips, Eliza stared at her for a moment with sad blue eyes and an exasperated thinness to her mouth. Shaking her head, she sighed and crossed over to the bed.

     

                “You’re really determined to get yourself killed,” she said with a click of her tongue. “I’m starting to think they picked up the wrong person because if your IQ was as high as they’ve reported, I’d think you’d make better decisions.”

     

                “Ever heard of a mad genius?”

     

                Giving her an admonishing look, Eliza picked up her chart and took a look. “We both know you’re not mad .”

     

                “I wouldn’t be so sure; it’s in my genes.”

     

                “Is it in your genes to be obedient, by any chance?”

     

                Lena choked on a laugh, “I’m not sure I know what that word means.”

     

                Eliza hummed, her expression grim as she glanced up at Lena. “You’ve broken your tibia. You were running a temperature of 102 yesterday, and with the way you were walking on it, infection wasn’t far off.”

     

                “What did you give me?”

     

                “Morphine for the pain. A course of antibiotics for the inflammation. Fluids for dehydration. One more day and you probably would’ve wound up with a tube down your throat to feed you.”

     

                “How long have I been out?”

     

                “Two days. Eight in total since you escaped.”

     

                Humming as she processed the information, Lena sighed and then rattled her cuffs. “Any chance of getting these off?”

     

                “You’ll be lucky if they don’t swap them for a straitjacket once you’re out of here.”

     

                “I thought they saved those ones for the dangerous ones. Like Kara - apparently.”

     

                Eliza smiled slightly, a rueful crooked thing. “Kara’s dangerous enough, there’s no denying it, no matter how gentle she seems. You’d do well not to encourage her; it never ends well when she rebels. And I say that as someone who genuinely cares for that girl's wellbeing, who’s seen her grow up and done my best to shield her from how brutal this place is. Encouraging her to act out for your own agenda is selfish, Lena. They’ll hurt her a lot more than they can hurt you because they know she can withstand it. If you don’t care that a man is dead, then care about what they did to her so she could buy you a few days of scurrying around with the rats.”

     

                Lena looked appropriately chastened, two splotches of red on her pale cheeks as she looked down, embarrassed. “Is she okay?” she whispered.

     

                Sighing, Eliza plucked a penlight from her pocket and leaned over Lena. “Look at me.”

     

                Staring straight up, Lena tried not to blink as the light moved across her eyes but she felt a prickling feeling that she wasn’t entirely sure wasn’t tears. Blinking rapidly once Eliza finished, she lay still and let the doctor slip the cold disc of the stethoscope beneath her hospital gown and listen to her breaths.

     

                “You’ve been coughing in your sleep,” Eliza informed her, “from the cold, I’d wager. I’ll need to keep you in for another day for observation, just to make sure it’s not pneumonia.”

     

                “Is she okay?” Lena said through clenched teeth, her eyes smarting now.

     

                Mouth thinning, Eliza’s shoulders dropped and she laid a hand on Lena’s arm. “She’s fine.”

     

                The door opened and Lena struggled to sit up, her expression blank as she felt keen relief cut through her. When Alex stepped inside the relief dimmed a little, her throat closing up at the memory of warm blood spraying her face and the large man crumpling from the bullet Alex put in him.

     

                Glancing at her mother, Alex raised her chin a fraction. “I’d like a moment alone with Prisoner LL93 please.”

     

                Eliza hesitated before nodding at her daughter’s order and gathering her things up. She gave Alex a stern, muttered warning as she passed by before she exited the room and left Lena alone with Alex, an uneasy feeling clouding the air as they stared at each other.

     

                “So … how’re your hands now?” Alex asked.

     

                A ragged, choked sob escaped Lena and she hunched over, the chains of her handcuffs pulled taut as she covered her face, feeling hot tears against her palms. “Fuck you.”

     

                “You brought this on yourself. Every bad thing that’s happened to you in here has been your own fault.”

     

                “I shouldn’t be here.”

     

                “Neither should I,” Alex snapped back, bristling with anger now. “But I haven’t gotten anyone killed over it.”

     

                “As if he didn’t deserve it,” Lena scathingly replied, dashing a hand across her cheek as she scowled.

     

                Sniffing, she blinked quickly, her face flushed with embarrassment from her tears. Alex stared at her, brown eyes unwavering but not quite as hard as Lena would have imagined them, given the circumstances.

     

                “Maybe he did, but there are still consequences. For me and you. And Kara.”

     

                “What’s she got to do with it?”

     

                Lip curling in a bitter smile, Alex folded her arms over her chest. “I may not be a genius like you but it’s not hard to figure out why the girl who I grew up alongside, who’s practically family, suddenly started going nuts once you were out of your cell. If I hadn’t had to go and sort her out, you wouldn’t have gotten the better of Agent Schott.”

     

                “Maybe, but do you really think Kara’s that manipulative? I mean … if you’re like family, surely you trust her.”

     

                Alex’s expression hardened and she spluttered for a moment. “I trust her. I don’t trust you. You’re manipulating her.”

     

                “Kara’s an adult. She can make her own decisions.”            

     

                “Kara has grown up in a fucking prison cell. She’s smart , she’s kind, but she knows absolutely nothing about the real world here. She’s gullible and naïve and anything she knows about humans has been learnt while she’s been inside, and we’re not exactly the pinnacle of humanity in here, so leave her alone. Actually, I’ll do you one better; that guard that you knocked out and stole your disguise from? Yeah, that was the Deputy. ”

     

                Lena’s stomach lurched as unease threaded through her, and she stared at Alex with a slack look on her face. Letting out a huff of laughter, Alex shook her head. 

     

                “Yeah, you’re not quite as smart as you think you are. As soon as you’re out of here, you’ll be straight into isolation. And I don’t think you’ll find yourself back on cell block D again anytime soon.”

     

                Expecting that didn’t make it any easier for Lena to swallow, her expression hard as she clenched her teeth and stiffly nodded. “Tell her I’m sorry.”

     

                “I won’t tell her anything. It’ll be as if you never existed. You’ll be a two-month blip in her otherwise relatively smooth imprisonment and she’ll forget all about you in the same amount of time. You might think I’m cruel but I really do care about her, even if I don’t care about the rest of you. This is how I keep her safe; not by filling her head with fantasies of escaping.”

     

                “You’re a coward. I would’ve helped you too, you know. For her. You, your mom, your girlfriend. But you’re a coward who’d rather see them all die slowly instead of choosing a quick death or freedom.”

     

                “You’ve been in here for two months. You don’t know a thing about this place. You have no idea, none at all, so don’t call me a coward because you’re angry that you’re stuck here, just like the rest of us.”

     

                “You are a coward. We could help each other but you refuse. For what reason, other than you’re afraid? Let me tell you something, when I find a way off here - which I will, I can guarantee you that - I’m going to take her with me and I’m going to take your mom and your girlfriend and leave you here all alone and you’re going to spend the rest of you pathetic life thinking about how you could be outside of this hell hole if only you’d had the guts to do something. ”

     

                Alex stepped up to the foot of the bed, gripping the metal bars in a tight grip that whitened her knuckles as she stared at Lena with false bravado, fear visible in her brown eyes as her pulse raced at her throat. Lena would have pitied her if she wasn’t so angry.

     

                “You go ahead and do that from the inside of the shoebox they’re going to let you rot inside.”

     

                With nothing else to say to that, Lena bit her tongue and scowled at Alex. Lingering a moment, Alex opened her mouth as if to say something else, a grim look of pity quickly flashing across her face before she clamped her jaw shut and turned on her heel, walking back over to the door. Curiosity got the better of Lena as she stared at the Agent’s ramrod spine and she couldn’t stop herself from seizing her moment to ask, confused by what had transpired, even without the haze of drugs.

     

                “Why’d you do it?” she called after Alex.

     

                Pausing, Alex’s shoulders squared as she raised her head. “I’m a guard. Not a murderer.”

     

                “You are now. May as well have let it be me.”

     

                “You were right. You’re not a criminal. You’re just a prisoner.”

    Chapter 10

    Chapter Notes

    hey besties tw for a fake suicide attempt in this chapter just in case you need to skip this one

                Cuffed to a hospital bed for two more days, with brief reprieves to hobble to the bathroom with Eliza’s assistance and one hand freed three times a day so she could feed herself. She had a cough that rattled in her chest, congested and phlegmy from the dampness and dust, and Lena looked ghastly as she lay in bed, staring at the ceiling panels for hours on end in between rounds of antibiotics and painkillers for her broken leg. It was only out of Eliza’s pity that she was kept in for two more days for observation, the cuffs chafing her wrists raw and the needles in her arms tugging with her movements, and Lena knew she should be grateful for the delay in her punishment but she was bitter and silent. 

     

                “I’m going to have to discharge you today,” Eliza said as she listened to Lena’s chest.

     

                Lena didn’t reply, a glazed look in her eyes as she stared ahead, aloof as she placidly permitted the doctor to do her assessment.

     

                “How’s the leg feeling? Sit forward for me.”

     

                Shrugging indifferently as she sat up, leaning forward with what limited range the handcuffs offered her, Lena shivered at the touch of the metal stethoscope pressed against her skin. Inhaling deeply and then exhaling sharply, she let Eliza listen to her lungs and then laid back against the bed.

     

                “I’ll give you a script of painkillers for another week. They’ll bring them to your cell with your vitamins.”

     

                Nodding, Lena’s mouth flattened into a hard line. She purposely avoided looking at the doctor as she filled out Lena’s chart and checked her vitals on the beeping machines before letting out a soft sigh.

     

                “They’ll come for you soon. To see the Deputy.”

     

                She nodded again, her churlish self-pitying somewhat ruined by the fact that she couldn’t cross her arms over her chest, two wrists and an ankle chained to the bed frame. Eliza’s mouth twitched with dismay at Lena’s silence and she let out a soft sigh.

     

                “I’ll make sure you’re allowed to shower first. I’d let you now but I don’t have keys for the cuffs.”

     

                Staring up at the ceiling, Lena swallowed thickly. She didn’t want Eliza’s kindness and didn’t want to feel like she’d disappointed the woman with what she’d done. Jaw clamped shut, a muscle twitched there and she remained silent until the door screeched open and one of the Agents stepped inside, wheeling a wheelchair with him. 

     

                Lena was uncuffed and Eliza helped her hobble into the bathroom, bidding her to wait as she wrapped her cast in a plastic bag and then helped Lena out of her hospital gown. The water  was mercifully scalding and Lena washed out the dust that lingered in her greasy hair and powdered her skin, feeling clean for the first time in a week and a half. Eliza had to remain in the small room with her to spare Lena and the male guard the discomfort, and she afforded Lena a few extra minutes before she murmured it was time for her to get out.

     

                Accepting the towel from her, Lena wrapped it around herself, shivering in the chill of the space. Fear coiled in her stomach as she started to dry off, and when it choked her up, a broken sob passed her lips as her eyes stung, Eliza took the towel from her and finished wiping the water from her arms and back as Lena cried, covering her face with her hands as the doctor towelled the ends of her hair and gently shushed her. 

     

                Giving her a clean, dry prison uniform to change into, Eliza unwrapped her cast and helped Lena struggle into the pants, the drawstring pulled tight to keep them from sagging. She’d lost even more weight, hip bones prominent and the ridges of her spine visible through the long undershirt she pulled on first before the baggy grey scrub top enveloped her. The cold weather had persisted with numerous storms sweeping overhead in rapid succession and she burrowed into the warmth of the pilled grey sweatshirt given to her. 

     

                Once she was dressed and as presentable as possible, her dark hair damp tangles leaving wet spots against the sweatshirt, Lena folded the towel neatly and set it down on top of the toilet seat. Wiping her face, blotchy from her crying, she inhaled sharply.

     

                “You’ll be alright,” Eliza whispered, giving her arm a quick squeeze and then hesitating before pulling her into a hug.

     

                It was such a maternal gesture that it made Lena cry harder, pressing her face into Eliza’s shoulder as she breathed in the antiseptic smell clinging to her scrubs. Lena hadn’t regretted her choices up until that moment, the gravity of her situation creeping up on her as fear knifed through her chest. She didn’t think she’d see Kara again.

     

                Giving her back a reassuring pat, Eliza pulled back. “You’re strong-willed. They can’t break that if you don’t let them.”

     

                “I’m sorry,” Lena quietly replied, wiping her cheeks.

     

                “It’s too late to take it back. Just … don’t do anything else stupid.”

     

                Nodding, Lena let out a shaky breath and raised her head. Eliza opened the door and helped Lena out before she was seated in the wheelchair and cuffed to the arms and legs of it. Thoughtfully tucking a waffle blanket over her lap, Eliza looked at her with concerned blue eyes as she stepped back.

     

                “Thank you,” Lena gravelly replied.

     

                Touching her shoulder briefly, Eliza moved aside and the guard pounded on the door for the Agent outside to open it. They manoeuvred Lena out into the hallway beyond and the cold crept in immediately, making her realise that Eliza must have cranked some old heating system for her in the medical room. She couldn’t even hug her arms to herself to stave it off, just tightened her jaw and tensed her shoulders against the tremors that wracked her as she was wheeled off to her fate.

     

                They stopped outside a nondescript iron door, rusted at the hinges, and the Agent knocked on it before a muffled voice drifted through. It screeched open as he ducked his head inside, Lena waiting silently as they conversed.

     

                “Deputy, I have Prisoner LL93 for you.”

     

                “Great, bring her in for me.”

     

                He ground the door open wider and pushed Lena over the lip before shifting a chair away from the desk to make room for the bulky wheelchair. The office was grim, with two old filing cabinets against one wall, a potted cactus, which was about the only thing that could survive in the prison without sunlight, and a few framed photos on the desk with a clunky computer. Behind the desk was the woman Lena had stupidly knocked out and stripped of her clothes and she wanted to cringe at the thought of what came next, wondering how much pride the woman had and how much of her dignity Lena had taken from her when she’d left her unconscious in her underwear.

     

                “You can wait outside. Thank you,” the Deputy said, giving the man an easy smile.

     

                A clock ticked on the wall, filling the silence as the Agent stepped back out, closing them in together, and Lena stared at a water stain in the corner of the ceiling, trying not to restlessly shift beneath the feeling of the Deputy’s eyes watching her closely. Eventually, the woman let out a weary sigh, lacing her fingers together on the desk.

     

                “Prisoner LL93,” she lightly declared, a hum of amusement in her voice. “The infamous Lena Luthor. I always thought you would’ve been older but you’re not even thirty and your life is already over.”

     

                Giving her a venomous look, Lena’s mouth twitched with bitter regret and her knuckles whitened as she clutched the arms of the wheelchair. She didn’t reply, knowing that any response would be angry and scathing and dig her into a bigger hole. 

     

                “You would know by now that this prison was created to contain alien and superhuman beings for the safety of the United States - and the world, to a lesser extent - and is staffed by humans who have been unfortunate enough to find themselves implicated in some political or legal trouble. I, myself, am ex-military, here because of my father’s actions. Like most of my employees. All of us, down to the last guard, nurse, janitor or administrator are human. And everyone in a cell is … something else - except for you. You’re the sole exception to that order, and do you know why?”

     

                Lena didn’t respond, turning her head slightly to the side, letting the woman’s words wash over her as she kept her expression blank. The woman let out a small laugh and sighed, tapping idly on the desk.

     

                “They said you have superhuman intelligence. I don’t believe that’s true, although your intelligence apparently exceeds that of a twelfth-level intellect like your block mate, Prisoner QD91. You know, if you were a bit dumber, you would’ve found yourself outside of a cell, maybe working in I.T. to manage the prison security, maybe engineering to keep this shithole from falling apart. Instead, they figured that someone as smart as you would be able to find a way out of here, that you’d be a safety hazard to be allowed to walk around freely, even with a mop in your hand. So, that’s how you became the first human prisoner to grace us, and you’ve been a pain in my ass ever since.”

     

                Running a hand through her brown hair, a few shades lighter than Lena’s and inches shorter, not quite a good enough disguise for someone who hadn’t been desperate to buy some extra time. It had worked well enough for a moment though and Lena couldn’t begrudge herself that. Deputy Lane couldn’t have been more than a few years older than her, around Alex’s age if she had to guess, but she looked tired and stress weighed heavily on her as she heaved a sigh.

     

                “The question now is what to do with you? You’ve become a bit of a problem, and I don’t like problems. If you’re sitting before me, that means the Warden knows about you, and that doesn’t look good for me, you or any of my Agents. Isolation is a given, but Doctor Olsen advises me that the dysregulation of routines only increases misbehaviour so that’s not a viable long-term solution. You also don’t seem like the type to crack under that sort of punishment.”

     

                Lena’s eyes slid back to her and they stared at each other for a long minute, the clock ticking each passing second before the Deputy leaned forward, elbows on the desk and a shrewd look in her eyes. A faint smile, not unkind and almost pitying in its knowing, curled her lips and she toyed with a pen plucked from the desk as she chose her words carefully.

     

                “I’ve been told there’s a certain prisoner that you’ve grown close to, that you’re negatively influencing. Prisoner KZ64 is one of the more high-security prisoners here, one we keep an extra close eye on, and with you encouraging her to act on her more violent tendencies … that doesn’t bode well for anyone. At best, a few people get killed before we subdue her with our methods, at worst … well, she sinks this whole prison. I don’t think you understand the gravity of our situation here, what we do as a government black site.”

     

                Anger flared white-hot inside Lena now, her green eyes sharpening as she curled her lip contemptuously. “You think you’re doing something noble by keeping us all trapped here? You expect me to feel sympathetic to your cause of keeping innocent people locked away in cells for your own safety?”

     

                She scoffed, grinding her jaw as she looked away. “I know Alex has put you up to this; that’s fine, lock me away for a while, I don’t care. Just don’t take it out on Kara, okay?”

     

                “I didn’t know you were on such familiar terms with my employees. What Agent Danvers thinks is irrelevant to me; you injured three Agents, myself included, and attempted to escape while evading capture. One of my Agents is dead-”

     

                “Wasn’t me.”

     

                “You are the reason why,” Deputy Lane said, bracing her hands on the desk and climbing to her feet. “You’ve been here a fraction of the time as some of the worst prisoners and have already managed to end up in deeper shit than all of them. I’d be impressed if it wasn’t my head on the chopping block.”

     

                Straightening, she slowly rounded the desk and leaned against it, forcing Lena to look up with a scowl on her face, pink-cheeked at the derisive tone the Deputy used. Arms folded over her chest, Deputy Lane’s mouth thinned slightly and she nodded at the cast on Lena’s leg.

     

                “You’ll be in iso until the cast comes off. After that, you’ll be transferred to a new block.”

     

                Lena’s stomach lurched and her face went slack with surprise, lips parting as her objection got caught in her throat. She floundered for a moment, blinking rapidly as her heart rate kicked up, palms turning clammy.

     

                “I- you- no. No, you can’t do that. That’s my cell.”

     

                “That’s where you’re wrong. You misbehave, you deal with the consequences. If you wanted to stay in your cell , you should’ve sat quietly instead of making trouble for yourself.”

     

                Tears stung Lena’s eyes and she was rigid and brimming with anger as she scowled up at the Deputy. Her throat constricted and she worked to swallow, her throat bobbing and her voice coming out hoarse.

     

                “Please. Don’t move me.”

     

                “You hold no power here.” 

     

                “Put me in isolation,” Lena agreed, a desperate rasp to her words. “That’s fine, I deserve it, just … please let me go back to my cell.”

     

                “This is where it stops,” the woman said, reaching out to touch Lena’s shoulder.

     

                She jerked back as Lena shrugged her touch off, straining against her cuffs. Chained to the wheelchair, that wasn’t much she could do to object, just pulling tight against the cuffs until they bit in painfully while the wheelchair was jostled about a bit. Her eyes dried, hardening with hatred, but her breaths were quick, shallow sobs as she struggled. 

     

                Grim resignation turned the Deputy’s face solemn as she walked over to the door, opened it and spoke quietly to the Agent. The man came in and grabbed her handles, jerking her backwards over the lip of the door and into the hallway. The Deputy gripped the door frame and cocked her head to the side, watching Lena for a moment.

     

                “Bad behaviour is punished, Prisoner LL93. You should be thankful for my leniency.” 

     

                “Fuck you,” Lena snarled.

     

                Hastily wheeled away, the sounds of a door squealing shut following her down the hallway, Lena was left seething in silence with no outlet for her anger. The areas of the prison she was wheeled through were unfamiliar, and she had no reference point for where she’d started, letting it all blur together in a series of turns and doors and bleak water-stained hallways with peeling paint and tarnished metal. 

     

                Eventually, she was brought before a cell with a wheel lock mechanism, the Agent straining as he turned it and hauled it open to reveal the tiny interior, barely big enough for the narrow cot, a sink and a toilet, with practically no walk space between them. He couldn’t even wheel her inside and had to uncuff her on the threshold, his brawn no match for her weak softness. Lena didn’t even have time to try and resist as he picked her up from the wheelchair and tossed her inside, jostling painfully on the mattress as she lay splayed awkwardly, watching the door close behind her.

     

                Pushing herself up, plastered leg at a heavy, awkward angle, Lena stared at the door for a long moment before taking stock of the room. She didn’t even have it in her to fuel her rage and pound on the door and threaten them to let her out, just stared at the old pipes - not as many as last time, leaving the room pleasantly warm instead of boiling hot - and stared at the high ceiling panels that she’d never be able to reach. 

     

                Defeated and tired, Lena just sat there, blinking as she tried to process her circumstances. Isolation had been awful last time, but she’d been angry and had more fight in her then. Now she felt hollow and resigned, not quite enough to give in to her fate but enough to know that there would be no escaping for the time being, no way out of isolation until they opened that door and let her out. She tried to think rationally, trying to spin it as a way for her to plot accordingly, stringing together everything she’d learnt from her stint in the crawl space of the ceiling, but Lena knew that forced optimism would only stretch so far.

     

                Exhausted and feeling the ache in her leg flaring brighter with each passing minute, Lena flopped back onto the thin, lumpy mattress and let sleep drag her under. She’d been resting up for days, unconscious for the most part, so she didn’t sleep for long but it was the sound of the door flap scraping open that woke her as food was pushed in.
