                Staring blearily at the hatch, Lena watched it shut and took in the paltry offerings of a cup of water, her vitamins and painkillers, a plain bread roll, a hunk of cheese and an unpeeled orange. Her thoughts were quiet and slow, no longer the rapid hunger of equations and schematics and physics as she hunted for answers and solutions to her engineering feats, to her business models. 

     

                Running a hand over her pallid face, grazing the scab of the burn at her hairline and the aches and pains of where she’d fallen or nicked herself, bruises dotting her skin in varying shades of greens and purples, Lena found it hard to formulate a plan. The deliveries were the first Monday of every month, but what time? How long did they breach the surface of the ocean to accept the delivery? How long did the helicopter linger? How many Agents were present as part of an armed retinue? There were too many variables that Lena couldn’t account for in her plans and the unknown was a risk she wasn’t sure she was willing to take just yet. Better to continue her reconnaissance and be sure of her success, but if worse came to worst, better to risk her life and die rather than stay shut away in an underwater cell until old age or pneumonia came for her. 

     

                Eyes closed, she ran through the information she’d collected and tried to piece together what she could, the rough outline of a plan sketched in her mind. Without any real substance, she may as well not have gone through the effort it had taken to gather it all, but when the lights guttered occasionally and the pipes hissed or spluttered, she had to hope that it was her doing, and maybe somewhere down the line the chaos she had wrought on the infrastructure would come to fruition. 

     

                Hours slipped by and when hunger came gnawing, Lena picked up her tray and rationed her bread and cheese in between sips of water, thinking about what she would have done for a cup of good coffee. Picking up her vitamins, she hesitated as she shook them into her palm, a small collection of pills and two distinct painkillers. Swallowing the former, she made it seem like she took them all as she squirrelled away the painkillers in the cuff of her sweatshirt for a last-ditch effort if all else failed.

     

                Saving the orange, she rolled it between her palms as she sat cross-legged on the bed, a thoughtful look on her face and a pinch between her eyebrows, the heaviness of the cast making her feel off-balance. Mouth thinning, Lena found her own thoughts incessant and frustrating and ended up focusing on the Fibonacci sequence as an easy mental exercise to keep her occupied and sharp. After her last stint in isolation, she knew how it could affect her, how boredom could very well dip down near to insanity if she didn’t keep herself mentally stimulated. That was perhaps the worst part about prison; Lena could have stayed in one spot all day if she’d had a computer or a microscope or a calculator in front of her with something to solve, a challenge that kept her busy and determined. She wasn’t built to let her intellect go to waste, and that would drive her insane faster than being alone ever could.

     

                She fell asleep with the orange clutched in her hands and woke to the sound of another meal passing through the hatch. It became routine, bland rations sent through as she was left to entertain herself, hiding her pills in the corner of her pillowcase and letting her mind run through translations of famous poems in every language she knew, formulating chemical equations or math problems, mentally putting together and pulling apart computers and machines. The days passed by slowly and Lena tried to keep to her routine, rinsing her mouth out every morning with the freezing water of the tap, trying to keep herself clean as she raked some through the roots of her hair and over her face, wearing the same set of clothes as she was denied even a shower.

     

                The pills stopped coming with her vitamins and Lena calculated a week spent inside the cell, twenty-eight little pills tucked in the corner of her pillowcase at an oversight of the Agent who brought her food. A second week slipped by, a meal a day sustaining her on little more than bread and cheese and an orange for Vitamin C to make sure she didn’t develop scurvy. It was worse than the last time she’d been in isolation, her cast itching, her skin sweating over old sweat and the cough in her chest persisting. 

     

                By the end of the third week, after deliberating how far they’d go to save her life, Lena pulled the pills out and cupped them in her palm, wondering if they’d even notice and how much time it would buy her out of isolation. If she was that much of a nuisance, they might end her sentence then and let her plot from inside a new cell block. It was a better alternative that at least provided her with the opportunity for more intel, even if she was still angry that they’d moved her away from Kara. She’d thought of her friend often over the last two weeks, wondering if she was okay, hoping she wasn’t making herself a nuisance for Lena’s sake, knowing any punishments heaped onto Kara would be far worse than what they did to Lena.

     

                With a resigned sigh, hoping her bluff would work and a slight tremor in her hand at the prickle of fear that it wouldn’t and she’d be killing herself preemptively, Lena thumbed the pills into a neat pile in the middle of her palm. She wasn’t suicidal, just playing a risky game with a fatal hazard, knowing that if they pumped her stomach she’d at least get a few days with Eliza, who was kind and malleable even if it made Lena feel somewhat guilty to manipulate her. Still, she hadn’t accounted for Alex, a constant pain in her ass and more attentive than she’d given her credit for, considering she’d caught no sight or sound of her since that day in the medical bay when she’d told her her fate and Lena had been bitter and accusatory and perplexed that she’d been saved.

     

                Unfortunately, they were bound to repeat that a second time, a jolt of electricity shooting through her as her whole body tensed and writhed on the cot, her fingers curling tightly around the pills as she waited for it to subside. A minute later, the door screeched open as Lena’s eyes widened in alarm and she quickly forced her hand to her mouth, opening wide to tip the pills in before they could shock her again. Alex was quick though, her face pale and hard as she threw herself at Lena, out of breath from running through the hallways, fingers curling around her wrist in a vice-like grip.

     

                “No, no, no, you are not fucking killing yourself,” she snarled, panicked and shocked as if she couldn’t believe Lena’s gall.

     

                A few of the pills fell astray by Alex dragging Lena’s hand from her face, but the majority went in her mouth, a few stuck to the dry back of her throat while the others started dissolving on her tongue. Alex’s knee dug into Lena’s stomach and she grasped her cheeks tightly, relinquishing her hold on her wrist to prise her jaw open, fingers scrabbling inside her mouth for the pills. Lena gagged at the act, convulsing beneath the pinning weight of the agent, and Alex dragged a few pills out, contempt on her face as she tossed them aside while Lena coughed up a few more. She tried to swallow the rest and Alex swiped the fallen ones onto the floor as Lena scrabbled for them on the rumpled blankets.

     

                Arm going around her throat, Alex jerked Lena up in a headlock, fumbling for her radio. “Agent Danvers, reporting a code white. Removing Prisoner LL93 from iso for an emergency section.”

     

                She hauled Lena off the bed with her, surprising the prisoner with her strength, and Lena staggered out of the cell, hobbling on her cast. Alex stalked out after her and propelled her into the opposite wall.

     

                “Hands flat,” she ordered her.

     

                Lena held her hands up, her heart hammering in her chest and the powdery taste of the pills cloying on her tongue. Removing a pair of cuffs from her belt, Alex snapped it around one wrist and then pulled Lena’s arms down to cuff the other behind her back. Pulling her away from the wall, she held her arm tightly and towed her along quickly.

     

                Stumbling in her haste to keep up, wincing at the occasional misstep that made her broken leg hurt, Lena glanced sideways at Alex’s face. “I didn’t swallow enough-“

     

                “Shut it. Shut the fuck up,” Alex snapped. “You’re a fucking idiot, you know that? What do you think was going to happen? We’d let you swallow them all and kill yourself while we watched on camera?”

     

                “It would save you a headache,” Lena rasped, giving her an uneven grin full of false bravado.

     

                Pulling her to a stop, Alex tightened her grip on Lena’s arm. “I don’t pity you, you know. You’re manipulative and I don’t trust you at all, but I’m not going to let you die on my watch. It’s a shit job but I take it seriously - even if you think this is all fun and games.”

     

                She dragged them back into motion and Lena let out a grating laugh. “Oh, yes, I’m having a grand time in here. I’ve been saying for years that I need a vacation.”

     

                “Poor little rich girl isn’t cut out for life behind bars, huh?” Alex snorted. “Welcome to the club. You think it was easy for the rest of us to end up in here?”

     

                “How is she?”

     

                “Not your business.”

     

                Struggling to come to a stop, turning into dead weight as Alex tried to move her, Lena sneered smugly. “How is she?”

     

                “I’ll just get someone bigger than me to come and haul your ass for me. Don’t play with me.”

     

                “It’ll be quicker if you just tell me.”

     

                Considering it, her hand on her radio, Alex cocked her head to the side. “Difficult.”

     

                Lena faltered for a moment as she straightened, shoulders slumping, and Alex pulled her into motion again. Licking her lips, Lena swallowed dryly. “Did you tell her-“

     

                “No, Lena,” Alex roughly sighed, impatient and annoyed. “I didn’t tell her anything. I didn’t pass on a goodbye, I didn’t tell her what you did, I didn’t say shit to her. And I’m not going to because she’s better off without you. She has me, okay? I look out for her and I don’t get her hurt. You know what it looks like to actually look out for someone in here? I sneak her an extra snack from my meals when I can, I let her use staff bathrooms with hot water, I sneak her coffee sometimes.”

     

                With a scathing sound of contempt, Lena’s lip curled and she scowled at the Agent. “That’s fuck all and you know it. Where’s a cup of coffee going to get her? Absolutely nowhere.”

     

                “It’s a small comfort, which is the best anyone can offer in this hellhole. You know, I’d do the same for you if you just gave it a rest. If you stopped fighting it every step of the way, you’d like it a lot more.”

     

                “Are you fucking kidding me?” Lena choked out. “You want me to like prison?”

     

                “You know what I mean,” Alex muttered, flushing as her jaw twitched with annoyance. “No more talking. You’re not out for a joyride; we’re going to section you for seventy-two hours.”

     

                Snorting, Lena shook her head. “Oh, come on. Suicide watch?”

     

                “Play stupid games, win stupid prizes. Enjoy being chained to a bed for three days.”

     

                Mouth thinning with annoyance, Lena didn’t reply as Alex led her the rest of the way to a medical bay. The place smelled of mould and bleach, a window with a metal grille covering it on the inside set into the door. Alex made her sit on the bed, leaning against a wall as she scowled at her.

     

                There was a knock on the door and Lena saw the top of Kelly’s head through the window before she opened it and stepped inside. Her eyes went from Lena to Alex, who straightened, a stressed look of exhaustion on her face as she murmured a hello.

     

                “My mom hasn’t checked her out yet.”

     

                “She’s with another prisoner. Thought I’d get the eval out of the way while we wait.”

     

                Gesturing to Lena, Alex remained in the corner as Kelly warily approached, cautious and wide-eyed with concern. “Lena? I’m just going to ask you a few questions, is that okay?”

     

                Snorting at the gentleness of her tone, Lena’s mouth twitched with amusement. “I’m not crazy. You don’t have to treat me like I am.”

     

                Kelly blinked, glancing over her shoulder at Alex before licking her lips, stopping a safe distance from Lena. “I don’t think you’re crazy,” she replied. “I’m just curious. What was it you were trying to do?”

     

                “Get out of isolation. Obviously.”

     

                “Okay. I understand; it can be lonely in there, can’t it?”

     

                Lena scoffed, rolling her eyes at the sympathetic softness of Kelly’s approach. 

     

                “Do you want to tell me what you’re feeling?”

     

                At the cutting gaze Lena threw her, Kelly let out a small sigh. Still, she persisted through a series of questions, logging it all in the tablet she carried as Lena refused to answer for the most part. Finishing up quickly, Kelly’s mouth thinned and she gave Alex a half-hearted shrug. There was nothing she could do for Lena, and they all knew she didn’t want to kill herself, that she wasn’t insane and just wanted to escape the prison. They had to treat it as such though and Lena rankled at the thought of them thinking she was even remotely like her brother, although her erratic behaviour hadn’t helped dampen that thought.

     

                Turning her back on Lena, Kelly conversed quietly with Alex, which was still loud enough for Lena to hear in the small confines of the holding room. Cuffed and content to patiently await what came next, Lena watched the two of them together with an odd pang of jealousy. They might be stuck here, but at least they had each other and at least they were on the other side of a cell.

     

                “When was the last time they let her shower ?” Kelly quietly asked. “It’s a violation of human rights to deny her that at least.”

     

                Alex looked apologetic, a plea in her brown eyes as she swallowed. “Lucy said Haley instructed her to-”

     

                “I’m her psych; I say she needs a shower for her own sanity, as well as basic hygiene. Unless your mother wants to be treating her for dermatitis, or- or a UTI or bacterial infection.”

     

                “I’ll let the Deputy know.”

     

                Kelly moved in closer to her girlfriend, grabbing her arm and lowering her voice. “Alex. You’re better than that.”

     

                “She’s the reason I killed someone,” Alex snapped, her eyes darting over to Lena. “And she’s not under my supervision anymore. I’m not the one denying her proper care. Take it up with Maggie; I’m sure you’ll have even less luck than I would.”

     

                Sighing, Kelly dropped her hand and turned away. “You can wait outside.”

     

                “No, I-”

     

                “Outside. I’m with a patient; my work is confidential.”

     

                Grinding her teeth together, Alex curtly nodded and yanked the door open, jerking it shut behind herself and locking it from the outside. Kelly stood at the end of the bed and folded her arms over the tablet, cradling it against her chest as she gave Lena a glum look.

     

                “Lover’s quarrel?” Lena innocently asked.

     

                “That’s private. Why don’t you tell me what it is you’re trying to do.”

     

                “Escape,” Lena honestly replied.

     

                “Mhm. And the pills?”

     

                “Got me out of isolation.”

     

                “Very reckless. Very risky.”

     

                Shrugging, Lena’s lips twisted wryly. “You can’t push the boundaries of the known if you don’t take risks. Every scientific advancement that’s been made pushed some sort of boundary, even the little harmless ones.”

     

                “This risk was perhaps too far, Lena. You’re a risk to yourself and others. Do you know what that means? It means medications, extra precautions, it means constant supervision and limited human contact. No socials, individual showering, individual walks, weekly counselling. You’re whittling away at your own freedom while looking for an escape, and you’re quickly wearing out your welcome.”

     

                “I do have that sort of effect on people.”

     

                Sighing, frustration creasing her face, Kelly shook her head. “I’ve made my assessment; I don’t think you’re suicidal or insane, I don’t think you’re manic or sociopathic. I think you have a naturally antisocial personality, and yes, maybe being in here has exacerbated some depressive tendencies. But it’s out of my hands what the Deputy decides next, and I won’t fight her on her decision. For the safety of everyone else in here.”

     

                Nodding, a muscle twitched in Lena’s jaw and she fixed her eyes on the flaking paint on the wall opposite her. It was a moment later when the lock scraped and the door opened, Eliza stepped inside, looking harried and weary as she crossed over to the bed, blue eyes roaming over Lena.

     

                “You saved the pills,” she said with a softly defeated sigh.

     

                Lips quirking ruefully, Lena swallowed drily. “I needed a contingency plan.”

     

                Clicking her tongue, Eliza removed her stethoscope from around her neck and put the buds in her ears. Lena was still as she let her listen to her heart and lungs, breathing slowly, and then let Eliza shine her light in her eyes and mouth. 

     

                She moved over to the cabinets crammed with medical supplies then, found a sachet of something and filled a paper cup with water at the tap. Shaking out the contents, she dissolved it with a wooden stirrer and handed the cup to Lena.

     

                “How many did you manage to swallow?”

     

                “Nine, I think. Alex stopped me before I could get most of them down.”

     

                “Lucky for you. Do you know what the side effects of an Aspirin overdose are?”

     

                “Death, obviously, although I didn’t have enough for that. Gastrointestinal bleeding, drowsiness, fever, hallucinations, seizures, vomiting, shaking,” Lena rattled off.

     

                “Are you experiencing any of those?”

     

                Lena deliberated for a moment, arching an eyebrow as Eliza felt her brow. “That depends on if you’re actually here right now.”

     

                “Funny,” Eliza flatly murmured. “Drink.”

     

                “Activated charcoal?”

     

                “Yes. Are your ears ringing? Throat burning? This isn’t a joke, Lena. Even a mild overdose like you took is enough to cause damage if your body can’t clear it. Drink it.”

     

                Her levity vanished at the grave look on Eliza’s face, Lena’s mouth turned down at the corners. She stared into the gritty grey solution. “I’m fine.”

     

                Draining the cup in two gulps, choking down the solution, Lena grimaced and coughed as she raised her cuffed hands to wipe her mouth on her sleeve. Eliza plucked the cup from her hand and tenderly brushed a greasy strand of hair out of Lena’s face as her brow furrowed with concern. Shaking her head, Eliza turned to Kelly. 

     

                “Bring Alex in. She requested an emergency section. I’ll keep her here for a seventy-two-hour observation.”

     

                Kelly opened the door and Alex stepped inside, a murmured conversation filling her in as Alex moved to the side of the bed and grabbed the first set of cuffs on the right. 

     

                “Lay down,” she ordered Lena.

     

                Hesitating, Lena let out a quiet sigh and obeyed, allowing herself to be cuffed to the bed again while her other cuffs were removed. It made her feel claustrophobic, the sensation of being trapped making her heart rate jump up and her breaths turn shallower. Eliza raised the head of the bed and rummaged around in a cupboard, coming up with a bedpan that she set beside Lena on the bed.

     

                “I’ll stay with her for now,” Eliza said, glancing down at her watch. “Tell the Deputy I need to speak with her.”

     

    vAlex and Kelly left then, the silence of the room deafening as Eliza went about hooking Lena up to several machines and started an IV drip for fluids. By the time she was finished, Lena’s stomach roiled as the charcoal made nausea bloom inside her, and Eliza was quick to snatch up the bedpan and raise it to Lena’s face as a gout of grey vomit came out.

     

                It kept coming as she emptied her stomach, left gasping and clammy with the sour taste of bile on her tongue as she hunched over. Eliza murmured softly as she plucked a tissue and dabbed Lena’s mouth for her, and Lena was starting to question her own commitment to escaping.

     

                Once she’d finished her duties, Eliza sat on the small wheeled stool beside the bed, keeping an eye on her. Lena didn’t attempt to talk and neither did Eliza, leaving her tongue-tied and wishing she would say something, even if it was to chastise Lena. Anything would’ve been better than the silence, and after isolation, Lena had had enough of silence.

     

    vIt was over an hour before the door squeaked open, spent with frequent checkups from Eliza listening to her chest and checking her temperature, and the Deputy stepped inside. Lucy was cordial but firm as she greeted Eliza, her green eyes shrewd as they fixed on Lena.

     

                “Doctor Danvers, I thought I’d take the liberty of coming to see you myself.”

     

                “Deputy Lane. There’s been an incident-“

     

                “Yes, Agent Danvers briefed me. I shouldn’t be surprised at the cause of it. What have you given her so far?”

                “To contain her, Doctor.”

     

                Eliza blinked, mouth opening and closing for a second. “Nothing. I don’t believe she’s a threat while chained to the bed.”

                

                “I’m not willing to take risks with this one. Far too clever for her own good and too unpredictable. What’s your standard course of treatment for psychosis?”

     

                “I don’t believe she-“

     

                “That wasn’t my question.”

                “What do we have for sedation?”

     

                “Clozapine.”

     

                “Good. Administer it to Prisoner LL93.”

     

                “Deputy Lane,” Eliza started, slightly aghast and chastising.

     

                Lucy looked at her, squaring her shoulders as she swallowed. “The Warden has told me to take all necessary measures,” she dubiously informed Eliza. “Keep her here for the next three days and then return her to iso.                 Spluttering for a moment, Eliza swallowed her objects and curtly replied. “Is she allowed to shower and eat now? Out of medical necessity?”

     

                “Yes. Under high-security supervision. Give her that sedative once she’s done.”

     

                Nodding, Eliza’s mouth thinned but she didn’t object anymore. Deputy Lane slipped her thumbs through the loops of her pants as she stood at the end of the bed and stared at Lena for a moment.

     

                “Listen to me very closely, Prisoner LL93. Every mistake you make trying to outsmart me only escalates the punishment after the fact. We’re a mile under the sea in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean; there’s nowhere else to go. Time to accept that.”

     

                “Yes, ma’am,” Lena drawled, her throat hoarse from vomiting and her stomach aching. 

     

                Even that didn’t dampen her contempt and Lucy’s mouth turned down at the corners with regret, as if she hated being complicit in this. Not enough to grow a spine and object to it, following her orders while dishing out her own, trickling down the chain of command as the prison tried to govern itself outside of the law. Lena didn’t know why they didn’t just kill them off and save themselves the hassle, except she did know because they all had some sort of skill or strength that could be useful one day. Maybe one day they’d need a nuclear weapon designed to wipe half of the globe off the map, and who better than her to design it? She’d let them shoot her before she did it but they didn’t know that.

     

                Fetching two agents, one of them familiar as Vasquez came in with another woman, they both uncuffed her and hauled her from the bed. Lena made a choked sound of surprise at the back of her throat, her eyes going to Eliza for guidance.

     

                “High-security supervision.”

     

                The three of them remained inside the tiny bathroom while Lena showered for the first time in three weeks, furious as she scrubbed herself with the small bar of soap, scalding water turning her skin pink. There was no shampoo, of course, and she worked the bar through her greasy hair, doing her best with one hand.

     

                She dried herself off once Eliza handed her a towel before they uncuffed her again. Batons were held in hand, the Agents stiff and alert, and Eliza hurriedly helped her into the layers of warm clothes. Feeling refreshed and a little hot from the steaming air, Lena felt better than she had in days, although her mood plummeted as soon as she was chained back to her bed in the medical room.

     

                “Fetch her food. A double serving of her usual calorie intake,” Eliza instructed Vasquez.

     

                Once they were alone again, Eliza sighed and gave her a pitying look. “How’re you feeling?”

     

                Lena’s chin dimpled as she swallowed thickly. “Alex said Kara’s been difficult.”

     

                “I’m asking how you are.”

     

                “Can you tell her I’m sorry? Tell her I don’t want her to do anything stupid.”

     

                Eliza let out a quiet huff of laughter. “You know, she said the exact same thing to me at her last checkup. She’s worried about you; that worry is making her … a bit of a problem on the cell block.”

     

                A rough exhale scraped Lena’s throat as she slammed her head back against the pillows, frustration welling inside her. Kara wasn’t supposed to get in the middle of it all; she was supposed to let Lena hatch a plan and then punch their way out of it. Lena didn’t want her involved for the simple reason that any punishment inflicted would be severe, and Lena didn’t want her to tarnish her standing as a model inmate for her.

     

                “Tell her to stop. I don’t want her to get hurt. Not for me. Can you tell her that for me? Please.”

     

                “I’ll tell her,” Eliza murmured, stroking Lena’s damp hair. “Now you listen to her as well. No more trouble.”

     

                “I won’t be able to if you give me clozapine.”

     

                “You’ve left me little choice.”

     

                “I know. I’m sorry for that. You genuinely do seem like you don’t want to and I’m sorry for forcing your hand.”

     

                Giving her a withering look, Eliza folded her arms over her chest and reclaimed her seat on the stool. “It’ll be a depot injection for slow release. Do you know what that means?”

     

                “Yes,” Lena muttered.

     

                “I’ll hold off on it until the end of the seventy-two hours if I can. That’s dependent on your behaviour though.”

     

                “I won’t cause any problems for you.”

                

                “Thank you.”

     

                Her food was brought shortly after that and they uncuffed one hand so she could feed herself. The rice was starchy with a glue-like texture and the chicken was bland but it was hot and filling at least, the frozen carrots and peas more nutritious than anything she’d had in weeks. Lena was actually grateful for the prison food, eating it without complaint and savouring the little container of custard pudding for dessert. She felt full for the first time in months and her stomach ached as she set the spoon down.

     

                “Can you make a cup of coffee for me please?” Eliza asked Vasquez. “Two sugars and some cream. Thank you.”

     

                The coffee was brought in a paper cup and Eliza assured the guards she’d be fine supervising Lena alone. They’d cuffed her to the bed again and Lena felt exhausted, both physically and mentally. 

     

                Walking over to the side of the bed, Eliza held the cup up to her lips and Lena blinked at her with surprise. “Here. Drink. Empty calories, but at least it’s something.”

     

                “Thank you.”

     

                Lena sipped it slowly and her eyes stung with tears over the simple pleasure of a cup of coffee. She never took her coffee with cream or sugar and it was too sweet for her liking but it was heavenly as she drank it bit by bit, Eliza holding the cup to her mouth and patiently tipping it for her.

     

                “You should sleep now.”

     

                Eliza turned the lights off, plunging them into dim grey as the medical equipment screens emitted a wan glow, the beep of them filling the small room. Retreading back to her stool, Eliza quietly updated Lena’s file on the tablet she’d brought in with her and after a while Lena fell asleep.

     

                When she woke, Eliza was gone and the lights were on, Alex filling out a book of Sudoku puzzles as she kept watch. Lena was surprised she was there and they didn’t say a word to each other, even when their eyes locked for a brief moment. She slept again and a different agent was monitoring her then, and Lena felt warm and a little dizzy as she breathlessly asked to use the bathroom.

     

                It was a long seventy-two hours, a rotation of guards watching her for any signs of medical issues, Eliza drawing her blood to test it, bigger meals to compensate for how she’d been half-starved, and the merciful bliss of daily showers again. She knew she shouldn’t have been thankful for basic decencies but after being denied them by the people in charge of her care in isolation, it was a drastic improvement so she was thankful. 

     

                At the end of her section, Lena lay cuffed in the bed and watched as Eliza readied her antipsychotic medication with derision. Alex came in a few minutes later and uncuffed all but one of her wrists and Lena hitched the triple layers of shirts and sweatshirts up before scooting the pants down. 

     

                “Have you had a depot injection before?”

     

                “No, I can’t say I’ve ever had a needle in my ass,” Lena snorted.

     

                “It might hurt a little.”

     

                “I can guarantee I’ve had worse.”

     

                It did hurt a little and Lena stiffened at the pinch, but she was more affronted by the dose of clozapine than anything else. It almost felt insulting, and particularly pointed, for her to be put on antipsychotics as if she’d followed in her brother’s footsteps and lost her mind. Maybe she had a little but Lena refused to be held accountable for what she did while wrongfully imprisoned. 

     

                “All done.”

     

                “Great,” she muttered.

     

                “You’ll most likely feel drowsy. Maybe a little dizzy or nauseous. I’ll make sure they give you extra water in case you have a dry mouth. It’ll be a slow release so I’ll give you your next shot at your checkup with the other ones. We should probably do your contraceptive now though; I think you’re just about due.”

     

                “Perfect.”

     

                She’d hitched her pants back up and let Eliza help free her left arm from her sleeves so she could slip another needle into the muscle, administering the contraceptive. Once Eliza had noted everything down, she gave Lena a pointed look.

     

                “I’ll need to see you next week for another blood test to make sure it’s not causing any problems. Don’t give me a reason to see you again before then.”

     

                Giving her a hollow grin as Alex uncuffed her other hand and then cuffed them together behind her back, Lena imagined she could feel the cold seeping effect of the drug slip into her bloodstream, knowing in a couple of hours she’d be a shell of herself.

     

                “You just made sure of that.”

    Chapter 11

                After the distraction she cobbled together for Lena, tearing apart her mattress and pillow and tossing it around, working herself into a state until the collar jolted her with green kryptonite exposure, the red sun lamps that left her cell in a ghastly red light flaring even stronger as the guards watched her from the blinking red cameras in the corners, Kara was slumped grey-faced on the floor of her cell. They were always quick to subdue her, fearing the parameters they’d set on her containment wouldn’t be enough. 

     

                Kara wasn’t even sure if they had truly contained her. Sure, they kept the red sun lamps emitting a low enough radiation to leave her weak - but not so weak that she had to fear bruises and broken bones for long - and they’d figured out that green kryptonite was a weakness, but she knew she’d never make it out of the prison alone, no matter how strong she was. Not without condemning the hundreds of heartbeats she could hear inside to death.

     

                Still, Lena had a plan, or the beginnings of one, and maybe it was Kara’s childish naïvety that led her to believe she’d get them out, but she trusted her. She just hoped her small outburst had bought Lena enough time to do whatever it was she’d been planning but as she listened to her heartbeat somewhere up in the ceiling, she was left perplexed.

     

                Another heartbeat, as familiar as her own, entered the cell block and Kara weakly pushed herself up to her knees. Her face was drawn with the lingering effects of kryptonite, still dully emitted from the collar as they took no chances. There were already two other guards outside her cell, guns drawn and faces pinched with worry as if they expected her to break down the forcefield barrier of her cell.

     

                Alex came into view, the red glow spilling out of the cell making her look severe, although her eyes were wide with worry. She pressed a hand against the invisible barrier and Kara struggled to her feet, off balance and weak-kneed as she swallowed drily.

     

                “What’s going on?” Alex asked, her voice low and concerned.

     

                “Sorry,” Kara hoarsely apologised walking over to her, a thin smile crossing her face.

     

                “What’re you doing?” Alex asked, spreading her hands as she gave Kara a bewildered look.

     

                Kara’s smile turned slightly sheepish and beseeching as she bit her lip. “Nothing.”

     

                “Don’t try that bullshit with me, Kara. You start having a meltdown and now you want to act like everything’s fine?”

     

                “I’m just feeling a little restless.”

     

                “Then use your words . You know I’ll take you for another walk if that’s what you want.”

     

                Pursing her lips, Kara’s brow furrowed slightly, a pouting look of churlishness as she rolled her neck, the collar making her skin burn with the sensation of a thousand knives pricking her. 

     

                “Sorry.”

     

                They stared at each other for a long moment, suspicion in Alex’s eyes as Kara swallowed thickly, trying to keep her guilt off her face. They’d been locked up together for so long that Kara practically considered Alex a sister, the two of them the only children in the prison, albeit on opposite sides of a wall. Eliza’s pity had freed Kara for a few hours a day for tutoring, her broken English rapidly improving and her aptitude for learning and quiet disposition as fear of this unknown planet endearing her to the doctor. Alex knew Kara better than anyone and she felt a flicker of guilt for lying to her.

     

                “Clean the mess up and I’ll take you for a walk,” Alex said with a soft sigh. “If you’re still up for it. Is the collar giving you any grief?”

     

                Teeth gritted, Kara let out a quiet, strained laugh. “It’s like having my skin peeled off.”

     

                With a regretful sigh, Alex splayed her fingers on the forcefield. “Rest a bit then. You look a little pale.”

     

                “Really? Darn, I was hoping my summer tan would last a bit longer.”

     

                Snorting at her weak joking, Alex shook her head. “You’re still not funny, kid. I’ll see if I can swing you an extra pudding to help you feel better.”

     

                Wrinkling her nose, an easy smile crossing her face, Kara pressed her hand against Alex’s over the forcefield. “Thanks.”

     

                “Behave,” Alex sternly warned her. “I’ve already got to deal with your trouble-maker neighbour.”

     

                “Where’d she go?” Kara innocently asked.

     

                “Pulling her weight,” Alex replied with a wry smile. “She’ll be back soon, don’t worry.”

     

                Nodding, Kara swallowed and then turned around, slowly gathering up the mess she’d made and setting it in a neat pile near the forcefield. She was fortunate that Alex looked out for her, a new mattress and pillows immediately swapped out for the ruined one while a timid Agent swept out her cell, four guns trained on Kara as she lounged against the back wall of the cell, trying to look as unthreatening as possible.

     

                Once they were done, she remade her bed, carefully smoothing out the blanket and arranging the pillow before she lay down on it. The lingering effects of the kryptonite, coupled with the increase in the radiation of a red sun, Kara felt drained and she closed her eyes to the gory tint of the cell and let her mind wander. When it wandered, it sought out Lena’s heartbeat amidst the others beating around her, almost unbearable at times when her senses overwhelmed her, but after almost two decades, she’d gotten used to it.

     

                Tracking Lena through the crawl space of the ceiling, Kara grew increasingly worried as she heard her heartbeat approach until Lena made it to her own adjoining cell. Sitting up straight, Kara frowned up at the ceiling panels and listened to the scrabbling sound and then the quiet cracking, wondering what she was doing. She wished she could’ve communicated with her, tried to assist from inside her cell, but Kara couldn’t do anything but listen out of concern and curiosity.

     

                A short while later, Lena’s heartbeat moved on and Kara’s throat closed up as she fiddled with her fingers, sitting cross-legged on her cot as she tried to stifle her worry. Lena had been alone which could only mean she’d slipped her guard, which could only mean bad things to come. Kara wouldn’t give her away though, leaning against the wall as the waning kryptonite made her skin feel tender.

     

                Her stomach jolted with unease as she heard Alex’s approaching footsteps a while later and Kara tried her best to look relaxed as she closed her eyes. She didn’t have to wait long for Alex to pound her palm against the forcefield to get her attention. Cracking her eyes open, Kara turned and raised her eyebrows slightly, her face softening with a warm smile.

     

                “Hey.”

     

                “Where is she?”

     

                “Who?” Kara asked, feigning ignorance.

     

                Alex scoffed, rolling her eyes as her mouth tightened at the corners. “Don’t play dumb with me right now, Kara. Tell me where she is; I know you can hear her.”

     

                Climbing to her feet, Kara crossed the small cell. “Is this about Lena?”

     

                “Kara,” Alex impatiently ground out.

     

                “I thought you were making her do some job.”

     

                “We were but she’s attacked a guard. Winn. Now she’s loose and we need to find her before she causes any further harm. So please, tell me where she is.”

     

                “I don’t know,” Kara mumbled.

     

                Desperation and panic made Alex’s expression turn pleading, pressing her hand against the invisible barrier. “Please. I know you like her but she’s dangerous . She could hurt someone else, and it’ll only be worse for her when she’s found. We will find her eventually. Do you want her to be punished?”

     

                Swallowing thickly as she ducked her head down, long blonde hair falling in her face as she chewed her lip, considering it, Kara’s brow pinched with doubt.

     

                “You’re manipulating me.”

     

                “Wha- no. No, I’m not, I wouldn’t do that to you,” Alex earnestly replied. “I’m just telling you the truth; it’ll be so much worse for her if we don’t catch her quickly. I’m- I’m trying to help her too - for you. I know it doesn’t look like it.”

     

                Raising her head, Kara blinked blankly at Alex. “If you wanted to help her - help me - you would’ve agreed to help her with her plan.”

     

                “Oh, don’t give me that shit,” Alex quietly snapped. “I’m trying to make sure none of us get killed. She’s doing a damn fucking good job of leading herself down that path.”

     

                Hesitating, a seed of doubt growing inside Kara, she pressed her lips into a flat line and drew back slightly. “Lena wouldn’t want me to tell you. Even if it means helping her.”

     

                “Kara-” Alex started, frustration colouring her words. She cut off, mouth opening and closing before she inhaled sharply as her face tightened. “I’m not going to be able to stop the others from killing her if it comes to it, so just remember that while you sit here silently instead of helping us.”

     

                Turning away, she made it a step before Kara’s low voice made her pause. “Hurt her and I swear I’ll tear this prison apart.”

     

                “I won’t but I can’t promise the others won’t.”

     

                “Alex.”

     

                Hesitating a moment longer, turning her head as if to reply, Alex closed her mouth and walked off. Kara clenched her hands into fists, fear stuck in her throat like a lump as she listened to Lena’s heartbeat and hoped she knew what she was doing. Even if it meant getting herself out and leaving Kara locked in her cell, Kara hoped she took the chance if it meant escaping harm’s way. She trusted Alex’s word that she wouldn’t hurt her but it was a cold comfort in a prison where half of the other Agents were brutal and cruel. 

     

                Closing her eyes, a small sigh escaped Kara and she turned away from the barrier. Running a hand through her hair, she paced anxiously, feeling like a caged animal she’d seen on the boxy TV at the socials. Pressing her fingertips to her brow bone, Kara tried to stifle the jittery restlessness as she worried about what came next. She wished she had J’onn’s shackled ability to communicate telepathically, so she could talk to her and warn her against doing anything rash. She would’ve settled for J’onn being able to use his own ability too, but that was beyond him now, his powers inhibited just like the rest of them.

     

                Kara also felt torn in two. She didn’t like being caught in the middle of Lena and Alex and their butting heads, used as a device by both of them to get to the other one. It had been relatively peaceful before Lena had shown up, Alex something of a sister to Kara, life following its monotonous routine of imprisonment, but now things felt unsettled and off, Lena’s unpredictability throwing things into disarray. Kara couldn’t fault her for resisting the claustrophobic feeling of a cell and endless boredom, but she didn’t like the rift that was opening up between her and the woman she’d grown up alongside. 

     

                Alarms sounded beyond the confines of the cell block and her other block mates were cautious and on edge, loud assumptions swapped back and forth as they wondered aloud about Lena’s absence and the uneasy tension that suffused the guards that came. There were no daily walks or showers over the following days, Mon-El, in particular, growing very angry and impatient as he cursed out the guards and made a lot of loud comments about Lena for Kara’s ears. 

     

                Kara spent most of the five days of Lena’s absence sitting on her cot, listening to her heartbeat as she tracked her through the prison, hearing it drop down to her level on occasion and then slip back up into the ceiling again. There were moments when Lena’s heart rate spiked and Kara would straighten on her bed, spine rigid and hands curled into white-knuckled fists in her lap as her own heart rate sped up in tandem.

     

                It was at its worst at one moment when Lena dropped down from the ceiling and Kara wondered for a moment if she’d been caught. It stayed elevated though and she stayed put for three days, undiscovered as Kara kept her mouth shut, despite Alex’s frequent visits to her cell, where she stood on the other side of the forcefield in silence and waited for Kara to speak. She never did, not up until Lena’s heartbeat started drawing closer and closer, and then she could hear the frantic sounds of the guards beyond the cell block, radios squawking and heavy footfalls as Lena slipped them again.

     

                Alex stormed in a minute later, her brown eyes wide and desperate. “Tell me where she is. Jensen’s out for blood so you tell me now .”

     

                Biting the inside of her cheek, Kara deliberated for a moment before she caved beneath the knot of fear that had been growing in her stomach for days. Nodding, she tried to visualise the prison as she heard Lena’s heartbeat drop down from the ceiling.

     

                “The guard bathroom on the left.”

     

                Alex took off running the moment Kara divulged the information, a breathless thank you left in her wake, and Kara dug the heels of her palms into her eyes as she listened to it all play out. Shoulders taut beneath the layers of her uniform, she felt a stab of guilt at betraying Lena to Alex and hoped she wouldn’t be too angry.

     

                A minute later when she heard the sound of a gun firing, she shot to her feet, heart pounding and the cold sweat of fear prickling her back. Mouth dry, Kara walked over to the forcefield and pressed a hand against it, the few fellow inmates with above human sensitivity climbing to their feet as well, wariness clouding all of their faces. There was another shot a moment later, preceded by Alex’s shouting, and Kara hardly dared to breathe as she listened to the hummingbird heartbeats of the two people she cared about most.

     

                No one came into the cell block and Kara was left trying to piece things together as she eavesdropped, cursing the red sun lamps that inhibited her sensitivity, anxiously pacing back and forth as she waited. It was just after lunch and she paced for hours, ignoring the gossip flitting back and forth and between cells, the hours stretching out into agonising lengths until she finally heard Alex’s approaching footsteps and the squeak of the trolley for dinner.

     

                Jittery as she bit her nails and felt panic well up with each passing moment as dinner trays were slid into each cell, one by one as the wards came down, Kara waited for her turn. She practically pounced on Alex when she stopped in front of Kara’s cell, Vasquez wheeling the trolley and removing the one with her designated number of calories.

     

                “Alex, what’s happening?” Kara frantically asked, her voice a low murmur.

     

                “Back against the wall,” Alex wearily instructed her.

     

                “Tell me what’s going on. Please.”

     

                “Prisoner KZ64, move back against the wall.”

     

                She spoke to her with the tired patience of someone talking to a child, her expression drawn and panicked, a tremor in her hands as she toyed with her fingers, waiting for Kara to obey. Staring at her for a long moment, Kara turned on her heel before marching to the back of her cell and leaning against the wall as the barrier was brought down. She was quick though, and when Vasquez stooped down to set a tray on the concrete floor, Kara pushed off and crossed the cell in half a dozen strides, twisting past her as Alex stepped into her path.

     

                Her hands were empty and Kara knew she wouldn’t hurt her, the same way she would never hurt Alex, but that didn’t mean that the guard would let her do whatever she wanted. Hands coming up, Alex grabbed her shoulders as she blanched, her grip tight and her face pleading.

     

                “Kara, don’t-”

     

                Taller than her by a few inches, and stronger even though she was kept weak and wiry, Kara gripped Alex’s biceps and pushed back against her, forging onwards. Her mouth was set in a determined line and blue eyes were wide with surprise at her own audacity. Kara hadn’t caused much of a fuss over the eighteen years behind bars, especially not after the first year, when Alex had arrived and she hadn’t felt so alone and frightened, having someone to share in her fear. 

     

                Now, she found herself at a stand-off with the same woman who’d saved her from the darkness of a place like Fort Rozz. It gave Kara pause for a moment, blinking as she stopped pushing against Alex, who she’d been driving back, the low setting of the sun lamps not quite leaching all of the inhuman strength from her limbs.

     

                “Kara,” Alex whispered, her brown eyes shining with tears. “Don’t.”

     

                Lips parting as her face dropped, the gravity of the moment weighing on her, Kara went to reply when agonising pain suffused her, her vision dimming as her knees buckled. Her grasp on Alex went slack and she scrabbled for purchase on the tactical vest, on the cuffs of her polo shirt, on the utility belt, her legs giving out from beneath her as the kryptonite collar neutralised her as a threat.

     

                Blinking away black spots, Kara let out a small sound of pain, surprise on her ashen face as she knelt on the floor, staring up at Alex. There was a prickle of fear on Alex’s face now, doubt clouding the trust that had built over years, and Kara let out a ragged plea as her hands went to the collar around her neck, wanting to tear it in half to free herself from the all-consuming pain of it. Alex grabbed her wrists, trying to keep her from sagging to the ground as Kara hung her head, blonde hair spilling to the floor and shoulders tense and narrow as she choked on a gasp.

     

                Gritting her teeth, the tendons straining in her neck, Kara pushed herself onto one knee. She used Alex to anchor herself, gripping her as she hauled herself to her feet, taking every ounce of her strength as the collar kept up a constant stream of exposure to the green kryptonite nestled within it. 

     

                “Stop,” Alex gently whispered, fear written in the lines of her face - for Kara now, not for herself - her hands going to her shoulders as she tried to urge her back down. “Don’t fight it. Please. Please stay down.”

     

                Kara didn’t give any sign that she’d heard Alex and the guard’s hand went to her radio. “Agent Danvers requesting a sedative for Prisoner KZ64. Code white. I repeat, code white.”

     

                There were more guards spilling in now, the sounds of guns being cocked, voices clamouring and Alex’s snarling response. Vasquez jabbed the end of her electrifying baton into Kara’s waist to no avail, doing nothing to mitigate her threat, and Alex protectively hunched over Kara as she slowly sank back to the floor, feeling as if the skin was being flayed from her body.

     

                “Vasquez, get my mom. Now.”

     

                “Danvers, get out of the way.”

     

                “You are not shooting her. You don’t have my authorisation. Stand down.”

     

                Panting, her grey face beaded with sweat as she curled in on herself, Kara found herself cradled by Alex, who sank down with her. “Alex, move,” she mumbled through numb lips.

     

                “You shut up,” Alex said through her teeth.

     

                The doors opened a moment later and Kara caught a glimpse of a white doctor’s coat, Eliza pushing through the dark uniforms of DEO agents. Her expression was slack with surprise before she hoarsely instructed her daughter to move aside, a sedative already in hand, specially adapted to knock Kara out if she posed a threat. Eliza hesitated for the briefest of moments before slipping the needle tip into Kara’s neck and pressing down on the plunger.

     

                A wounded look of hurt crossed Kara’s face as she blinked up at the two women who’d become her family, feeling as if a line had been drawn between them as unconsciousness welled up to drag her under. A long, defeated sigh slipped past her lips as her body went slack, residual tension fading along with the pain of the collar, which hadn’t let up the entire time. It was almost a relief.

     

                She woke an unknown length of time later, blearily blinking through the fog in her mind as she stared at the ceiling. It was one of the isolation cells she hadn’t found herself inside in a decade, not since she’d sneezed so forcefully she’d headbutted an inmate and started a small brawl at a social, and she let out an airy sigh, finding herself unable to move. Kara already knew what state she’d find herself in; a straitjacket binding her arms to herself and thick bands of steel locking her to the slab of concrete she lay upon. 

     

                As she grasped tightly to consciousness, Kara became aware of a heartbeat in the room with her and she turned her head slightly, limited by the band crossing her throat over the collar. She met Alex’s hard stare and swallowed thickly, her stomach lurching with guilt. 

     

                “Sorry,” Kara whispered, her throat dry and voice cracking slightly.

     

                Alex didn’t respond and Kara could practically feel her anger and disappointment radiating from her. A weary sigh escaped Kara and she blinked slowly a few times, shifting against the trappings keeping her flat on the table. Chewing on her words for a moment, Kara’s eyes cut sideways.

     

                “Are you okay?”

     

                “You could’ve been killed,” Alex said with steel. 

     

                “Thank you for stopping them.”

     

                With a scathing sound of anger, Alex climbed to her feet, standing over Kara, her brown eyes frightened and swimming with tears. Her pale face flushed with two pink spots on her cheeks and her breath hitched as she inhaled, making Kara’s chest spasm with pain as guilt knifed through her.

     

                “Why are you doing this?” Alex asked, bewilderment creasing her face. “She showed up here and you’ve undone so many years of good behaviour all because she’s filled your head with some fantasy of leaving. Why are you letting her get inside your head? Turning you against me.”

     

                Eyes filling with tears, Kara squeezed her eyes shut as a sob built in her chest. “I’m sorry. I’m sorry, I just- I want to get out of here. I’m scared. I’m scared I’m going to live in a cell for a thousand years and die without ever feeling the sun on my face again. I’m scared I’ll lose you and Eliza and I’ll be- I’ll be all by myself again. I don’t want to be alone, Alex. I just want to be free.”

     

                Letting out a pent-up breath, Alex reached down and gently stroked Kara’s hair, taking in the crumpled look of gut-wrenching sadness on her face. Chin dimpling with the effort of holding her sobs at bay, Kara sniffed, unable to even wipe the tears from her cheeks as she rankled against her restraints.

     

                “I’m sorry. I’m sorry but I care about her and I trust her. Nights and- and days … hundreds of them. She’s the only thing that makes these long nights bearable anymore. I haven’t felt so alive in years; I feel how you felt when you had Maggie and then Kelly. Do you remember what it felt like when you fell in love?”

     

                “You don’t love her, Kara,” Alex tightly replied, reaching down to wipe her cheeks for her. “You don’t know what that’s like; you don’t even know her.”

     

                “I do,” Kara whispered, fresh tears falling. “I know what it’s like. I had a family - once - and then I had you and your mom. I know what it’s like. Don’t tell me I don’t know. I care about her.”

     

                “Okay,” Alex whispered, her mouth turning down at the corners as her hand trembled slightly. “Okay, I believe you. But she’s going to get you hurt. Badly. I- she- I killed Jensen. I shot him to save her.”

     

                She was freely crying now, hastily wiping away her tears as she struggled to swallow past the tightness in her throat, and Kara looked up at her with mournful blue eyes, understanding her fear. Kara had heard the gunshots, of course, and had even feared it was Lena for a moment, but she hadn’t known the rest of it. Hadn’t known what had happened, who had done it. Now she just felt regret, for Alex being caught in the middle of it all.

     

                “I think I want to believe that I saved her for you because I know that you like her and I don’t think I could bear it if you hated me, but … I think I would’ve saved her anyway because I- I don’t really think she’s a bad person. I’m just afraid that … she’ll drag you into her mess and that scares the shit out of me.”

     

                “Please just tell me she’s okay.”

     

                “Kara … I don’t think you’re going to see her again. She’s in a lot of trouble and the Warden caught wind of it all and she hurt Deputy Lane. I shouldn’t be telling you any of this but you need to forget about her, okay?”

     

                The breath caught in Kara’s throat and she let out a small sound of objection, a plea that didn’t quite form. Her vision blurred with fresh tears and she opened and closed her mouth, stammering as she tried to speak.

     

                “No.”

     

                “I’m sorry. It’s not up to me but it’s gotten out of hand.”

     

                “No. They can’t- please don’t let them.”

     

                Hesitating, Alex stroked Kara’s hair and then leaned down to kiss her forehead. “You’re like a sister to me; I’m trying to keep you safe but you need to cooperate. Do you hear me? They won’t be so lenient next time and I can’t afford to make any more mistakes. I have to think about Kelly and my mom as well.”

     

                “Alex, please,” Kara whispered, the sound frayed and desperate.

     

                “I’ll get you out of here as soon as I can,” Alex promised, her voice uneven as it wavered.

     

                She left then, locking Kara into the lonely cell, unable to move an inch as tears ran down her temples and into her hair. Weak and tired, she drifted in and out of sleep with nothing to measure the passing of time until food was eventually brought to her.

     

                Alex brought a tray in herself and pushed a button to rotate the table so Kara was perpendicular to the floor. She’d been this way before, strapped down and fed as if she was a child, and she could see Alex was slightly embarrassed to be the one to do it now, trying to coax cold instant mashed potatoes past Kara’s lips as she kept her jaw clamped shut.

     

                Growing impatient, Alex sighed and sharply commented on her idiocy before rotating the slab back down and leaving her alone. She was kept in that room for twenty-four hours before returning to her cell, her good track record affording her some trust and leniency.

     

                But Kara wasn’t prepared to go quietly. Back in her cell, Alex enclosed inside it with her after assuring the guards that Kare wouldn’t hurt her, she was relieved of the straitjacket. Alex promised to bring her breakfast first thing in the morning and left Kara to sleep, her block mates already stretched out for the night, some fast asleep and others lightly dozing.

     

                The moment the forcefield was back in place, Kara was there, slamming her palm against the invisible barrier. “Bring her back.”

     

                “Go to sleep.”

     

                “Bring her back. Alex. Alex!”

     

                Kara’s hoarse shouts fell on deaf ears and she slammed her palm against the barrier again. Then she pounded her fist against it, grinding her teeth together as frustration welled up, shoulders tense as she turned away from the barrier. Hands balled into fists, she struggled to swallow and then dragged her bed from the cot, going through the motions of a meltdown all over again - this time not as a distraction but as a way to vent the conflicted feelings building in her chest. 

     

                She kicked a pillow across the room, flipped the lumpy mattress and tore a blanket in half, a torrent of Kryptonian spilling from her lips as she cursed the prison out in the native tongue she had no use for anymore. Her ranting and pacing and rage roused her block mates, Mon-El angrily telling her to cut it out as the others grumbled about their disturbed sleep but Kara was set on digging herself a deeper hole. She knew that they feared her the most out of any other prisoner and that if she kept it up, causing a fuss and putting the guards on edge, they’d eventually cave to what she wanted. Sure, they might put her in isolation and fill her with kryptonite and weaken her with the radiation from her home planet, but they would eventually give her back Lena to keep the peace and keep the prison in one piece.

     

                Kara didn’t think she was strong enough to break out of it, not without a few hours of sunbathing in the warmth of a yellow sun to re-energise herself, but just her breathing was enough of a threat. They tried to subdue her a few times through the night, jolts of weak kryptonite exposure giving her pause as she curled in on herself, tendons taut and teeth gritted against the pain before she continued in her anger-fuelled tantrum. She knew Alex was the only thing stopping them from fully incapacitating her, but as the night dragged into the morning, the guards grew tired of her antics.

     

                Pain only served to make Kara angrier though, her cheeks red, her eyes dark with rage as she threw herself at the forcefield, over and over again. They turned the sun lamps up in strength, depleting her until she felt practically human, proven when she ran head-first into the barrier and broke her nose with a sickening crunch. Blood ran over her chin and stained her teeth red as she bared them, eyes smarting with tears as she shouldered the forcefield, her voice a frayed plea after hours of shouting herself hoarse.

     

                “Let me out. Alex! I know you can fucking hear me . Don’t do this. Come on.”

     

                “Kara,” J’onn tried to reason, as infuriatingly serene as always.

     

                “I swear I’m going to shut you up permanently at the next social if you don’t shut your mouth, you Kryptonian bitch,” Mon-El snarled, leaning against the forcefield and glaring at Kara from his cell, situated at the end, diagonally from hers.

     

                Kara ignored them all, even the soft pleas from the ones she was friends with, Nia and Querl watching with fearful eyes, Andrea, Psi and Imra quiet and peevish in the adjoining cells. She knew her performance was ruining the peace of their cell block and she felt a little bit guilty but it was eclipsed by her concern for Lena and her determination to cause a big enough fuss to get her back. With blood running down her chin and dotting the floor, Kara was quickly subdued, the dose of green kryptonite so large that she blacked out for a short period.

     

                She woke up in a straitjacket on her bed, blinking up at the red lights overhead and taking stock of her body. It ached and her nose smarted where she’d broken it, unable to heal itself as the red sun lamps kept her healing factor at bay. Struggling into a sitting position, Kara took in the tray of her cold oatmeal, a piece of plain toast and a bruised apple and felt anger flood her anew.

     

                Climbing to her feet, she lashed out at the tray, sending her breakfast splattering across the cell and listened to the multiple groans in tandem from her fellow inmates. Mon-El started swearing, warning her to pipe down, and then Nia ripped into him in response, ever at Kara’s defence, and Kara returned to her assault on the forcefield, slamming her forehead against it hard enough to bruise as her body struggled to fight against the leaching radiation suffusing her cell in its ghastly glow.

     

                They gassed her cell then, leaving her gasping and retching as the kryptonite burned her throat, a particularly brutal punishment that got into her lungs and eyes and nose as she wilted. Out cold again, Kara was taken to the isolation cell set aside for her, strapped to the slab, immobilised for another day before Alex wrangled a release for her. 

     

                The ensuing week followed much the same process until Alex was short-tempered and frustrated and tensions were running high inside the cell block, where the only reprieve from Kara’s troublemaking was the hours she spent locked inside an isolation cell. Her body slowly recovered enough away from the radiation to heal herself each time, bruises fading and her broken nose stitching itself back together, mercifully realigned by Eliza while Kara was out each time. The guards grew tired and cranky and Kara barely ate a thing, and there was a general air of weary irritation and exasperation each time she started back up again.

     

                After two weeks of protesting, Kara found herself in one of the medical rooms, blinking up at plain fluorescent lights as they hummed angrily overhead, loud to her sensitive ears as the lack of red sun lamps reinvigorated her slightly. She was bound and restrained, as per usual, and two familiar heartbeats joined her inside the room, conversing quietly.

     

                When they became aware of her consciousness, Alex and Eliza trailed off, the former’s brown eyes bloodshot from crying while the latter looked stressed and saddened. They drifted closer to her and Eliza’s face softened with a smile.

     

                “Hi, sweetheart.”

     

                ‘Eliza,” Kara croaked, a fleeting smile on her own pale face. 

     

                “I’m going to do a checkup today, okay? Make sure you’re doing alright.”

     

                Kara let out a choked laugh, tears stinging her eyes. “What day is it?”

     

                “You haven’t been out for very long. Just a couple of hours.”

     

                “Oh,” she mumbled, falling silent for a moment. “Have you seen Lena?”

     

                Letting out a rough sigh, Alex turned her head aside, rolling her eyes as a muscle jumped in her jaw. She swallowed whatever warning was on the tip of her tongue and Kara was grateful for it, her hopeful gaze focused on Eliza, who hesitated.

     

                “No, I haven’t. They won’t let me see her yet; she’s not due for her next checkup.”

     

                “Can you tell her not to do anything stupid?”

     

                Cupping Kara’s cheek, Eliza gave her a tight-lipped smile of regret, eyes creasing at the corners, looking a little older and wearier than she used to when she’d first arrived there. “Sure, I’ll tell her.”

     

                “Mom.”

     

                Some of the tension bled out of her and her lips twitched with a relieved smile, a lump stuck in her throat for a moment. “Thank you,” Kara whispered, ignoring Alex.

     

                “Is it alright if I listen to your heart?” Eliza murmured, brushing a strand of hair out of Kara’s face.

     

                She managed a shallow nod and Eliza smiled warmly before looking at her daughter. “Alex, let her up and get her out of that infernal jacket, for God’s sake.”

     

                Shifting uneasily, her eyes darting to Kara and then to Eliza, looking agonised and apologetic, she licked her lips. “Mom, you know the protocol-”

     

                “Get Vasquez inside and we’ll have the mandated three supervisors,” Eliza said, “but I can’t do my job if she’s wrapped up like that. Kara will behave, won’t you sweetheart? The quicker I can examine you, the quicker I can talk to the Deputy about having a moment alone with Lena to see how she’s doing.”

     

                Eliza’s tone was slightly patronising but Kara was all too willing to play along, mumbling a promise as Alex relented. It didn’t take much convincing and Kara knew she was bitterly lucky to have ingratiated herself with the doctor and her daughter to be afforded the benefit of the doubt. She couldn’t help but wonder whether the same consideration had been given to Lena. By Eliza, she was almost sure of it, but Kara wasn’t sure how deep Alex’s compassion went for the troublemaker Kara had clung to with enthusiasm. 

     

                Rolling her shoulders and stretching out the joints of her arms, Kara let Eliza listen to her chest and go through the usual process of the checkup, asking Kara about her moods as she checked her eyes and her mouth and her blood pressure, ran multiple screenings and took a blood sample for any deficiencies. It was all a familiar routine and Kara forgot she was supposed to be difficult, even with the presence of the two guards inside the room with her. 

     

                “All done. How about a shower before we get you back to your cell?”

     

                “I want to see Lena.”

     

                Pausing for a moment, her mouth flattening, Eliza nodded. “Okay, well, that might take a couple of days to arrange. How about you shower in the meantime and get a good meal in you and I’ll see what I can do. How does that sound?”

     

                Nodding in agreement, Kara slid off the bed, Vasquez’s hand going to her gun before Alex nudged her with a shallow frown on her face. They followed Kara into the adjoining bathroom of the medical bay, where she’d been kept for the easy convenience of the ensuite, lessening the risk of her breaking free from any guards as she showered, locked behind two doors. 

     

                She’d never learned human self-consciousness and any discomfort at being watched had long since vanished after almost two decades without any semblance of privacy. Washing quickly, old blood and new sweat rinsed away, Kara changed into her new uniform and was greeted by a hot meal on a tray waiting for her in the medical bay. Perching on the edge of her bed, she ate the rice and beef and chocolate pudding, like a fidgety child as she smiled and laughed like the last two weeks hadn’t happened.

     

                When Alex escorted her back to her cell, Kara behaved herself, getting a proper night’s sleep for the first time in two weeks, instead of relying on her bouts of unconsciousness for rest. Everyone was in a better mood the next day and they were all allowed their usual walks and showers with no one posing any risks, and Kara patiently bided her time over the following few days until she grew restless with waiting.

     

                “So?” she asked Alex as her breakfast was dropped off, fidgeting as she leaned against the back wall, watching her oatmeal get set down with an orange and a piece of bread. 

     

                “What?”

     

                “What did Deputy Lane say when your mom spoke to her?”

     

                “Oh, well … she didn’t really change her mind.”

                

                Kara stiffened, her face crumpling. “What do you mean? Lena’s still being brought back here though, right?”

     

                An awkward look of uncertainty crossed Alex’s face as she stepped back out of the cell and put the forcefield back into place. Clearing her throat, her mouth thinned with regret.

     

                “No one said she was coming back here, Kara.”

     

                “Your mom promised-“

     

                “She promised to talk to the Deputy. That’s all. And she did.”

     

                “No,” Kara murmured, a tremor in her low voice as she pushed off the wall, brimming with pent-up disbelief as it tried to escape as anger. “No, you lied. You’re a liar.”

     

                Alex looked taken aback by the accusation. “No, I’m not. I never promised you anything. I would never give you false hope like that.”

     

                Loudly scoffing, Kara’s mouth twisted with contempt and her cheeks burned with embarrassment at how easily she’d been played. She thought if she behaved they’d change their minds, that she’d be able to convince them to bring Lena back to her cell, but Kara had made the grave mistake of thinking she was accountable for Lena’s actions. She wasn’t the one being punished, Lena was, and she could be as destructive and violent as she wanted to but they’d just punish her for it, they wouldn’t cave.

     

                As this realisation dawned on her, Kara let out a huff of laughter which turned into a broken sound of amusement and then slightly hysterical as her shoulders caved with disappointment and her fingers slid weakly down the forcefield. Laughing until tears were running down her cheeks, Kara suddenly fell silent and inhaled deeply.

     

                “Fuck you,” Kara snapped, wounded and angry. Kicking her tray of food, she sent oatmeal splattering in all directions as Alex roughly sighed with annoyance. “You’re just like the rest of them.”

     

                “Don’t say that,” Alex whispered, a pleading look on her face.

     

                Dashing the tears from her cheeks, Kara turned around and stalked back over to her bed, collapsing onto the cot as she hugged the thin pillow tightly and buried her face into it. Her shoulders shook as she cried, frustration and sadness coalescing in her chest, and Alex watched her with surprise etched on her face. Kara had never been good at inhibiting her emotions, feeling things fully and deeply, never afforded the opportunity to grow up properly and learn how to self-regulate, how to process things. The most she’d managed over the years was hours of learning to control her breaths so she didn’t dissolve into tantrums every time she’d become upset, and for the most part, Kara was a happy and placid person, but when her emotions threatened to overwhelm her, there was no stamping them down.

     

                She cried for hours, and when she finally stopped, her hitching breaths levelling out, she stared red-eyed at the wall with her cheek pressed against the wet patch her tears had made. Wearing herself out, she lay limp on the scratchy blankets, feeling wrung out and used, embarrassed by her naïvety. Oblivious to the sense of unease that permeated the cell block, anticipating another meltdown from her, Kara wallowed in her own self-pity and misery as she listened to Lena’s heartbeat, a few hallways over in their block’s solitary confinement cells. 

     

                Her tactic changed over the course of the day, her anger simmering to stubborn determination as Alex brought another tray of oatmeal and a janitor cleaned up her mess, the new congealing breakfast turning greyish and cold as Kara ignored its presence. It was whisked away and replaced with lunch, which also went uneaten, and then dinner that she likewise ignored. Hunger was gnawing at her stomach but if shouting wouldn’t work, Kara would suffer in silence.

     

                “Prisoner KZ64, eat your food,” Alex called to her, an hour after dinner time, grim and exasperated.

     

                Turning her head to face the wall, Kara scowled, closing her eyes and ignoring her. Alex let out a small laugh of disbelief, her tone affronted when she continued.

     

                “Silent treatment, really?”

     

                When Kara still didn’t reply, she sighed heavily, her boots scuffing the concrete floor as she hovered, hesitating before her voice softened.

     

                “Let me know if you get hungry. I’ll bring you a snack.”

     

                It was a peace offering, or rather an attempt to let Kara know that Alex cared, but Kara sulked in silence until her friend left her alone. It went on for another two days and Kara was lethargic and hungry as she dozed in the weakening light of the red sun lamp, resisting the offers of walks and showers and the chocolate puddings that Alex slipped her. She knew she was wearing the patience of the guards thin - even Alex, whose patience for her had always felt endless - and when her friend crouched beside her cot, so close that Kara felt an ache in her chest to know that Alex still trusted her to not harm her, Alex’s face was drawn tight with worry.

     

                “You need to eat before they put a tube down your throat.”

     

                Her fingers lightly brushed Kara’s hair and Kara swallowed thickly before slightly jerking her head away from her touch. Eyes closing, she inhaled deeply and then exhaled sharply, reaffirming her stubborn determination.

     

                “So be it. I won’t be complicit in doing that to you but it’s out of my hands and I won’t let you starve. I’m not sticking around to watch though.”

     

                She left, angry at Kara for her stubbornness, and a couple of hours later four guards arrived outside her cell. Maggie was the first one in, slow with caution, and Kara’s eyes snapped open, tracking her movements. 

     

                “Don’t make it difficult,” Maggie warned her.

     

                Kara’s lips twitched with a faint smile and she closed her eyes again, breathing slowly as she let her body become dead weight. She was denser and heavier than a human, no matter how much they depleted her of her strength, and that meant that between the four of them, they struggled to shift her limp body.
