                One of the guards, a relatively new one, jabbed his electrified baton into her side and Kara just blinked at him, a small laugh escaping her, until Maggie instructed the guard station to shock her collar. A jolt of kryptonite made Kara tense against the blinding pain, weakness flooding through her as she curled in on herself, eyes screwed shut and teeth grit. 

     

                Once she started thrashing, it took six of them to pin her until Maggie pulled out a sedative and stabbed it into the side of Kara’s neck with a sigh. Drawn into unconsciousness, Kara was oblivious to the process of them restraining her and the ensuing argument as Eliza had a fit, adamantly refusing to force-feed her with a tube until they got a doctor from a different quadrant to come and do it. 

     

                She woke up strapped to a bed with a tube disappearing up her nose and down her throat, feeding her nutrients. Mouth dry and body aching, Kara let out a small groan as her eyelids fluttered. Her mind was sluggish and it took her a minute to make sense of herself before she honed in on the sound of a heartbeat at her bedside. Glancing over, Kara’s mouth thinned as she took in the sight of Alex.

     

                “Why didn’t you just listen?” Alex asked, her voice low and brimming with frustration.

     

                Kara laughed awkwardly, her mouth feeling raw as her eyelids fluttered. She could feel the slender tube down her throat and it tickled as she swallowed. “You’re not being fair.”

     

                “There is no fair inside here. Look, I’ve helped her as much as I can, I need you to know that, but they’ve taken her from under my direct supervision because it’s on me that she knocked Winn out and escaped. I vouched for her to do some extra work, thinking that maybe after last time she’d be happy for a hot shower and a few benefits from good behaviour, and this is what she did so now my ass is in deep shit and she’s in isolation. This isn’t good for anyone.”

     

                “But only one person is getting punished for it.”

     

                “She shot a guard.”

     

                “You killed one.”

     

                Shooting to her feet, Alex looked shocked and affronted as she stammered, her cheeks reddening. “Next time I’ll just let them shoot her then, shall I? If this is the thanks I get for looking out for your stupid fucking crush then I’ll step back and let the Deputy have her way and make an example out of her.”

     

                “I didn’t mean-”

     

                “No, see, you’re fine hanging shit on everyone else except for her. But as soon as I say that’s fine, let her see the consequences of her own actions, suddenly you want my help. That’s not how this works, Kara. I’m not your fucking guard dog. I’m not at your beck and call to do you favours when you feel like it.”

     

                A choked sound escaped Kara as she flushed at Alex’s words, striking a little too close to home as she ground her teeth together and closed her eyes. Pretending that her friend wasn’t there, that she was alone in her cell, Kara tried to sleep but Alex was having none of it.

     

                “I’m not going to argue with you about her, okay? You know that I love you, you know that I trust you. This is just a small hiccup and we’ll get past it, you just need to keep your head down. The Warden caught wind of this from Lucy so the guards have been instructed to keep you here for the next week to make sure you’re eating. I’ll visit on my breaks but don’t give the guards any more grief, alright? For me. Eat your food and I’ll do what I can for Lena. I promise I’ll try my hardest to get her moved back.”

     

                The breath caught in Kara’s throat and she swallowed, feeling the gentle squeeze of Alex’s hand on her arm before she left. It was a lonely four days of being fed by the tube and visited by Alex when she could. She saw Eliza once, her anger palpable even as she maintained her usual gentle disposition and warmth with Kara, making sure she was healthy.

     

                She was the one to remove the tube after the fourth day, but they kept Kara in the room for another three days, away from the other inmates as they watched her eat from the blinking red camera in the corner. Kelly visited her on the fifth day, bringing coloured pencils and some paper as she perched on the edge of a chair and Kara sat cross-legged on the bed, unbound with the scraps of her lunch beside her.

     

                “I’m glad you’re eating again,” Kelly commented, as she watched Kara draw, the simple delight of her artistry in the soft lines of the alien’s face. “Do you want to tell me why you stopped?”

     

                “I’m protesting.”

     

                Kelly laughed, her brown eyes warm as she cocked her head to the side. “What’re you protesting?”

     

                “Injustice. I think it’s wrong for them to take Lena away. Wouldn’t anyone try and escape if they could?”

     

                “Do you think everyone would hurt people to do that?”

     

                “Yes.”

     

                “Would you?”

     

                Blinking, Kara’s mouth turned down at the corners. “I wouldn’t want to. I wouldn’t kill anyone but … if I could be free, maybe I would hurt them.”

     

                “Did you think about hurting any of the guards the other week, when you got out of your cell? I saw it on the cameras; you looked like you wanted to hurt Alex.”

     

                “I would never hurt Alex,” Kara firmly stated, her brow furrowing. “I don’t like hurting people.”

     

                “Just yourself?”

     

                Shrugging, Kara picked up a different pencil and hunched over her drawing. “I don’t like that either. But I know they’re frightened of me - the Warden, the Deputy, most of the guards - so maybe if I cause a fuss they’ll give me what I want. Don't you think so?”

     

                “They might. Maybe they’ll just punish you instead. You’ve spent more time in isolation and been dosed with kryptonite more times in the last month than you have in the last decade. Do you think it’s working?”

     

                “No.”

     

                “So … what next?”

     

                “I started eating again. Alex said she’ll speak to the Deputy and get Lena back.”

     

                “Did she? Hm.”

     

                Kara raised her head and fixed Kelly with a piercing stare. “She promised she’d try if I ate my food . ”

     

                “Oh, well … what happens if Deputy Lane says no?”

     

                A deep furrow formed between Kara’s eyebrows and she fiddled with the pencil until she accidentally snapped it in half. A small sound of disappointment escaped her and she sharpened the other half so she had two small pencils of the same colour. Once she was finished, she cleared her throat.

     

                “I heal a lot faster than everyone else so I can keep causing trouble until they listen.”

     

                “Do you think that will work?”

     

                Mouth thinning, Kara returned to her drawing. “I don’t know. We’ll find out.”

     

                “Let’s say Lena’s causing trouble as well; don’t you think they’ll continue to punish her, regardless of what you’re doing?”

     

                “Yes.”

     

                “How are you planning on getting around that then?”

     

                “Maybe I’ll ask nicely.”

     

                Kelly laughed, nodding. “You could always try. You know what I think? I think that the more trouble you cause, the less likely they’re going to put two troublemakers on one cell block. Good behaviour rewards itself, and bad behaviour punishes itself.”

     

                “Alex knows that I’ll stop causing trouble once she’s back.”

     

                “So it’s blackmail?”

     

                “Kind of,” Kara agreed with a huff of laughter. “I don’t think I’m very good at it though.”

                

                Lips twitching with a smile, Kelly nodded at the paper, “what’re you drawing this time?”

     

                Holding the drawing out, Kara smiled as the psychologist took it and studied it. “Another bird. You haven’t drawn this one for me before, have you?”

     

                “No. It’s a storm petrel; Lena’s favourite.”

     

                “Is that what you two talk about? Birds.”

     

                Shrugging, Kara’s expression softened with bewildered amusement. “Sometimes. I mean, it’s not the main topic of conversation, no, but we did talk about them.”

     

                “What do you talk about with her?”

     

                “Getting out of here. She teaches me Latin and French words I don’t know. She’s teaching me chess.”

     

                “Chess? How’s that working? You don’t have a board.”

     

                Tapping the middle of her forehead, Kara smiled impishly. “Up here. We … visualise. ”

     

                Looking mildly disbelieving, Kelly hummed and returned the drawing to Kara to finish off. “What does she say about getting out of here?”

     

                “That she’ll find a way. She’s trying to convince Alex to help her but Alex won’t bite. Even when Lena said she’d get you and Eliza out as well.”

     

                Eyebrows rising slightly in surprise, Kelly blinked. “She said that?”

     

                “Mhm. I guess she likes you.”

     

                “Right. Well … I have another patient soon so why don’t you finish your drawing quickly before I go.”

     

                Nodding, Kara focused on her drawing, quickly finishing it off and then holding it out to Kelly. She couldn’t keep any of her drawings and Kelly had taken to saving them since the first time she’d figured out letting Kara draw was a good way to get her to open up and sit still long enough for them to complete a session. There was a whole stack of them in a drawer in her office and Kelly folded the storm petrel in half and tucked it safely in her pocket before gathering up her notes from their hour-long session and accepting the box of pencils from Kara. She counted them all to make sure she hadn’t hidden one, trusting Kara but never quite knowing what any of the inmates would do if any of the staff slipped up. They were all there, including the blue one snapped in half and sharpened into two pencils.

     

                “I’ll see you at our next session,” Kelly said with a warm smile. “Think about what we talked about, okay?”

     

                “Sure, Kelly.”

     

                “And eat your food.”

     

                Rolling her eyes in an exaggerated manner of exasperation, Kara grinned and gave her a lazy two-finger salute before winking. Shaking her head as she tried to fight back a smile, Kelly knocked on the door and the guard turned to peek through the window before letting her out. Alone again, Kara thought about Lena and storm petrels and how she didn’t have to think much about Kelly’s words; Kara would continue to be a nuisance until they gave her what she wanted. 

     

                She eventually found herself back in her own cell after dinner that day and took up a new tactic of being irritating. Taking one of her shoes off, Kara spent about an hour tossing it at the wall, a dull thud filling the silent cell as it bounced off and clattered to the floor, and there were collective groans and complaints from her block mates as the long hours between dinner and bedtime were filled with the repetitive thuds. 

     

                After an hour, Alex strode into Kara’s cell and stole her shoe, gently whacking her with it and telling her to take the other one off. Folding her arms over her chest and stubbornly jutting her chin forward, Kara refused and a struggle ensued between the two women as Alex crouched and grabbed her foot and Kara tried to shake her off. Falling on her ass, Kara’s legs followed the momentum of the movement and she all but threw Alex across the cell, shoe in hand.

     

                Rubbing her elbow but victorious, Alex pointed one of the shoes at her in a warning. “Knock it off.”

     

                Next came the singing, old Kryptonian lullabies and war songs punctuated by muttered curses as she was given quick jolts of kryptonite to startle her into silence. When her voice grew dry and scratchy, Kara started kicking her pillow around and then got the idea to try and knock one of the panels out of her ceiling. It was way beyond her reach, even with an attempt to use the walls for a boost, which she’d tried many times over the years, and the dust and dirt had sealed the panels down too tightly for her thin pillow to dislodge a panel anyway.

     

                Still, her attempts weren’t appreciated by the guards and Alex arrived outside her cell, arms folded over her chest and a blank look on her face. After a few minutes of tense silence, staring at each other across the gap, Alex turned and stalked off, ordering Vasquez to move J’onn into Lena’s cell.

     

                Kara briskly crossed over to the forcefield, slapping her hand against it as her stomach lurched and disbelief devastated her expression. “Agent Danvers,” she hoarsely demanded.

     

                Eyes cutting across to her, Alex arched an eyebrow. “Prisoner KZ64.”

     

                “That cell’s taken.”

     

                “No, that cell’s been vacated. And now it has a new occupant.”

     

                Swallowing thickly as she let out a quiet gasp, the breath caught in her throat, Kara’s shoulders dropped. “You’re unbelievable.”

     

                An uneven smile crossed Alex’s face and she left the cell block without another word. Digging the heels of her palms into her eyes, Kara exhaled sharply and then watched as J’onn was removed from the cell across from hers. He’d occupied it for the last decade, more than half of his prison sentence, and just like that he was taken from his cell and made to move just to punish Kara - or punish Lena. One of them was definitely being punished here.

     

                “I’m sorry, Kara,” J’onn murmured, his serene voice low and weary.

     

                “I thought they’d bring her back,” Kara whispered.

     

                Sitting heavily on the edge of her cell, she mourned the loss of Lena’s company as it slipped away from her until she heard the faint conversation growing louder as the participants slipped further into earshot. 

     

                “If you reward bad behaviour, it just sets a precedent,” Lucy sighed.

     

                “It’s not really rewarding it,” Alex reasoned. “It’s … mitigating a risk. She’s strong, Deputy. Strong enough that I think she’ll eventually slip through our grasp and go straight to her herself, and it won’t be good for anyone.”

     

                “So, what you’re saying is that you can’t do your job and keep a prisoner imprisoned?”

     

                Alex made a quiet scathing sound that she managed to choke off. “No, I can do my job just fine, ma’am. I just think it’s … bad for morale - for the prisoners and guards - to let this carry on. If it progresses, I think we’ll end up with a riot on our hands and we know the cause of her sudden turn in behaviour, so it’ll be easy to put a stop to it.”

     

                “If one person is having such a negative effect, don’t you think it would be better to keep them apart?”

     

                “I thought so but … I imagine it gets lonely in there, ma’am. I can’t fault her for wanting her friend back. Not at all. Even if I wish we’d never put them in the same block before.”

     

                “You’ve become overfamiliar with Prisoner KZ64. There’s a line, Agent Danvers. Don’t cross it.”

     

                “I’m not. After what happened the other day … they’re both hazards to themselves and others when parted. And Doctor Danvers has taken the precautions you requested so I think we’ve already solved one problem. Now it’s just KZ64 to subdue. I’ve taken the liberty of moving JJ25 to LL93’s cell to put a stop to any further conspiring.”

     

                There was a pause and Lucy sighed heavily. “Don’t tell the Warden I’m going soft. She’s supposed to spend another two weeks in iso before her cast comes off.”

                

                “Doctor Olsen thinks five weeks is too much.”

     

                “Perhaps.” With a weary sound of resignation, Lucy’s footsteps started to retreat. “You owe me, Alex.”

     

                “Thank you,” Alex lightly called after her.

     

                “Stop making friends with the inmates,” Lucy warned her.

     

                It was over an hour later when Kara heard the sound of a familiar heartbeat making its way towards her cell. She’d tracked it as they’d taken Lena from her cell to another room, one of the further bathrooms Kara thought, and was brimming with nervous energy as she wondered what Alex was doing with her. 

     

                When her heartbeat was just outside the door to their cell block, Kara was practically pressed up against the forcefield as she eagerly watched what was unfolding. Alex had a firm grip on Lena’s arm as she came into sight, dark hair damp and tangled, pale face narrow and slack, a vacant look in her eyes as she limped along, one leg encased in a cast. 

     

                “Lena,” Kara breathlessly called out, pressing a hand against the forcefield as she watched them stop in front of J’onn’s old cell, directly across from her. 

     

                Vasquez brought down the forcefield and they filed Lena into the cell, setting her down on the cot, loose-limbed and compliant, before stepping back outside.

     

                “Her leg,” Kara hoarsely said to Alex, who turned and crossed over to her.

     

                “She fell.”

     

                “Oh. Is she alright? I- what did you do to her? She seems …”

     

                “It’s a slow-release sedative. So she won’t cause any more trouble.”

     

                Kara jerked back slightly, face furrowing as her hand slipped from the forcefield. Mouth thinning, Alex gave her a wan look of apology. “My mom tried to stop it. This is the best I can do. You can see her - you can see that she’s safe - and you can talk to her, if she feels like talking, but no more plotting. No more whispering and colluding.”

     

                Throat closing up with the pang of longing to hear Lena’s voice again, to wriggle beneath her cot on the cold floor and whisper together in the long hours of emptiness, Kara nodded. Her eyes were fixated on Lena, who lay limp on her cot in her new cell, drinking in the sight of her as if seeing her for the first time. They so rarely got to look at each other that it didn’t quite feel like a punishment to be denied her voice when she was gifted her face.

     

                “Thank you,” Kara whispered, her eyes filling with grateful tears. “Thank you, Alex.”

     

                Reaching up, Alex put her palm against the forcefield and Kara placed hers against it, dragging her tearful eyes from Lena to stare at her friend. A wavering smile lit up her face as she let out a small laugh. 

     

                “No more trouble now. Please.”

    Chapter 12

                A few weeks passed by in a blur, everything existing at an arm’s length haze of the sedative slowly working its way through her bloodstream. For the first week, Lena had barely been aware of her surroundings at all, sleeping long hours and led around in a lurching shuffle as she went through the motions of showering and eating, her mind lagging behind her body. That was the worst part, the disconnect between herself, her mind which was usually so sharp, thinking quickly, keeping her sane as she unravelled theories and fixated on languages and formulas and schematics. Now, it was like she’d been stuffed with cotton wool, compliant like a doll as she was puppetted about.

     

                Slowly, her body did adjust to the drugs, some of the haze receding until her mind was just fuzzy and slow. Lethargic but aware of her surroundings again, Lena came back to herself in increments, until the sight of Kara roused something in her, a flicker of a spark trying to light itself, taking root in her mind as something to latch onto. They couldn’t speak with the distance between them, short of the loud conversations had between the rest of the prisoners, but as she regained the energy to rise from the cot and sit in front of the forcefield, Lena spent hours staring at Kara’s face across the gap as her friend mirrored her pose and softly called out to her, asking if she was alright, if she could hear her, what had they done to her. Lena couldn’t respond, her tongue feeling clumsy in her mouth as she stumbled over mumbling responses.

     

                Even when she tried to stir herself up as a month passed by and she was almost back to herself, albeit a depressed version that lacked the motivation to do anything but merely exist, Lena just got irritated because she couldn’t make anything come out right. In the middle of the night, she lay there thinking about everything that had happened, all of her plans that were dead in the water now. If she didn’t get back on track somehow, she’d be dead, but there wasn’t a single strong emotion inside of her, not even for Kara.

     

                Until she woke one day and ate her breakfast and had her frigid shower and was returned to her cell again, Kara already showered and dressed, damp blonde hair curling at her hairline as she sat cross-legged on the floor. A hopeful smile broke her face and Lena’s lips twitched in the ghost of an answering smile.

     

                “Do you want to play chess?” Kara called out.

     

                Lena frowned in response, shrugging helplessly. She gruffly cleared her throat, which hadn’t had much use recently. “My mind is too slow, Kara. I don’t- I don’t know if I’ll keep it straight.”

     

                “Oh. Okay. Well … I could keep it straight for you.”

     

                Closing her eyes, Lena let out a small sigh and then nodded, a twitch of her lips all the smile she could manage. “Alright, I’ll be white though. Knight to C3.”

     

                “E7 to E5.”

     

                “Knight to D5.”

     

                Slowly fumbling her way through the opening as she tried to remember Kara’s moves, Lena felt exhausted and unable to find any enjoyment in the familiar game of mental chess she’d taken to playing with Kara, the two of them stretched out under their cots as they whispered their moves back and forth. It felt like a long time ago since then and Lena had been subdued, the ordeal of solitary confinement and the depot injected into her leaving her a shade of herself.

     

                It was almost a relief when Vasquez appeared in front of her and told her to back up against the far wall. Hauling herself to her feet, Lena walked to the back of her cell and allowed herself to be cuffed and led out, meeting Kara’s eyes briefly as her friend climbed to her feet, leaning against the forcefield with worry brimming in her eyes.

     

                Lena didn’t ask where she was going and she wasn’t offered an explanation, but a few minutes later she was outside a door that looked familiar, despite it being indistinguishable from the other doors in this area of the prison. She thought she remembered that scuff in the paint. Her thought was proven correct when Vasquez banged on the door and Kelly opened it a moment later, dressed warmly in a knitted sweater as she smiled warmly at Lena.

     

                “Lena! Come in, come in.”

     

                Uncuffed, rubbing at her wrists, Lena slowly walked inside and curled up on the chair, the air stuffy as a vent pumped out hot air. She’d been shivering in her cell and they didn’t abate as her body took a while to adjust to the warmth. Watching the psychologist closely as she grabbed Lena’s file and took a seat, Lena was silent and her face was impassive.

     

                “It’s been a while since our last session.”

     

                Nodding in response, Lena’s mouth thinned as if she was doubling down on her silence. Kelly was patient though, and had worked in the prison long enough to have dealt with more than one defiant prisoner.

     

                “Do you want to tell me how you’re feeling?”

     

                Shaking her head, Lena picked at the fraying seam of the clean uniform she’d donned that morning, the thin scrub pants coarse and doing little to keep her warm as the weather above made the sea deathly cold. It seeped in through the thick walls of the prison, damp and chill in the very foundations, and Lena wondered how much longer until winter was over. At the very least, she imagined it would be slightly less cold and they’d have to weather fewer storms in the warmer months, even if the dampness would persist.

     

                “That’s okay. How about we talk about what happened?”

     

                Met with a wall of silence again, Kelly sat forward with her elbows on her thighs and waited. After a minute, she started to write and that caught Lena’s attention enough to warrant her finding her voice, scratchy and faint.

     

                “What are you writing?”

     

                “Just making some general notes on your appearance. It’s important for Doctor Danvers to know if the medication you’ve been prescribed is impairing your ability to function as usual.”

     

                Snorting, Lena’s lips twisted and she let her eyes scan the room, avoiding the other woman’s gentle stare. “It’s obvious for the depot injection to impair the ability to function as usual. It’s the entire purpose of it, to be a slow-releasing agent.. The purpose of my sedative is to keep me limp like a puppet. No trouble.”

     

                “Is it working?”

     

                Eyes cutting to Kelly’s face, Lena’s expression was hard, her stare brittle and piercing. “All I do is sleep.”

     

                “How’s your cognitive functioning?”

     

                Running her tongue over her teeth, Lena was slow to reply. “Slow. I feel like I’m … existing outside of my body, two steps behind. I’m all there, at a distance, but … I can’t make my body cooperate, which I guess is their intention.”

     

                “I believe so, yes. Do you think perhaps it’s also partially psychosomatic?”

     

                “How so?”

     

                “Maybe your subconscious is relieved for the break, from your attempts to break out of here. By having an excuse in the sedative, perhaps your body has given up on the fight.”

     

                Stiffening, Lena gave her a hard look. “I don’t give up . It’s not how I was raised, it’s not in my nature. This is just a- a setback. My body will adjust, and … I’ll be able to- to feel motivated again, to have the ability to fight back. Resist.”

     

                Clicking her tongue, Kelly gave her a wry smile. “Well don’t tell me that; if I have any cause to think your medication isn’t working properly - whether because the dose is too strong or too weak - I’m obligated to tell Doctor Danvers.”

     

                “Doctor Danvers didn’t want to sedate me in the first place.”

     

                “Doctor Danvers is a good woman.”

     

                “Well I’m glad you have a good prison mother-in-law,” Lena said, her voice droll as she rolled her eyes.

     

                Kelly laughed lightly, “I don’t think we have an ordained minister in this place.”

     

                “No wedding dress and church bells in your future then? What a pity. Alex would make such a beautiful blushing bride.”

     

                “You have good reason to dislike her; I won’t defend her, no matter my own feelings. That’s private and separate from her work.”

     

                Brow furrowing as her mouth turned down at the corners, Lena replied somewhat reluctantly. “She’s not the worst here, no matter how much I dislike her. I’d help her too, for Kara’s sake, if she would be my inside contact to help. I already offered but she said no. Won’t have a bar of it. Maybe you’re smarter than her - you’re a trained psychologist at the very least. Surely you can see that it would be better to help me get us out of here than for us to die slow deaths. In Kara’s case, a very slow death.”

     

                “That’s a matter of opinion. Do you think you have no regard for your own life? I think most people would withstand imprisonment if it meant they were alive. That’s one of the base human instincts, to keep ourselves alive. Of course, mental illness can change that instinct entirely. How are you feeling after you attempt to overdose?”

     

                Lips twitching as a spark of amusement brightened Lena’s eyes, she ran her fingers through her hair. “How do you think I’m feeling?”

     

                “I don’t pretend to be telepathic. If you’re feeling depressed-”

     

                “Don’t pull that shit,” Lena snapped, bristling now as she pointed her finger at Kelly in warning, her anger slow to bloom as it rose through the fog of veiled feelings. “Don’t try and make this into me being mentally ill when the only thing wrong with me is I’m being held here unlawfully. I’m not suicidal, I’m not crazy, okay? I’m desperate. Maybe I don’t have a lot of regard for my own life but I’d rather be killed quickly than stay locked up in a cell with a sedative pumping through me for the next sixty years.”

     

                “I don’t think you’re crazy. I think being in isolation for weeks, being mistreated by some of the DEO agents here, putting a lot of stress on your body with injuries and illnesses and different drugs … that can have a severely negative impact on someone’s mental health.”

     

                “Obviously.”

     

                “Do you think being back on your cell block has helped improve that?”

     

                “You mean have I calmed down now that I can sit across from Kara and stare at her for fifteen hours a day? Yes, I’ve been sedated.”

     

                “Sedated but your personality or your intelligence hasn’t been dimmed, I see. That’s good.”

     

                Closing her eyes, Lena ran a hand over her face. “No, but … I can’t bring myself to do anything. I- I can barely speak to Kara anymore, I don’t like it. I don’t have the energy; it’s exhausting to be awake.”

     

                “Just because of the sedative?”

     

                Lena shrugged, a twist of her mouth and a haughty look on her face as she crossed her arms over her chest. “I’m bored. My mind, my hands … they were made for finding solutions and creating things. That’s why I’m in here. I can’t sit still; I can feel myself becoming more stupid with each day without something to hone my intelligence.”

     

                “That must be difficult for you.”

     

                Scoffing again, peeved by Kelly’s tone of patient understanding, Lena shook her head. “Difficult? Difficult is finding a way out of here. Being denied access to the one thing I was made to do is unbearable . Unbearable enough for me to try and find a way out of here.”

     

                “Why do you think it’s the one thing you were made to do?”

     

                “I’m the smartest person alive. It might sound cocky but it’s true. What else is someone as smart as I am supposed to do? Waste my potential? I was born with more money than I could ever want, every single resource at my fingertip and a business empire that I increased tenfold since I took over as CEO. I’m not made for a cell; I was meant to change the world. For the better .”

     

                “Is that still your intention, once you make it out of here?”

     

                “Yes. I want to help people. And that starts with myself and with Kara.”

     

                “It’s always good to prioritise oneself when everything else seems a little unmanageable,” Kelly approvingly replied. “Can I ask you a personal question though?”

     

                “Yes, but I might not answer it.”

     

                Laughing at Lena’s obstinate reply, Kelly nodded, smiling, and narrowed her eyes as she shrewdly appraised her. “What’s the nature of your relationship with Kara? I understand that relationships can progress rapidly in an isolated environment, and the intensity of them can be exacerbated as a result of that. You clearly believe that you have a special bond with her, I guess I’m just curious what the extent of that is.”

     

                “She’s my friend,” Lena replied, her voice brittle and flat. “What else could she be?  I know what you’re insinuating but … it’s not like that. It would be impossible anyway. We’re not allowed to touch, we’re not even allowed to speak now privately, we weren’t allowed to see each other before.”

     

                “Do you equate romantic relationships with sexual relationships?”

     

                “No, but they go hand-in-hand, don’t they? You want me to say that I’m in love with her, that I’ve got myself a prison girlfriend? It wouldn’t be true. I feel sorry for her. Sorrier for her than for myself.”

     

                “Ah, so it’s empathy that binds your friendship together?”

     

                “I feel less alone when we talk.”

     

                “Do you feel alone often? From our previous conversations, it sounds like you’ve always been someone who craves her own company.”

     

                “That was before this place. It’s different in here; I don’t have anything to distract me from the loneliness, and I don’t have to guess who’s going to hurt me. The answer is anyone outside of a cell.”

     

                “Do you believe I would hurt you?”

     

                “Not intentionally. Maybe you’d tell a guard or Doctor Danvers that I was going to do something to harm myself. I think they’d take measures against that and … it would hurt me.”

     

                “You understand that I’m obligated to report anything I perceive as a risk?”

     

                Lips twitching with a quick smile, Lena cocked her head to the side. “Like planning to break out of here?”

     

                “Yes.”

     

                “Have you reported that?”

     

                “No.”

     

                “Why not?”

     

                “Why do you think so?” Kelly coyly replied, turning it back on Lena.

     

                Considering it for a moment, Lena cupped her chin in her hand, her green eyes unwavering as she stared at Kelly. Neither of them broke off the eye contact first and Lena slowly exhaled as she straightened on her chair.

     

                “You don’t want to be stuck here either, and you know that I’m right. I can get us out of here. You’re not committed to helping me but you’re not going to hinder me either. Not until you’re sure what my plan is. If it would benefit you to jump on board.”

     

                Blinking, Kelly sat back and gazed down at Lena’s open file. “Your IQ is incredibly high - I believe you when you say you’re the smartest person on the planet. If you had the abilities of your fellow inmates, you’d be out of here already, there’s no doubt in my mind.”

     

                Giving her a droll smile, Lena arched an eyebrow. “I’m flattered by your confidence.”

     

                “But you don’t have powers.”

     

                “No, I don’t.”

     

                “That’s where Kara comes in, right?”

     

                Stilling, Lena was impassive for a moment before she nodded shallowly. “I’m not sure what her powers are, other than she’s powerful. The most dangerous one in here, right? Or is she bullshitting me? She doesn’t seem like the type to over-inflate her ego.”

     

                Clearing her throat as she masked a laugh, Kelly nodded. “No, that’s about right but … she hasn’t told you? What she can do? Where she’s from?”

     

                “No.”

     

                “Interesting.”

     

                “Why’s that interesting,” Lena abruptly asked, her green eyes narrowing slightly with suspicion. 

     

                She didn’t like not knowing things, feeling like she was on the outside of information. Cracking her knuckles in an anxious manner, Lena gave Kelly an expectant look as she waited for a response. Waving a hand in an airy manner, Kelly shrugged.

     

                “You’ve grown close and have a lot in common. I assumed you would have discussed it.”

     

                “We try not to talk about things that are too personal. It hurts too much.”

     

                “So she doesn’t know why you’re in here?”

     

                “Vaguely,” Lena shrugged.

     

                “Okay. Well … I think that’s just about time. Unless there’s anything else you think I should know? Anything you’d like to discuss? Have you given much thought to your escape plan recently?”

     

                “No. My mind’s been a bit … uncooperative. I still have the plan, of course, but I guess I just haven’t gotten anywhere else.”

     

                Nodding, Kelly scrawled down a few notes in Lena’s file and then gave her a quick smile. “Think about it over the next few weeks. I’d be interested to know what you’ve planned so far at our next session.”

     

                Snorting at the idea of divulging her plan to her therapist, who she didn’t trust at all, despite Kelly’s insistence that it was confidential unless the prison needed to know, Lena nodded and climbed to her feet. Kelly beat her to the door, knocking before she opened it, and Lena was cuffed again and taken back to her cell.

     

                Kara was anxiously pacing as she waited for her return and her expression brightened as relief cut through the tense set of her shoulders. Some of the knotted feelings in Lena’s chest eased as well and she smiled slightly as she was put back in her cell, sitting cross-legged at the forcefield as she gave Kara a thumbs up.

     

                In the weeks that followed, Lena was brooding and quiet, refusing to have loud, public conversations across the cell block like the rest of her inmates did as they played their usual games and swapped gossip. They’d tried on numerous occasions to coax Lena back into it, usually Kara trying the most, but she felt even less like socialising than usual. 

     

                Instead, Lena had uncovered the knowledge that J’onn knew sign language and he became a quiet translator for Kara, their sensitive hearing allowing the both of them to converse in whispers as Lena signed things rapidly and Kara slowly picked up the language. Within a few days, Kara knew enough rudimentary signs to string clumsy sentences together for them to talk without the aid of J’onn translating what some of the signs meant. Kara rapidly gained fluency with a speed that impressed even Lena. 

     

                Being able to communicate with her again in a somewhat private manner sparked something in Lena, a flicker of her old determination solidifying. It might have just been her body adjusting to her sedative, evening out until it didn’t incapacitate her anymore but just left her mildly numbed against her motivation to act on any thoughts. Still, it wasn’t quite as lonely to sit there and sign back and forth, even though she missed the sound of Kara’s voice. To see her was its own reward, drinking in the blue eyes, the wild long blonde hair, the way her cheeks dimpled when she smiled, or her eyes crinkled at the corners and her nose wrinkled at the bridge as her face furrowed with bewildered amusement. Her happiness in spite of the soul-sucking despair of the prison was still surprising to Lena, who couldn’t fathom staying so positive after almost two decades cooped up inside.

     

                By the time the next social event rolled around, Lena was nervous for some unfounded reason, as if being so long apart from Kara had made their relationship regress and she no longer knew where they stood. She wasn’t used to feeling so uncertain and when she was led into the communal area with Andrea and Psi, deemed the least dangerous of the cell block, Lena immediately claimed their usual table and kept to herself as the other woman settled in and were soon joined by their other friends from the cell block.

     

                They cast glances at Lena as if waiting for her to try and join them and when Mon-El was brought in, his glances were less than friendly. Lena ignored them all, quiet as her knee bounced and her teeth worried at the quicks of her nails. Her eyes stayed glued to the door for Kara’s arrival. 

     

                As usual, she was brought in last and Lena’s stomach dropped at the sight of her wrapped up in the straitjacket they were prone to leading her around in for everyone else’s safety. Alex freed Kara from it as soon as she was locked inside the room and Kara stretched her arms out, flexing her fingers, as she grinned at Lena, giving her a quick wink as she crossed the room to sink down onto the seat across from her.

     

                “It’s good to see you,” Kara murmured, a smile creasing her face as some of her worry was banished at the sight of Lena, conscious and cognizant. 

     

                Lena swallowed thickly, a faint smile playing at the corners of her mouth. “All I do is see you now. I miss hearing you.”

     

                Kara laughed, her nose wrinkling, and she put her hands in the middle of their table, stretching her index finger out to tentatively touch the back of Lena’s fingers. “We have rotten luck, huh? We’re only ever allowed half of each other, except for the one day a month we’re fortunate enough to be in here. If we’re allowed in here.”

     

                Her eyes travelled around the room and Lena’s stayed glued to Kara’s face, drinking in the sight of her, the sound of her voice as she talked. She seemed fine , she looked as if they’d never so much as touched her, as if she’d been the exact opposite of a problem while Lena was gone. Up close, Lena could see the dark circles that the distance between their cells hid from her, the ghastly red lights masking Kara’s complexion and turning her expressions into something darker. She’d forgotten the precise shade of blue of her eyes.

     

                Turning her hands on the table, palm up, Lena slid her fingers beneath Kara’s and ran her thumb over the knuckles. Their eyes met again and a sweet smile curled Kara’s lips as her expression softened slightly. 

     

                “Are you okay?” Lena asked.

     

                “Better now,” Kara whispered, a shy look on her face as her cheeks turned rosy. “I missed you while you were gone.”

     

                A surprised huff of laughter escaped Lena as her lips twitched ruefully. “I missed you too. I’m sorry for what they did to you because of me. I should never have asked you to cause a distraction.”

     

                “I wanted to, and it wasn’t that bad. I- well, I brought most of it on myself. My track record of good behaviour is pretty much gone now. They were all sick of me, and maybe a little bit scared - even Alex.”

     

                Lena hummed thoughtfully, “ah, is that why they brought me back then? They thought you were going to break out of here if you didn’t get your own way? Or are you the darling of the prison and can get whatever you want inside?”

     

                “If I could get what I want, I’d have a cell with two cots and have you with me all the time,” Kara quickly replied, looking a little embarrassed as she finished, as if she’d said too much.

     

                Another laugh escaped Lena, coming surprisingly freely after long weeks of a sense of indifference that had blanketed her, her conversations with Kara via J’onn barely able to keep the despair away. Giving Kara’s fingers a quick squeeze of reassurance, Lena drew her hands back.

     

                “Shall we play?”

     

                Eagerly nodding, Kara rose slowly from her seat, moving off to fetch the chess set, a few pencils and a sheet of paper to create more pieces. Bringing it back to the table, they went through the dwindling plastic chess set and the few paper ones they’d made before and replaced the lost pieces with their hastily drawn figures and torn pieces of paper. 

     

                Lena beat Kara twice as they talked, quietly explaining everything that had happened while they’d been apart. It was the most awake Lena had felt in weeks, her expression not quite so slack or stiff as she relaxed into the familiarity of conversation with Kara, not realising how much she had missed the simple privilege of speaking to her every day until it had been ripped away from her.

     

                Kara was slowly getting better at chess as well, maybe not understanding the mechanics of different openings and plays well yet but memorising them so she didn’t make the same mistake next time. Under different circumstances, Lena would have liked to sit and play chess with her, somewhere warm and surrounded by trees, far from water, with birds and gourmet food and expensive liquor. It felt as impossible to her as it had once felt to imagine winding up in prison for an experiment and Lena felt wistful for the imagined freedom with Kara for company. She’d always been alone, predominantly spending time with herself, but now Lena didn’t imagine she’d ever want to be alone again.

     

                They were tucked away in their quiet corner while the other prisoners entertained themselves, episodes of Jeopardy on the boxy TV, Imra and Andrea conversing with Nia at a different table, Querl reading the smattering of books for the umpteenth time. The guards watched closely and Lena spotted Alex’s disapproving expression more than once behind Kara’s shoulder as she tried to ignore the Agent and her grudge. An hour passed by quickly and Lena had forgotten how nice it could be to sit and do something so ordinary while talking face-to-face with a friend, about things other than the prison, about the beatings and escaping. 

     

                They did talk about escaping though, of course, Lena filling Kara in on all the things she’d seen while she’d been up in the ceiling or skulking through adjoining rooms. Kara whispered information she’d gathered over the years, things of note that she hadn’t mentioned before, things she’d eavesdropped on through walls and doors, routines and shift changes and how many people came with a shipment each month and how many left - if any. 

     

                Eventually, they were told to wrap it up, their social coming to an end, no matter how badly they wished it would drag on for hours longer. Grimly packing away their shoddy chess set in the battered cardboard box, Lena wanted to linger longer as she watched Kara obediently don the straitjacket and let Alex tighten the straps to bind her into it. It left a sour taste in Lena’s mouth and her eyes darkened as she climbed to her feet, a handful of pencils clutched in her hand as her lips twisted derisively.

     

                “I’ll see you back in there,” Kara murmured, her voice warm and light, harbouring no resentment as she was bound like a mad woman.

     

                “See you,” Lena agreed, nodding as she gave her a fleeting smile.

     

                Alex gave Kara’s back a quick pat to urge her into motion and Lena turned towards the shelves they’d taken the chess set from, crossing the room to return it. Crouching down to stow it away, Lena straightened, dusting off her hands, and turned. She blinked, pulled up short by the presence of Mon-El standing uncomfortably close to her. Moving to side-step him, Lena suddenly found his hand around her throat and her feet inches off the worn linoleum flooring. 

     

                Making a choked sound of panic, she scratched at his hand and was slammed against the wall, to the left of the low bookshelf, a moment later. Black spots danced across her vision as a dull pain throbbed at the back of her skull, and Lena couldn’t formulate a word as her ears started to ring, his angry words seeming distant. 

     

                “You cost me two socials, you dumb bitch.”

     

                Lena’s face was quickly turning pink, inching towards red, and it had all happened so fast that she hadn’t even had time to process it. But then a moment later, a figure in grey was shouldering Mon-El aside, and Lena slumped to the floor, coughing as her hand fluttered at her viciously red throat.

     

                Kara was wrapped up in her straitjacket, but that hadn’t stopped her from moving across the room with elegant speed, her face like thunder as she turned her torso and drove her shoulder into Mon-El’s side. He staggered off balance, losing his tight grip on Lena’s throat, and whirled around, eyes going wide. Drawing herself back, Kara whipped her head forward and slammed her forehead into Mon-El’s nose with a sickening crunch and a spray of hot blood.

     

                Swearing, he cupped a hand over his nose, doubled over, and then straightened up, swinging and punching Kara squarely across the face. She didn’t have her hands to help balance her and was sent staggering right, lurching around as she tried to stay on her feet, careening into a table and cracking the top in half. Shouts and activity were filling the room, the crackle of radios and exasperated prisoners and Lena watched with wide eyes as she willed Kara to stop.

     

                Managing to straighten up, Kara ignored the smarting pain on the left side of her face and hooked her foot around Mon-El’s, pulling him off balance and then pressing her foot into his stomach, holding him firmly in place. Her chest was rising and falling quickly, her pale, thin face flushed with anger now as she stood over him, stronger and faster even with the precautions they took. For the first time, Lena understood just how dangerous Kara could be if she wasn’t so closely guarded inside a cell, how alien she really was beneath the seraphic sweetness of her golden looks.

     

                “You think you’re tough, laying hands on her like that, huh?” Kara seethed as she leaned over him, her foot pressing down firmly. “You spineless Daxamite scum. Touch her again and see what happens.”

     

                Kara went rigid then, head thrown back, tendons taut in her neck. She managed to fight it for a second before her knees buckled and she dropped hard to the floor, sagging into a heap. Lena scrambled forward, a hoarse cry falling from her lips as she gathered Kara up in her arms, patting her cheek as she tried to rouse her, fearing the worst.

     

                “You’re not so tough once they pump you full of that green shit, are you, you spoiled Kryptonian cunt,” Mon-El smugly replied as he climbed to his feet, giving her a contemptuous look. He spat on the floor in front of the two women before Alex was there, strong-arming him into submission to cuff him against the wall.

     

                More guards poured in then, and the other prisoners all lined up against the wall with their hands above their heads, staying out of the scuffle. Lena was hauled off Kara without any fight, her strength fleeing her even as she ached to make sure her friend was alright, her mind struggling to process Mon-El’s words as everything else paled in comparison to the limp form on the floor, veins of green mottling her ashen skin.

     

                Cuffed and light-headed, blinking slowly as her raw throat ached with the ghost of Mon-El’s fingers squeezing tight, Lena sank down to her haunches as she watched three guards escort Kara out of the room - two carrying her on a stretcher and a third with his gun trained on her - before Mike was hauled out by two more and a pair of polished black boots came into Lena’s line of sight. Craning her neck back, making her throat flare with pain, Lena blinked up at Alex.

     

                “Why is it always you?” the guard wearily asked.

     

                Letting out a broken laugh, Lena closed her eyes and swallowed thickly, the pain making her wince. Hauling her to her feet, Alex kept a loose grip on her arm as she towed Lena through the warren of corridors, leaving the rest of the guards to take the remaining prisoners back to their cells. Lena had anticipated her own cell to greet her and was surprised when she was deposited in a medical bay, the sterile room quiet and bright white as she sat on the edge of the padded bed and waited for the inevitable arrival of Eliza.

     

                It was forty minutes before the door opened and admitted the stressed-looking doctor, the lines of her face a little more prominent as she moved to the counters and snapped on a pair of latex gloves. Letting out a soft sigh as she stopped in front of Lena, Eliza reached out to gently cup her chin.

     

                “You can’t catch a break, can you?” Eliza pityingly greeted her.

     

                Eyes smarting with tears, Lena scowled as she swallowed, her throat painfully tight and tender. She was slightly breathless as she raised her chin a fraction, letting Eliza get a good look at her throat, which was already mottling with fresh blue and lavender bruises.

     

                “Oh, that man,” Eliza softly clicked her tongue as she probed the bruises. 

     

                “Don’t worry, Kara got him good,” Alex commented from her position in the corner, arms folded over her chest.

     

                “Mm, so she said. Looks like he got her back almost as well.”

     

                “She’s awake?” Lena croaked.

     

                “Don’t talk,” Eliza ordered her.

     

                Mouth thinning as she fell silent, Lena let the doctor continue her examination, trying not to wince as her fingers gently pressed on the spots where the alien’s fingers had dug in hard. Reassured that he hadn’t broken anything, Eliza checked Lena’s eyes for any burst blood vessels and listened to her heart and lungs before giving her some painkillers and apologetically letting her know there wasn’t much else she could do. Lena hadn’t expected much, hadn’t even expected the painkillers, and she curtly nodded as she numbly listened to her speak.

     

                It was perhaps one of the few times she was grateful for the slow-release sedative she’d been given, her mind sluggish and her body limp, knowing that sleep awaited her as soon as she was back in her cell. It felt like all she did was sleep lately, unable to find the motivation to do much else, her only source of comfort in the prison torn away from her and set opposite her to taunt her by sight alone.

     

                “Can I see her?” she eventually asked, her voice rough and trembling.

     

                Hesitating, Alex glanced at her mother, who was peeling off her gloves and let out a resigned huff. “I shouldn’t but … just for a moment.”

     

                Nodding, her stomach knotted with worry, Lena felt a rush of gratitude for the agent and slipped off the bed. She murmured her thanks to Eliza and trailed Alex out of the room. Alex stopped at a door guarded by Vasquez and another agent and she dismissed them and unlocked the door from the skeleton key at her waist, ushering Lena inside as she glanced around for any witnesses.

     

                Kara was stretched out on the bed, a red lamp suspended over her and restraints strapping her down. Although she couldn’t even raise her head from the table, Lena knew that Kara was aware of their presence. 

     

                “Are you alright?” Kara asked, her voice strained and uneven.

     

                Lena almost tripped over her own feet in her haste to reach her bedside, hands cuffed before her as she curled her fingers into fists, keeping her hands to herself. A lump closed her throat and her vision blurred, obscuring Kara’s face from view as tears filled her eyes. Letting out a pitiful sound, the breath gusted out of Lena, almost a sob.

     

                When she blinked, tears rolled down both cheeks and restored her vision. Kara was staring up at her, a furrow between her brows and the left side of her face mottled with a fresh bruise, her eye half-swollen closed.

     

                “Are you?” Lena choked out.

                

                Giving her a thin smile, eyelids shuttering, Kara let out a quick laugh. “I’m fine. It’s not the rowdiest social I’ve ever been to.”

     

                A shuddering laugh of surprise escaped Lena and she sniffed, unable to resist the urge to reach out and stroke Kara’s hair. Their eyes met and Lena let her fingers linger in her blonde hair, her chest aching.

     

                “You shouldn’t have done that.”

     

                “He shouldn’t have done that,” Kara corrected.

     

                “Kryptonite,” Lena stressed, her face clouding with unease. “That’s what it is, isn’t it? The special tranquiliser in your collar. Kryptonite. You’re from Krypton.”

     

                Kara blinked up at her, surprise blooming in her blue eyes as her lips parted and a shaky laugh of surprise escaped her. “How do you know about Kryptonite?”

     

                “I- it’s the reason I’m in here,” Lena said with a broken laugh of her own. “I managed to-”

     

                “That’s enough,” Alex softly interrupted her.

     

                Ignoring her, shoulders tense and eyes bright with reignited anger, Lena’s lips twitched bitterly. “I managed to manufacture it to affect humans.”

     

                “Enough,”  Alex snapped, crossing the distance as Lena spoke to grab her arm, giving her a quick shake. 

     

                “Alex,” Kara softly pleaded. “What does it matter now? We’re already in here.”

     

                “I don’t want her filling your head with ideas.”

     

                Lena quietly scoffed, a wry smile twisting her lips. “I can’t manufacture it inside here, don’t worry. I don’t have the resources.”

     

                “Make it quick,” Alex said, her voice a low warning as she let go of Lena’s arm.

     

                Looking back down at Kara, Lena’s smile wavered slightly. “You never told me where you were from.”

     

                “I didn’t think you’d have a clue about Krypton. No one knows about it really. It’s only me and my cousin that made it off - or maybe not. Maybe there were more who came here after me; maybe the whole prison is full of my kind.”

     

                “No,” Lena sadly whispered. “No, it’s just you. And your cousin. My brother … he was smart. Had all the information he bought from the government and the black market. Kryptonian tech, databases, Kryptonite. I researched it after he was killed. I didn’t … I didn’t think that you still existed. Your kind.”

     

                “I’m the last of us,” Kara said, her blue eyes bright with a film of tears, mouth twisting bitterly. “I’m all that remains of a people that were so intelligent, so advanced, and look at me. Strapped to a bed in an underwater prison. I think it would’ve been kinder if my mom and dad had let me die along with them.”

     

                “Don’t say that.”

     

                “It’s true.”

     

                “Do you remember much?”

     

                “We’re an eidetic people; I remember all of it. I remember the planet, so … barren. The jets, the towers, the Genesis chamber I was born in. I remember how it felt to be free. I remember my parents - my father used to tell me stories before bed and my mother took me travelling with her. Our culture heavily relied on arranged marriages between the noble houses but they loved each other. They had an ordinary life, full of ordinary things. They had me . I loved science, I was going to be just like my dad, inventing things. And then I wound up here and all I can do is remember. This is not the life they sent me here to have.”

     

                The tears welled up and spilt over, running down Kara’s temples, and Lena reached out to wipe them away on the right side of her face. Swallowing thickly, her eyes closing for a brief moment as her throat tightened painfully, Lena let out a forceful breath.

     

                “Look at me. I’m going to get you out of here, alright? And you and I … we’re going to go somewhere we can be alone together. Safe. With birds and ice cream. I’m going to give you the life they wanted for you.”

     

                Her hand cupped Kara’s cheek and as fresh tears slid down her friend’s face, they were warm against her palm. Turning her head the slightest bit beneath the strap across her forehead, Kara’s lips brushed against Lena’s palm in the faintest semblance of a kiss and Lena felt her own eyes smart, a shakiness in her chest as the pit of grief and sadness and anger opened up, threatening to drag her back into it.

     

                “Alright, wrap it up,” Alex interrupted, shifting uncomfortably as she tucked her thumbs into her belt.

     

                Letting out a pent-up breath, Lena sniffed, stroking Kara’s cheek before hesitating and ducking down to press a kiss to her cheek. She was straightening up again before Alex could scold her for the forbidden contact, backing away from the bed with her eyes glued to Kara’s face until the agent gently took her arm and guided her to the door. 

     

                “You need to stop saying things like that to her.”

     

                “Like what?” Lena roughly asked, raising her bound arms to dash the tears from her face with the sleeve of the pilled sweatshirt.

     

                “Making all these promises. Do you see how you’re not good for her? She’s hurt again, defending you. I know it’s not your fault that dick attacked you but she … I don’t know, she has this thing about you. She’s always been a kind soul, always been the one to try and stop a fight before the guards had to step in with the collars and batons, you know? She’s never attacked someone though but for you she did. I don’t think it’s fair; you’re using her as a means to an end but she’s built up this attachment to you, like a lovesick puppy. You’re going to break her heart once you get what you want.”

     

                Coming to a stop in the hallway, Lena turned to face Alex, her face furrowing with bewildered annoyance. “And how do you know that? How do you know what I feel, what I think about her? You don’t know shit . Not about me, not about me and her, not about what I’ll do when I’m out of here. You think I’m using her? You think I’d be trying to find a way to take her with me if I was planning on double-crossing her at the last second?”

     

                Her voice grew louder, angrier, her sharp words somewhat diminished by the rasp of being strangled. Face taut and a muscle jumping in her jaw, Lena shook her head, lip curling slightly with contempt.

     

                “Think what you want, I don’t care, I’ll prove you wrong in the end. You’re not the only person who cares about her, you know.”

     

                “Why do you care about her so much?” Alex asked, a slight defensive edge to her voice that made Lena think she was being interrogated.

     

                Shrugging as she shuffled along again, mouth turning down at the corners with grim resolution, Lena sighed. “I guess … I just know what it’s like to be mistreated as well. And she’s the first friend I’ve ever had. I won’t leave her behind.”

     

                “You’re still convinced you’re going to get out of here? Your arrogance is astounding; the Deputy has you on a slow-release sedative that’ll make sure you never get an ounce of motivation to cause trouble again and you’re under constant surveillance. You had your chance and you blew it with that broken leg.”

     

                Lena let out a soft laugh, trying not to agitate her bruised throat. “I don’t care if it takes me a year or a decade; I’ll find a way out.”

     

                “We both know you wouldn’t last a decade in here. You’re not built like Kara.”

     

                “I don’t think Kara is built like Kara either,” Lena sniffed derisively. “It’s inhumane.”

     

                “There are prisons all around the world doing the exact same to other humans. You have it a lot better than some of them. We could have you all packed in a cell, one per square foot, with no room to lay down and sleep. No clean drinking water, no showers, no daily walks. Is it humane to do it to them as well? No, but what goes on here is no worse than other people have it, and those are prisons that are known around the world. You think a black site prison for the world’s most dangerous aliens and metahumans gives more of a shit for you than they do about their own kind?”

     

                “Of course not but that doesn’t make it right anywhere else. No sunlight, no fresh air … how she’s managed to stay sane for so long, I don’t know. Probably thanks to you. Probably thanks to the resilience of kids. Maybe because she wasn’t a spoiled billionaire reduced to slops and public showers.”

     

                Alex snorted, her eyes sliding sideways to Lena as she refrained from replying for a second before relenting. “She was the only daughter of one of the high houses. House of El. That’s where her prisoner name comes from - KZ64. Kara Zor-El - they were a patronymic naming culture - and the year she was born. She was kept in stasis while travelling here though so she didn’t age at all. Based on the tests they did on her when she arrived … well, she’s not going to look old anytime soon either.”

     

                “She said she’s practically immortal.”

     

                “Seems like it.”

     

                “Are you really okay with her spending forever locked up in here? For no crime except existing. You want to think I deserve to be here because I created something that’s a global threat, fine, but can you look me in the eye and tell me you think she deserves a life sentence for existing? Even if it’s a century, a small amount of time in her life, do you think that’s fair?”

     

                “No, it’s not fucking fair. It’s not fair for me to have spent as long as I have here either, all because of my dad. It’s not fair to my mom or Kelly, it’s not fair to J’onn . Yes, granted, there are some people in here who do deserve it for what they’ve done but I know some people are in here purely because they exist. It’s shit but … that’s the way it is. It’s the way it’s been for me too, since I was sixteen. You forget that I’ve been here longer than most prisoners.”

     

                “Help me,” Lena asked, her lips barely moving as she tried to sound like she wasn’t as desperate as she felt. “I’m not going to pretend it’s for a selfless reason, purely to save her or the rest of you, but I will. I’m not leaving her here. When I go, she comes with me.”

     

                “You’re not going to get out.”

     

                Wearily sighing, Lena smiled thinly. “Humour me. Say that I can , it would be a hell of a lot easier with someone on the inside helping me out. Once we’re out of here, I could give you everything you’ve ever wanted. I’ll expose this place and have my lawyers take this as high as I can, right up to the Supreme Court. My assets will be unfrozen, I’ll have that puppet in the White House impeached, I’ll do whatever I can to make sure the whole fucking world knows and no one ever gets sent here again.”

     

                “You either have a lot of nerve or you actually need psychiatric care. You think you’re going to get out of here and take down the President? The man who put you in here?”

     

                “I have money, I have power and a public platform. I can get whatever I want.”

     

                “Except for a ticket out of here.”

     

                “Except that,” Lena reluctantly agreed. “Just name your price.”

     

                Alex laughed, shaking her head. “You just don’t get it, do you? I can’t be bought. I’m not corruptible.”

     

                “This place is already corrupt; to corrupt you would mean you’d be doing something morally good.”

     

                Shrugging as she considered it, Alex hummed dubiously. “Maybe. I don’t care about money though, you can offer me a billion dollars and it means jack shit to me in here. All I care about is my family’s safety.”

     

                “I’ve told you, I’ll get you all out. Your mom, your girlfriend. Hell, I’ll even let you bring your ex if you really want to.”

     

                “Funny,” Alex flatly replied, falling silent for a moment. “What would you need me to do?”

     

                “I’m not going to tell you that, am I? You’ll do everything in your power to stop me.”

     

                “What if I wouldn’t?”

     

                “I don’t trust you.”

     

                “Then how am I supposed to trust you? Trust your stupid plan to get us out of here. I need to know what you need me to do.”

     

                Lena deliberated and her eyes cut sideways to Alex. “Give me your word. If you’re in, you’re in, otherwise, go and fuck yourself.”

     

                They walked the rest of the way back to her cell block and Lena glared at Mon-El’s cell, finding it still empty, and was led to her one on the right at the very end. Bringing down the forcefield and leading her inside, Alex uncuffed her, taking her sweet time as they stood close together.

     

                “I’m in,” she murmured.

     

                Stomach lurching with surprise, Lena’s eyes sharply darted up to Alex’s face, reading the stiffness on her face as fear. Their eyes met for a brief moment and the corners of the guard’s mouth tightened. Nodding slightly, Lena rubbed her wrists and backed away a step until Alex’s hand reached out to grab a fistful of her sweatshirt, pulling her in close until they were almost nose to nose.

     

                “You’re bringing the four of us with you and if you even think about double-crossing me, you even consider betraying any of us to save yourself, I’ll take you down with me and fill you with enough bullets to make sure you won’t be walking out of here anytime soon - if at all. Understood?”

     

                “Yes, ma’am.”

    Chapter 13

                “So, what’s the plan?” Alex muttered as she led Lena down a hallway, loosely holding her arm as she stood close behind her.

     

                “There isn’t one.”

     

                “Bullshit.”

     

                “It’s a work in progress,” Lena wryly replied, her lips twitching with a smile.

     

                “I’m not risking my neck for a work in progress.”

     

                Scoffing, Lena put one foot in front of the other and let the guard steer her towards the shower room with the other two metahumans she’d been deemed docile enough to return to her routine with. Vasquez led the line of prisoners and Lena and Alex lagged behind a little, not enough to be suspicious but enough to afford them a brief moment to talk.

     

                “You won’t be risking anything at all,” Lena replied, disgruntled and a little bitter. “All you have to do is fill in the gaps of my knowledge. Until it’s time.”

     

                “Which will be when?”

     

                There was an irritable agitation to Alex’s demeanour that morning, as if she was already spooked by the thought of helping a prisoner escape, even if it was for her own freedom as well. She was someone who’d spent almost her entire life following orders from within the prison and Lena would have pitied her if she didn’t dislike her so much. As it was, she was only offering to bring her along for Kara’s sake. She had to admit that having someone on the inside help did also benefit her too.

     

                “That depends on how long it takes you to get me everything I need.”

     

                “Starting where?” Alex impatiently asked.

     

                “A layout of the prison. I’ve already covered a fair bit of it myself but most of that was from up in the ceiling so it’s harder to visualise it. I need to know where each airlock is, vent access points, cameras, guard rooms, numbers on the manpower here. The most efficient route to the loading dock. Any potential places that will bottle-neck us. The plan will be to try and draw as little attention to ourselves as possible while still having the speed to get onto the delivery chopper before it’s finished unloading.”

     

                Nodding gravely, Alex’s brown eyes were serious as she stared at the back of Lena’s head. “On it.”

     

                Doubt flickered in Lena’s chest but she didn’t voice her distrust of the agent, knowing she had to make do with the resources available to her. If Eliza and Kelly were remaining on the sidelines, the more bearable of the three options she had, Lena would have to resort to the prickly woman who didn’t trust her either. It made it a lot easier to know where they stood with each other, to know they didn’t have to pretend, and Lena knew to be cautious with what she divulged in case Alex got cold feet.

     

                They arrived at the bathroom a minute later and Lena was quiet and obedient as she shivered beneath the cold water, her skin stinging from the frigid pressure as she used the twisted lump of soap with cold hatred nursed in her chest. Drying off with the ratty towel provided, she dressed in the uniform provided and let Alex cuff her again.

     

                Once the three of them were appropriately restrained, Alex led the way back out of the bathroom and they retraced the path back to their cell block until Alex came to a stop. Lena halted behind her, glancing around her to take in a large puddle of water spreading out from beneath a closed door, the reflection of the harsh fluorescents overhead wavering as the puddle expanded.

     

                “Oh, for fuck’s sake,” Alex sighed.

     

                “What’s wrong?” Vasquez called from the rear.

     

                “We’ve got a leak.”

     

                “Shall I call Schott to check it out?”

     

                Alex turned and her eyes landed on Lena’s impassive face before she looked at Vasquez across the gap separated by prisoners. Lena knew that this was a result of her tampering with the prison, was sure of it, and it took everything in her to not look too smug. Considering the question for a moment, Alex looked at Lena again, her eyes narrowed slightly before she shook her head.

     

                “No. Take AR91 and GM90 back to their cells. LL93 can make herself useful and clean it up.”

     

                Hesitating, Vasquez nodded and prodded Andrea in the back. “You heard her ladies. Keep it moving.”

     

                Lena stepped aside, loitering near the wall as the trio filed off. Watching them go for a moment, Lena looked at Alex and raised her eyebrows expectedly. The guard moved towards the door, unlocked it and yanked it open, hissing as a billowing cloud of steam came pouring out, assaulting her face. Quickly reeling backwards, Alex coughed at the humid lungful she inhaled, fanning the air in front of her face as Lena’s cold skin prickled at the wall of heat. It was a soothing balm against the chill of the prison.

     

                “Stand there,” Alex instructed Lena, pointing to the wall beside the door. “Hands up.”

     

                “They’re cuffed.”

     

                “You could be hanging upside down in a straitjacket and I have no doubt you’d still cause trouble. Hands as high as you can get them - for the cameras.”

     

                Obeying, Lena pressed her back flat against the wall and raised her arms as much as the cuffs allowed while Alex unlocked another door and rummaged around, reemerging with a mop and metal bucket. Setting the bucket down with a heavy clang, she moved over to Lena and undid her cuffs before pushing the mop handle into her hands and gesturing at the spreading puddle.

     

                “Start with that first.”

     

                “Yes, ma’am,” Lena dryly replied.

     

                As someone who had never mopped a single day in her life, Lena found it a simple process that left her mind free to think over what potential problem was occurring and how it could benefit her. Steam was still billowing out of the room but thinner now, less scalding, and Alex cast Lena a wary glance before carefully stepping through the puddle to see what was going on inside. 

     

                From her spot in the hallway, as she mopped up the hot water and wrung out the mop for the next pass over, Lena heard the guard groan. She didn’t stop but slowed as she glanced over at the door, trying to squint through the mist as she shifted her mopping closer to the room. Pausing in the doorway, she glanced around and then met Alex’s frowning face from where she knelt amidst a mess of broken clapboard, dirt, dust and insulation. 

     

                Glancing up, Lena took in the big hole in the ceiling, the source of the water and steam. Letting out a quick bark of laughter, she looked back down at Alex and laughed again, watching as disgruntlement shadowed the guard’s face.

     

                “Your handiwork, I presume?”

     

                “Potentially. I will take credit for it regardless.”

     

                “How about you take credit for cleaning it up?”

     

                Snorting, Lena raised her mop and let the head slop down in the puddle of water as she started moving it around again. Wringing it out, grey water filling the bottom of the bucket, she continued her menial work with the delighted look of someone who was enjoying themselves far too much from within the walls of an impenetrable underwater prison. Alex muttered angrily to herself as she fetched trash bags and a broom from the supply closet, leaning the latter against the wall and squatting as she picked up the bigger chunks of the ceiling panels that had slowly rotted through over the weeks since Lena’s sabotage to the pipes above. 

     

                “So … what was the plan with this?” Alex asked.

     

                “Cause chaos.”

     

                “Yeah, I figured. How does that help anyone?”

     

                Shrugging as she moved the water around, a poor effort of mopping as she prolonged the freedom from her cell, although her shoulders sagged with the drug-fuelled exhaustion of merely existing, Lena wrung out the mop again. 

     

                “I don’t know, a big hole in the ceiling might help.”

     

                “And a busted pipe?”

     

                “Guess you’ll have to turn off the boiler until it gets fixed,” Lena clicked her tongue with feigned regret.

     

                “Enjoy freezing in your cell without the district heating system working.”

     

                “Will do,” Lena curtly replied.

     

                They didn’t talk after that and Lena finished mopping up and then scooped up handfuls of the ceiling before switching to the broom.
