Steam was still spilling out of the burst pipe up in the ceiling and Lena knew there would be other potentially weakened pipes that might have burst or were on the verge of bursting, hot water seeping into the bones of the prison, rotting away the cheap construction, nursing patches of mould that could make everyone sick unless it was cleared properly, which wouldn’t happen. The small seeds of discontent would be sown in the restless prisoners and Lena was quietly pleased with her efforts, even if it meant suffering along with them.

     

                Alex radioed in the issue and had the boiler shut off, the steam dissipating entirely a few minutes later with the arrival of Winn, who glared at Lena as he set down a toolbox a safe distance from her. Alex gave him a withering look as she crossed her arms over her chest, mouth thinning.

     

                “I don’t think a wrench will solve the problem. I have a sneaking suspicion it’s not the only pipe that’ll be bursting soon.”

     

                Her eyes slid to Lena with grim annoyance. Lips twitching with amusement, Lena arched an eyebrow and then returned to her sweeping. Gesturing to the hole in the ceiling, Alex sighed and then shook her head at Winn.

     

                “Can you just … check for water damage, patch it up? Whatever you can do in the meantime. We’ll need to check the whole heating system before we turn the boiler back on or it’ll just happen again.”

     

                “That could take days,” Winn complained.

     

                “Then you’d better get started or you’ll be having cold showers.”

     

                Surly and annoyed, he picked his toolbox up again and stepped into the room, staring up at the hole as water trickled down to the floor in steady drops and the dank smell of the close ceiling space filled the room. It smelled stagnant and damp but it wasn’t unfamiliar to Lena, who had spent more time than she would have liked holed away up there. Her skin itched at the mere thought of the dust that had coated her skin for days during her excursion. 

     

                “LL93, leave the broom. It’s time to head back.”

     

                Nodding, Lena set the broom against the wall and let Alex cuff her before falling into step beside the guard. They didn’t speak to each other for the rest of the walk back to her cell and Lena absentmindedly rubbed at her wrists as soon as they were freed, catching sight of Kara’s anxious figure pressed up against the forcefield, awaiting Lena’s delayed return to her cell with a questioning look in her eyes. Giving her a thin smile, Lena stretched out on her cot and sighed wearily as she tried to think about the next step of her plan.

     

                Over the next few hours, a chill seeped into the cells and she found herself thinking back on the decision to disrupt the heating system. They had cold showers anyway and despite the cool air of the cells, there were still the steam pipes running throughout the prison, staving off the low temperatures of the frigid ocean surrounding them. Without the boiler running, the heat of the pipes slowly faded, no longer burrowing through the wall and ceilings, and Lena slowly started to feel the cold, first enough to stave off with the scrubs, long-sleeved cotton shirt and pilled sweatshirt, and then by the thin blanket on her cot but eventually even curling in on herself to warm herself with her own body heat wasn’t enough.

     

                Shivering in a ball on her cot, Lena’s chin trembled with the effort to stop her teeth from chattering, her jaw starting to ache, and she could hear complaints from the other prisoners on her block as the true temperature of the prison was ushered in without the pipes keeping it at bay. Trying not to regret her destruction too much, Lena wedged her fingers into her armpits to try and warm them and was determined to sleep to pass the time.

     

                After getting a fitful few hours in as her whole body was tense from the shivers that wracked her, Lena was irritable when she pushed herself up slightly, blinking blearily and listening to the snappy voices of the guards. When she exhaled, her breath hung visibly in the air before her and Lena froze, her fingers stiff as she ran a hand over her face, wondering how badly constructed the prison was if turning off the boiler could reduce the place to a freezer.

     

                The guards made their way along to each cell and Lena remained curled up on her cot, her blanket drawn around her shoulders and held tightly closed at the front as her teeth chattered, puffs of white exhaling with her shuddering breaths. Alex paused outside hers and arched an eyebrow in a reproving manner before lowering Lena’s forcefield.

     

                “Here. Extra sweatshirt, socks and blanket. Do you want tea or coffee?”

     

                “Feeling sympathetic, huh?”

     

                Snorting, Alex rolled her eyes. “Tea or coffee?”

     

                “Coffee.”

     

                Nodding, Alex poured some out of the heated urn on the trolley and set it on the floor just inside the forcefield boundary. She looked like she wanted to say something else but just put the barrier back up and then wheeled the trolley over to Kara’s cell. They had a quiet conversation before Alex moved back over to Lena’s cell and lowered the barrier again, setting down another blanket and a second cup of coffee. She pressed a finger to her lips and then retreated quickly.

     

                As soon as she was gone, Lena hurriedly uncurled herself and stiffly crossed over to the folded pile, pulling the second pair of socks on over her feet and then yanking on the sweatshirt. Her nose felt numb and when she cupped the paper coffee cup in her palms, she felt the faint steam thaw her face slightly. Taking a sip of the mercifully warm coffee, it traced down her throat in a line of heat and Lena didn’t think she’d ever been so grateful for something before.

     

                Setting the cup down and pulling both blankets around herself, she sat on her haunches and jerkily signed to Kara across the gap between them. You don’t have extras.

     

                I don’t get cold.

     

                Really?

     

                Yes. I don’t get hot either. You need it more than I do.

     

                Lena realised Kara must have been convincing Alex to give Lena her useless allotment and she felt her fondness for the alien grow. Lips twitching with a ghost of a smile, Lena watched Kara take a sip of tea, purely for the pleasure of it, giving her a quick wink. Taking a sip of her coffee, Lena held it tightly, leaching as much warmth from it as she could before setting it back down.

     

                Thank you.

     

                Was this you?

     

                I think so. Problems will help. Maybe they’ll riot.

     

                He will. 

     

                She gestured scathingly towards a cell along the same row as Lena’s and she didn’t have to wonder who Kara was talking about. One thing about Mon-El, he wasn’t quiet about voicing his discontent or his intentions and she knew that if he wasn’t happy, he would be a problem. That could work in her favour but he was unpredictable and she wasn’t sure about relying on him reacting how she wished to advance her plans. It wouldn’t do for him to incite a riot that left them all under tighter restrictions. Although, Lena seemed to have exhausted all of her restrictions, drugged into a tired version of herself that could only muster the energy for the short walks she was allowed and brief conversations with her cellmates via sign language.

     

                I won’t let him hurt you again.

     

                I know. I don’t want him to hurt you either.

     

                I’m stronger than him.

     

                Kara flashed a grin as she finished signing and Lena let out a quiet huff of laughter. Nodding, she hesitated and then quickly signed as a furrowed look clouded her expression.

     

                I’m stuck.

     

                How?

     

                The plan. I don’t know what to do.

     

                We have time.

     

                Agony cut through Lena with a ripple of taut anger on her face as she thought about how long she’d have to plot their escape. She was young, it didn’t matter if it took a decade, she’d still be alive. But she wouldn’t let herself live that long in a place like that. Lena was too much of an extremist, too all-or-nothing to idly sit by and succumb to captivity for the next ten years of her life. And Kara had been inside for too long already; if the sense of urgency for her own self-preservation wasn’t encouraging enough, Lena wouldn’t let her friend spend a second longer inside than she had to.

     

                I don’t want it.

     

                Picking up her coffee, she drained it quickly and set the paper cup down before picking up the other one and retreating to her bed. Sinking onto the cot, she huddled up with her two blankets and the other cup, nursing it until it was lukewarm and she had to drink it all in one go, her hands red from how hot the cup had been but the coffee tepid as it slid down her throat. She felt warmer though, less stiff, although the healed break in her leg ached in the cold.

     

                Lunch was brought shortly after, a thin broth with pitiful vegetables and stringy lumps of meat swimming in it, and Lena was thankful for the steaming heat of it as she skimmed the oily sheen of fat from the surface and wolfed down the rest. When she was done, she curled up into a ball and tried to sleep again until there was the thud of a baton striking the forcefield.

     

                “Prisoner LL93, on your feet.”

     

                Grumbling, Lena uncurled herself and rose, scowling as she hugged her arms to herself. Maggie let down the forcefield and gestured her out of the cell with a slightly smug look on her face as she narrowed her eyes and smiled thinly.

     

                “Time for your walk.”

     

                The last thing Lena felt like doing was shambling around the large room in the freezing cold, knowing she wouldn’t be allowed to move fast enough to get her blood moving properly, warming her up. She would have preferred to stay wrapped up in her blankets but knew she couldn’t afford to piss off any of the other guards. Now that she had Alex’s attention and assistance, Lena was hoping to keep a low profile with the other guards, in case her antics led her back to solitary confinement or a different cell block right when things were starting to line up with her plans.

     

                Joining the other two women in her group, the three of them were marched out by Vaquez and Maggie and taken to the room to walk their designated laps. The open space of the room made it even colder, the ventilation system only serving to further add to the chill that seeped from the damp stained concrete walls. Walking in a circle for an hour at a slow, plodding march, Lena was slumped wearily, finding it harder than usual to keep herself upright as the numbing edge of the drugs was worsened by the bone-deep cold of the prison. It wasn’t doing her any good to sabotage her own comfort but Lena had to look at it as an opportunity, but even that didn’t spark as much determination as she’d hoped. 

     

                Finally allowed to stop the monotonous laps, Lena was led back to the cell block just as Kara was being led out in her straitjacket, giving Lena a quick wink as they passed each other in the hallway. Although she’d been close to her before, touched her, held her crumpled body, and kissed her cheek, it still made Lena’s stomach swoop to be in such close proximity, even though they never said a word to each other. There was a shared, knowing look exchanged and Lena’s lips twitched with a faint smile, cutting through the morose expression on her pale face, hollowed out with exhaustion and cold.

     

                Climbing back onto her cot and wrapping herself back up in her blankets, Lena tried not to slump against the cold cement wall as she brooded over her plan. She needed delivery sheets, guard rosters and shift rotations, schedules for meals and exercise, passwords and keys, and so many tiny facets of information to make the whole thing cohesive and airtight. To miss one piece could mean they would all end up in a cell, which Lena didn’t think particularly concerning for the three women on the outside who would perhaps have more understanding if they’d been put in her shoes, but it wouldn’t do her any good to get them all captured. The other outcome was they would be gunned down where they stood the moment they encountered a problem that tipped off the guards who weren’t in on her plan. Even with Jansen dead, Lena knew the other guards were brutal enough to accelerate a situation to execution at the drop of a hat if it meant saving themselves.

     

                Kara returned a while later to find her still brooding over the same thoughts. Lena had already told Alex where to start but it would be a long, pain-staking process of data collection before Lena would feel confident enough in her plan. There were definite steps - getting out of the cells and their collars, getting through the airlock, making their way to the loading bay, getting on to the helicopter - but that didn’t mean it would be easy just because she knew the process. It was the gaps between the steps that would be difficult to fill in, to straighten out into something cohesive and possible, even if a little reckless.

     

                The days moved slowly after that, dragging on with the same routine she’d grown accustomed to over the months she’d been there. Months longer than she’d anticipated. It was a humiliating experience to think she was so smart yet couldn’t escape and as the boiler remained shut off for the ensuing days, Lena found herself thinking her intellect was perhaps slipping away because affecting the heating was surely the most ridiculous idea she’d had so far, and she’d swallowed a handful of pills in a last-ditch effort of freedom from isolation. 

     

                In her initial reconnaissance through the ceiling to make repairs, she’d sabotaged all she could get her hands on and some of those efforts were paying off now. Others would probably never come to fruition, wires not quite frayed enough, the crossed sections not able to override the programming of the computers and electrical circuits they ran between but whatever she could try to do, Lena had done it. Winn was still in the process of checking the pipes of the district heating system, making sure no other leaks had been found, rotting through the infrastructure - if any had been found, it didn’t make its way back to Lena - and they’d been kept warm - if you could call it that - with copious amounts of tea, coffee and walking. They had been spared the inhumane act of showering beneath freezing cold water out of fear of pneumonia, a directive that Lena knew had come from Eliza, but that only served to make the cell block stuffy with the body odour of the prisoners confined there. 

     

                But it wasn’t just the heating. A few days later, once the heating had been turned back on and Lena was left shivering in a cold sweat as her body adjusted to the new temperature and her immune system tried to combat a fever and a chest infection, the lights went out. It wasn’t the first time, of course, but it was just as unwelcome, leaving them all sitting in the pitch black as they listened to their too-loud breaths, calling back and forth with questions none of them could answer. Kara tried her best to eavesdrop, relaying the news that it was a prison-wide blackout, the power tripping due to a storm but the generators were out for some unknown reason. Lena imagined she was the reason for that too. 

     

                The only person who seemed entirely unaffected by any of the troubles going on in the prison was Kara. She didn’t get cold, could see in the dark, and was all around amenable and well-behaved unless it was for Lena’s sake. In fact, when the lights went out, it killed the ghastly red sun lamps as well, hooked up to the same circuit as the fluorescents, and she was in an even better mood as the radiation-dampening lamps stopped working for the two days it took for Winn to patch the spliced wires back together properly. Lena thought the guards should have been fortunate the power generating the forcefields and keeping the collars active were still running. They would have been better targets but she was flying blind and couldn’t have known what she was getting her hands on up in the ceiling, only that causing havoc was the way to go.

     

                When the lights came back on, the guards relented and allowed them an early social, over two weeks earlier than scheduled, to boost morale. They hadn’t let anyone out of their cells during the blackout, not wanting to lose track of a prisoner in the dark, and they were cautious of pent-up energy, walking everyone for longer than usual before directing them all into the recreation room to socialise. Lena tuned out the sounds of Jeopardy on the TV and fished out the chess set, scowling at Mon-El as she waited for Kara to arrive.

     

                When Alex led her in, Kara smiled widely and patiently waited until she was removed from the straitjacket before dragging the seat out and taking a seat across from Lena. With a stern warning for everyone to behave, Alex retreated to the far wall to supervise with the other guards. 

     

                “Fancy seeing you so soon,” Kara greeted her, a little shy as she grinned like a kid.

     

                “Aren’t you a sight for sore eyes,” Lena sighed, her lips twitching slightly as she fiddled with the makeshift chess pieces. 

     

                “Ah, well, I don’t mean to brag but some of us could see in the dark.”

     

                “If only I was so lucky. I missed your face. At least last time I had your voice.”

     

                “Yeah, it’s really not the same having to practically yell our conversations across the block. It’s fine; it won’t be for much longer, right?”

     

                Mouth opening and closing, Lena started to set the board, the corners of her mouth turning down with dissatisfaction. “I don’t know, Kara. There’s still a lot to plan. It might not be for a while.”

     

                “But you’re smart. You’ll figure it out.”

     

                “I- yeah, of course, but … I’m finding it … hard at the moment. It’s …” she blew the air out of her cheeks, shaking her head as she met Kara’s eyes with dismay. “I find it hard to concentrate. It’s not- it’s not helping. Um … I thought that Alex would but …”

     

                “She is,” Kara murmured through lips that barely moved. Clearing her throat, she shifted on her seat. “Up my sleeve. She wanted me to pass it on. I like to draw with Kelly in my sessions so she slipped it to her and then Kelly slipped it to me and now I have to give it to you. But you can’t get caught with it.”

     

                “What is it?”

     

                “Blueprints. Only a little bit. She had to tear it up into pieces so it’ll take a while to get the whole thing to you. She said to memorise it and then destroy it. You’ll either have to flush it or eat it but be discreet.”

     

                “How do we …?” Lena asked, trailing off as her eyes flickered around the room with apprehension.

     

                Smiling, Kara let out a quick laugh, reaching across the table to cover Lena’s hands with her own. Giving her a quick wink, Kara smoothed her thumbs over the backs of Lena’s hands, moving towards her wrists and then brushing the cuff of the sweatshirt with a pointed look. Swallowing thickly, Lena repeated the gesture on Kara’s hands, revelling in the heat of her fingers, her finely bone knuckles, her slender wrists, all of it hiding the power beneath them. Fingers slipping beneath the cuff of the right sleeve, Lena felt the edge of a folded piece of paper and started to work it free.

     

                They were both tense, Lena’s heart racing, her pulse jumping at her throat, and Kara tried to feign nonchalance as she leaned in, propping her chin up in her other hand. “So, what do you need me to do? I’m not just the muscle, you know. I’m smart too.”

     

                Her earnestness made Lena soften slightly, forgetting to be nervous about their covert exchange of information, and her face creased with amusement. Green eyes regaining a spark to them, her lips twitched and she inched the paper out of Kara’s sleeve. Kara’s hand slid over Lena’s, covering the paper between the two of them as Lena coaxed it out fully and towards her own sleeve. Catching the end of it with her fingers, Kara urged it along as well, continuing to quietly rattle off her list of skills to make it seem like they were casually talking, sneakily touching.

     

                As soon as the scrap of paper was up her sleeve, Lena gave Kara’s hand a quick squeeze as Kara smiled triumphantly. Glancing at Alex over Kara’s shoulder, Lena raised her eyes imperceptibly and the guard straightened, squaring her shoulders.

     

                “No touching,” Alex called out, affecting a bored tone.

     

                Snatching their hands away from each other, Lena scowled and it wasn’t entirely part of the act. The folded piece of torn paper was loose in her sleeve and she moved her hands under the table and adjusted it securely as Kara finished setting up the chessboard. Lena went first and then fell into their routine and spoke about whatever came to mind. Mostly, Lena peppered Kara with questions about Krypton.

     

                “My brother’s research I got my hands on said that it’s the yellow sun radiation that gives you your powers on Earth.”

     

                “Mhm. That’s why I have those red lights in my cell. It’s artificial radiation emulating Krypton’s red sun. That’s how they depower me.”

     

                “So when the power was out …”

     

                “I was stronger. Not as strong as I’d be if I was above sea level in direct sunlight. But even without the sun, the air on Earth has that radiation.”

     

                “So, realistically, it would be best to manufacture an escape during a blackout so you could use your powers. And the quicker we get you up to the helipad, the better.”

     

                “Theoretically,” Kara agreed.

     

                “Oh, no, nothing theoretical about it. That’ll have to be the plan.”

     

                “You’re forgetting my collar.”

     

                “No, I’m not. I just haven’t worked out that solution yet.”

     

                “Worst case, I can fight through it for a while if I’m not depowered. Potentially long enough to get us out.”

     

                Lena’s brow furrowed and she moved her rook, taking one of Kara’s pawns. “No, I won’t let you suffer while we’re escaping. It’ll make it harder to be quick if you’re not at peak performance - well, peak for in here.”

     

                Letting out a quiet huff of laughter, Kara raised her eyebrows, “you know, I’d still be the fastest person in here even with Kryptonite making me feel like my skin is peeling off.”

     

                “Well … last resort, anyway,” Lena reluctantly conceded. “Hopefully Alex can solve that problem.”

     

                “And the lights too,” Kara readily agreed, all too willing to place her trust in the guard.

     

                “Right. Um … maybe let’s keep this to ourselves for now. Just while I figure out the steps leading up to it. I don’t want Alex to try and do something prematurely, you know? I’m glad that she’s on board now though; maybe things will go quicker with the three of us working on it.”

     

                Her forced faith in Alex was taken earnestly by Kara, who saw the logic in planning everything out in full before they started to act. She also readily accepted Lena as the planner and was willing to go along with whatever she suggested and Lena felt a prickle of guilt at that. Alex wasn’t entirely wrong in her deduction that Lena was manipulating Kara - only a little, and only for her own benefit. Once they were out, it wouldn’t matter how Lena radicalised her into action after almost two decades of compliance, it would only matter that they were free. 

     

                They spoke of lighter things afterwards, talking about the differences in their childhoods, the places Lena had been that she thought Kara would like and promised to take her there once they were out, the planets Kara had travelled to and the races of aliens she’d met, so fascinating to Lena but not so much as the alien sitting across from her. Under different circumstances, they could have talked all day, maybe over lattes and coffee cake, enjoying the warm weather of California or maybe even overseas. Instead, they were afforded the grim recreation room and an hour of chess with half a set. It went by entirely too fast.

     

                Once she was back in her cell, Lena curled up under her blankets and slipped the piece of paper free, unfolding it and staring at the portion of the prison with her immediate cell block, the guard room down the hall, the bathrooms for prisoners and staff and supply closets and guard accommodation, mess hall and kitchens. Committing it to memory, she scrunched it up tightly and then emerged from the blankets and pretended to use the toilet behind the low privacy wall, flushing the paper and washing her hands before climbing into bed and visualising her near vicinity with better clarity and detail.

     

                The next scrap came two days later, slipped into her hand as Alex re-cuffed her after showering and quickly squirrelled away up her sleeve. In her cell, Lena repeated the process, glad the guard was smart enough to give her adjoining sections of the stolen blueprints so she could orient it in her mind. 

     

                Over the next two weeks, Lena was fed the scraps piecemeal, finding one folded up in her cup of vitamins, another beneath the cup of water on her tray at dinner, another pressed into her hand as Lena was uncuffed in her cell after a walk. Once Alex had gotten the last piece to her, Lena found herself feeling more confident about her plan; the prison wasn’t that big once she’d seen the entirety of it, counting two hundred viable cells and the same number for staff. Only a portion of the staff were guards as well, with a number of janitors, cooks, technicians, engineers and administrators swelling the ranks. Once she had the bigger picture of their circumstances, it seemed more possible to make the trek to the elevator at the loading bay, which she memorised the route to with every door and room behind them to know what she was up against.

     

                “What’s next?” Alex muttered as she took Lena to her next appointment with Eliza.

     

                “We need to figure out a way to disarm Kara’s collar. And mine, I guess, but hers is harder.”

     

                “I can’t.”

     

                “You need to find a way. Kara’s confident she can withstand hers for a bit but if I get shocked on the way out, I’ll go down like a sack of bricks. We can’t afford delays.”

     

                “There’s an easier solution than that.”

     

                “What?”

     

                “I take it off when the time comes. It is biometrically programmed to react to my thumbprint.”

     

                “It’ll be too noticeable to remove them prematurely; it would be easier to disarm them in the computer system but I’m assuming your mother and girlfriend can’t access the software to do it. That would be a huge flaw in the security of the prison.”

     

                “Correct. But I do have a few cowardly friends here that I’m sure can help.”

     

                Lena’s mouth was a flat line for a moment as she weighed Alex’s answer. “Absolutely not. Getting five of us out is already an inconvenient risk we could do without. We’re not bringing anyone else.”

     

                Scoffing, Alex rolled her eyes. “Who put you in charge?”

     

                “Me. It’s my plan. You’d be twiddling your thumbs and doing laps of these halls until you got old and useless enough for them to off you if it wasn’t for me.”

     

                “Yeah, yeah, don’t get too far ahead of yourself; we’re both still stuck in this shithole. But for the record, I didn’t say we were bringing anyone else. I have a gun and I’m very persuasive.”

     

                “As you’ve showcased. Probably for the best that we don’t leave a trail of bodies behind us though.”

     

                “I can be discreet.”

     

                “Good. Well, you work on that and I’ll figure out the rest.”

     

                Snorting, Alex opened her mouth to speak and then closed it, shaking her head. Arching an eyebrow, Lena waited expectedly. “What?”

     

                “What?”

     

                “You were going to say something.”

     

                Hesitating, Alex’s lips twitched with annoyance as she glanced sideways at Lena. “I’m just surprised getting her collar off was your first thought.”

     

                “Why wouldn’t it be?”

     

                “I don’t know, I was expecting you to say the next step would be giving you placebo drugs.”

     

                “That’s not important. My body’s adjusted.”

     

                “Yeah, but you still sleep a lot and half the time you look like no one’s home.”

     

                Making a sound of annoyance at the back of her throat, Lena’s lips twisted derisively. “Obviously. It’s unavoidable for the time being.”

     

                “Maybe.”

     

                They stopped outside the medical bay then and Lena went through the motions of the medical assessment as Eliza said little but muttered exasperations at how pale she was, the lingering rattle in her chest that needed more antibiotics, the hollowed-out exhaustion of Lena’s face as she questioned her sleeping habits. Lena mumbled her responses to questions and endured the rest of it, a fog of depression clouding her, a near-permanent companion these days, as she waited for it to be over. 

     

                Eliza didn’t have much to say, Lena’s bloodwork from the last time was as normal as expected, and her noncommittal responses to questions about the depot injection were no cause for alarm as Eliza checked her blood pressure and weight. Given a cup of juice and a packet of Oreos to increase her blood sugar after the latest batch of vials was taken from her, Lena tried to prolong her time away from her cell for as long as possible. 

     

                Listening to mother and daughter make chit-chat as Lena sipped her apple juice, she deduced that Eliza was ignorant of Alex’s covert assistance with Lena’s plan. The conversation was mundane and didn’t speak of any end to their ongoing confinement to the jail and Lena was almost tempted to bring it up, to rope Eliza into it but she didn’t want to piss Alex off and didn’t have a use for the doctor in her plan yet. Keeping quiet, she finished off her cookies and then climbed to her feet, Alex already readying the cuffs.

     

                Leaving the medical bay, they walked in silence for a moment, Lena’s shoulders curving as the weight of the cuffs made her arms hang limply before her. She had an inch on her right shoulder that she tried to shrug off, frustrating and maddening and decided to bring up her observation as a distraction.

     

                “She doesn’t know,” Lena guessed.

     

                “Are you kidding me? She’d chew me out big time if she thought I was doing something as reckless as trying to stage a jailbreak.”

     

                Snorting, Lena’s lips twitched with amusement. “Scared of your own mom?”

     

                “More like I’m sparing myself the headache - for now.”

     

                “Fair enough. I won’t mention it to her then.”

     

                Alex was silent for a moment before clearing her throat. “Thanks.”

     

                Nodding, Lena fell silent, taking the relevant turns unaided as she knew the route by now. She imagined it would be relatively easy to navigate the prison, now that she knew where she was going from her mental map. The difficult part would be the airlocks and guard stations, but even then, she’d avoided those in the crawl space in the ceiling, which was kept at a consistent pressure throughout and could be navigated with some difficulty past the airlocks and guards where they’d find themselves trapped with Alex trying to get them through the doors. 

     

                From her mental map, there were three they would have to circumvent, but it would be difficult to keep their bearings in the ceiling if they traversed the prison from up in the ceiling, which was cramped enough for one person winding around the pipes, electrical wiring, the narrow beams surrounded by clapboard and insulation and wide foil tubes of the HVAC system, let alone the five of them. It would take hours and they’d miss their narrow window of opportunity, which Lena still didn’t have a timeframe on if they did it that way.

     

                “What do you need from me next?” Alex asked after a minute.

     

                “Schedules. Guard rosters and the delivery one. We’ll need to know how long it takes for the helicopter to land and take off again. That’s how long we’ll have to pull it off.”

     

                “Guard roster is twelve-hour shifts on a four and three roster of day and nights. No days off. There are three crews with overlaps of four hours between crews. The deliveries are usually scheduled for ten o’clock in the morning on the first of each month.”

     

                “What’s the margin of error?”

     

                “I don’t know, give or take ten minutes depending on the weather. I think maybe a dozen times since I’ve been here they’ve had to delay until the next day for severe weather warnings but otherwise it’s just about wind currents.”

     

                “How long to unload the cargo?”

     

                “They make four runs with the cargo elevator. They take it down to the loading bay so it’s probably ten to fifteen minutes to unload from the chopper, load it onto the pallet truck, bring it down and unload it. So forty minutes to an hour. If they have a new prisoner for us, that’s an extra five to ten minutes; they’re out cold when they’re brought in so it’s relatively quick.”

     

                Snorting, Lena gave her a withering look. “Well aware. When’s the next delivery?”

     

                “Losing track of the days, are we?”

     

                “Don’t piss me off.”

     

                “Ten days.”

     

                “Alright, well, time it next time. I’ll need more accurate figures than your guesses to work out a timeframe. If we’re out of our cells too early, that gives the guards too much time to question why you have us out and sound the alarm. If we’re too late, well, we’ve missed the chopper and we’re out of our cells.”

     

                “Sure.”

     

                Hesitating, Lena’s brow furrowed slightly before she narrowed her eyes and glanced at Alex. “Where does the shipment come in from?”

     

                “Utqiagvik. It’s the northernmost town in-“

     

                “The United States, ninth overall worldwide, yes, I’ve heard of it,” Lena finished, brusque and uninterested. “It’s surrounded by the National Petroleum Reserve which is owned by the federal government so that explains why they’d choose that place. Not a strong military presence either, aside from the Point Barrow site.”

     

                “How would you know about government military sites?”

     

                Shrugging, Lena rolled her eyes. “That’s all public information. I’m assuming there’s a government black site on the federal property though. Somewhere to take the prisoners to during transit to the prison. I’m also assuming we’re in the Arctic Ocean?”

     

                “Correct again,” Alex wearily sighed, tiring of Lena’s smug satisfaction. “About seven-hundred miles out.”

     

                “Bit of a problem for us. Once we’re in the chopper we want to find land as quickly as possible to minimise our chances of being picked up on any radar for air space. Alaska wouldn’t be my first choice - too remote to be too helpful for us - but it’s better to be on American soil so I can access my resources and assets.”

     

                “Your resources and assets were seized and frozen upon your arrest.”

     

                Scoffing, Lena gave Alex a patronising look. “Do you really think someone as intelligent as me, coming from my family, wouldn’t have contingency plans for any scenario? I have cash-bought properties through a dozen shell companies that are very difficult to trace back to me, all of them with enough to get me by in a crisis. Now, if we can make it to Anchorage, we’ll be fine. I have a place where we can lie low until we sort out new IDs and paperwork for us all and enough cash to split it five ways and say good riddance to each other.”

     

                “Why do you have all of this ready to go?”

     

                “My brother’s a lunatic, are you kidding me? I’m a shrewd businesswoman and a mad scientist but I’m not stupid enough to tie all my finances up in property and stocks linked to myself or L-Corp. I have a place in every major city in the world and strategic, remote locations in case I need to disappear. Lex has tried to assassinate me enough times for me to take precautions. And my mother is almost as bad.”

     

                “Right,” Alex slowly replied. “You know your family is insane, right?”

     

                Sighing heavily, Lena’s mouth thinned. “Very clearly I know that. At least we’re down to two of us; I’d hate to give my mother the satisfaction of being the only Luthor left alive.”

     

                “Too bad you didn’t have a way of getting word to her.”

     

                “I’d sooner stay in here than let her gloat about saving me from a life sentence,” Lena said with such venom that it was almost believable.

     

                Alex snorted and didn’t respond as she led her the rest of the way back to her cell. Debriefing Kara as well as she could via sign language, Lena retreated into her mind and spent the rest of her day feeling a little out of sorts as the new depot injection crept through her body, reclaiming that muffled distance between her body and mind that had shrunk as the first dose had waned over the week. Mind slowly descending into a fog that she knew she’d adjust to, Lena was lethargic and depressed as she willed her plan to work.

     

                Ten days later, Alex was cuffing her for her walk as she relayed the gathered information. Lena knew Kara could hear every word and was glad she’d be clued in so they were all on the same page. She was finding it increasingly hard to communicate her thoughts and planning without the ease of whispered conversations held beneath their bunks as they had before.

     

                “Chopper landed three minutes earlier than scheduled. They didn’t have any prisoners so it took forty-nine minutes to bring everything down to the loading bay and ready for takeoff again. Fifty-three before they were back in the air.”

     

                “How many?”

     

                “They run a crew of five. One pilot and four DEO agents from the black site.”

     

                “And how many from here are involved?”

     

                “Usually six agents up top to help with the unloading.”

     

                Making a mental note of the numbers, Lena nodded. She was silent for a moment, running the risk, punching the numbers, plotting the possibility of the gamble being pulled off. Nodding again, she inhaled sharply and then exhaled deeply.

     

                “What month are we in?”

     

                “March.”

     

                Her eyes landed on Kara’s face across the gap between their cells, her friend sitting cross-legged on her cot as she listened intently. There was a tense set to her shoulders, an almost palpable air of expectation, and Lena gave her a quick nod.

     

                “We have thirty days.”

    Chapter 14

                Their thirty-day deadline was passing by quickly, plans of rations, of gear to brave the arctic weather, guard shifts and Lena asking a multitude of questions about the camera hardware, their security systems, trying to think of a way to loop footage. Alex was tech-savvy enough to sort that out herself, mining Winn for answers at dinner in the guard cafeteria and stealing his computer login for the eventuality. He was also her mark for someone friendly but meek enough for her to threaten into taking the collars off the two prisoners.

     

                It had been a slow, intricate process of ensuring they thought of every potential issue, from who to free first - Kara, who would be able to tear through the guards with only mild difficulty, instead of risking being riddled with bullets - to meeting points and timestamps for each of them, Kelly aware but Eliza still in the dark about the plan. It was made difficult by the limited contact Lena had with Alex, using Kara as a messenger where they could to transfer more information. They’d eventually come up with a system for Kara to eavesdrop on Alex with her sensitive hearing and relay information to Lena via sign language.

     

                Despite the confident face she put on, mostly for Kara’s sake but for her own sanity as well, knowing this would be their one chance, Lena couldn’t help but feel like they were missing something. There was something they hadn’t accounted for, some bump in the otherwise relatively smooth and uncomplicated plan, and she didn’t know how to shake that feeling.

     

                Five days before their imminent prison break, she found herself at her next therapy session with Kelly, who she hadn’t seen since setting the date for their escape. Alex had kept her up to date and there was a tense energy in the air in anticipation of their escape, Kelly perhaps even more anxious than Lena felt, even though she had no hand in planning it, wouldn’t be held accountable for four other lives. Lena was starting to wish she’d never agreed to bring anyone else along.

     

                Curled up in her seat, Lena was as surly as usual, her thoughts like sand running through her fingers as she tried to focus on one but found herself easily distracted. Kelly was used to her black moods and fumbling conversation now, Lena’s slow agitation a permanent fixture since being pumped with drugs, and she was patient as the silence stretched on, waiting for her patient to say what was on her mind. 

     

                “You seem more distracted today,” Kelly eventually noted. “Are you worried?”

     

                Eyes cutting to the psychologist’s, Lena softly snorted, closing her eyes. She chewed on her words for a moment before reluctantly replying. “Aren’t you?”

     

                “Yes,” Kelly honestly replied. “Although, our imprisonment hinges on different sides of the cells, so I can imagine you feel as if you have more to lose than myself or Alex.”

     

                “Yes. And I dislike the fact that … the plan hinges on trusting people I don’t trust.”

     

                “Trust can only be proven once tested.”

     

                Lips twitching with wan amusement, Lena opened her eyes, eyebrows rising. “It’s one hell of a test to prove it with.”

     

                There was a brief bout of silence and Kelly drew in a shaky breath, leaning forward. “Lena … are you sure-”

     

                Shifting restlessly, Lena’s mouth thinned as her throat bobbed, swallowing thickly past the tightness of her fear. Shrugging noncommittally, she closed her eyes. “I don’t know. I don’t know what will happen. The plan is set, we just- if something goes wrong … we’re all completely fucked. Come if you want, or don’t, it makes no difference to me, but you’re either in or you're out because no one is stopping me from trying.”

     

                “We’re all in. Alex will get you and Kara out. I just- run through it with me. There can’t be any gaps.”

     

                Eyes opening, Lena hesitated and shook her head as her mouth turned down at the corners for a brief moment. “Alex doesn’t want you brought into it. You or Eliza. If it goes bad … she’ll throw me under the bus, I know that. She’ll set me up to take the fall so you don’t have to.”

     

                “I wouldn’t let her do that.”

     

                “You would if you were smart. I would plan to do the same. Why let five people go down for something one person, who is nothing to you, can take the blame.”

     

                “And would you be okay with that?”

     

                Green eyes bright with amusement, Lena smiled sharply. “I’d take the blame but next time - and there would be a next time - I wouldn’t trust a soul. I’d do it all by myself. But don’t worry, there won’t need to be a next time. The plan’s solid; even Alex thinks so.”

     

                “Okay,” Kelly murmured, both of them falling silent as they thought anxiously about five days’ time and whether they’d still be alive this time then.

     

                The peace of their session was disrupted a minute later by the door banging open and four guards bursting into the small office, one after the other, the bulk of them intimidating as they quickly filled the space. At the intrusion, Lena staggered up from her seat and tripped over her feet, striking the back wall and sinking down it as she curled in on herself, confused and panicked. Her palms turned clammy and her heart jackhammered in her chest as the cacophony of shouts overwhelmed her. 

     

                “What are you doing? What is this?” Kelly demanded, rising from her own seat, Lena’s file clutched in her hands and a tightness to the corners of her eyes and mouth as she stood her ground. “This is a confidential session.”

     

                Vasquez unholstered her gun and pointed it straight at Kelly’s face, the psychologist blanching as some of her tension went slack, the guard’s face an expressionless mask. “You’d better sit back down if you know what’s good for you.”

     

                “I-” Kelly faltered before sinking onto her chair, file in her lap and hands raised.

     

                She met Lena’s eyes, a warning glance that told the prisoner not to speak, not to move. Lena had enough sense to know this was not the moment to be taking risks when everything was lined up for them to make their escape in five days. Getting herself locked up for a stint in solitary confinement would all but guarantee to fuck up the plan.

     

                “May I ask what this is about?” Kelly curtly asked.

     

                Three of the guards tore the room apart, seizing Kelly’s clunky computer, tearing her thick books on psychological theories and therapy methods free from the shelves, creating a pile of mess on the floor. Pens were scattered, a framed photo of her family on her desk smashed, spilt coffee seeping across the small desk wedged in the corner. When they went for the filing cabinet, Kelly bristled.

     

                “Those files are protected by patient confidentiality. Hey. ”

     

                Her words fell on deaf ears, the filing cabinet drawers opened one by one as everything inside them was dragged out, one guard carting them out and returning for more. Kelly was on her feet again, outrage darkening her usually placid expression, and Vasquez spared her a dismissive glance.

     

                “You’ll have them back once they’ve been reviewed,” the guard said, eyes flitting down to the one Kelly gripped tightly in her hand. Reaching out to tear it free, Vasquez held it up and then tossed it onto the pile in another guard’s arms. “Can’t forget this one.”

     

                “The Warden will hear about this,” Kelly fumed.

     

                “It’s sanctioned by the Deputy,” Vasquez shrugged. “I’d worry about yourself first.”

     

                Brow creasing with confusion, Kelly’s lips parted but she paused momentarily and Lena felt a similar prickle of unease creep over her, her mind trying to parse through the event to figure out what was going on. Inhaling sharply, Kelly tried again.

     

                “What’s that supposed to mean? I’m in the middle of a session with a prisoner and you barge in here accusing me-”

     

                “Oh, no, not you,” Vasquez said as her mouth thinned with regret.

     

                “What-”

     

                “Take her to a holding cell. And take Prisoner LL93 back to her cell. The Deputy will want to speak to her later.”

     

                Doing a double-take as she glanced from Vasquez to Kelly and back to the guard, Lena’s mouth opened and closed wordlessly. She watched as Kelly struggled for a moment, affronted by the treatment, before she was hauled out of her office and a guard stomped over to Lena to haul her to her feet. Unable to resist as cuffs were clamped around her wrists and she was manoeuvred like a ragdoll under the guard’s brawn, Lena was soon prodded into motion and helpless to do anything but obey as she was led through the prison and back to her cell.

     

                Once she was on the block again, she found herself disoriented by the sight of Querl sitting in Psi’s cell, quickly glancing to the one beside hers and finding it empty, along with Kara’s directly across from hers. Blinking, Lena’s brow quickly furrowed and she craned her neck, trying to see who else, if any, had been shifted. The guard shoved her onward between her shoulder blades, sending her stumbling, trying to right her balance before she struck the floor face-first, arms pinned behind her back with the cuffs. She heard him chuckle and ground her teeth together, hunched over but still on her own two feet, reluctant to give him the satisfaction.

     

                Making her way into her cell, Lena was uncuffed and she glared daggers at the man until he vanished, leaving her trapped behind the barrier as she tried to figure out what was going on. Anxious and impatient, Lena moved over to the forcefield and met J’onn’s eyes from across the block, licking her lips as she asked.

     

                “J’onn?” she frantically whispered. “J’onn, what happened? I- where’s Kara? They moved Querl …”

     

                “I’m not sure what’s going on,” he tensely replied, an undercurrent of unease to his low rumble that did little to soothe Lena’s concerns. “They came in about a half hour ago and removed Psi from her cell and took her out of the block. Then they did a shuffle and moved Querl into Psi’s cell. Kara went for her medical checkup with Agent Danvers, by the sounds of things, but … that was-”

     

                “Before I left,” Lena weakly finished for him, her worry seeming more concrete now that J’onn had noted the lengthy duration of Kara’s absence too. “Is this a semi-regular thing? The reshuffling? It hasn’t happened since I’ve been in here but maybe-”

     

                He sighed regretfully, “no, it’s not. Only bad behaviour gets people shifted around, and unless you were up to no good in that therapy session of yours, I’m not sure what’s happened.”

     

                Swallowing past the tightness in her throat, Lena closed her eyes. “The guards interrupted. Trashed Kelly’s office, took her files and then her too. I don’t know what’s going on but … it wasn’t me. ”

     

                “I guess we’ll have to wait and see.”

     

                It proved a longer wait than Lena was used to, Kara’s absence a cause for concern as she bit her nails and paced anxiously, brimming with so much nervous tension that she couldn’t burn it off quickly enough. Her eyes felt heavy and her body was sore, as keyed up she was, and Lena continuously rubbed her forehead as she tried to make sense of it all, feeling sluggish and stupid as she couldn’t connect the dots fast enough. Something was wrong but it couldn’t have been something she’d done or they would’ve come for her already. And Kara had done nothing, was merely a messenger for Lena and Alex as they cobbled together the brunt of the plan. If it was about the plan to escape, surely Lena would have been implicated in that immediately.

     

                She judged it to be roughly another hour of waiting before the cell block doors hissed open and the tramp of heavy boots lured Lena over to the forcefield. Cheek pressed against the solid barrier as she tried to crane her head to see, Lena’s frustration grew as she had to wait for the noise of footsteps to grow closer, her stomach swooping with sickening panic that it wouldn’t be Kara, that they’d taken her away. Relief cut through her a moment later at the sight of the lanky blonde alien, trussed up and chained beyond the norm, being taken back to her cell across from Lena.

     

                Once she’d been set back in her cell, half a dozen military-grade rifles trained on her with kryptonite bullets no doubt loaded, Kara was freed from her restraints and she sank heavily onto her cot, blonde hair falling in her face as Lena tried to get a proper glimpse of her. 

     

                “Kara,” Lena whispered.

     

                Her head rose and Lena could see that Kara’s eyes were red raw from crying as she pressed her hand against the forcefield as if she could pass through it if she tried hard enough, would be able to go to her friend and wrap her in her arms, ask her what was wrong and fix it. She didn’t have time to speak further, to sign anything, before the cell block doors hissed open again and Vasquez and Winn escorted in a new prisoner dressed in washed-out grey, two black eyes and split lips making her face an almost unrecognisable mess. Alex.

     

                Dread knotted Lena’s stomach with a rush of surprise as she watched Alex’s coworkers shove her forward, right into the empty cell beside Lena’s, a second human prisoner taken into custody. Lena’s chest felt tight and her eyes shot back to Kara, wide with panic as their plan fell apart right before her eyes. Face turning a shocking shade of white, Lena opened and closed her mouth, eyes flitting between Kara and the guards slipping from her field of view as they moved into the cell beside Lena’s. She could still hear the grunt of pain as Alex was roughly shoved to her knees in the cell with a collar around her neck, sagging to the cold concrete floor as her knees gave out.

     

                “What’s going on?” Lena rasped, already knowing. “What the hell happened?”

     

                Fixing her with a mournful look, Kara’s bottom lip trembled and she shrugged wordlessly. Floundering as she tried to figure out what had gone wrong, where they’d slipped up, Lena felt sick to her stomach as the pressing confines of the prison closed in around her. They were never going to get out now. She should have been getting ready to breathe the fresh air, feel the sun on her face, and now the rug had been pulled out from under her and Lena was beginning to wonder if she’d ever make it out of her cell again.

     

                Anger bubbled up through the fog of confusion and Lena slammed her hand against the forcefield, whirling away as she started to restlessly pace. Her eyes stung fiercely as the urge to cry crept up on her, and she had to dig the heels of her palms into her eyes to stifle it. Drawing in shaky breaths as she tried to steady herself, tried to hold the unspooling months of planning in her palms as it shredded to pieces.

     

                She had started to crack as the weeks slipped by, and then months, the fissures in her confident facade deepening, widening, and now the last bit of hope she’d clung to had been torn away. Exhaling sharply as she struggled to catch her breath, Lena let out a ragged sob as her hope shattered. 

     

     

                Taken from her cell after she’d eaten her breakfast, Kara was led through the hallways by Alex, as she had at least once a month for almost two decades now, quietly conversing, the ease of their familiarity making it seem less like a prison escort and more like a chaperoned stroll. Of course, Kara could never forget the boundaries that set them on opposite sides but she clung to the nerve-wracking excitement that it would be non-existent in a few days’ time.

     

                Freed from her restraints inside the medical bay, she rolled her shoulders and grinned at Eliza, obediently placid as usual as she took a seat on the padded table and allowed the doctor to go through the motions of poking and prodding her. Kara had long since stopped feeling like an experiment or an exhibition, just another alien amidst the mass of them locked away, but she knew Eliza had a soft spot for her on account of watching the little girl grow up alone in a cell.  

     

                Eliza always worked slowly on her prisoners to give them a few extra precious minutes outside of their cell, and she was still working away on Kara, doing a thorough examination of her eyes and how they dilated and contracted, jotted down notes in a neat, slow hand and asked dozens of questions for Kara’s records, when Kara’s efforts to tune out her surroundings faltered at the sudden uptick in activity. She hadn’t been paying attention to the droning of distant guard’s voices, hadn’t kept track of where certain people were in relation to the prison, and shifted restlessly as she listened to the sounds of tactical gear and heavy footsteps and doors hissing open and closed. 

     

                “You alright?” Alex called out, noticing the restlessness of the prisoner.

     

                Licking her lips, Kara’s eyes flitted back and forth, her throat going dry as she tried to quell the feelings. “I don’t know. Something- something’s not … right. Something’s wrong.”

     

                “What do you mean?” Alex asked, expression furrowing as she kept her arms folded but straightened against the wall. 

     

                Face clouded with unease, Kara shrugged, listening to the sounds of activity. “I don’t know. The guards are busy.”

     

                Hesitating, Alex’s mouth thinned and she reached for her radio. “This is Agent Danvers, just requesting clearance for transport. Prisoner KZ64 will be leaving the medical bay shortly. Over.”

     

                There was no response and Alex tried again before her mouth turned down at the corners and she met Kara’s wary blue eyes. “Might be an issue with the channel. Could be something your girlfriend has cooked up.”

     

                Rolling her eyes as she quietly scoffed, Kara gave the guard an exasperated look as Eliza pushed up her sleeve to take a blood sample. “She’s not … my girlfriend,” Kara tightly replied as the sliver of the kryptonite needle pierced the crook of her elbow, ruby red blood flowing through the tube.

     

                The bay was silent for a minute as Eliza let the test tubes fill and then taped a little cotton ball to the pinprick, Kara giving her a sweet smile through the faintly nauseous feeling of the minuscule piece of green kryptonite beneath her skin. Rolling her sleeve back down, Kara cleared her throat as Eliza turned to fetch her a juice box and cookies from her supply.

     

                “Am I looking healthy?”

     

                “Well, you could do with a good tan, as ever, but other than that, healthy as a horse,” Eliza said, removing the latex gloves and delicately wrinkling her nose as she reached up to cup Kara’s cheek in her hand. 

     

                Returning her smile as she tore open the packet of cookies set in her lap, Kara opened her mouth to thank her when she heard the synchronised thud of heavy boots down the hallway. Skin prickling with concern, she set the cookies aside and slid off the padded table, listening to the sound grow louder.

     

                “Eat your cookies,” Alex coaxed her, glancing down at her watch. “It’s almost lunchtime.”

     

                “Alex,” Kara hoarsely replied, her voice slow and rasping. “Something’s wrong.”

     

                “It’s fine. You’re just … paranoid. Keep it together for five more days and-”

     

                “Five days?” Eliza asked, glancing over her shoulder at her daughter with a sharp look on her face. “What’s happening in five days?”

     

                Waving dismissively, Alex shrugged as she toyed with her radio, a pucker between her eyebrows. “Nothing.”

     

                “They’re getting closer,” Kara continued, her stomach knotting, her heart rate picking up as her shoulders went taut. “Alex … get away from the door.”

     

                “Sit down. Mom, can you finish up? Please.”

     

                “Alex,” Kara shouted. “Now.”

     

                The door burst open as Alex started to reply and she pushed off the wall, lips parting in surprise as she watched her colleagues file inside, riot shields strapped to left arms, stun batons armed, a few of them glowing a nasty green with kryptonite. Face crumpling with confusion, Alex started to demand an explanation before she was cut off by the tip of an electrified baton jamming into the gap between her Kevlar vest and the top of her cargo pants. 

     

                A ragged sound of pain escaped her as her knees buckled and Kara grabbed Eliza, moving quickly without the red sun lamps impeding her ability, putting her back to the doctor and herding her back towards the far wall as the guards filed in. Kara counted ten of them and they quickly overwhelmed the small confines of the medical bay, shields up as they fanned out on either side of the padded table. Alex let out another sharp cry as she fought back, batons slamming into her as she unholstered her gun and fired off two shots before it was kicked out of her grasp. 

     

                Running forward, glad she was allowed to be uncuffed inside the medical bay, Kara vaulted the table and slammed her feet into the back of a guard. He went flying at the impact, his shield colliding with the shields of two other guards as they went down in a tangle of limbs and gear. Grasping the top of another shield, Kara landed a square punch on the jaw of another guard, hearing the sickening crack of breaking bones as she shattered the entire thing with what little power she had. One of the batons whacked across her back and Kara heaved at the feeling of white-hot pain lancing through her, buckling beneath the wave of weakness, and she threw herself forward, catching one of the guards around the legs and taking her down.

     

                Another man came at her, catching her across the face with a kryptonite baton, veins of green webbing across her cheek as she choked on the agony, and Kara looked up, blue eyes smouldering with annoyance as she grabbed his hand in her grasp and twisted sharply. Blanching at the cracking of the bones as she squeezed tightly, Kara let him go and climbed to her feet, blinking owlishly as she hunched her shoulders, shrinking in on herself.

     

                Kara was always reluctant to fight, a passive person unless pushed to it, and she knew she could endure a lot of pain, and would heal just fine given enough time, but she couldn’t abide people she cared about being hurt. She watched as Alex took another fist to the face and then squared her shoulders wading into the middle of the fray, confused as to why Alex was facing the brunt of the beating. Grabbing a man by the scruff of his neck, Kara tossed him aside like a ragdoll and repeated it with two more agents. One of them was a small woman she recognised as Maggie.

     

                Breaking a baton in half with her bare hands, Kara tossed it aside and then punched through the plexiglass of a riot shield to grab a woman by the throat, squeezing tightly until she went limp, unconscious. They were still overwhelmed though, the guards too numerous and violent despite their broken bones as they relentlessly fought against them. And then they shocked her with her collar, the pain of green kryptonite suffusing her, a larger dose than the batons held as it brought Kara to her knees, turning a shocking shade of grey as she reached up to grip the collar, a whimper escaping her.

     

                Staggering to her feet again, pinned in by three of the guards as her head spun, Kara knocked over the trolley of gauze and cotton swabs and medical instruments, the clattering of metal joining in with the cacophony of overlapping shouts. Her breaths were shallow and frantic and she scrambled to her feet, resisting the urge to clap her hands over her eyes, overwhelmed and overstimulated, before two guards prodded her with their batons and the collar wiped her out again. The third guard wrestled her down and Kara rolled onto her back, pinning the man beneath the weight of her as she gritted her teeth, tendons in her neck going taut. 

     

                Kicking a kneecap sideways, Kara rolled over and managed to crawl beneath the padded table and out the other side, throwing herself into the back of someone’s knees and taking them down. Alex was fighting her own battle against the ordinarily armed guards, blood streaming from her mouth and nose, spitting curses as she punched and kicked and refused to give in. Dragging her to her feet, Kara touched a hand to her friend’s bleeding chin and turned to take a shield to the face, immovable as she held her ground against the harmless attempt against her. Gearing up for another wave of assault, they both knew they were in deep shit, although Kara was still at a loss as to why Alex had been caught in the middle of it.

     

                “Ah, ah,” Maggie said, holding Eliza tightly by the throat, the barrel of her gun pressed to her temple. “None of that.”

     

                Alex and Kara both paused, backed up together as they drew in frantic breaths, eyes darting around to take stock of things. When Alex’s eyes landed on her ex and her mother, she threw herself forward in a panicked dash to help when two guards intercepted her, one’s fist catching her square in the eye, the other’s arms wrapping around her waist as he picked her clean up off her feet and wrapped his other arm around her throat, pinning her back to his chest.

     

                “Don’t you fucking touch her,” Alex snarled, fighting against the tight grip of the man holding her steady.

     

                “Stand down, Agent Danvers,” Maggie drawled.

     

                Kara sagged against the wall as another surge of kryptonite wracked her, pure agony screwing her eyes shut as her neck felt shredded from it. The room was still and tense, prisoner, guard and doctor all silent in their fear and confusion as the guards staggered to their feet, nursing broken bones, bloody noses, and shattered gear. Two of them hoisted an unconscious one up between them and filed out and Kara could see six more guards in the hallway, guns unholstered, legs spread apart as they waited expectedly. 

     

                Four guards grabbed her arms then, dragging her away from the wall and getting her face-down on the cold ground, arms twisting painfully in their sockets as her whole body felt raw. Alex was likewise strong-armed to the ground, both of them cuffed as Kara raised her head enough to watch with confusion, her stomach-wrenching with disbelief and cold fear. They knew, they had to know. She just didn’t know how they could.

     

                Shoving Eliza aside, the ashen-faced doctor catching her cheek on the edge of her desk as her legs gave out beneath her, causing Alex and Kara to struggle against their restraints, Maggie slowly crossed over to her ex. Sinking to a crouch, Maggie cupped Alex’s chin in her hand, forcing her head up at a painful angle as she smirked faintly.

     

                “Did you really think we wouldn’t find out what you were up to?”

     

                “I don’t know what you’re talking about,” Alex stiffly ground out through swollen lips, her face a mess of blood and bruises. 

     

                “Don’t you?” Maggie snorted. “Well … we’ll see about that.”

     

                She pushed herself to her feet again and glanced around the room dismissively before lazily tucking her thumbs into the loops of her belt. “Take Doctor Danvers and Prisoner KZ64 to holding cells. Prisoner AD89 is wanted in the Deputy’s office.”

     

                “Prisoner?” Eliza choked out, her eyes wide with fear for her daughter as she crouched near her desk, passive and quiet until now. “Alex-”

     

                “Quiet,” Maggie snapped at her as the guards leapt into action, dragging Alex to her feet. 

     

                Eliza climbed to her feet, face slack with panic but squaring her shoulders as she opened her mouth, outraged. She grabbed Maggie’s arm as she started to berate her, plead with her, and another guard stepped in to backhand her across the mouth, forcing a choked sound of worry from Kara as she watched from the corner of her eye, pinned to the floor with kryptonite coursing through her, keeping her controlled. 

     

                Boots squeaking on the floor as she fought against their inevitable advantage of size and strength, Alex was towed towards the door. “Mom. Mom, it’s fine. Don’t do anything. Mom.”

     

                Her shouts trailed off once she was out in the hallway and Kara was hauled to her feet next, locking her muscles to make herself heavier, taking six guards to get her standing and four of them to stop her from sagging back to the floor. Only the flinching jab of the green kryptonite batons forced her muscles slack as the surprising jolt periodically caught her off-guard. 

     

                The slow step of Maggie’s boots approached and Kara shook her long, bedraggled hair out of her face before she stared down the shorter woman. Half a foot separated them but as Maggie’s lips twitched with sneering amusement, Kara felt anger flash through her, her vision narrowing as she saw red.

     

                “Do it. I dare you,” Maggie goaded her. “Give me a reason to put you down like a dog.”

     

                Hesitating for the briefest moment, Kara’s mouth thinned and she nodded to herself before standing straight, jerking her head back and then slamming it into Maggie’s nose in a small act of defiance, knowing anything more would see her riddled with green bullets. It broke easily beneath the hardness of Kara’s skull and the shorter woman started to sag, shock widening her brown eyes as she grasped for consciousness. Blood sluiced down her chin and another guard steadied her before she gave Kara a look of pure hatred and slapped her harmlessly across the face. 

     

                Biting back the bitter urge to laugh, Kara just stared at Maggie, watching her scramble for the reins of power seized from Alex and handed off to her. She wasn’t sure if it was the long-term side-effect of being locked up in the prison, a whistleblower detective exiled miles beneath the sea as punishment, or just her personal vendetta against Alex for their failed relationship that caught Kara in the crossfire because of the guard’s fondness for her, but Maggie had always disliked Kara. And now she was in a prime position to do as she pleased without the veneer of protection Alex had provided.

     

                But Kara’s headbutt had gotten her good and, a moment later, the guard hissed through her teeth and waved a hand dismissively, embarrassment staining her cheeks a furious pink as she pinched the bridge of her broken nose and winced. “Get her out of my sight. Now.”

     

                Kara didn’t resist as she was taken to a holding cell, propelled through the prison and then forced into her straitjacket and strapped down to the bed in the cell they kept for their most dangerous prisoners. Staring up at the concrete ceiling speckled with mould, Kara strained her ears, trying to tune out the relentless noise of the prison as she sought out the voices she was listening for.

     

                “I’d start talking if I were you. I don’t want to drag the Warden in to deal with you if I don’t have to.”

     

                “Do it,” Alex spat back at Lucy. “It makes no difference to me.”

     

                “It can be easy or hard. Up to you, Danvers. Just know I gave you the option.”

     

                “Go to hell. You want to freeze me out and have them jump me in the middle of a shift and expect me to play along like a good girl? Fuck you.”

     

                “Don’t play innocent. I have enough evidence here to put a bullet in you and send your body to the incinerators. No one will care - except maybe your mom and Kelly. But no one will stop me either, not even them. I don’t want to do that, so … start talking.”

     

                Kara closed her eyes, swallowing thickly, feeling nauseous and faint as she lay strapped to the bed, silently willing the guard to just tell them what they wanted to know. She didn’t know what evidence they thought they had on Alex, what her supposed crime had been, if she’d been breaking any laws the unlawful followed but Kara baulked at the thought of them killing Alex. That brooding teenager who’d exasperatedly helped teach her English over their cobbled-together school lessons, the only two kids in the prison. She’d known Alex longer than she’d known her own parents, knew her better than she knew anyone else, knew the bad parts of her and the insecurities and fears of the guard who’d always been too scared to do anything but what she was told, her mother’s life hanging over her, and then Kara’s too. 

     

                And now she was in deep shit and Kara couldn’t help but think that it was her fault. In her bones, she had the sneaking suspicion that it was her fault for being unwilling to leave the prison without the people who’d shown her a sliver of kindness, forcing Lena’s hand to involve the guard to get them out. And Alex had reluctantly agreed after much back and forth and contempt, mistrust and anger at the whole situation, at Lena for filling Kara’s head with the notion of a freedom they all wanted but weren’t ambitious enough to achieve themselves.

     

                “-telling you shit. Whatever you think you have, you don’t. It’s just Maggie’s petty vendetta against me and you know it.”

     

                “An interesting theory but you’re wrong, actually. Maggie found out about an hour ago when you were stripped of your position and it was handed to her.”

     

                “Wha- then who? ”

     

                Lucy was quiet for a long minute, Kara’s mouth dry as she listened, her body coiled with tension, heart pounding in her chest. “Prisoner ME62.”

     

                “Prisoner ME62? Mon-El? You’re going to believe a word that comes out of that piece of shit’s mouth?” Alex asked, outraged.

     

                “You know, I’d maybe think it was personal, given the known history of warfare and hatred between Krypton and Daxam, if he’d thrown Prisoner KZ64 under the bus but … well, it wasn’t just against her. It was Prisoner LL93, mostly, and you. And what motivation would he have to lie about the two of you?”

     

                “What could he know?” Alex dismissively scoffed.

     

                “A lot,” Lucy lightly replied. “He might not be on par with our Kryptonian but his hearing’s a right sight more sensitive than a human’s. Sensitive enough to hear your whispered plans. You know, it really pays to have a rat. Especially one the employees don’t know about.”

     

                “He’s lying,” Alex snapped, voice flushed with anger, wavering slightly at the doubt seeded in her mind.

     

                “No, he’s not. Why don’t you tell me about the snowsuits?”

     

                “I needed a new one for top-deck supply deliveries.”

     

                “You checked out one but the stocktake shows we’re down four . They were found in your room. I’m struggling to find why one person would need so many for one day a month.”

     

                “That’s your proof?”

     

                “A piece of it. How about you swapping your supply delivery shift with Vasquez? Odd to need a new snowsuit when you’re not even going to be at the next one.”

     

                “My mom’s booked me in for a blood test. You know how mothers are.”

     

                There was a momentary pause. “No, your mother has Prisoner KZ64 booked in for her monthly checkup. And Kelly has Prisoner LL93 booked in for another session. Funny, my guards are just about to disrupt their current session. Any reason why there would be a need for another one in five days?”

     

                “I can’t presume to know what goes on in their private sessions. Maybe she’s suicidal; she has attempted before.”

     

                “She’s on a slow-release sedative; she spends half her days sleeping now, thanks to me. How about you tell me about the blueprints?”

     

                “What blueprints?”

     

                Lucy laughed, the sound warm with amusement, and Kara’s face spasmed with worry as she listened to their plans unravel. It didn’t matter how much Alex denied it - they knew . And now they were utterly fucked with their insider likely to be joining her and Lena on the cell block.

     

                “Do yourself a favour, Alex, and just confess. I don’t like making threats. You know that. I’m trying to do you a favour here.”

     

                “Shove your favour up your ass.”

     

                A weary sigh followed the slow scuffing of boots. Kara strained to hear the sound of a chair dragged back and the barely audible tone of the landline buttons being pushed, three staticky rings preceding the honeyed, indecipherable voice that picked up the call. Lucy cleared her throat softly.

     

                “Sorry to disturb you, Warden. It’s about the matter I discussed with you earlier. Yes, Agent Danvers, ma’am. Nothing so far. How would you like to proceed? Yes, ma’am. Thank you.”

     

                Kara hadn’t been able to make out the faint words on the other end before the phone was hung up and she murmured to herself as she willed Alex to just tell them. She wouldn’t have cared if she got thrown under the bus, although she hoped Lena was left out of it, reassured by the strong beat of her heart a few hallways over, cooperating with the guards intruding on her session with Kelly. 

     

                Listening to the ensuing conversation circle around and around, Kara was starting to feel the lingering discomfort of the kryptonite fade away and she scrabbled for a way out of this.
