The only viable solution in her mind was she fought herself free from the steel bands holding her down, shed the straitjacket and went on a brutal killing spree that left them able to flee the prison in five days’ time. Anything short of a bloodbath wiping out the armed guards would leave them vulnerable to being trapped there indefinitely.

     

                The sound of the Warden’s heartbeat drifted closer from the depths of the prison and the warren of offices and administrators keeping track of budgets, databases and pushing prisoner paperwork around. Kara had only met the Warden a handful of times, finding Haley stern and stubborn as a rock, and entirely apathetic towards the prisoners. Listening to the squeak of a door opening and the sound of chair legs scraping against the floor, Alex’s heart rate picking up as panic set in, Kara twisted against her bonds. She didn’t care if she couldn’t get them out, if she was killed in the process, but she couldn’t stay strapped to a bed while people were hurt. It wasn’t in her, no matter the circumstances of her relationship with Alex, that it was warped by the ache inside Kara to have someone in her corner. Whatever loyalty had been forged in the years of loneliness inside the prison, it counted for something.

     

                “Agent Danvers,” Haley coolly greeted her employee.

     

                “Warden.”

     

                There was a moment of silence and then a weary sigh. “I expected more loyalty from someone who’s been here for such a long time.”

     

                “With all due respect, ma’am,” Alex scoffed, “you have no clue about my loyalties. You have no idea what you’re talking about. I have been good at my job, I’ve never once shied away from orders. Is this what my years of service gets me?”

     

                “I have no use for people I can’t trust.”

     

                “This place is filled with corrupt agents; you can’t trust anyone . Least of all a prisoner.”

     

                “I’m not here to discuss the semantics on why I should or should not believe you. The fact of the matter is I don’t - the evidence is … damning. What I want from you now is the truth. I think you’ll find yourself very cooperative. Bring her.”

     

                Kara went rigid at the sound of a chair scuffing, a door squeaking open and the drum of footsteps as a retinue of guards escorted Alex, the Warden and the Deputy down the hallway. Tracking them, Kara listened to the familiar heartbeats as she tracked who was present and who was not. They filed into another room, one Kara had never been inside and couldn’t visualise as she listened, and it was a few tense minutes of silence before she heard two heartbeats escorted down the hallway and into the room, filling her with dread.

     

                “Danvers, Olsen, thank you for joining us. Now, perhaps Agent Danvers will be more cooperative with your presence and we can get this over and done with quickly. Vasquez, chain them both to the chairs.”

     

                “Let them go,” Alex breathlessly demanded, her fear audible in her voice, even if Kara couldn’t hear the way her heart started to race. “They have nothing to do with this, you sick fuck.”

     

                “That remains to be seen. Unless you’re going to start talking.”

     

                “I don’t know what you’re talking about.”

     

                There was the sharp sound of a clean slap punctuating Alex’s objection, and Kara listened to the round of swearing and complaints from the three women tied to their chairs, unsure which one had been on the receiving end of it. All three of their heart rates were elevated, all three of them angered by the treatment. Kara knew Alex wouldn’t last long with the threat of harm to Kelly or Eliza hanging over her.

     

                “The next one will be with a closed fist.”

     

                “Fuck you,” Alex spat.

     

                Kara strained against her bonds at the meaty sound of the punch, hearing the ragged sound of pain that she knew came from Eliza without a word being said. Metal ground as she strained against the bands, twisting and wriggling as she listened to Alex do the same, shouting obscenities, guttural threats and breathless sobs that caught Kara off-guard, listening to her friend’s composure slip.

     

                “Mom. Mom!”

     

                “I’m fine,” Eliza slurred and Kara’s eyes prickled with tears as she felt so helpless.

     

                “Don’t you lay a finger on her again. I swear to God , you even dare-”

     

                Struggling, feeling the rivets loosen, the screech of metal filling the cell, Kara heard a sharp cry of pain from Kelly this time, adrenaline flooding through her as she managed to cobble together enough strength to break free of the restraint across her chest. Shifting down to free her head from the one strapped across her brow, Kara sat upright and jerked her arms away from her chest, tearing through the heavy canvas of the straitjacket before she grabbed the steel across her thighs and tore it apart, following suit with the one across her ankles.

     

                Staggering to her feet, her heartbeat going wild, the stress of listening to people she deemed friends getting beaten for the sake of it, knowing regardless of what was said, Alex would be locked up in a best-case scenario. Worst case … well, Kara wouldn’t sit by and let them go that far without trying to stop them. She didn’t even make it to the door before an alarm started wailing, the blinking red light from the corner of the room watching her closely, and she fell to her knees on the cold concrete floor as the collar sent a fresh wave of kryptonite through her. Resenting the fact that if she’d been miles above in the open air with the waves of yellow radiation, Kara wouldn’t be brought so low by the dose of kryptonite, she fought against it until ghastly green gas started pumping out of a vent overhead.

     

                Coughing as it seared her throat, tears streaming down her cheeks, Kara scrabbled at the concrete, gouging furrows in the crumbling foundations. Feeling as if her skin was bubbling away from her flesh, Kara’s whole body went taut as she shut her eyes, grit her teeth, each breath like fire until she couldn’t help but cough, retching and heaving as it got into her lungs, making her feel sick. Grey and weak, she pressed her cheek into the gritty concrete as her strength fled her, vision dimming as she battled for consciousness. 

     

                Kara didn’t know how long she was on the floor, how long she’d existed in that haze of pain, tuning out everything else, only she was listless and confused when the heavy door scraped open and multiple sets of hands hauled her up. Muttered grumbles at the ruined bed fell on faintly ringing ears and she was manoeuvred like a ragdoll into another straitjacket before they lifted her back onto the bed as she twisted helplessly, and was restrained with chains this time. Shackles bit into her wrists and ankles as she was spread out, kryptonite in the cuffs chafing her skin raw until it bled from the effort of her struggles.

     

                They left her alone to endure the agony and Kara knew that this time no one would end it, no one would stop them from doing it, berate them for the harshness of it. Alex may have been a thin veneer of protection but she’d done what little she could to minimise the pain and keep the punishments short. This time, Kara was alone in her cell, struggling to tune out the noise of the prison to zone back in on the three women trapped inside a different room, dimly aware of Lena’s heartbeat from back on their cell block.

     

                “We can do this all day, Alex,” Haley wearily said. “You can put a stop to it very quickly. Just tell us what you were up to. Give us names and details and the three of you walk out of here.”

     

                “They had nothing to do with it. I swear. No, no, don’t. Please. I mean it.”

     

                “Nothing to do with what?”

     

                “The plan,” Alex raggedly sobbed, her breaths short and fast, defeated and agonised. “The plan to escape. It was me. I did it. Me, not them.”

     

                Haley was silent for a moment and the breath caught in Kara’s throat as she bit back a groan at Alex’s confession. It had been inevitable but she hated the thought of what came next for her. Swallowing thickly, Kara tightly squeezed her eyes shut, tensed expectantly. 

     

                “I don’t believe you.”

     

                “I’m telling you the truth,” Alex spat, her voice low with anger. 

     

                “Five snowsuits. Five people. You expect me to believe two of them weren’t for your mother and girlfriend?”

     

                Alex was silent and Kara heard the sound of another beating, the grunt of pain, the soft snarl of warning as the guards laid into her, an encouraging threat.

     

                “Talk. Now.”

     

                “They were but I didn’t tell them about it. Why would I? They would’ve tried to stop me.”

     

                “And who were the other two for?”

     

                “Don’t do it,” Kara whispered to herself in the quiet cell, a pleading ache in her chest as she willed Alex to be silent. “Don’t do it.”

     

                “Prisoner LL93,” Alex confessed. “You know how smart she is. She’s the mind behind it.”

     

                “And you’re just the inside man?”

     

                “Yes.”

     

                “Who else? Who’s the fifth? KZ64? She seems the likeliest; I'm well aware of your fondness for her.”

     

                Going limb against her bonds, Kara let out a weary sigh, knowing it was over. There was no coming back from it; they’d have her taken away from Lena, put Alex in a different cell block too. They’d never be allowed around each other to collude for another escape plan. Tears stung her eyes as she felt anger well up at Alex naming Lena, but then what else could she have done? To keep her own family safe, she had done what she had to and Kara let out a pent-up sob as she steeled herself for the final nail in the coffin of her own imprisonment. They would likely leave her to rot in the pitifully small isolation cell for a month before they remembered her existence.

     

                Alex let out a bitter, ragged laugh, verging on hysterical. "Her? Why would I help loose one of those freaks out into the world? No, it wasn't her."

     

                "Then who?"

     

                “I don't-”

     

                At the sound of a guard laying into Alex again, this time Kara willed her to just say it, to name her. It wouldn’t matter now; none of them would be getting out in five days.

     

                “Maggie,” Alex thickly exclaimed, breathing raggedly, a mewling cry escaping her before she sighed heavily. “It was Maggie.”

     

                “Maggie? Sawyer?”

     

                There was a tense moment and then Haley snapped her fingers and the sound of chains clinking filled the silence. 

     

                “Vasquez, you have command. Take them back to their rooms. Lock them in. I’ll speak to them both tomorrow. Clean her up and process her. I want her on the same cell block as LL93 so we can keep an eye on them. Two humans won’t cause much trouble. Someone fetch Sawyer for me. Oh, and sort out KZ64 while you’re at it.”

     

                The gathering of heartbeats dispersed and Kara was left reeling from the turn it had all taken, her eyes roaming around the room restlessly as she found herself stunned by the lack of accountability for her own part. She wanted to curse Alex out for covering for her, for not letting her take the fall for it as well, just as complicit as the others and able to withstand the punishment better than a human ever could. Even the kryptonite was durable and was only temporary; broken bones would hurt longer. 

     

                Listening to footsteps approach, Kara was still and helpless as she listened to the groaning of the hinges and the screech of the door hauled open before four guards in their tactical gear came to free her. Unchained and then appropriately cuffed again, Kara was dragged out of the cell and towed towards her cell on Block D. Brought to the airlock doors, she saw the guards hauling Alex along with her, shivering in the same grey prison uniform Kara was wearing, hugging her arms to herself as she choked on breathless sobs, a stricken look on her face as her eyes met Kara’s.

     

                Devastation softened Kara’s features as her lips parted, bloodshot eyes defeated as she swallowed the lump in her throat. Anger rushed in then, belated and not entirely directed at Alex but mostly at the unfairness of the situation. She’d thought she was getting out, she believed Lena when she confidently told her that, thought she’d be feeling that invigorating touch of the sun on her starved skin, would be sitting on the beach with the birds, filled with so much life and power. 

     

                Cheeks turning a blotchy red, Kara shrugged out of the touch of the guards escorting her and stormed towards Alex, her arms chained behind her back but the threat of her hidden strength, hidden powers, making the ex-guard quickly back up against the hallway wall. The other guards all shouted over one another as they held batons and unholstered guns, taking an offensive stance as they trained them on Kara’s back.

     

                “Why didn’t you lie?” Kara ground out between clenched teeth, her eyes stinging.

     

                Guilt and shame crossed Alex’s mess of a face as she hung her head, swallowing audibly. “I’m sorry. I’m so sorry. I didn’t have a choice, I had to.”

    Chapter 15

                The next morning, they were given their dismal breakfast and she heard the guards harshly instructing Alex to eat her portion. Despite their escape completely gutted, all hope gone in the blink of an eye, Lena couldn’t help but find enjoyment in the ex-guard’s discomfort at finding herself on the inside of a cell, eating the cold, congealed oats, the stale bread, withered apples. It was a bitter sort of amusement and Lena held back her snarky comments at Alex getting a taste of what she’d helped dish out but she still harboured that prickle of satisfaction as Alex refused to let it go.

     

                All of the day before, once she’d gotten over the shock of finding herself in a cell, Alex had made herself a nuisance the same way Lena had when she’d first arrived, shouting obscenities, cursing out the guards, pounding on the barrier and subjected to rounds of electrocution from her new collar, until Lena could hear her retching on the floor from the exertion. She had to hand it to Alex though, she was cold enough to not cry, no broken sobs escaping her as she beat her hands bloody on the forcefield, her anger fueling her instead of pity.

     

                Still, none of them got any rest that night and Lena poked at her own breakfast with glum disinterest, a depressive fog stealing over her as her motivation to keep going, to hold onto the plan and the approaching date of their escape. Kara hadn’t moved from her bed since she’d curled up on it the day before, Lena’s quiet coaxing unable to convince her to speak to her, to sign back and forth with the full story of what had happened. There were gaps in what Lena had cobbled together and she hated to not know things.

     

                After splattering her breakfast all over her cell, Alex stewed in her anger as she fell silent, and Lena knew that feeling all too well. The shock settling in, the horror at the idea of this being her new reality. She wondered if she’d been subjected to her mother’s needles and questions, whether Eliza had done the same to her daughter that she’d been forced to do to everyone else. It felt vindicating somehow, even though Lena didn’t wish it on anyone. She hadn’t thought they’d end up here, with Alex in a cell beside her but it was a form of karma even if it fucked them all over. 

     

                When the guards came to collect their trays, Maggie worked her way down the line and Lena stiffened at the sound of Alex’s tray being kicked against the forcefield, clattering noisily to the ground. “You-” Alex snarled.

     

                “You fucking told them it was me?” Maggie interrupted, seething. 

     

                “You really think I wouldn’t after you laid hands on my mom?”

     

                “The doctor should have-”

     

                “Don’t you fucking dare tell me what she should have done. You’re a piece of shit, you know that? Still holding onto your grudge because I reported you-”

     

                “You reported me for what they did to her but now look who’s inside a cell,” Maggie sneered. “And your plan backfired anyway because they knew it wasn’t me. A long talk with the Warden ironed that out. But good luck keeping her safe from inside here; your little pet is fair game now. I know she was the other one - the one you were planning on helping escape. I wonder how the rest of your inmates feel, knowing you were going to free your beloved Kryptonian and leave them here to rot. Well, now you can rot alongside them.”

     

                Alex let out a caustic laugh, slapping her palm against the forcefield. “And you’ll rot in here too, same as the rest of us.”

     

                “Prisoner AD89, away from the forcefield,” Maggie drawled. “Back against the wall.”

     

                There was a brief standoff followed by the sound of Alex’s frantic breaths and writhing form on the floor, followed by a quick beating and the collection of her tray before Maggie moved to Lena’s cell with Winn pushing the cart. She didn’t argue as she backed up to the far wall and watched them collect her finished breakfast, glaring daggers at them the whole time. Lena took pleasure in the faint shadows of bruises on Maggie’s face, hoping the Warden had taken her time questioning her, even if she was off the hook in the end.

     

                Once the trays were collected, they started taking prisoners for their showers. Lena was taken with Andrea and Alex, the three humans on the block deemed a small threat, even if one of them was an ex-guard. They weren’t as slack with security as they usually were, bringing three female guards for the three of them, standing around as they let them have their brief, freezing showers before handing over their clean set of old clothes. The guards had no love for their old coworker though, giving her a threadbare towel to dry off with, dropping her clothes onto the wet floor where the run-off from the showers pooled, pushing her around roughly.

     

                Pressing her lips together, Lena didn’t offer any objections and she felt almost indifferent to watching the torment, knowing she’d suffered worse and Alex had similarly done little to stop them. At least when the guard had interceded, her coworkers had backed off; all Lena would get for speaking up was a beating of her own. 

     

                They were taken back to their cell as Kara was being led for her own shower, eyes still red, her face pale and an aloof demeanour to her as she jerked her chin up, looking away as their paths crossed in the hallway. Lena was left staring at her with a yearning look of concern, and Alex was desperately pleading.

     

                “Kara-”

     

                Shooting her a dark look, full of wounded betrayal, Kara’s mouth thinned and the guards told Alex to be quiet before moving them along. Lena didn’t know what had happened and was quick to lay the blame on the guard, worry for her friend filling her as she was walked past Mon-El’s empty cell, to the end of the row, and locked in her cell.

     

                Hesitating a moment, she crawled beneath her cot, wriggling closer to the narrow airflow gap. “Hey!”

     

                Listening to the scraping sound of Alex shuffling under her own cot,  Lena waited until she was close enough. “What?”

     

                “What did you do to her?” Lena quietly demanded, her voice stiff with anger.

     

                Alex choked on a laugh, the sound broken and hollow. “Oh. I gave them your name.”

     

                “Oh.”

     

                There was a brief pause and Lena didn’t know what to say next, confused but not surprised. If she was in Alex’s position, she probably would have given the guard up too if she’d had a family she needed to protect. If they’d held Kara against her, Lena would have done the same to spare her friend any pain.

     

                “You understand why, don’t you?” Alex breathlessly asked, a rough, pleading edge to her low voice. “I had to tell them. I had to tell them it was us because … we can’t do anything in here anyway. Now it’s up to them.”

     

                Lena’s heart was in her throat and she swallowed thickly, replying after a moment. “I know. They’re going to be watching them, though. We won’t be able to plan another escape, not for months at least, or-“

     

                “It’s still on. We’ll lay low for the next month and-”

     

                “No,” Lena slowly replied. “We can’t, we- , Alex . You think we’re going to pull this shit off when you’re in here?”

     

                “ She knows what to do. I told her what to do if something happened to me,” Alex interrupted. “I made sure of it.”

     

                “Wha-“

     

                “We get one shot. We’re not wasting it, we’re just- we’re just delaying it.”

     

                Licking her lips, Lena’s forehead furrowed as she tried to process things. “But Kara-“

     

                “Is mad I gave you up. She would never do that unless it was to save your life and I- I get that but … this is bigger than feelings. I made a logical call. For me, she knows I’d protect my own family first, so she thinks it’s purely emotional but … I never gave them her name. When the moment comes … she’ll understand why.”

     

                Letting out a weary sigh, Lena closed her eyes, her anger growing. “She wasn’t supposed to be the mastermind. We’re not using her to steamroll our way out of here; she’ll get killed for it, are you out of your fucking mind?”

     

                “Quiet,” Alex hissed. “You didn’t think I would leave my own life and future in the hands of me getting you out of your cell, did you? It’s a good plan, I’ll admit that much, but risky as hell to rely on one person making it possible.”

     

                “Your mom, Kelly, they can’t pull this off,” Lena said through her teeth, frustration welling up inside. “You’re going to get them both killed trying to get the three of us out of here. You should have told me if you were making other plans.”

     

                “It’s the same plan,” Alex quietly snapped. “It’s fine. I just- I tweaked it.”

     

                “You tweaked it and we could all end up dead.”

     

                “I know it’s asking a lot but … trust me. You do your part, you figure out how to fly the chopper and get us to a safe house, and I’ll do my part and get us out of here. We’ll stick to the plan. Just … be ready.”

     

                Lena scoffed, the sound contemptuous as she shifted away from the wall. “Trust you? No, I don’t trust you at all.”

     

                “Lena-”

     

                “Welcome to your new reality. You’re in for a rude awakening but … well, once you learn to take it, you’ll feel right at home,” Lena scornfully told her. “Just don’t hold your breath on getting out of here. We had one shot and you blew it.”

     

                “I didn’t do shit,” Alex hissed. “Mon-El, that’s who- the sly bastard was eavesdropping the whole damn time.”

     

                Lena went still, her mind reeling as she tried to catch up, trying to make sense of things. But she was so tired, rubbing her forehead as the stress of the last day caught up to her, things not making any sense, unsure of who to trust. Without a word, she ducked out from under the cot and sat on her bed, staring at the damp-stained wall of her cell until the block doors hissed open and Kara was filed back in. 

     

                Waiting until she was settled, the block quiet as the prisoners dwelled in the tense atmosphere of having a guard in their midst, Lena climbed off her cot and took the blanket and pillow with her, sitting on the latter and draping the scratchy wool over her shoulders as she kept her hands free. It took Kara a moment to notice her but the alien sat up, looking so sad that it made Lena’s chest ache as she raised her hands.

     

                Are you okay?

     

                Fine.

     

                Did they hurt you?

     

                A little.

     

                What happened?

     

                They knew. He told them.  

     

                Kara gestured down the end of the cell block, towards Mon-El’s cell, confirming what Alex had said. Mouth thinning with anger for the man, Lena swallowed thickly and nodded before Kara continued.

     

                Alex told them you planned it.

     

                I did. It is my plan. Do not be angry with her. She has a family to protect. And she protected you.

     

                I wish she gave them my name instead of yours.

     

                They would make it harder for us to get you out. You are dangerous. They are scared.

     

                Kara’s chin wobbled slightly and she hesitated, head ducked, before signing. Me too.

     

                I will keep you safe, Lena signed, her expression severe, a stubborn set to her jaw.

     

                I am not scared for myself. I am scared for you. I need to keep you safe.

     

                I can keep myself safe. I will be okay.

     

                I will tear them all apart if they hurt you.

     

                The look on Kara’s face made Lena’s stomach lurch at the intensity of it. She didn’t doubt for a second that the peaceable alien who had placidly endured almost two decades of imprisonment would snap and bring the prison down if she had to. She just didn’t know why Kara hadn’t done it before, ripped the place apart and punched her way through to the sea beyond so she could swim to safety. If anyone could survive the Arctic waters, it was an alien that was invulnerable to practically everything . Of course, she knew that Kara was a pacifist unless pushed to that breaking point, but surely there had been so many breaking points over such a long period of time.

     

                You could have done that when they hurt you.

     

                I had no reason to think it would be better outside. Not until Alex was here and told me about Earth. Then I could not leave them behind.

     

                You should have.

     

                They are my friends.

     

                Lena scoffed to herself, frustration welling up inside her as she closed her eyes and exhaled sharply through her nose before composing herself. They are not your friends. If they cared about you, they would have helped you escape a long time ago. 

     

                She tried. Once. The Warden was the Deputy’s father at the time. It went badly. Alex framed him for it. They shot him. Lucy does not know it was Alex who got her locked up in here. They brought in Haley as the new Warden. That is why she was so against helping you.

     

                That is not the only reason. She is a coward.

     

                Yes. We are all scared.

     

                That still is not a good excuse. We will all die in here anyway. Why not try?

     

                She is trying now.

     

                It may be too late.

     

                There is still hope.

     

                Hope is for fools.

     

                Then I will be a fool who hopes for us all.

     

                Unfolding her legs and climbing to her feet, Kara stalked back over to her cot and Lena could tell that she’d annoyed her friend, gotten beneath her skin, purposely argumentative when it served no purpose. Kara was too idealistic though, too trusting and willing to overlook the flaws of others in an effort to find the light in the dark oubliette of the prison. 

     

     

                The next few weeks passed by in a drab grey blur of monotony, their days filled with walks, showers, and meals that Lena could only bring herself to eat to keep up her strength. She was denied the chance to have another session with Kelly, her next medical appointment with Eliza was postponed indefinitely and the social was cancelled with the smug announcement to the cell block that it was thanks to Lena and Alex. Everyone on the block was restless being cooped up without the relief of an hour of Jeopardy! on the boxy TV, absentminded colouring with the waxy crayons or rereading the same books or having the opportunity to congregate in small groups and talk freely instead of yelling back and forth. 

     

                Talk of escaping was scarce between the three women, Lena unwilling to put any faith in Alex’s apparent contingency plan, which relied on Kelly getting them out to complete the plan they had set out before. If it wasn’t for Kara, Lena wouldn’t have entertained the idea at all, and would have cobbled together a new plan for just the two of them, leaving Alex behind to suffer the lengthy imprisonment, regardless of Kara’s desire to take her with them. Lena knew that Kara could be given a pardon by the government and allowed to walk freely out of the prison and she wouldn’t do it without the people she cared about. It was almost a miracle she hadn’t asked Lena to bring the whole cell block with them. 

     

                Her bitterness towards Alex dimmed over that first week but conversation was scarce between them, and not only because of their mutual dislike for one another but because they were very aware of the ears around them now. The others who could hear their whispered conversations had stayed out of it so far, content to let them try their plan and either die trying or get out and let the world know they were all there. It was a way to potentially be freed without risking their own necks and Lena couldn’t fault them for that. At the very least, J’onn and Querl had kept quiet about it, unlike Mon-El, who was the one they were concerned about eavesdropping.

     

                Kara was on her daily walk when Lena crawled beneath the cot, listening to the hacking cough of the guard next door as the damp worked its way into Alex’s lungs. She didn’t feel too badly about it but it was a potential problem if - and that was a big if - the plan was on for the end of the month, as Alex had initially insisted it was after last month’s attempt had failed. A sick prisoner towing along with them wouldn’t make for an easy escape if Alex had pneumonia and could barely stand on her own two feet. Her worry was warranted; there were only three days until the next delivery.

     

                “Hey,” Lena called through the hole.

     

                Alex was beneath her cot a minute later, the rattles of her breaths louder as only the concrete wall separated them. “What?”

     

                “Ask them for antibiotics for your chest.”

     

                “Come on,” Alex laughed, “I know you’re not that naive.”

     

                “You’ll be no good to anyone if- if what you said was true.”

     

                “I’ll be fine.”

     

                “Right. Well … you sound like shit.”

     

                “Surely you’re not fussing over me. You wouldn’t give a shit if I kicked the bucket here and now.”

     

                Lena let out a slight laugh, mouth twisting wryly. “You’re right, I wouldn’t. Still, it’s a shit feeling. Speaking from experience.”

     

                “I thought you would have loved me getting to experience it. And only for a month so far, so … not even as long as you.”

     

                “Oh, I’m enjoying it a lot. Karma really bit you on the ass and I’d be having the time of my life if you were stuck in here and I was back home in my nice penthouse, warm and away from this shithole. It’s just not as satisfying when I’m also in this shithole.”

     

                Wracked by a coughing fit, Alex cleared her throat, the sound wet and sharp, and let out a frayed laugh. “There’s always hope.”

     

                They fell silent for a moment and Lena stared up at the grille of her cot as she fretted over the plan, the dreaded feeling of allowing herself to hope again. No matter what anyone said, it would never be an easy thing for her to feel. Lena’s main motivation was spite, and no amount of sedatives would take that away from her, clinging to it through the fog in her mind, even when motivation and hope evaded her. After a minute, she rolled back towards the vent.

     

                “That thing you and Maggie were talking about a few weeks ago,” Lena slowly ventured, “what was that about?”

     

                Alex was slow to reply, “what thing?”

     

                “You reported her.”

     

                “Yeah.”

     

                “For what?”

     

                There was a long pause and Lena wondered if she would reply. She knew that Alex was still there because she hadn’t heard her move away, and after a minute, the ex-guard sighed heavily.

     

                “A few of the other guards … they were slipping kryptonite into Kara’s food. Poisoning her. Not a lot but enough.” Alex cut off and let out a huff of laughter. “Kara didn’t say anything, of course , but my mom knew she was sick from her medical results. Turns out that Maggie knew they were doing it and … she didn’t stop them. When I found out what was going on, I told the Deputy and the guards got moved to a different cell block, away from her, except for Maggie because she wasn’t directly involved. She got mad at me, said that I- I shouldn’t have ratted them out. This was … eight years ago now. We were together at the time but, well, you can imagine how that went after that.”

     

                “Oh.”

     

                “I know- I know you think I’m spineless. That I just stand by and let things happen. You’re right, I do but … it’s only because I’ve been here long enough to know that there’s no changing things. I tried my best, I just- I’m not … like you. I’m not smart enough, or gullible enough like Kara. I’m sorry. I just- I’ve done the best that I could. It wasn’t much.”

     

                “No, it wasn’t,” Lena bitterly replied. “Hopefully, you’ll be out of her life for good soon enough. One way or another.”

     

                “She’ll need people-”

     

                Rankling, Lena clenched her teeth, her expression clouding. “Me. She has me. I will look after her.”

     

                Heavily sighing, Alex took a moment to reply. “I know you care about her but you’ve known her for barely a few months. She knows me, she knows my mom. Think what you want but … I wouldn’t abandon her.”

     

                “You have a fucked up way of thinking, you know that? You helped put her through all of this and you’d still keep her dependent on you like some Stockholm syndrome victim. Is it not enough for her to have suffered so much, now you’re talking about not letting her move on from it.”

     

                “You-”

     

                “I’m done talking,” Lena scornfully cut her off before moving out from under the bed.

     

                Restless, she started to pace, raking her hands through her hair as her shoulders were taut from the tension. A minute later, Alex shouted through the hole, “you’re not the only one who cares about her, you know. We’ve all known her longer than you have.”

     

                Crossing over to the bed, Lena kicked the grille, the loud clang of metal punctuating Alex’s words, the cell block seeming too still and quiet for the noise. Turning around, she paced away again and it wasn’t until Kara was brought back in, blonde hair a dull brass as it hung in a damp mess around her shoulders, falling to her waist. Her blue eyes were aching as their eyes met across the gap between their cells.

     

                Once they were alone, Lena walked over to the forcefield and stood there for a few minutes as Kara mirrored her stance, both of them staring at each other. A furrow formed between Lena’s eyebrows and she thought she should have been glad they weren’t afforded the close proximity for a private conversation; her throat was so painfully tight she wouldn’t have been able to speak.

     

                You know I care about you.

     

                I know. I care about you too.

     

                I will look after you once we are out of here.

     

                I will look after you too. All of us.

     

                It can just be us. You and me, Lena signed back, her mouth a firm line. We can go somewhere with a beach just for us. So much sunlight. Always warm. Ice cream and birds. You and me.

     

                What about your life? What about what you want to do when you are free?

     

                Lena’s face split into a wavering smile. I want a hot bath. With shampoo. Alcohol. Any kind. Even cheap. And then I want to forget this ever happened. Except for you.

     

                I will make sure you have it all. I promise.

     

                I promise too.

     

                Kara nodded, a faint smile on the corners of her lips before her eyes darted sideways to Alex’s cell before she returned her attention to Lena, her expression more solemn. Nodding again, Kara pressed her hand against the forcefield and Lena mirrored it before they retreated back to their cots.

     

                The rest of the afternoon passed by slowly and Lena’s mind was heavy with her thoughts. Everything seemed ordinary, save for the fact that it was three days until they could even attempt their next escape. Lena wasn’t sure what Alex had told Kelly, what would happen, and so after they’d finished eating their dinner and their trays had been taken away, the block was quiet as they anticipated being left alone for the rest of the evening. There was a smattering of conversation between a few of them but Lena was tired.

     

                And then the forcefield flickered.

     

                It seemed like a trick of the light at first, a glitch from the corner of Lena’s eye, and she pushed herself up onto her elbows slightly, staring at it. It was solid, still there, that telltale sheen of it penning her in. But Kara was sitting up, staring at it as well, and Lena knew she hadn’t been imagining it. Then it flickered again, blinking out of existence.

     

                Rising from her cot as caution stole over her, Lena met Kara’s eyes across the cell block as her forcefield came down as well, the entire cell block seemingly glitching as the faint disturbance in the air winked in and out of existence. Slowly walking over to it, Lena was wary as she pressed her hand against the barrier before it vanished again and her hand went through. She drew her hand back again and a second later the barrier flickered back into place as the security cameras faltered for a moment before shuddering back on.

     

                “Alex,” Lena cautiously called out. “Was this part of your plan?”

     

                “No,” the ex-guard slowly said from next door as she stood at her own barrier. A moment later, she stepped out of the cell, appearing in front of Lena’s cell. “I think this was you.”

     

                Mouth opening and closing, Lena’s heart thudded in her chest and she quickly looked at Kara. The alien was on her feet, her face a ghastly shade of red in the tint of her sun lamps, and she slowly crossed the boundary of her own cell a moment later, expression drawn with suspicion.

     

                Then the barriers died completely and Lena hurriedly stepped over the threshold of her own cell, looking back and forth between two women, a firm set to her jaw and shoulders. “It’s still three days until the next- Kara.”

     

                The other prisoners had started venturing out of their own cells and Kara’s eyes shot to Mon-El. The Daxamite was looking around cluelessly and his nonchalant arrogance quickly turned into frozen panic as he caught the attention of the Kryptonian he’d attempted to rat out. Before Lena could stop her, before she and Alex could figure out what to do, Kara squared her shoulders.

     

                “You rat,” she shouted down the length of the cell block, all heads turning towards her. “You cowardly, spineless Daxamite asshole.”

     

                He sneered, blustering anger and ego lending Mon-El a swagger as he strolled forward. “You really think I’d let a piece of shit like you get out of here before me? I’m a prince; on Daxam, you’d be the dirt on the bottom of my shoes, no good for anything but on your knees. You and that cunt of a guard.”

     

                Jerking his chin towards Alex, who stood rigid beside Lena as she anticipated the prisoners mobbing her, Mon-El curled his lip and spat on the floor. Then attempting a charming smile, he arched an eyebrow.

     

                “I’ll make you a deal; hand her over to learn her lesson and we can call it quits.”

     

                “Over my dead body,” Kara snarled.

     

                Striding towards him as he blanched, Kara shoved him hard, sending Mon-El flying ten feet into the concrete wall beside the locked doors. His shoulders cracked the concrete and he dropped into a heap at the base of the wall. Advancing on him, Kara was bristling with anger, her eyes bright with tears, and she didn’t listen to Alex’s pleading call from behind her.

     

                Knowing their time was limited, the shock collars undoubtedly ready to be deployed, although she hadn’t realised the cameras were out yet, Lena scrambled for some way to help them. If Alex was confident the plan wasn’t a complete bust yet, they could use this moment. They could use the distraction Kara was giving them to work out something. Clutching her head in her hands, Lena squeezed her eyes shut as she murmured to herself.

     

                “Come on, come on. Think.”

     

                “Are you okay?” Alex demanded, gripping Lena’s shoulders. “Don’t go crazy on me now, Luthor.”

     

                Shrugging her off, Lena’s eyelids snapped open and she ran through their options. Feeling the urgency of time being wasted, she looked around, trying to find an answer, to find some way to boost their chances of getting out. Tipping her head back as she closed her eyes again, her lips moved soundlessly as she ran through their possibilities. Opening her eyes, she stared up at the ceiling for a moment before blinking. The panels.

     

                “Quickly.”

     

                Grabbing Alex’s sleeve, Lena dragged her towards Kara’s cell. Feeling an odd swoop in her stomach at being inside the cell Kara had spent over half of her life inside, as if intruding into some private space, Lena stopped and stared up at the ceiling.

     

                “Boost me,” she instructed the guard.

     

                “What?”

     

                Impatient and panicked, Lena roughly repeated herself. “Boost me up.”

     

                Face furrowing with confusion, Alex laced her hands together and bent her knees slightly and Lena stepped into her palms and used the somewhat solid foothold to bridge the gap up to the ceiling. She practically had to scramble onto Alex’s shoulders as the guard muttered and cursed, staggering about a bit unsteadily as she tried to adjust to Lena’s precariously balanced figure.

     

                Pushing against varying panels with no success, Lena grew more frantic and almost pitched them both over as she over-extended, slamming hard into the wall as Alex swore at her, managing to keep a hold on Lena’s feet planted firmly on her shoulders. 

     

                “The other one,” came Kara’s strangled shout. “It wasn’t my cell. It was yours.”

     

                The distant sound of her voice cut through Lena’s one-track mind and she jolted with surprise, sinking down and all but falling off Alex. Hands grabbed the back of her sweatshirt as she went staggering forward, the concrete floor jarring the soles of her feet, saving her from falling face-first and smashing her nose across her cheeks. 

     

                Breathing rapidly as she caught her balance, a cold sweat covering her, Lena moved quickly with Alex close on her heels as they went into Lena’s old cell. J’onn still occupied it, reclaiming his seat on his cot as the brawl down the other end of the cell block raged on, the meaty sound of fists, crumbling rock and loud voices clamouring together.

     

                Without a word, Alex laced her hands together and boosted Lena up again, the panels prodded until one gave way with ease. Relief flashed through Lena, until she’d shifted the panel aside and gripped the edge of the dark hole. Even on Alex’s shoulders, the distance between the floor and ceiling was so high that Lena had barely been able to push the panel up, reaching as high as she could. It was enough for her to grip the edge of the hole with her fingers but not enough for her to pull herself up.

     

                Panting as she strained herself, pushed precariously up onto her tiptoes, Lena felt frustration well up. “I can’t- I can’t do it. I’m not strong enough.”

     

                Alex made a rough sound of impatience at the back of her throat, exacerbated by her chest infection, before wryly grumbling, “couldn’t you have … spent your imprisonment … doing pushups?”  

     

                “It’ll have to be you,” Lena grimly informed her, scrambling down off her shoulders and using her head and thighs as hands and footholds, the guard looking less than impressed.

     

                “Me? No, it has to be you. You lasted days up there before.”

     

                “I can’t. I can’t get up there, alright? And you know the prison better than I do. Get your own fucking hands dirty for a change.”

     

                Scowling as Lena laced her fingers together, Alex gripped her shoulder and set her foot in Lena’s palms. Gritting her teeth against the weight of the guard, Lena heaved, her muscles straining and tendons taut as she tried to stop her legs from buckling beneath her. Alex managed to clamber up on her shoulders, Lena’s face reddening from the exertion as she breathed shallowly, trying to keep her steady as Alex shakily attempted to stand. 

     

                Before she made it to the hole in the ceiling, her foot slipped as Lena stumbled slightly, and Alex went crashing to the floor. Cursing loudly as she grazed her palms and slammed her knees into the concrete with enough force to badly bruise, Alex took a second to stifle her pain and climbed to her feet again. Lena repeated the process, boosting her up, desperation leaving her mouth dry and throat tight as she mumbled quiet reassurances to herself.

     

                “I can’t-” she rasped, “I can’t hold you.”

     

                “Just a little more,” Alex urgently encouraged her. “I’m almost- I can get it. Come on. Come on.”

     

                And then two hands gripped Alex’s feet on Lena’s shoulders and smoothly lifted her. Startling, Lena whirled around as she staggered away and watched J’onn push Alex up towards the ceiling. The guard fell silent, mouth snapping shut, and Lena was white with surprise as she met J’onn’s dark eyes.

     

                “You get out and tell them about us, alright?” he ordered them.

     

                Lena silently nodded, her heart pounding in her chest as she watched Alex grab the edge of the hole. Holding her breath, anxiously wringing her hands, Lena watched the guard haul herself up, her lithely muscled form executing a perfect muscle up before she managed to get a leg up, foot braced against the edge of the hole, and then another one.

     

                “Your turn,” J’onn quickly beckoned Lena, cupping his hands for her as he glanced over his shoulder, bellowing. “Kara, time to go!”

     

                He had Lena halfway up to the ceiling when the malfunctioning cameras winked back on, red lights in the corner of each cell and the rest of the block showcasing the madness within. Alex was reaching down to grab her, to help haul Lena up where her own strength failed, when the collars were activated. Grasping Alex’s hand, both of them clammy, Lena strained and then felt an intense wave of pain immobilise her as her vision went black.

     

                J’onn’s solid form beneath her went rigid and dropped slightly as he hunched over, Lena’s feet scrabbling for purchase on his back. Alex still had hold of her, her own collar sending volts of electricity through her as she tasted the punishment inflicted onto the prisoners while she’d been on the other side of the cell. Lena could feel her hand slipping in Alex’s grasp and she let out a choked sound of agony.

     

                “Don’t you fucking dare,” Alex snarled.

     

                “Stick to the plan,” Lena ordered her. “I’ll make sure she’s alright.”

     

                Another spasm of pain wracked her as the collar shocked her again and Lena let go of Alex’s hand, her body folding without the other woman’s grip keeping her up. J’onn’s knees gave out under him and Lena blacked out for a moment, coming to on the cold floor, a pain in her elbows and her right ankle, the back of her head pounding where she’d struck it on the floor. Her breaths were coming as shallow wheezes and she shook her head to get rid of the black spots, catching sight of Kara likewise, trying to compose herself on the threshold of J’onn’s cell. 

     

                Pushing herself up, Kara crawled towards Lena just in time, the barrier flickering back into place again. Recovering quicker from the electricity than Kara did from the green Kryptonite, Lena crawled beneath the bed, fumbling for the hidden scalpel she’d stolen weeks ago now. She hid it in her sleeve, the metal cool against her skin, before she crawled over to Kara, cupping her face in her hands, smoothing blonde hair out of her ashen face.

     

                “You’re alright, you’re okay.”

     

                “Alex?” Kara listlessly queried.

     

                Giving her a wavering smile, Lena shallowly nodded. “She’s out. Just sit tight now, okay?”

     

                Making a low sound of agreement at the back of her throat, Kara swallowed thickly, her eyelids shuttering. There were the pink marks of a few lucky shots from Mon-El but her own knuckles were split and bloody, showing signs of a definite advantage on her end, but with the faint veins of neon green lingering on her face and neck, Kara looked exhausted and sickly.

     

                “Is she alright?” J’onn softly asked, approaching and crouching at her feet.

     

                “She’ll be okay,” Lena murmured, touching the backs of her fingers to Kara’s cheek in a tender manner. Blinking, she looked up at the alien and gave him a wary look of gratitude. “Thank you.”

     

                Nodding, his dark eyes were piercing. “Remember what I sa-”

     

                The three of them let out varying sounds of pain as the next wave from their shock collars incapacitated them. Holding onto Kara tightly, Lena clenched her teeth and blinked back the tears that pricked her eyes as she tried to stamp down the pain, hoping that Alex had been smart enough to make herself scarce as soon as Lena had let go of her hand. 

     

                The square panel had been put back into place at least, and Lena knew Alex would be feeling the effects of the collars as well, left writhing and in pain as she crawled through the pitch black of the crawl space. But at least they had a shot now - a better shot than they’d thought. As long as Alex could keep it together and not get caught.

     

                The good thing about being locked inside the cell with the most dangerous prisoner was they resolved the issue of Kara first, bodily moving Lena aside before they hauled Kara’s limp form up between the six of them. Lena watched through the haze of exhaustion, pain and waning adrenaline, her body aching and stiff on the cold floor. They came for her next and she was dead weight between the three of them that quickly bundled her into her own cell, dumping her on the floor and slamming the barrier back into place via the little panel set in the wall outside. Lena thought they were stupid for trusting their shoddy, malfunctioning technology and felt a smug stab of satisfaction that her meddling was slowly paying off in fits and starts. Sometimes a little frayed wire a few months ago could cause bigger problems down the line.

     

                As the cell block was slowly brought back into order, the crackling radio orders sent back and forth between the annoyed guards revealing it wasn’t just their block having issues, Lena sat on her cot and watched Kara. Her friend was laid out on her cot and Lena wasn’t sure if she was unconscious or asleep but they’d stopped pumping her full of Kryptonite at least so she knew Kara would recover quickly. 

     

                Waiting out the remainder of the activity in the cell block, the guards whisked Mon-El away and Lena hoped that Kara had gotten him good enough that it took a while for him to heal, and Lena was patiently waiting for the panic to start about the missing guard. So far, as they dumped unconscious or incapacitated prisoners back into their cells, one by one, they hadn’t done a head count or realised the conspicuous absence of one of their numbers. It wasn’t until Maggie shut Nia into her cell that she realised, her voice loud in the deafening silence of the cell block.

     

                “Where’s Danvers?”

     

                Quickly laying down, curling in on herself, Lena was tense as she listened to the low sound of voices outside Alex’s cell, unable to hear what was said but knowing from their tones that they were confused, angry and panicked. They started by making their way down the row of cells, crouching to look beneath each cot, in case they’d accidentally locked two of them in together. When that turned out to be fruitless, they conferred again for a moment before approaching Lena’s cell. At the sound of the forcefield outside her cell being banged on, Lena raised her head and glanced over her shoulder, a blank look on her face.

     

                “Where is she?”

     

                “Who?”

     

                “Don’t play dumb. Tell me now or-”

     

                “Why don’t you check the cameras?” Lena snidely asked.

     

                “I mean it, LL93,” Maggie warned her. “I won’t ask again.”

     

                They engaged in a long minute of staring, neither of them faltering, before Maggie nodded and dismissively gestured to Vasquez, giving her a fleeting glance. “Radio in for KZ64 to be immobilised. She’s being … difficult.”

     

                Quickly on her feet, Lena crossed over to the forcefield and slammed her fist against it, right where Maggie’s face was, wishing the barrier wasn’t in the way. “Don’t you fucking dare,” she quietly snarled as Vasquez unclipped her radio from the shoulder of her vest.

     

                “Then tell us what we want to know,” Maggie firmly replied. They stared at each other for a moment and then the guard let out a quiet, bewildered laugh as her face furrowed. “Why are you protecting someone you hate? You know she gave you up, right?”

     

                Licking her lips, Lena swallowed past the tightness in her throat. Her eyes flickered upwards to the ceiling panels beyond her cell, and Lena’s mouth twisted into a faint sneer, eyes flashing with anger. 

     

                “I can show you where,” Lena said with dismissive arrogance as she arched an eyebrow. “She won’t have gotten far with her collar on.”

     

                Grinding her teeth together, Maggie glanced at Vasquez, hesitating before she deflated slightly, wearily sighing. “Go on then.”

     

                “For a price,” Lena cut in, a sly smile on her face.

     

                “I’m not bargaining with you. You either tell me, or she pays for it,” Maggie snorted, jerking a thumb over her shoulder.

     

                “I’d like a meeting with the shrink. My session was interrupted the other day.”

     

                “That’s not up to you.”

     

                “Well, this is none of my business then.”

     

                Lena was bluffing, her steps jerky and stiff as she tried not to think about Kara getting hurt, but before she turned away, she saw the alien signing to her, telling her to stall. The quicker they started looking for Alex, sounding the alarms, the quicker they’d find her. Of course, they didn’t want to sound the alarm, knowing they’d be fucked for the massive oversight in security, an even bigger breach than when Lena had been crawling through the warren of pipes, wires and ventilation shafts. A guard with all of the knowledge and intel of the inner workings and mechanisms of the prison was far more dangerous than a desperate genius scavenging for information.

     

                “Vasquez, shock her.”

     

                “Agent Vasquez, requesting a-”

     

                “Wait!” Lena ground out, her voice rough with anger at how easily they could control her with the threat of harming the only person in the prison she cared about.

     

                And maybe that was a weakness, something that Lena should never have let form in the first place, held against her when the guards wanted something from her when she would’ve let them beat her black and blue if it was only her own welfare on the line. But she also knew it was a strength to care so much for Kara, that unshakable steadiness of her company that had gotten Lena through the worst of it. She was so beautifully selfless and kind that Lena couldn’t let them hurt her. She couldn’t let them hurt her when she loved her. 

     

                Turning back around, she couldn’t bring herself to feel guilty about it, ignoring the pleading look on Kara’s face. Even if it meant their plans were derailed by Alex’s capture, Lena would still give the agent up a million times before she let them hurt Kara. They could put a bullet in Alex for it and it would mean absolutely nothing to Lena, save for a flicker of guilt at giving her up. But she’d still do it to protect Kara.

     

                “The ceiling,” Lena sighed, her shoulders caving. “She’s in the ceiling.”

     

                Maggie turned to Vasquez. “Get a ladder.”

    Chapter 16

                They were kept up all night, the lights in the cell block remaining on as guards searched the crawl space in the ceiling, the muffled sounds of radios, and the wailing of the prison alarm. Everyone was limp and dry-eyed as they tried their best to sleep through the activity, most of them used to some sort of antics going on after the arrival of Lena and her inability to give up or go quietly. Stretched out on her cot, tense and silent, Lena could feel her heart pounding in her chest as time wore on, waiting for the inevitable triumph of the guards as they found Alex and dragged her out of the ceiling. Undoubtedly, she would not return to the cell block.

     

                Much to Lena’s surprise, her fellow prisoner turned out to be as elusive as she’d dared to hope, Alex slipping the guards and leading them on a long chase through the ceiling without them catching wind of her. Of course, Lena knew the ex-guard would know the prison better than anyone else, having been raised there since she was fifteen but it was still a relief to think they had a better chance now. It might not have been the original plan but it was a chance, and as Kara relayed Alex’s progress to her with quick signs, Lena’s hope solidified, reassured that the time they’d bought Alex wasn’t wasted. 

     

                Still, Lena didn’t sleep for the rest of the night, anxiously waiting through the long hours with the worry that Alex would make a mistake somewhere, that they would be more efficient now, after Lena’s initial escape. Nothing changed though, the same palpable hum of tension and activity between the guards as they made regular rounds, the cell block doors groaning open and closed as the hours stretched on, Lena pretending to be asleep whenever footsteps approached her cell. Even if they’d been allowed to have the lights off, she wouldn’t have been able to sleep, and it felt like it was an eternity before breakfast was brought around and she safely determined it was morning.

     

                Picking at her breakfast, her stomach tied into too many knots to even consider eating, Lena kept glancing up and meeting Kara’s equally anxious gaze as she ate her food. Abandoning her tray near the forcefield, Lena walked laps around the small confines of her cell, pausing when the harried guards came to collect her tray, silent and tense as they went about their business.

     

                It was a slow day, no shower or walk allowed for any of them, their idle chit-chat drifting off into bouts of silence as they all grew bored as they waited for the fallout of Alex’s escape. Lena wondered if this was what it had been like when she’d made her own escape, and when she signed her query to Kara she was given a sheepish grin and the confession that Kara had kept them all entertained with her antics, even if some were none too pleased about it. The day dragged by with little interference from the guards, the block rather tense and quiet until the lights were turned off shortly after dinner with the intention that they all sleep.

     

                Stretched out on her cot, Lena closed her eyes to the deep grey dimness of the cell block, the red light of the cameras watching her, the palpable hum of the forcefield keeping her penned in, the air wavering slightly with the nearly invisible sheen of it. She could hear the mumbling sounds of cell mates talking in their sleep, or lightly snoring, sounds that had soothed her to sleep for months now, familiar in the ugliest and most devastating way possible. Lena did not want to get used to any of the other atrocities of the prison and she could feel that hollow pit of despair in her chest as she curled in on herself, clinging desperately to her hope. 

     

                The next days followed the same routine and Lena was cagey by the end of it, feeling almost as if she was in solitary confinement herself. The energy from the guards became more fraught with unease, all of them surly and stressed, exhaustion etched in the lines of their faces, all of them on near round-the-clock duty as they crawled throughout the prison, or so Kara relayed it to Lena. The whole time, it felt like they were waiting for the other shoe to drop.

     

                Much to Lena’s surprise, Alex wasn’t caught though. Not on the first day or the second. She lasted longer than Lena had thought she would between, the due date of the next supply run slowly slipping by without a single word from her. A part of Lena had the sneaking suspicion that this was it. She was locked inside a cell with Kara and Alex was loose in the prison, able to access her mom and girlfriend with relative ease, shepherd them through the prison while she stayed hidden and let them walk around uncontested. It would be a lot easier for Alex to get just the three of them out, instead of working through the difficulty of freeing two prisoners from a locked cell block, and Lena started to stew in her bitter anger, convincing herself that her initial distrust had been well placed, that Alex had turned on them, selfishly leaving them to rot in jail while she saved her own loved ones.

     

                She slept fitfully each night, troubled by her thoughts and left exhausted the next day, even though she did little else but sleep, lay on her cot or roam around her cell. The night before the morning’s delivery, Lena felt nauseous, so pale and coiled with so much tension that she had a pounding headache and couldn’t even look at Kara. She’d promised her so much and now it was all hanging by a thread. Lena couldn’t bear to disappoint her; more than anything, she wanted to give Kara a sunset, ice cream, birds and a comfortable life. Whatever it was between them, that bond forged in such a bleak place, it tied them together so tightly that Lena could not have left her unless Kara had chosen otherwise. 

     

                She loved her, deeply, confusingly, tenderly, in so many ways that she wasn’t sure which was the truth, hadn’t had the opportunity to make sense of it, only that it was there, born from their inseparable imprisonment. Maybe Kara felt differently, having been inside there for so long, with friendships that had lasted years from within their cells. Still, Lena knew how she felt, how different it was from anything else in her life, and a part of her worried about what it would all look like once they were outside. At worst, she was prepared to let her go. As long as they were free, she could bring herself to do that and do what little she could to regain a semblance of a life again. One without the only person who truly knew her - her past, her flaws, her fears, at her lowest and most helpless.

     

                Clinging to that shred of belief she had in the ex-guard, Lena went to sleep that night with a hollow feeling of dread, believing she’d still be sitting in her cell at noon the next day, the shipment coming and going. In the event of that, she was petty enough to hope the chopper crashed before making it to Alaska. Despite the worry that ate away at her, having to sit with the uncomfortable feeling of being useless, she did manage to sleep, drifting in and out as she restlessly tossed and turned. Time passed by unnoticed inside the prison, with no windows to show the passage of the sun or moon, and so Lena didn’t know what time it was when the cell block went silent.

     

                It was a stark enough change that Lena was woken by the palpable difference, groggy and confused as she looked around through half-lidded eyes, unable to make out a thing in the pitch black, different to the usual greyish-pink darkness of the cell block. Pushing herself up, she couldn’t see her hand in front of her face, the hairs on her arms rising with the feeling of something off. The power was cut, including the generators, and there was no blinking red light of the security cameras, no hum of the forcefield, no backup lights, and no ghastly red glow from Kara’s cell. 

     

                Rubbing her eyes, Lena squinted as her mind sharpened, trying to work out what was going on. She couldn’t hear anything else, no one else stirring, no alarms or the heavy stomp of guards boots yet. From what she gathered, it had just happened and she was a light enough sleeper to have noticed immediately. Sitting up fully, Lena could hear her pounding heart as she tried to think of what to do next, her mind immediately going to Kara.

     

                And then she was there, the faint scuff of her canvas shoes on the concrete floor, the light pad of her footsteps too light to be anyone else. Lena could hear her shallow breaths as she came closer, shaking off sleep as she tried to make out the shadowy figure of her as her eyes adjusted.

     

                “Come on,” Kara frantically whispered, holding a hand out, her face pale as she loomed over Lena. “We have to be quick.”

     

                “I- wha-? What’s going on?” Lena asked, her voice too loud and scratchy in the silence.

     

                Kara gently shushed her, reaching down to pull her to her feet, brimming with nervous tension. “We need to be quiet, okay? Alex is waiting for us.”

     

                “She did this?”

     

                “Yes. We need to go. It’s almost sunrise.”

     

                By Lena’s reckoning, that meant it was around six o’clock. Hours before the delivery. Her whole body went alert, sleep scattering to the corners of her mind as her thoughts sharpened, her expression almost hawkish as she blinked, looking around and then crouching to collect her stolen scalpel from beneath the frame of the cot. 

     

                “That’s too early.”

     

                “We have to go though, this is our only chance,” Kara helplessly replied, looking peakish in the dark as Lena tried to make out her features. “Come on.”

     

                She took Lena’s hand in her own, the gesture so shockingly intimate after months of virtually no contact as tender as that, and Lena looked down, feeling the intense warmth of Kara’s fingers enveloping her own, palms smooth and her grip strong. Squeezing back reassuringly, her own palm clammy with fear, Lena allowed herself to be tugged over to J’onn’s cell, Kara’s footsteps light enough to be inaudible, while Lena scuffed her feet and felt blind as she stumbled along.

     

                “What’s going on?” Nia’s quiet voice drifted through the silent cell block.

     

                “Power’s out,” Lena called back. “Go back to sleep.”

     

                “Are you out of your cell?”

     

                “No. Go back to sleep, Nia.”

     

                “Everything’s fine,” Kara followed up, her voice wavering slightly, thick with emotion.

     

                Lena turned her head towards her friend, gripping her hand tightly, her heart stuttering in her chest. Kara was whispering to J’onn as she slipped into his cell with Lena in tow, trying to wake him without alerting any of the other prisoners. He woke quietly, seemingly unsurprised, and Lena could hear him shifting on his cot.

     

                “Kara,” Querl softly called out, making the three of them pause. Lena searched blindly in the dark for the direction of his voice, lacking Kara’s enhanced vision. “There is a sixteen-point-two percent chance all of you will get out.”

     

                Hesitating, Kara closed her mouth into a flat line and nodded. Lena’s stomach lurched and she tugged on Kara’s sleeve, her heart in her throat. Putting her arm around Lena’s back, Kara ushered her forward, talking quietly with J’onn.

     

                “Thank you for this.”

     

                “Good luck to all of you.”

     

                “You’re a good friend,” Kara shakily replied. “I won’t forget this. I won’t forget-”

     

                “It’s okay,” J’onn murmured, cupping her face in his hands as he cut her off. “Be well, be happy; you have earned it.”

     

                “I’ll come back,” Kara promised.

     

                Giving her a sharp look, Lena’s brows furrowed together slightly, her mouth turning down at the corners. She would not come back here for all the money in the world and never wanted to set her eyes on any form of prison again but she didn’t try to reason with Kara then. Kara, who had spent half of her life with some of the people on that cell block, felt more loyalty and responsibility for them than Lena ever would. J’onn was kind and smart, a voice of emotional reason in such a bleak place, but Lena would leave and never look back if that’s what she had to do.

     

                Then Lena was being lifted by Kara’s gentle hands, the ease with which she did it surprising Lena as she wobbled slightly, raising her hands upwards in anticipation of the ceiling. She had the scalpel clamped tightly in a clammy hand and her throat felt tight with worry, the unknowable state of the prison, of the plan, making her overthink things. Perhaps most surprising of all was Alex was keeping her promise, and Lena was startled a moment later at the sound of her voice coming from above, her hands grabbing Lena’s arms to help haul her into the ceiling, straining as she dragged her through the hole.

     

                “What-”

     

                “Quiet,” Alex brusquely hushed her, sounding hoarse and exhausted. “Kara?”

     

                Then J’onn was lifting Kara as Lena shuffled through the dark of the ceiling space, insulation and wires brushing her skin as she tried to stick to the wide metal beam Alex knelt on. With J’onn lifting her, Kara was tall enough to reach the hole in the ceiling by herself and strong enough to pull herself up into the ceiling with ease, the vague shadowed form of her clambering through visible to Lena’s poor eyes. 

     

                “Okay,” Alex said with faint relief, “good. We’re on track.”

     

                “On track?” Lena hissed. “The shipment won’t arrive for hours. We’re done for, you fucking idiot.”

     

                “They changed the time,” Alex snapped back. “It’s at the crack of dawn now, thanks to our plan. Harder to make a jailbreak in the middle of the night, isn’t it? Especially when we’re not supposed to know they’ve changed it.”

     

                “Oh.”

     

                “Now, keep your mouth shut and come on.”

     

                Alex shuffled away from the hole in the ceiling and grabbed the square panel, shifting it back towards the hole to hide the evidence of their escape. Kara was silent as she watched Alex slot it back into place, hesitating as she brimmed with nervous energy, torn in half.

     

                “We could help the others-” 

     

                “No,” Alex sharply cut her off, grabbing the shoulder of Kara’s sweatshirt. Her voice softened as she continued, gravelly and firm. “No, we can’t. No one else comes. I’m sorry but … we’ll have to help them once we’re out.”

     

                Kara drew in a shuddering breath and Lena could hear the guilt in her agonised reply. “But-”

     

                “We don’t have time.”

     

                “Lena?”

     

                Her heart skipped a beat at the sound of her name coming from Kara’s lips, soft and pleading, as if she would be enough to veto Alex’s order. Ideally, it would be nice to get revenge on the prison and liberate the others who were unjustly held there, but it was not an ideal world and Lena was scared and a little bit broken and she wanted to forget all of it had ever happened.

     

                Ducking her head, feeling Kara’s pleading stare on her face even though it was so dark she couldn’t see, Lena’s mouth hardened into a flat line. As much as her resolve wavered, wanting to give in to Kara, knowing it was the right thing to do, Lena couldn’t bring herself to sacrifice their chance to escape to bring a bunch of relative strangers with her. She wished she could have played the hero then but it was self-preservation to pick herself, to pick the person she cared about. There were already three more than Lena had initially intended, who Kara cared deeply for, and that was more than enough to increase the risk. 

     

                Turning away, she waited for Alex to lead them, feeling Kara’s fingers ghost her sleeve, the stunned silence of her disbelief making Lena roll her shoulders as she tried to focus on helping them first. That was all that mattered and she couldn’t let her feelings dictate her actions - no more than they already had - shuffling along the beam after Alex, feeling blindly in the dark and listening to the delayed sound of Kara following. Lena was quietly relieved, thinking for a brief moment that Kara would back out of the plan, stubbornly insist on trying to help everyone else out too. It was clear that without Kara, none of them would get out. Once their escape was noticed, once they made it to the sections with working cameras and lurking guards, they would need Kara’s invulnerable brawn to carve a path out for them.

     

                Firstly, they needed to fetch the other two members of their escape party and it felt like an eternity of fumbling through the dark before Alex shifted the cover of a wide vent and eased herself in. There was a thin shaft of light from a slatted vent opening within the ventilation system that lightened the black to a deep grey, enough for Lena to see what Alex was doing and follow after her, trying not to make too much noise as her canvas shoes squeaked on the metal. Crawling through the dust and cobwebs that had accumulated over decades, it was hard not to cough as they shuffled through the vents, Alex making a left turn, two rights and then stopping at a slatted vent cover.

     

                She eased that off and slithered out of the vent, falling face-first but making little noise as she landed. Dragging herself forward on her elbows, Lena peered over the edge to see a laundry cart full of drab prison grey and thin towels waiting below, Alex already out of it and holding the cart steady. Falling into the cart, Lena climbed out and waited for Kara to follow, getting a good look at the ex-guard as she waited.

     

                Alex looked like shit, covered in dust and dirt, sweat at her hairline, blood on her hands and a hollowed look of exhaustion. Her breaths seemed to rattle in her chest from the cold she’d had, which had persisted, but she was otherwise the same, looking a little anxious but her expression severe as she waited for Kara. With more grace than the other two, Kara climbed out of the vent and vaulted over the side of the cart, lanky and wide-eyed, mournful betrayal in her gaze as she shifted restlessly.

     

                “Now what?” Lena asked, turning the scalpel over in her grasp.

     

                “Kelly is fetching my mom. They both have the clearance to get us through the airlock. We’ll need to be careful, though; Kelly did what you told her to and managed to loop the camera footage on your cell block and kill the lights, but it’s all still functioning out here. The control room is just past the next intersection so I’ll sort out Winn. You stay here.”

     

                Kara quietly scoffed, rolling her shoulders, a serious look on her face as her blue eyes darkened with determination. “We’re not splitting up. We go together.”

     

                Pausing, Alex nodded and waited a second as Kara reached out to stop her from opening the door, cocking her head to the side and listening closely. She pulled her hand back once she was sure the coast was clear and Alex jerked it open, slinking out and moving quickly, intent on getting to the control room before the alarm could be sounded. Kara was quicker though, darting past Alex with a speed that almost verged on inhuman, making it to the door of the control room before Lena was even fully out of the laundry room.

     

                Taking a deep breath, Kara turned the handle and shouldered her way in, jaw set. Lena picked up her pace as she listened to the thud inside, skidding to a halt outside the open doorway as Alex ducked inside, watching as Kara held a fistful of Winn’s uniform and gingerly held his gun in her other hand.
