He was playing Tetris on an old Nintendo console, hooked up to a boxy TV, the cameras looping the same infrared footage of the cell block on repeat, courtesy of Kelly.

     

                “Please don’t hurt me,” Winn blurted out, pale and wide-eyed as he held his hands up.

     

                Alex rolled her eyes, taking his pistol from Kara and tucking it into the waistband of her pants. “Do as I say and she won’t hurt you. I promise.”

     

                “What do you want?” he shakily asked, his eyes darting around as Lena stepped inside and shut the door behind herself. 

     

                “I need you to shut down all communications within the prison.”

     

                “I can’t do that.”

     

                “Yes, you can.”

     

                “No, I can’t. Really. It’ll take me ages.”

     

                Pulling the gun out, Alex pulled the hammer back and levelled it at him. “Then I suggest you get started.”

     

                Kara steered Winn around and pushed him onto his desk chair, keeping a firm hand clamped on his shoulder as he hesitated and then slowly started to type. Lena kept a keen eye on the screen, watching him open Command Prompt and start typing in strings of text, piecing it together as she made sure he wasn’t using it to trigger some backdoor alarm. He typed away for the better part of fifteen minutes, the silence tense as they all watched him, counting down the minutes. Alex had anticipated this though, and had timed it in, because she didn’t seem all that bothered and Kelly and Eliza hadn’t shown up yet. 

     

                What she didn’t anticipate though was someone else showing up. Kara was still straining her hearing even as she kept a firm grip on Winn, and she sharply looked up, wariness in her blue eyes as she cocked her head slightly. Her eyes narrowed a fraction and there was a tense set to her shoulders. Eyes flitting to Alex, her mouth tightened at the corners.

     

                “They’ve been cornered by the Deputy. They’re trying to shake her off but she’s heading this way.”

     

                Shifting with uncertainty, Alex’s face rippled with worry. “Can you handle it?”

     

                Eyes straying to Lena and then back to Winn, Kara hesitated and then nodded. “You’ll be alright?”

     

                Alex gestured with the gun and Kara nodded before relinquishing her grip on Winn and crossing over to the door. Lena had been leaning against it, arms folded over her chest, and she pushed off, straightening as Kara approached. Pausing, Kara reached out to cup Lena’s face in her hand, giving her a fleeting smile before she opened the door and slipped out, shutting it behind her.

     

                Taking up position beside the door, Lena kept her eyes trained on Winn as Alex adjusted her grip on the pistol, a looming threat at Winn’s side, making sure he didn’t stray from his task. He anxiously typed away, working quickly, if a little shakily, face ashen and hairline damp as his forehead prickled with sweat. It was tense and quiet and Lena was relieved when the door handle squeaked as it turned, thinking it was Kara returning with the rest of their party.

     

                Stepping aside, Lena’s soft expression turned to one of slack surprise when the door opened inwards and she found herself face-to-face with Vasquez instead. The guard was equally as surprised, mouth opening as she took stock of Alex with a gun pointed at Winn and Lena blocking her way in. Hand quickly dropping to her holster, Vasquez backed out into the hallway and Lena went with her, grabbing the front of her kevlar vest in her left hand to keep her from backing away far enough to aim her gun, and jam the sharp point of the scalpel into the side of her neck. It all happened quickly, merely a handful of seconds passing by, but it was still a shock, the spray of hot blood, the slack look of disbelief on Vasquez’s face mirroring the one on Lena’s.

     

                Pulling the scalpel free, her blood-slick hand violenting shaking, Lena let it clatter to the ground as blood gouted from the small hole, too quick to stifle as she clapped a hand over it, Vasquez making a strangled whine as she clawed at Lena’s hand. She sank to the floor with her as blood soaked into her prison grey, making the floor slick as it spilt down her neck and over their hands. Lena knew how much blood was inside a person but it still surprised her how endless it seemed, running out of Vasquez so quickly that she couldn’t put enough pressure on it.

     

                Kara came skidding around the corner a moment later, white with fear as she hastily returned, pausing at the sight of Lena kneeling in a pool of blood with the guard weakly clinging to life. She floundered for a moment, rooted to the spot, and it allowed Kelly and Eliza to catch up, breathing heavily and expressions quickly turning to shock at the sight that greeted them. Eliza warily stepped forward, sinking to a crouch at Lena’s side, the hem of her white doctor’s coat brushing through the vivid red blood. 

     

                “Move your hands. Quickly,” she gently urged Lena.

     

                “What’s going on?” Alex called from inside, her eyes and gun still trained on Winn, keeping him seated.

     

                Kara had to pull Lena away from the body, her bloodstained hands still reaching for Vasquez’s neck as blood pulsed out of it, and Eliza inspected it quickly before letting out a resigned sigh. “You cut her carotid artery. There’s nothing I can do.”

     

                Face deathly white, bottom lip quivering as she held her bloody hands away from her, Lena couldn’t look away, watching the shallow rising and falling of the guard’s chest slowly come to a stop as the wound stopped pulsing. Kelly was pulling the holstered pistol free, tucking it into the waistband of her jeans with grim practicality as Eliza slid the guard’s eyes closed and then it hit Lena fully.

     

                “Is she- is she dead?” she hoarsely asked.

     

                “She’s dead?” Alex exclaimed. “Fuck. Fuck, fuck, fuck.”

     

                “It’s fine,” Kara quickly said, babbling nervously as her voice broke slightly. “It’s fine. It’s okay, no one will find out. I’ll take care of it.”

     

                Kara let go of Lena, who sank back against the wall, slinking down it as she stared hollowly at her hands, feeling sick. And then she was sick, on her knees at the base of the wall, coughing and retching as Kara picked Vasquez up with surprising tenderness and carried her across to a store closet on the opposite side of the hallway. Breaking the lock as she twisted the handle, Kara hid her inside and then emerged with a filthy mop and started pushing it around, making a streaky mess. Kelly started to help her as Eliza crouched in front of Lena, brushing her hair back and softly speaking to her.

     

                “You’re alright, you’re fine, it’s just the shock. Take a deep breath for me, okay? Put your head between your knees.”

     

                “Mom,” Alex snapped, “we don’t have time for this. Get her on her feet.”

     

                “Don’t you take that tone with me, Alexandra Danvers. She shouldn’t even be in this situation.”

     

                “No one told her to kill her.”

     

                Moving quickly, Kara was in the control room, bristling with anger, her face pale enough to make her faded freckles stark across the bridge of her nose, eyebrows furrowed together in a severe look. “You are the one with the gun; you should’ve used it.”

     

                “You’re supposed to be the muscle.”

     

                “Well I had to take care of the Deputy.”

     

                “Enough,” Kelly shouted, cutting through the noise. “Unless you’d like to rouse every other guard in this place. We’ve already got one dead, one out cold and the other under gunpoint. We really don’t have time for this so pull yourselves together.”

     

                Her eyes slid to Lena, lips twitching with regret. “All of you.”

     

                She had a fistful of cloths from the store closet in hand, wet with blood, and looked as worried as any of them, everyone’s hearts pounding as the tension was thick enough to be unbearable. Sniffing, Kelly wiped her face on her sleeve and then crouched back down, mopping up the last of the blood, a faint, reddish smear left behind. It was the best they could do.

     

                Moving over to Lena, Kara murmured indecipherably and wiped her face with the cuff of her sweatshirt. The sour taste of bile was caught at the back of Lena’s throat and her mouth thinned, the taste of someone else’s blood on her lips where the spray of it had splattered across her face. She looked like she belonged in a horror movie, hollow-eyed, ghostly and gory. Smoothing a hand over her dark hair, Kara gave her a weak, unconvincing smile and then found her hand - the left one, which was the cleaner of the two.

     

                “Stay with me.”

     

                There was a momentary pause, the silence awkward until Winn cleared his throat. “All done.”

     

                Glancing at him, Alex nodded, her mouth thinning. “Thank you.”

     

                He opened his mouth to say something else but Alex whacked the pistol across his temple and Winn sagged in the chair, out cold. Slipping her gun back into the waistband of her pants, Alex unhooked his handcuffs from his belt and cuffed his right arm to the chair so he couldn’t follow after them. As they all filed out into the hallway, Kara reached inside and wrenched the door handle off, tossing it on the floor and then shutting the door with the handle outside. She was still holding Lena’s hand, her grip unwavering warm and grounding, and she gestured for Alex to take the lead. Kelly brought up the rear, her stolen pistol in hand, her ex-military training leaving her the best shot of the bunch.

     

                With Kara listening to the others in their zone, she was able to guide them on a circuitous route without them bumping into anyone else. It wasn’t until they reached the airlock that they knew they’d be in trouble, the cameras in the other zones still working, monitored by their relative command rooms and leaving them vulnerable. That was where Kara would come in though, and as Kelly let the panel scan her handprint, Kara dropped Lena’s hand and stepped forward, shoulders squared in anticipation.

     

                Things quickly dissolved into chaos. No sooner had they all passed through the airlock and made it halfway down the hallway did they find themselves spotted, the blaring of the alarm sounding up, three prisoners resisting the knee-buckling pain of the collars around their necks. Kara’s skin glowed green from the veins of kryptonite but she grit her teeth, lips pulled back in a snarl as the first guards made it to them. Alex and Kelly had limited bullets and were careful to conserve them as they flanked Kara, who grabbed the first guard and dashed him against the wall until he went limp in her grasp, a bullet grazing the corner of a wall as a guard peeked out and quickly retreated.

     

                Lena found herself behind Eliza, the doctor partially shielding her as they hung back, watching the fray unfold. A bullet tore through Kara’s sweatshirt but did nothing to slow her down, pinging off her skin beneath and clattering to the floor as it worked itself free from the layers as she carried on, tearing a riot shield from another guard hard enough to snap his arm before she kicked his knee out and Alex put a bullet in his face. The ease with which she did it startled Lena, who had never thought it possible to kill with such little thought, but then again, she was covered in the blood of the woman she’d just killed without even thinking before she’d acted.

     

                The hallway was filled with the sounds of guns firing, overlapping shouts and thuds. Lena found herself on her knees, curled in on herself as the collar shocked her again and again, until Eliza had her on her feet, all but dragging her along as they kept up with the trio ahead. Guns were swapped out for fuller cartridges and Eliza had a riot shield in front of her and Lena, pushing onwards. Alex almost had her head blown off but went taut, slamming to her knees as electricity pulsed through her, and Lena watched the bullet shatter the plaster on the wall. Kelly held the corner of the next intersection, shooting around it to keep approaching guards at bay while Kara forged ahead, leaking a path of unconscious - or perhaps dead - guards in her wake. It was imperative that they didn’t allow themselves to get bottlenecked or surrounded. 

     

                Eliza dragged Lena to a stop beside the unconscious body of a guard, propping the riot shield against her thigh as she lifted the man’s hand and pulled Lena closer, close enough to press his thumb to the collar. It unlocked with a click and Eliza quickly yanked it open, leaving Lena feeling oddly weightless without the heavy burden of it around her neck. Raising her hand to her throat, she swallowed thickly but didn’t have time to thank her before Eliza threw the collar at another guard and grabbed Lena’s sleeve, pulling her after her.

     

                Now that Lena wasn’t likely to be incapacitated through heavy voltage unless she got in the way of an electrified baton - which wasn’t likely as the guards mostly had guns - Eliza tried to get to her daughter as Alex leaned against the wall, swapping out the magazine on her pistol for one taken from someone’s belt. Lena wasn’t a physical fighter, and had never been much good at it besides the occasional self-defence lesson, but she scrambled around for a dropped baton and hurled it at the guard going after Eliza. 

     

                Alex was soon freed of her collar, more guards pouring out of the other prison sections as the blaring alarm alerted them, even if their radios were useless as they all jostled in the hallways, clueless as they targeted the five women. It was mostly Kara doing the heavy lifting, going down beneath a crowd of guards, feral as she fought, smashing noses across faces, kicking kneecaps out of place, and caving in ribs. She was weak but only in comparison to a Kryptonian, and she fought tirelessly, seeming to not even feel the punches that struck her, although one guard definitely felt it when Lena saw her break her hand across Kara’s cheek.

     

                Using the chaos, Lena ducked and got another baton in hand, fending off a man advancing on her. He smacked her across the face hard enough for her to see black for a split-second as the left side of her face went numb, and as she staggered back, fumbling for the wall to steady herself, he advanced and slipped on a small puddle of blood from a bleeding coworker. It gave Lena enough time to backtrack, dark hair whipping around her shoulders as she glanced back and forth before slipping down a side corridor and making her way to the other command room. A bullet scored a line across her thigh and she hissed with pain before forcing her way into the room, each section of the prison a near mirror-image in the older parts, and she found herself greeted with a punch to the stomach, winding her enough to make her retch as she folded to her knees. 

     

                Throwing herself sideways, she kicked the knees out of the woman in charge of the room and groaned as she fell on top of her, elbow driving into her stomach. While not particularly strong, Lena managed to wrap her legs around the woman in a vice-like grip before getting an arm around her throat. She held on long enough for the woman to go slack in her grasp and shifted out from beneath her, kicking the door shut and then scrambling to her feet to lock it right as a guard slammed into it outside. Fortunately, the doors in the prison were all metal and rather solid, even if it did shudder slightly in its frame.

     

                Turning around, Lena wiped her brow on her sleeve and limped over to the console, her eyes flitting over two dozen screens with glimpses from every camera. It was chaos outside and she winced as she watched Kelly get tackled to the ground on one of the monitors. Quickly glancing at the array of buttons, Lena started pushing any and everything, causing as much damage as she could. In one fell swoop, she cut the lights to the entire section, including the four cell blocks, disarmed the forcefield and turned off the gas and ventilation system. Once she was done, she looked around and found a fire extinguisher, yanking it free and then slamming it into the panels until the system was fried.

     

                Once she was done, she turned towards the door, the guard still hammering on it, turned the lock and stepped aside as the guard barrelled through it unobstructed, only to find the heavy tank of the extinguisher clobbering him in the back of the head. Turning as he sagged beside his colleague, Lena held the nozzle in one hand and started to spray as she waded out into the hallway, green eyes blazing as she forged through the darkness. She conserved what she could until she reached the intersection, where the thick of the fighting had been, and then assaulted the guards loomed out of the pitch black with the choking dry powder she sprayed at them. 

     

                After emptying the contents, she fought off another guard until the woman went slack before her and Lena made out the solid form of Kara standing before her, pulling the fire extinguisher from her grasp. Lena was still and silent as she listened to the crunch of Kara pummelling someone with the tank and then reached forward to drag her friend down, fumbling in the dark for the nearest body and repeating Eliza’s process of freeing Kara from her collar.

     

                She heard the surprised inhale as the collar unlocked, and Lena could almost feel the weight off Kara’s shoulders as the residual pain of green kryptonite exposure faded. It clattered to the floor and Lena found her hand in Kara’s as she was hauled to her feet, and then was being carried, the breeze of their quick passing ruffling her dark hair as she had her face pressed against Kara’s chest, a hand covering her head. 

     

                Kara paused at the end of the hallway and kicked down the door, her strength returning to her bit by bit the longer she was away from the red sun lamps that had leached so much from her. Of course, it was nothing to what her power would be like with the exposure to yellow sunlight but it was enough for her to kick down the door to the airlock, the light of the section beyond beckoning them. She had to kick down another door as well to get them through, depressurising the section and ruining any chance of blocking off the guards that pursued them.

     

                In the light of the new section, which Lena knew from their discussions and relayed information was the middle of the prison, full of administration and offices, the kitchens and weapons rooms and the final central chamber with the generators and machines powering the prison, including the elevator up to the rooftop helipad, they forged onwards. Feet pounding on the floor, Lena ran past offices of stricken data entry clerks, accountants and admin assistants, one of them dropping their cup of coffee as they poked their head out to see what the fuss was about. Kara was bringing up the rear, catching bullets, tearing guns from hands, incapacitating anyone who got too close, while Alex and Kelly flanked her, walking backwards as quickly as they could, firing off shots to cover Lena and Eliza, who were in the lead.

     

                Lena followed Eliza, who knew the prison better than she did, relying on the doctor to guide them. It was quieter in this section, not as chaotic, although the alarms still blared at an annoyingly incessant wail, and most of the staff hid under their desks or barricaded themselves into their offices, hoping to be spared in the prison riot they assumed was happening. They wanted no part in the prison break and so they were left alone, with only the desperate guards on their tail. 

     

                Breaths coming sharp and shallowly, it was all Lena could do to keep going, weak and exhausted, her whole body aching and everyone else not faring much better. Eliza had a hand clamped over her left bicep where a bullet had nicked her and Kelly had a cut on her forehead that was bleeding freely, while Alex looked almost as bad as Kara, in terms of how much blood covered her face. Although, unlike the latter, the guard’s was mostly her own from receiving punches and other hits. They were losing speed now, all of them almost manic with the frantic desperation of ones who knew they were dead if they didn’t pull this off. There would be no coming back from it, and Lena worried how much damage had been done to the guards and the prison, how long their punishments would be dragged out or if a quick bullet each would suffice to ensure they never caused any trouble again. She almost felt a twinge of guilt for the doctor getting dragged into this as she followed right on Eliza’s heels, limping with the pain in her thigh.

     

                “Don’t let them out!”  

     

                The Warden’s shout cut through the pounding footsteps and Lena’s throat was dry with panic as she made it to the door in step with Eliza, the doctor pressing her hand against the panel as it hissed open. The doors were thicker here, two feet of steel, and they parted with a hiss, admitting the two women. They backed away to let Alex and Kelly in but Kara was swarmed by half a dozen guards weighing down her limbs as they tried to tackle her to the ground. The tension was unbearable and Lena’s eyes widened with panic as the doors started to slide shut.

     

                “Wha- no. No, open the doors. We have to wait for her.”

     

                “Go through!” Kara ordered them, the words strangled and frantic. “It’s alright … I’ll … follow.”

     

                Frigid air hissed into the airlock as it pressurised before the opposite doors slid open, and the four of them spilt out of it, quickly scattering far enough away in anticipation of Kara following them. The silence as the thick double set of doors muffled the fray on the other side of the airlock was deafening and it took Lena a moment to realise it was freezing in there. Her breath plumed before her and she could faintly smell salt and rain, looking around until she realised there was a gaping hole in the centre of the ceiling, the elevator shaft descending as the shipment was made. There were no alarms in this section of the prison, none of the chaos of the other sections, and she let out a hoarse laugh of disbelief, their freedom just within reach. But Kara was stuck and she stayed rooted to the spot, even as Alex strode over to the lone agent manning the control desk, shooting twice as the tall woman turned, already speaking.

     

                “You’re late-”

     

                The body fell to the floor and Alex glanced around, seeing no one else in sight and quickly retracing her steps back to the door. Barely a minute had passed but Kara was still on the other side and as Eliza slapped her hand against the door to open them, they found the second set of doors still tightly shut.

     

                “She’s not strong enough,” Alex stated as they watched the metal bulge slightly but hold firm. 

     

                “Then open it,” Lena demanded, her voice hoarse.

     

                Her demand was pointless though; Eliza had already opened the first door and it was a waiting game for it to slide shut and pressurise before opening on the other side. Jittery with panic as she grit her teeth, face crumpled with agonised unease, Lena felt nauseous as they waited, hearing the thump and muffled sound of shouts as Kara and the guards piled into the airlock. Slamming her hand against the panel again, Eliza leapt back as the doors hissed open and Kara sprawled backwards with a pile of guards on top of her. 

     

                While this was happening, the elevator reached the bottom and the old, salt-rusted doors creaked open as the agents wheeled in large pallets of supplies to leave with the pallets already set off to one side. At the sounds of brawling, gunshots and banging metal, they all abandoned their task and joined in. Lena ran towards a collection of pipes and ducked behind them, bullets pinging off the metal, worming through the tangled mess of them and coming out the other side. Darting towards the control panel, she slammed her hands over a variety of buttons, feeling the prison lurch slightly, her stomach jolting as the slowly plunged. She pushed the buttons at random until she found the one to stop that, realising very quickly it was the one to submerge the prison again. 

     

                Messing with the panel, she hit the button to lock all of the doors to the access chamber, cut the engines somehow, leaving them bobbing in the current, and shut off the gas and water pumping through the veins of the prison, keeping it pressurised. Alarms started to wail then, red lights flashing as she brought the main functions of the prison to a halt, looking startled by her own actions. A moment later, she was tackled sideways, slamming her head on the floor.

     

                The guard went limp on top of her with a thud and Lena rolled over, blinking back stars, finding Eliza breathing heavily over her with the small stool at the control panel in hand. Scrambling to her feet, the metallic taste of blood in her mouth, Lena pushed the doctor aside as a guard came at them, riot shield aloft and an electrified baton in hand. The guard struck the control panel, where Eliza had been standing, and then whipped sideways, catching Lena across the ribs. Reeling backwards, Lena hit one of the massive pallets and ducked, catching the woman across the knees and tackling her to the ground. 

     

                Clambering on top of her, Lena pushed her face into the ground as Eliza took the baton from her hand and then jammed it into the side of the woman’s throat. Panting as she climbed to her feet, legs shaking beneath her, sweat beading on her bloody face, Lena’s eyes darted around as she looked for Kara. 

     

                Kara, who was in the room lit by the pale grey of pre-dawn, closer to the sun than she’d been in almost two decades, standing firmer, with more colour in her cheeks. Staying back with Eliza, Lena watched the bloodbath that ensued as Kara slowly absorbed the radiation in the room, not as much as outside, up top, but more saturated than the filtered prison air that made it to their windowless cells. 

     

                A one-woman army as bullets pinged harmlessly off her, the guards ill-prepared for a Kryptonian with their plain weapons, and pitifully outnumbers, despite there being a dozen of them with the agents who had been assisting with the delivery, and only four humans and one alien, Kara tore through them all with the reserved air of someone who didn’t want to kill anyone. Pipes burst from the impact of a body slamming into them, water spilling into the room where it had gone stagnant from the main line being cut by Lena, the smell of gas strong in the air while some of the vents leaked thin steam as the pressure died.

     

                Another unforeseen problem arose with the fact that the prison was sitting lower in the water than it had been, the rough waves of the Arctic Ocean crashing over the deck and rushing towards the gaping hole in the roof. Freezing water sheeted down, making the floor treacherously slick as it pooled on the concrete, and Lena winced as Alex lost her footing, slipping backwards and slamming her elbow on the ground. She still had the gun in hand though and shot a guard in the chest as he bore down on her. 

     

                For the most part, Lena was useless with Eliza, keeping out of the way, watching as Kara threw someone into a light fixture, sparks flying and the broken plastic cover crumpling to the ground. Tugging on Eliza’s sleeve, Lena jerked her head towards the elevator just as a few guards managed to pry apart the dead doors of the airlock. Faltering mid-retreat, Lena’s mouth fell open at the sight of a prisoner who had been absent from their ward for the last few days.

     

                Mon-El was still collared but was uncuffed as he sauntered in under gunpoint, flanked by half a dozen guards and the Warden. His eyes were trained on Kara and he cracked his knuckles as he walked forwards. The other guards had mostly been taken care of by that point, the trio covered in blood, the humans bearing injuries and Kara looking more alive than Lena had ever seen her as she was consumed by the rising power within her, committed to her task. 

     

                “Take care of them,” the Warden said with a dismissive flick of her hand. “Kill them if you have to, just don’t let them leave.”

     

                “And I’ll be a guard afterwards?” Mon-El asked.

     

                Lena wanted to groan at how gullible he was but the Warden reassured him, the reward enough for the Daxamite to square his shoulders and move towards the Kryptonian, who registered his presence. Eyes blazing with anger, and then shockingly with the faltering signs of the heat vision that had been denied her, Kara narrowed her attention to Mon-El.

     

                “The last of the Daxamites and Kryptonians,” he called out, smiling. “Let’s settle the feud at last.”

     

                “You talk too much,” Kara replied with a grimace before she went to meet him.

     

                He caught her first punch but Kara kept going, driving him back as his smile faltered. Punching him in the stomach with her left fist, she sent him back into the wall and then followed it up with a kick to his chest. The concrete cracked slightly and Mon-El snarled, ducking as Kara tried to follow up with a punch. Her fist cracked the concrete further and Mon-El shoved her back, sending her sliding backwards through the water. He advanced on her and pushed her again, and then Kara was moving too quickly for Lena to keep track of, the two of them causing as much destruction as possible by the look of things. 

     

                At one point, Lena caught sight of Mon-El landing heavily on the control panel, crushing it nearly in half as it sparked and died, killing the lights and any other functions connected to it, and then Kara dented one of the pillars as she was kicked back into it, visible through the dim light of the sunlight filtering through the hole overhead. Mon-El picked her up by the collar of her sweatshirt and Kara wrapped him in a bear hug, lifting him off the ground and then slamming him down, kneeling on his sternum as she pummelled his face. Even the guards forgot about the four humans trying to escape, everyone standing around watching the whirlwind of brute force and violence as the prison received near-irreparable damage in the process. 

     

                It looked like Kara had the upper hand the next time they broke apart, bleeding and bruised but steady on her feet, while Mon-El weaved as he blinked past the furring edge of his vision. Kara was on him again, arm around his neck, kicking his knee out and lowering him to the ground as she choked him, the guards realising their rat was losing. They unloaded on Kara, the deafening ring of gunshots filling the space in their last-ditch effort to stop them, more guards spilling in through the open door as they were rounded up from other sections.

     

                “Go!” Alex shouted, joining in the noise of the chamber as she swapped guns and shot two guards, point blank.

     

                A bullet scored Lena’s ribs as it punched through the side of her sweatshirt and she hissed as she limped towards the elevator before releasing her grievous mistake in cutting the power. She turned to Eliza, and then Kelly, shadowing them over to it as Alex covered their retreat and left the aliens brawling. 

     

                “There’s no power,” Lena breathlessly explained, looking up at the central shaft with a bleak look on her face, seawater splattering her face as another wave batted their sides and flooded the top deck.

     

                This portion of the prison was taller than the rest of it, the roof thirty feet overhead, uninhibited by no crawl space, just a solid concrete structure in the centre, almost impregnable to any form of escape, unless you had inside help. There was no chance of them climbing the scaffolding of the elevator shaft to reach the lip of the open hole and Lena felt like crying until Alex reached them, breathing heavily, slick with blood and sweat, holding her side.

     

                “There’s an access ladder behind.”

     

                Kelly went first, rounding the elevator shaft and finding the rusted rungs of the old ladder. She holstered her gun at her waist and hauled herself up, the thing creaking and groaning in a less than encouraging manner. Once she was far enough up, Lena followed her, hand over hand, telling herself not to look down, even though she had her heart in her throat at Kara’s fate, the sea running over, soaking the back of her sweatshirt and plastering her dark hair to her shoulders. Muscles weak and limbs shaking, she reached the top after Kelly and was quickly followed up by Eliza and then Alex.

     

                Stepping onto the wet deck of the prison, Lena drew in her first breath of fresh air in seven months, the cold like a knife in her lungs as the intensity of it made her exposed skin prickle with pain, the healed break in her leg aching as she looked around. A halting laugh escaped her and she looked around at the seething mass of water and sea ice bobbing around them. It was endless, the sunrise just hitting the horizon, painting the sky orange. Lena wanted to sink to her knees there and drink it in but she was well aware they weren’t free yet.

     

                Alex moved off towards the pilot and remaining guard in the grounded chopper, the deafening roar of the propellers making it difficult to hear each other but Lena could still see the scuffle through the windows, one woman dragged out and knocked unconscious, while the pilot was shot in his seat. Working quickly, Alex struggled beneath his bulk as Kelly and Eliza went to help her. Lena hung back, standing near the open hatch in the roof of the floating prison, trying to keep her balance as another impossible tall wave dashed over the sides, freezing water soaking her canvas shoes as she almost lost her footing. 

     

                And then Kara was there, hauling herself out of the hatch, disbelief softening her face as she climbed to her feet and looked around. Slowly drifting forward a few steps, she drank in the sunrise, basking in the briny air as she turned, elation in the creased corners of her blue eyes, swimming with tears as she laughed, her cheeks dimpling. 

     

                “Look at that,” Kara said, close enough that Lena could hear her.

     

                She closed her eyes, wriggling her fingers as she inhaled deeply, the unbridled feeling of yellow sunlight suffusing her with strength and power. Basking in the feeling, Kara let out another laugh and then opened her eyes as tears streaked down her filthy cheeks. She laughed again, meeting Lena’s eyes, reaching out to cup her face, so tender despite her blooming strength.

     

                The moment was ruined by one of the guards reaching the top of the ladder but Kara was stronger than she’d been in a long time, since she’d been that thirteen-year-old girl tracked down and imprisoned, and she whirled around and thrust her hand out. It went through the man’s torso and ripped out the other side with almost no resistance, horrifying enough to make Lena’s eyes widen as her stomach turned, blood steaming in the frozen air as it splattered on the wet deck. Kara flung her arm aside and the man arced overboard, dead and bobbing in the water as the next guard came.

     

                If Kara had been dangerous before, now she was lethal, the ease with which she carved through them shocking to watch, and seemingly shocking to Kara too, who didn’t know her own strength. One of them was thrown into the side of the chopper with enough force to burst his skull in, a woman’s windpipe was crushed like paper, and still, they kept coming, Lena retreating to the chopper as Kara fought them off, wave after wave lapping over the edge, almost hovering as her power trickled back in but not enough for any prolonged use. 

     

                Torn between getting on the chopper and waiting for Kara, Lena lingered halfway between as the wind assaulted her and waves crashed overboard, fighting for her balance as the cold pierced her down to her bones. Brushing her hair out of her face, Lena swallowed thickly, her hoarse shout whipped away by the wind.

     

                “Kara! Let’s go. Leave them.”

     

                If she heard Lena, which she must have with her sensitive hearing, she ignored her, consumed by the swift action of dispatching as many of the guards as she could. Lena didn’t think of her as a particularly vengeful person but it was clear that Kara was experiencing so much that it overwhelmed her and the only outlet for her was beating back the tide of guards as they came up the ladder, one by one, making sure no one could follow them.

     

                “Kara!”

     

                Two guards came up almost at the same time, one right on the heels of the other, and the second one evaded notice for a moment, sprinting down the deck towards Lena, who started running towards the chopper, where at least one of the women there would have a gun. Kara turned away from the other guard and moved towards Lena in a blur, jerking the guard away from her and tossing the man into the propellers of the chopper, a look of horrified disgust on Lena’s face as she watched his guts splatter the deck before Kara angled back across the deck to circle around to the other guard. 

     

                Still reeling from the gory display as the dismembered man splashed onto the deck, Lena had the sudden thought that they were sinking . She was sure they were sitting lower in the water, that whatever damage had been done below was causing the prison to slowly sink, whatever buoyancy it had in tandem with the engines failing from the destruction wrought by two aliens. Water lapped at her ankles, swirling red from the blood of the bodies, and she was still rooted to the spot when a shout made itself just audible over the sound of the helicopter. 

     

                “Don’t fucking move!”

     

                Lena turned, her expression going slack at the sight of Maggie striding forward, raising the pistol held steadily with both hands to point it right at her. Lips parting, Lena drew in a sharp breath but didn’t even have time to respond before the gun went off.

     

                At the same time, she was roughly shoved aside, staggering across the watery deck of the prison as she tried to keep her balance and ended up grazing her palms and chin as she went sliding across the concrete. The icy wind whipped her wet hair around her face as she pushed herself up, her whole body tense with fear, face bloodlessly pale, her eyes darting back to Maggie as she feared another shot. 

     

                But Kara was there instead, pulverising the pistol with one hand as she wrenched it from the guard’s hand and wrapped her other hand around her throat. Maggie was small but it was still unnerving to watch as Kara lifted her off her feet, teeth bared as her eyes glowed. Lena’s heart was in her throat as she watched her friend, who, for all her humanness, truly looked like the alien she was as she thought Kara was about to melt Maggie’s face off. Lena knew enough of the powers of Kryptonians to know that, given enough time to recharge in the sun, Kara could put the prison at the bottom of the ocean.

     

                Instead, she tossed Maggie overboard, a quick flick of dismissal that doomed the guard to perhaps an hour at most of splashing around in the frozen Arctic sea before she died, if the brutal arc and hard impact hadn’t knocked her unconscious already. It was a death sentence all the same and Lena didn’t feel an ounce of pity for the guard, blinking rapidly as she tried to come to terms with how close she’d brushed with death. The bullet had missed her, of course, but it had been a close call and only missed because she’d been pushed aside.

     

                That thought came back to her and she slowly turned, looking at the sprawled figure of Alex, legs splayed awkwardly in front of her, leaning on her left elbow as she pressed her right hand to her chest. Red was quickly seeping out, soaking the front of her grey sweatshirt, staining her fingers, mingling with the water. Her face was deathly white beneath the dirt and blood and her brown eyes met Lena’s stricken face as she realised Alex had taken the bullet for her.

     

                Eliza and Kelly were already there at her side, kneeling as they babbled, relatively calm in the face of the severity of the wound. Lena found herself drawn forward, a pinched look of confusion on her face as she dropped to her knees, water lapping at her legs, the cold air stealing her breath as she reached out before pulling away.

     

                “Why did you do that?” Lena hoarsely asked.

     

                Letting out a strangled laugh, Alex flashed her a quick smile, teeth stained red with blood. Her eyes flickered over to Kara, who was making quick work of the new guards spilling out of the prison, catching bullets, moving quicker than they could make sense of as the early rays of morning sunshine filled her with radiation. Swallowing thickly, Alex’s mouth twisted ruefully.

     

                “We need …you to- to fly the chopper. Don’t worry … I’m not going … soft on you,” she said, eliciting a breathless laugh from Lena.

     

                Meeting Eliza’s gaze, taking in the deep lines of worry as she kept her hands pressed firmly on her daughter’s chest, pulse fluttering rapidly at her throat, Lena gave her an encouraging nod. “You get her on the chopper. Get ready; I’ll get Kara.”

     

                “No,” Alex waveringly shouted over the noise.

     

                “What?” Kelly sharply blurted out, dark eyes fixed on her girlfriend’s ashen face.

     

                “It’s bad, isn’t it? Leave me,” Alex said, her eyelashes fluttering, bloodless lips a thin line as her face went taut with the pain. “At least I … at least I can say I wasn’t a coward in the end.”

     

                Expression darkening, lips twisting contemptuously, Lena scoffed and pushed herself to her feet, Alex’s pistol in hand. She was unsteady and scornful, her hands shaking terribly, partially from the numbing cold, as she mustered her anger. Green eyes flashing dangerously, she gestured sharply at the chopper.

     

                “Get her on board. Now. I won’t be indebted to someone who doesn’t deserve to be a hero. Pick someone else to sacrifice yourself for.”

     

                Turning her back on them, Lena slowly jogged towards where Kara was finishing off the last guard, snapping the man’s arm as he wailed and then punching him unconscious, even as her heat vision flickered to life and burnt a hole right through his face. Kara dropped him with surprise, right down the open hatch. There was the faint splash of impact below and Lena blanched at the sight of how much water was spilling through, filling the chamber and no doubt running through the singular open doorway to the other sections. Any guards alive below would need to get through another airlock to seal themselves off from the rising water, and Lena wasn’t confident all of them would regain consciousness in time to avoid drowning. 

     

                Still, that was none of her concern and she splashed her way towards Kara, breath hanging in the air before her as the sky brightened, a painting of oranges and faint pinks. It was the most beautiful sunrise Lena thought she’d ever seen, although there wasn’t time to stop and appreciate it as the Kryptonian rounded on her, bristling with anger, her eyes glowing, stopping Lena in her tracks as she shied away.

     

                “It’s me. It’s me,” Lena breathlessly told her. “We need to go, okay? You can stop now. You’re free. You’re free.”

     

                “Free,” Kara replied, the glow in her eyes dimming, nothing but the sound of the water and the chopper filling the morning.

     

                As Lena watched, the brimming energy settled and Kara managed to shake off the fog of anger, frowning as she pressed her hands to her temples. It was overwhelming to exist in her body then, confusing to feel so much after decades of feeling not much at all. She was breathing quickly, shallowly, blinking as she looked around, streaks of red swirling around bodies - or the remains of them - as sea ice bobbed against the prison and water sheeted down into the chamber below.

     

                “We need to go,” Lena insisted, her voice wobbling, throat feeling tight as she had this creeping sense of dread. “Alex is hurt. We need to leave now to help her.”

     

                “I-” Kara faltered, shaking her head as she squeezed her eyes closed. Her hands were shaking badly as she curled them at her sides, covered in so much blood that Lena couldn’t see skin beneath it. “Oh. Oh no. No, no, what did I- no.”

     

                Kara babbled as she unclenched her hands, flexing her fingers as they trembled, the dawning horror of the destruction her body had wrought catching up with her mind. Pale beneath the blood, Kara staggered as she looked around, taking in the water, feet splashing through the freezing Arctic as it swept overboard, pouring through the hatch. Whatever she could hear below made her go shockingly white as her hollow gaze met Lena’s.

     

                “Come with me,” Lena softly coaxed her, holding out a hand.

     

                “The prison,” Kara breathlessly said, numb from the shock.

     

                “We’re free, we can leave.”

     

                Before she could say anything, Kara was gone in a blur of grey, the splash of water the only sign of where she’d gone as she dived overboard and vanished. Panic seized Lena and she ran across the deck, slipping twice, banging her knee, bruising her elbow, feeling the prison rock slightly as it rose an inch before inevitably settling back in the water. Then Kara was hovering above the choppy surface, absolutely drenched and looking distressed as she lightly floated over to the deck, lips parted, eyes anxiously darting around.

     

                “Kara,” Lena said, exhaling sharply, her voice breaking as she pleaded. 

     

                She felt her heart break a little at the obvious distress, watching the alien come apart, helpless in the face of freedom, unable to process what was happening after so long stuck with the same routine, kept on the brink of helplessness and now flooded with a staggering amount of power. Raking a hand through her hair as she reeled, Kara was murmuring to herself beneath the droning of the chopper and Lena tripped over her feet as she moved towards her, reaching out.

     

                “Please. Please, let’s go. It’ll all be okay now.”

     

                “They’re trapped down there,” Kara choked out, her bottom lip trembling as she looked at Lena with a distant, haunted gaze. “I can’t leave them. I can’t- my friends …”

     

                Shaking her head as she struggled to make sense of Kara’s words, Lena drew in a hitching breath. “No, you have to.”

     

                “I can’t,” Kara insisted, her voice wavering as she let out a breathless sob. “Oh God, what did I- they’re trapped. There’s so much water, so much blood. It wasn’t- it wasn’t supposed to … be like this. I killed them.”

     

                “It’s okay.”

     

                Face crumpling, Kara gripped fistfuls of her wet hair as she bared her teeth in agonised guilt, horrified at her own abilities. She squeezed her eyes shut and let out a frayed sound of pain and Lena stepped in closer, reaching out to graze the sleeve of her sweatshirt before Kara staggered away, eyes snapping open, stricken and stuttering with the glow of her heat vision. Flinching away, Lena watched as Kara accidentally scored a line in the deck, the water steaming and spraying at the impact. 

     

                Squeezing her eyes shut, Kara covered her face with her hands. “I’m sorry, I’m sorry. I don’t know- it’s so much . I can’t- what did I do?”

     

                “You’re alright, you’re okay. I’m going to help you, okay? Take my hand, Kara. Let me help you.”

     

                “No, I need to help them,” Kara sobbed, her hands falling away from her face as her eyes landed on the open hatch. 

     

                They were almost ankle deep now and Lena couldn’t feel her toes, nor her fingers for that matter, the cold so intense that every joint ached and she could hardly feel her body, save for the sickening hollowness in her chest as her heart ached painfully. Her lips were purplish and her cheeks were bitten red beneath the dried blood and she could hardly talk around the tightness in her throat, her larynx so constricted that it hurt to even swallow. She knew what was coming even before Kara spoke.

     

                “I can’t go with you.”

     

                “Yes, you can,” Lena managed to choke out. “You have to.”

     

                “I can’t. I need to get them out, I- my friends. They’re in there. I can’t leave them, not like this. Please. Please leave without me.”

     

                “No.”

     

                It came out as a growl, fierce and firm as hot tears spilt onto Lena’s filthy cheeks, freezing before they could even fall. She clenched her teeth, scowling as helpless frustration built in her chest and she drew in a shuddering breath, a pitiful whine escaping her as she desperately wished for Kara to leave them. It wasn’t right, it wasn’t noble or heroic but Lena didn’t care about any of that; she only cared about the woman standing in front of her, who she’d promised the world to.

     

                “I’m sorry. I’m so sorry,” Kara said, her voice cracking as she gave Lena a pleading look, begging her to understand.

     

                “No,” Lena repeated, anger flashing through her as she pulled the hidden pistol from her waistband, her hand shaking so badly she couldn’t even hold it steadily until she had the barrel pointed at her temple, trying to force Kara’s hand. “I won’t let you. I’ll- I’ll kill myself if you don’t come with me. I mean it, I’m not leaving here without you.”

     

                Kara choked on a laugh that was half a sob, her expression softening before she moved in quickly, her increased speed no match for Lena, who found the gun wrenched away from her head, disoriented as Kara turned her around. Back to Kara’s chest, breathing heavily as a shot rang out, the bullet splashing in the water at their feet, Lena could do nothing but open and close her mouth, weak at the knees as the gravity of the situation became clear.

     

                She hunched over, covering her face with her hand as she let out a broken sob, the sound ragged and raw, and Kara worked the pistol free, tossing it aside before she curled herself over Lena’s back, enveloping her in her burning warmth. Cheek to Lena’s spine, she squeezed her eyes shut, trying to put on a brave face, trying not to cave as she jutted her chin forward.

     

                “I’m sorry. Please forgive me.”

     

                “You don’t have to do this. You’re free.”

     

                “Then let my first act of freedom be helping my friends.”

     

                Kara straightened and turned Lena back around, her bloody thumbs wiping away half-frozen tears, leaving red streaks across her cold cheeks. She looked ashen and frightened and Lena let out a hitching sob, queasy and grey-faced as she balled her hands in the front of Kara’s sweatshirt, holding on as tightly as she could make her numb fingers. 

     

                “I know, I know,” Kara murmured, her touch so tender as she traced the lines of Lena’s face, standing so close that her lips ghosted over Lena’s in a whisper of a kiss. “I’ll be alright. Don’t worry.”

     

                “Don’t leave me. Please don’t leave me.”

     

                “Shh, it’s okay. I’ll find you again, I promise,” Kara said, her lips kissing away tears, lightly pressed to the corners of Lena’s mouth, to her temples, her hands sifting through Lena’s wet hair, holding her so gently that Lena fell apart. “I have to do this, okay? But I can find you anywhere you are in the world, even in the dark. I know your heartbeat so you have to leave so I can follow you.”

     

                “Please,” Lena whispered, almost soundlessly, her lips moving but her throat so tight she could barely make a sound.

     

                She couldn’t even see properly, her vision blurred with tears, and she held onto Lena, her chest rising and falling quickly. Kara gently hushed her again, her nose nudging Lena’s, her hand cupping the back of her head. Lena could feel her warm breath over her lips and she leaned in instinctively, so touch-starved that she ached for her, her mouth parting slightly, chapped lips brushing over Kara’s. And then she kissed her properly, none of the reserved tenderness of Kara’s comfort, crushing their lips together in a last effort of desperation. Lena would have been lying to say she hadn’t thought about what it would be like to kiss Kara but she hadn’t anticipated that Kara would kiss her back, her arms wrapping around Lena, so warm against the intense cold of the Arctic and the thin prison clothes that did nothing to keep it out.

     

                The kiss softened, indulgent, lingering, bittersweet, before Kara pulled back, her fingers tracing the sides of Lena’s face before cupping the underside of her jaw. She seemed more composed now, committed to her decision, although she was shaking badly and looked terrified of her own body as she stood in the sunlight, the dawn breaking around them with all the beauty of early spring in the Arctic. It was bitterly cold and the sunrise reflected off the water stretching in every direction, broken by sea ice but making the water look like it was on fire as their time together came down to a handful of remaining seconds.

     

                “I would have really liked falling in love with you on a beach somewhere, with ice cream at sunset,” Kara said, giving her a heartbreaking smile, her blue eyes full of tears, wet cheeks dimpling with the bittersweet resignation of a future she was turning away from as she pried Lena’s fingers off her shirt. “But thank you for the sunrise.”

     

                It took Lena a moment to process the meaning, to realise Kara was not nearly as convinced as she pretended to be that she’d make it back out again, that she was committed to sacrificing herself to save the people she cared about. It should have been obvious from the start; Lena knew who she was, had watched Kara struggle with the conflicted decision to leave behind friends, people who’d aided them in their escape and kept their mouths shut through months of planning. Still, it completely blindsided her as the blood drained from her face and she was left stumbling towards the hatch as Kara moved unnaturally quick, a grey blur disappearing down the ladder and using her strength to drag the two halves of the hatch shut against the increasing flow of water.

     

                Splashing after her, cursing her slowness, Lena fell to her knees in the water as it swirled over the hatch, still leaking through where the seal hadn’t pressurised because of the ruined mechanics. Lena thought that might have helped, scrabbling at the seams, trying to yank them apart. They were solid steel though, five feet thick against the weight of the water usually bearing down on it, and Lena couldn’t make them budge an inch. Sobbing as tears ran down her cheeks, she beat her hands against the closed hatch, splashing water as she hunched over, incoherently begging Kara to open it again.

     

                A hand clapped down on her shoulder then, startling Lena, who had almost forgotten about the chopper and the three women inside. Kelly dragged her to her feet, ashen-faced and wide-eyed as she gave Lena a searching look, a confused furrow between her eyebrows.

     

                “What happened?”

     

                “She’s trying to free them,” Lena managed to choke out. “We need to- we need to open it. Help me. Quickly.”

     

                Kelly’s expression was wary as she faltered, her mouth thinning with regret. “Lena-”

     

                “Help me,” Lena ground out, trying to sink to the deck as Kelly held her aloft by the shoulder of her soaking-wet sweatshirt.

     

                Straightening, Lena scowled as she tore herself free, staggering backwards, her breath hanging in the air as she stared at the psychologist with surprise. Neither of them spoke for a moment, their cheeks ruddy, covered in blood, shivering from the cold that would surely leave them with hypothermia and potential frostbite if they didn’t get someplace warmer and get into dry clothes soon. Lena knew that, she knew all of the facts, knew that each minute delayed meant less fuel to make it to the mainland, that Alex was bleeding out in the chopper from a bullet in her shoulder, that they were slowly sinking as water seeped into the prison, weighing them down, and Kara wouldn’t come back out unless it was with the family she’d made for herself over the last eighteen years. 

     

                “We have to go,” Kelly eventually said, her dark eyes pleading, bottom lip wobbling with fear for her girlfriend. “Please, Lena.”

     

                “Then go without me.”

     

                “You know that we can’t. You’re the only one who can fly-”

     

                “You think I’ve ever flown a helicopter? I had people to do that for me,” Lena laughed, the sound almost hysterical. “I don’t even like flying; I’m scared of heights.”

     

                A ripple of anger crossed Kelly’s face. “What, you were planning to make it up as you go along? Bluff your way through flying us out of here?”

     

                “Yes.”

     

                “Tell me you’re fucking joking. Tell me we’re not stranded out here with my partner bleeding out because we were all stupid enough to go along with your plan while you lied through your teeth. And now you won’t even try.”

     

                Shrugging indifferently, Lena swallowed thickly and turned her attention back to the hatch. She started to sink back down to a crouch, teeth chattering, hands red raw from the cold, feet numb in her soaked shoes.

     

                “Are you going to help me or just stand there?”

     

                Kelly pulled her up again, Lena fighting against her as her feed slid about and Kelly staggered as she tried to keep her balance. Letting go of Lena, who reeled backwards, the breath sawing in and out of her lungs as the air burned, the cold freezing her lashes together where they were wet from the tears, Kelly pulled out her pistol and raised it in a shaking hand.

     

                “Get on the chopper.”

     

                “Fuck you.”

     

                “She made her choice, okay?” Kelly shouted, her voice breaking as her expression crumpled. “If you want to save her, you need to save yourself first. Fly us out of here and we’ll come back, I promise you I’ll help you get back here. If you’re as rich and smart as you say you are, you’ll have access to all the resources you need to get her out. But we’re wasting time right now so … I need you to come with me. Please.”

     

                Lena’s resolve wavered and she licked her lips, grasping at straws, desperate to stay, to wait for Kara but knowing she wouldn’t survive long with the exposure to the cold. They should’ve had snowsuits, they should’ve had stolen rations and less blood on their hands. Kara should have been with them. None of it had gone according to plan, and they’d known that would’ve been a very real possibility, but they were all supposed to be together. 

     

                “She wouldn’t want you to do this.”

     

                Eyes snapping back to Kelly, the air was forced from Lena’s lungs as the words struck home, brutally true and wiping out any argument she could have given in response. Kara had told her as much, had made her goodbyes, and the only way Lena could bring herself to leave then was with the intent to come back for her, whether Kara willed it or not.

     

                Pausing a minute longer, the wind buffeting them around, the prison sinking lower in the water, the chopper continuing the monotonous whir of the propellers as the engine idled, Lena clenched her jaw and grabbed fistfuls of her hair as she tipped her head back. Looking at the sky, the pinks and oranges, the yellow ball of the sun peeking over the horizon, she blinked back tears and exhaled forcefully, wanting to scream at how helpless she felt.

     

                Feeling sick to her stomach as silent tears slid down her cheeks, Lena turned towards the helicopter and left Kara behind.

    Chapter 17

                It was rough going at first, Lena somehow managing to get the helicopter moving, lifting off the slowly sinking deck and wobbling about in the air as she moved the cyclic control stick around, getting her bearings as she sat in the large seat and tried to stifle the urge to vomit all over the panel. Making quick assumptions from what she knew of machines she’d helped build, Lena got the hang of things, as she’d anticipated - albeit, under different circumstances - and she managed to steady the chopper before hovering midair as her eyes ran over the dials and switches. 

     

                The fuel gauge was full, the agents having refuelled upon landing while the others unloaded supplies, which was a relief, and Lena looked at the compass and started heading south. She didn’t know where they were, or which coordinates she was supposed to be aiming for, but south would get them to land eventually, even if it wasn’t to Utqiagvik. Alex had once roughly estimated 700 miles and it was a military-grade chopper, which would make the journey quicker, but Lena still felt the sense of urgency as Eliza kept steady pressure on Alex’s bleeding shoulder, Kelly fumbling with a first aid kit she’d found beneath a seat in the massive hold. 

     

                Focusing on her task, Lena didn’t spare the agent a second glance, didn’t care too much about the jostling as they hit patches of turbulence, sometimes making them careen sideways before she managed to right the chopper. She was no expert, not by a mile, and it was slow going that it would have been for the guards who had flown the chopper out to the prison. With the military-grade equipment, they should have been able to cover the distance in a little over three hours but it took them almost five, Lena hesitant to push it to its limit, turbulence making her tense as she kept both hands on the control stick, a greenish tint to her face as vertigo made her nauseous and her hands shook, muscles knotted and stiff from the cold. She was sweating profusely, the adrenaline refusing to fade, pumping through her body as she unsteadily guided them back to the base, finally able to make sense of their bearings once land was in sight. 

     

                They came in too far east at the start, verging towards Canada, and she had to bring them around, staying high as the staticky voices of airspace controllers and pilots tried to communicate via the headset hanging limply from the wire. She hadn’t put it on, didn’t see any point in it, and Lena ignored the occasional squawking that was barely audible over the roaring of the helicopter and the wind as she stuck to the coast, trying to figure out where they were supposed to land. She didn’t know the coordinates, only knew it would be remote, a tiny town on the most northern point of Alaska, a government black site there that they’d need to find, if only for the supplies. No one questioned her, knowing that they’d all been briefed on this leg of the plan, how they knew they couldn’t fly a military-grade helicopter over Alaska unnoticed, couldn’t have made it to Anchorage, where Lena had a warehouse and enough money stashed to make them disappear, without refuelling, without resting and taking stock of things. Most importantly, Lena couldn’t have gone to Anchorage without Kara.

     

                “76, -156,” Alex rasped to her mother, limp and barely conscious as she mumbled the coordinates. 

     

                She hadn’t told Lena the coordinates beforehand, hadn’t given her the opportunity to double-cross the staff and just get Kara out, but she told her now and Lena corrected their course against the panels and screens before her. Lena was smart enough to make sense of it with what little she had to go by but it was still a miracle that they made it there in one piece, although she struggled with the descent, the chopper spiralling about in circles as they bobbed up and down, stomachs lurching until they made a hard impact, jostling around the pitted tarmac lot outside the unassuming building set within the confines of the National Petroleum Reserve.

     

                The view of their surroundings as they had descended showed nothing but the cluster of buildings making up the small town of Utqiagvik, a coastline of thin ice and a landscape of mud, snow and rivulets of stagnant water that had already thawed. It was much warmer than it had been at their high altitude, even though Lena had never climbed higher than a thousand feet, but it was still so cold that Lena could see her breath before her, hands practically frozen to the control as she struggled to make her fingers uncurl. Body aching and the adrenaline making her tremble as she went slack, Lena remained seated as she stared blankly out the windscreen.

     

                Outside, the door to the building squeaked open and a man stepped out into the cold, snowsuit and boots heavily padding him, a beanie pulled down over his head and thick gloves on his hands. He was dressed in DEO standard-issue black and stamped his feet as he exhaled a plume of white, shouting at them as the propellers slowed.

     

                “Took you long enough!”

     

                He moved too slowly for Kelly, who threw open the chopper door and shot him in the head before catching the woman who followed him out a minute later at the sound. The gunshots rang loudly in the silent landscape and they waited a few minutes before Kelly jumped out of the helicopter, adjusting her grip on the gun and glancing over at the other women.

     

                “Wait here.”

     

                Lena was still in her seat, chewing on the inside of her mouth as she resisted the urge to turn right back around. Logically, she knew at the very least she’d have to refuel, get something warmer - she’d take the clothes of the dead woman’s body if she had to - and try and find some information inside on the coordinates for the prison. 700 miles could be a wide swathe of area for a sunken prison to be inside and she didn’t have time to waste. It was clear to her that without the sealed hatch, the prison would flood with the slow but steady stream of Arctic water. And without the central control panel functioning and the damage inflicted, there would be no lights, no gas or water, no generators or way to resurface. 

     

                At this point, it would be a rescue mission with a very short deadline, although Lena couldn’t be sure how long the supplies inside would last; the delivery pallets had been inside the flooding chamber when they’d left so it would most likely be whatever they already had in the prison sectors beyond. It likely wouldn’t give her long at all, maybe a month or so.

     

                Kelly cleared the building, brushing aside the plastic curtain as she strode back out, nodding confidently as she slipped the gun into the waistband of her pants and moved over to the helicopter. Eliza was trying to lift Alex’s dead weight, struggling as Lena watched over her shoulder until Kelly reached her, assisting. Forcing herself to move, knowing she had to get warm, Lena followed after them, watching them bear Alex’s weight between them, arms around her waist.

     

                Inside, it was gloomy and took Lena’s eyes a moment to adjust. There was a short hallway through the doorway ahead and doors immediately to her right and left, branching off the small mudroom of an entrance. Kelly led them through the right doorway, into a weakly lit kitchen, metal worktops with a gas stove and a sink along the right wall, a boxy fridge with a chest freezer on the opposite and a metal island in between. Swiping everything off the island, an old yellow pages slumping on the concrete floor with an enamel coffee cup, a pen and a plate with a half-eaten sandwich for lunch, Eliza and Kelly lifted Alex onto it, the injured woman gritting her teeth as she muffled a sound of pure agony.

     

                Lena busied herself with looking around the room, which extended beyond to a vinyl-topped table with three rickety folding chairs, a sagging sofa set before a boxy TV, which must have been from the 80s, and a low bookshelf with a few books curling from the damp air and a radio set on top with a cactus that was managing to thrive. She nudged aside the mould-speckled canvas blinds covering a small, square window looking onto nothing, the glass thick and distorting the view beyond. A fan heater in the corner stuttered out hot air, not enough to combat the intense chill seeping in through the boxy concrete building, and Lena crossed over to it, fingers reaching for the warm air.

     

                “Lena?”

     

                She glanced over her shoulder at the sound of her name, her eyes landing on Eliza, who nervously forged onwards.

     

                “Do you have any experience with medicine?”

     

                “I’m an engineer and computer programmer,” Lena flatly replied, her damp clothes chafing, her stiff limbs like lead and her patience dangerously thin as she rubbed her forehead, dried blood flaking away. 

     

                At the defeated look on the doctor’s face, Lena swallowed her bitterness and curtly continued. “But I’ve dabbled in biomedical engineering so I know enough about anatomy.”

     

                Nodding, Eliza hesitated a moment, uncertain as she anxiously wrung her hands. “Would you help me?”

     

                Lena paused, although she’d known where the question was leading. Her lip curled in a faint sneer as she glanced at Alex, stretched out on the wobbly kitchen island, and it would’ve been so easy to let Eliza sort it out while she bundled on her layers and figured out how to refuel the helicopter before she went back for Kara. Moving over to the kitchen table, Lena picked up the resin drink coasters and walked over to the island, crouching as she worked enough of them beneath the short leg to stabilise it.

     

                “Were you a GP or a surgeon?”

     

                “Does that matter? I’m all she has,” Eliza countered, her voice frayed and cracking helplessly. “But yes, I was a general surgeon.”

     

                “And if it punctured her lungs?”

     

                Giving her a tense look, lines of stress ageing her appearance, Eliza swallowed thickly. “I’m all she has.”

     

                “And? What is she to me?” Lena haughtily replied.

     

                “Nothing. She’s nothing to you but she’s my whole world. She might not deserve your help, and I won’t defend her for what she’s done, or pretend that she has been good to you but … if you could find it within yourself to help me … I will help you get Kara out. I promise you. I swear on my life and I will get on my knees and beg if that will change your mind.”

     

                Tense as she stood before her, Eliza’s blue eyes were swimming with tears, her shoulders taut, and Lena really did believe that she would get on her knees and beg if it helped save her daughter’s life. Pity knifed through Lena, keener than her resentment, but she was angry and she balled her trembling hands into fists as she walked out of the room, moving through the small base without knowing where she was going. 

     

                She bypassed the entrance, ducked her head into the gloomy room with the control panels and computers, and then carried on down the short hallway. There were two doors on either side leading to two bedrooms, a bathroom and a supply closet, well-stocked with everything they could have wanted.

     

                Lena shouldered her way into the bathroom, the door warped from the damp and sticking as she opened it, and she tugged the light string, a naked bulb offering wan light. She was freezing cold but pulled off her filthy sweatshirt, dropping it to a damp heap on the floor, and pushed up the sleeves of the white undershirt, baring her forearms and running the water until it was hot. It made her skin sting, the cold so deep in her bones that it hurt, the salt and blood vigorously washed away with the handwash sitting on the edge of the basin until the skin beneath was soft and pink. 

     

                Shutting the water off, Lena grabbed the hand towel and dried off before looking at her gory reflection in the black spotted mirror. Sniffing, she swallowed thickly and stood there for a moment, taking stock of things. With a rough sigh, she threw the towel into the wall and closed her eyes before inhaling sharply and striding out of the room. 

     

                Pausing in the kitchen doorway, Lena watched as Eliza cut away her daughter’s clothes, medical paraphernalia spread out on the kitchen counters, Kelly disinfecting the instruments with boiling water from the tin kettle. Eliza glanced up at the flicker of movement and Lena swallowed her anger, walking further into the room and tugging clean latex gloves from the box as her mouth thinned with resentment.

     

                “Thank you,” Eliza murmured, meek with gratitude as Lena stepped up beside Alex, taking in the waxy sheen of her bloody face, her eyelids fluttering as she clung to consciousness, looking deathly grey and limp. 

     

                Lena couldn’t speak past the lump of fury caught in her throat, nodding curtly instead as she peeled back the cotton undershirt and exposed the bloody mess of the shoulder wound. It slowly oozed blood and Lena didn’t want to be the one to mention how much Alex had already lost. There would be no possibility of a transfusion but there was saline in the first aid kit and Eliza slipped the cannula into the crook of Alex’s elbow and had Kelly hold it up, replacing lost fluids, the best they could do under the circumstances. As far as Lena could tell, with what limited medical knowledge she had, it wasn’t that bad.  

     

                There was no exit wound and it looked like the bullet might have struck her collarbone, but either way, it was still a nasty injury and Lena felt a little unsteady at the thought that it should have hit her. She couldn’t fathom Alex pushing her out of the way, even if she was the only one who could have flown the chopper, which had been a bluff anyway. Silent, she allowed Eliza to take the lead and followed her instruction, Kelly holding Alex down, nothing strong enough to fully take the pain away as she writhed at the agony of Eliza poking around in the small bullet hole. Lena had to hold her arm down with her left hand as she blotted away the pooling blood for Eliza.

     

                The dim bulb cast a poor light over their work, their shadows making it hard to see what they were doing, shuffling around to try and get a better look as Eliza used a scalpel to widen the incision slightly. The sight of the scalpel made Lena’s stomach turn and she had to clench her teeth against the hollow shakiness, swallowing the taste of bile as she sniffed and cleared her throat, white as a ghost. Dabbing at the wound, she glanced at Alex’s face, taking in the sliver of whites beneath closed eyelids, the way her skin stretched taut over her features, how she stiffened at the bouts of pain as her mother poked around in the wound, trying to remove the bullet. She almost thought it would be a kindness to knock her out with a heavy-handed punch.

     

                The atmosphere was tense and they were all exhausted, damp and cold as they endured the long minutes of impromptu surgery, until Eliza finally removed the bullet with a shaky hand, letting it ping to the metal countertop. From what she could determine without any X-rays, the bullet had nicked the bottom of Alex’s clavicle, up near where it joined her shoulder, missing any arteries but splintering a piece off the bone and snapping it in half. Nothing that she wouldn’t heal from, given enough time. 

     

                Still, when it came time to stitch her up, Eliza couldn’t work the needle through the edges of the hole as Alex tried to swallow the ragged scream of pain. It made her mother stay her hand, pale and frightened as her fingers trembled and her blue eyes swam with tears. Gritting her teeth, Lena gently pried the hooked needle from her hand and nudged her aside, unbothered by how much noise Alex made as the two women held her down. Sewing her up with quick neat stitches, Lena snipped the end and stripped off the latex gloves, tossing them in the half-empty trash can and storming off without a word.

     

                Making her way to the supply closet, she rooted through the spare clothes, coming up with a polo shirt and cargo pants identical to the ones Alex had worn as a guard, and then a fleece and a snowsuit. There were spare boots two sizes too big as well, brand new in a box, and Lena shed her clothes, dumping them in a wet pile as she pulled on the clean uniform. She was working the snowsuit over the thick socks when Kelly appeared, after hearing the two women carry Alex down the short hallway, the creaking of a bed as she was laid down to rest. 

     

                Barely sparing her a glance, Lena continued to work the suit over her feet and pulled it up to her waist before shoving her arms through. Kelly chewed her lip for a moment before she spoke, her voice hoarse and hesitant.

     

                “Any other spares?”

     

                Lena didn’t speak, just gestured to the well-stocked shelves and zipped herself up before snagging the boots and brushing past her.
