Kara didn’t hesitate this time, didn’t slow down, didn’t dodge around any of the sailors she came across as she barrelled right towards them, shouldering through until she burst through the door and tasted salt on the harsh wind. Without pause, she let her momentum carry her to the railing and pitched herself over the side.

     

                It was a longer distance than what she’d covered trying to get onto the carrier but she fell quickly and without any fear, striking the water and plummeting down deep into the sea before she paddled back to the surface. Drawing in a gasping breath, she bobbed with the waves before setting off at an angle, the white mass of an ice floe in the distance the only visible place to go to. There were the other vessels of course, small naval ships from the United States and Canada, and a few Coast Guard ones too, but Kara wouldn’t trust any of them. Instead, she put her faith in a small sheet of ice that hadn’t melted in the summer warmth. 

     

                Cutting through the water quickly, she dragged herself onto the ice and was glad the cold didn’t bother her as she flopped down onto it, her chest rising and falling as a puddle formed beneath her. Staring up at the sun overhead, Kara wriggled her fingers at the strength coursing through her, listening to the brisk wind sweeping across the stretch of ice and water as panic filled the aircraft carrier and a heartbeat beneath the sea continued to steadily beat.

     

     

                Lena was kept under close watch within the confines of the abandoned office, her old block mates taking her protection very seriously - whether for her own sake or because of Kara - but it was an unpleasant situation to be in. Aside from the pilfered pills from the lockers in the medical bay, nothing stronger than an over-the-counter painkiller left on hand after months of treating the other wounded prisoners, Lena had nothing to dull the edge of pain from the wound in her side. She felt warm and was sweating, despite the chill of the prison, blinking up at the harsh fluorescents as she prayed that her plan worked.

     

                It was worse than she’d anticipated, being back in the prison, the smell of it making her feel sick with panic, her stomach jolting and her skin prickling with unease at the familiarity of the hallways, of the sounds of old pipes and flickering lights, dampness and mould. She thought she might be sick but just closed her eyes to it all, swallowing her gorge as she tried to blot out the world and waited for Kara’s rescue.

     

                Lena was confident that she’d made the right choice, that Kara’s abilities would be enough to get them all out. It was just a matter of how long it would take and she had no quantifiable information to determine that. After so long without full radiation to power her Kryptonian physiology, it was uncertain how long it would take for Kara to reach her maximum strength, and whether it would take all of her power to lift them. Perhaps she’d be stronger than any of them thought, but Lena didn’t know how to assess that, only that within a couple of minutes outside, she’d been able to tear people apart, so it was clear that her strength would rapidly return.

     

                Tired and weak, Lena was just relieved to rest, to know that it was no longer in her hands to find a solution. She’d done what she could now, had given everyone their best fighting chance to be freed by putting herself back in the place she’d never wanted to come back to again. Truthfully, she would have come back to put herself in there, even if it was to only free Kara. She felt that she owed her that much at least, the one person Lena felt any loyalty towards, the only person she felt strongly enough about to move her to do that. If it was between the two of them, Lena didn’t think she’d have it in her to save herself; the guilt would eat her alive. Even knowing Kara had willingly chosen to stay behind and help the others had been more guilt than Lena could bear, even though it wasn’t her fault. 

     

                Unsure of how much time had passed, Lena tried her best to sleep but managed nothing more than dozing off before she jolted awake, the eerie sound of dripping water, echoing hallways and the oppressive weight of the ocean surrounding the prison making it impossible for her to feel at peace. A headache was blooming behind her eyes as the pills wore off and she let out a pained sigh as her eyelids fluttered, a frown between her brows.

     

                “J’onn?”

     

                “I’m here,” his gentle voice reassured her from where he was seated in the open doorway, keeping careful watch for any trouble approaching.

     

                “What time is it?”

     

                “I’m not sure. A lot of the batteries ran out in the clocks. I can find out for you once we’re back on the block.”

     

                “I don’t want to go back there,” she listlessly whispered, a shakiness inside her chest as the fear of that cell ran through her.

     

                “It’s alright; we’re not in our cells anymore. It’s … well, it’s packed in there, to be honest, but it’s the safest place to be. I promise you that.”

     

                Eyelids opening as she pushed herself up slightly, propped up on her elbows so she could look at him, Lena hesitated as wariness stole over her, the hairs on her arms rising. “The safest place to be?”

     

                J’onn gave her a thin smile, the look in his dark eyes defeated and as tired as she felt. “We had to try and save the others in the other sectors, the other blocks. Kara wouldn’t have had it any other way - you know her. Once they had their taste of freedom … well, they didn’t take too kindly to the staff. She rescued as many as she could - even the injured ones - and loads of them died but … it wasn’t all from their injuries when you broke out. Some of the other prisoners … they took their revenge. It was bloody and brutal for a few days; Kara was the strongest, of course, but she couldn’t be everywhere and she was trying to sort out supplies as well. We had to scavenge for as much as we could and pile it in the cell block with the doors sealed shut. Only she was strong enough to open them so as long as they were shut, we were all pretty safe.”

     

                “Is everyone else … okay?”

     

                “Yes. We’ve been managing. The only one on our block who won’t make it out alive now is Mon-El. He caused a lot of problems so we had him in a cell; Querl said one of the others wandering about let him loose after they saw Kara open the doors of the cell block to get to you. I guess they thought he’d go straight for the rations maybe, or maybe they thought he’d deal with Kara. Either way, the other prisoners managed to snag one of the guards and a janitor as well, so …”

     

                “How many are left?”

     

                “After we shut ourselves in the cell block, the rest took each other out, for the most part. I’m not sure who’s still hiding out there but we’ve had to clean up a lot of bodies over the last few months. You may have noticed the smell.”

     

                Wrinkling her nose as a slightly hysterical laugh forced its way past her bloodless lips, Lena hummed at the back of her throat. “Mhm, I saw a fair amount of them when I was swimming in too.”

     

                “It’s a shame but … I can’t fault them. All they’ve known since they got here is brutality and mistreatment. If I hadn’t had my fill of war on Mars, I might have sought my revenge as well. I wish there had been a peaceful way for us to wait out our freedom though. But our friends are safe; Kara saved us all.”

     

                “She’ll have to do it once more.”

     

                “Yes. Let’s hope that she can. And quickly, too.”

     

                His expression was grave and his eyes flickered to Lena’s stomach before back to her face. She knew he was thinking of her injury, which didn’t seem that serious but was subjected to a filthy environment with no disinfectants or painkillers, and no proper medical treatment. They didn’t even have the means to stitch her up, so it was just packed to slow the bleeding, and Lena knew it was the unfortunate position of being back inside the flooded prison that was the biggest threat to her life. The longer she was stuck inside, the greater her risk of infection, sepsis and inflammation, or her body temperature skyrocketing with a fever. 

     

                Contrary to what she’d imagined, the prospect of dying then didn’t frighten her; it was almost peaceful in a way to know that she had fulfilled her promises - except for the one about ice cream on a beach at sunset. But then, so long as that was a possibility for Kara, Lena would feel at peace with the outcome of herself not being present for it. She would like to be there, but if it didn’t pan out that way, she could at least feel satisfied that she had come back for Kara in the end and made good on the promise that she would get them out of the hell of a prison.

     

                “We should move you soon,” J’onn interrupted her brooding thoughts. “It’ll be warmer in there - more comfortable for you too. And you should eat something to keep your strength up.”

     

                “I’d just- I’d like to sleep,” Lena sighed, her eyelids fluttering as her leaden body wished for the reprieve of unconsciousness. “I want to sleep until it’s over. I’m so tired, J’onn. She’s all I’ve thought about for months; I just want it to be over so I can see her.”

     

                “We’ll find you a bed and you can sleep until she comes for you, alright? You’ve done so well, Lena, you can rest now.”

     

                She was falling into a fitful sleep as he spoke, her expression clouded by the pain even as she dozed, no peace for her yet. When Nia came to check on them, J’onn asked her to take the others and sweep the area so they could move her to the cell block. She was oblivious to it all, murmuring to herself as she dreamt of the prison, waking once or twice to find the dream was also her reality before she was asleep once more.

     

                Once they were confident there were no prisoners around waiting to poach their rations or attack any of the staff, J’onn picked Lena up and carefully carried her through the hallways. They were quick, not wanting to chance a run-in with some of the more hostile residents they’d clashed with over the months since they’d been freed, and J’onn was through the doors first, moving to the back of the room and ordering one of the inmates off the cot of Kara’s old cell. 

     

                Lena was set down on the thin mattress and covered with a blanket as a murmur swept through the cell block. They struggled with the heavy doors until they got them closed and J’onn quietly spoke with his fellow block mates to agree that one of them would be at Lena’s side at all times. She’d been their friend, for the short time she’d been inside the prison, and she’d come back for them, as promised, and was partially responsible for their imminent freedom, even if it would be Kara to enact the plan. They repaid her efforts with their protection as she slept.

     

                It wasn’t restful and a fever settled in as the day wore on, her brow prickling with sweat as Nia and then Querl tended to her. They piled on more blankets, knowing how cold she got, and when she woke briefly they made her drink down a cup of water with some more painkillers, the cold of it making her teeth ache as the faint tang of salt made her gag. The block was noisy as well, and she was dimly aware of that as she tossed and sighed on the cot, too many people and not enough space as the close air of so many unwashed bodies made her nauseous. It was more than Lena could bear.

     

                Hours slipped by and the others all bedded down wherever they could find a spot on the concrete floor, some of them two to a cot as they shared blankets and mattresses. Lena was roused from sleep numerous times, groggy and flushed as she peered through the harsh brightness of the lights that never went off, her heart pounding in her chest. Each time she woke, she immediately knew where she was as if she had never left the prison and it had never left her. It was a harrowing night, worsened by the fever and the pain, so uncomfortable that she couldn’t help but toss and turn and wake at the sounds of coughing and whispers.

     

                Feeling half-delirious by morning, as if she’d imagined the whole thing, as if she was losing her mind and had always been there, Lena felt like crying. It was all too much and she didn’t feel good, the bandages around her midriff spotted with blood as it soaked through, her skin warm to the touch and her throat dry. She could barely open her eyes as she coughed, her head banging as she remained limply stretched out on the cot.

     

                Someone sat on the edge of the cot then, their silhouette indecipherable as Lena squinted through her lashes. A cup was pressed to her lips and a hand propped her head up as she choked down the water with relief, pills pressed against her tongue to be swallowed down for only the briefest reprieve from her pain. She finished off the water and was breathing heavily with the exertion of it by the time she was down, unable to keep her head held up to see who it was.

     

                “Thank you,” she rasped, her eyelashes fluttering as she brushed strands of damp hair off her clammy cheeks.

     

                “I’ll be honest with you,” Andrea murmured with wry amusement, looking down at Lena with a rueful smile twisting her lips, “I never thought we’d see you here again. I owe you an apology.”

     

                “Andrea?”

     

                “Yeah, me. Either you’re not as smart as everyone says you are, or you’re a lot less selfish than I am; if I’d gotten out of here, you’d never catch me coming back. But thank you.”

     

                “I didn’t- I didn’t do it for you.”

     

                “I know. I think that makes you a bigger idiot to be a lovesick puppy for an alien you barely know, but I’m thankful for it if it’s the reason I’m getting out of this hellhole.”

     

                “She’s the reason why; thank her for it.”

     

                “I will when I get the chance. Just wanted to let you know that you’re a better person than I gave you credit for. Maybe better than anyone’s ever given you credit for. A person like that should never have been here in the first place.”

     

                “None of us should have.”

     

                “Ah well, it’s only a little while longer. What was it like, being back out there?”

     

                Lena’s eyelids shuttered as a thin smile crossed her face. “I was a fugitive - it was horrible. It’ll never be the same again, though. For any of us.”

     

                “No, it won’t. We’ll have to find something to live for though, or what was the point?”

     

                “I’ve already got mine. Sunset, ice cream, a beach. That’s all I want.”

     

                “Even that seems like a dream come true after this place. That’s a good thing to live for, Luthor. Just make it through the next couple of hours, alright? It’s just past seven - I can’t imagine it’ll be much longer.”

     

                Already slipping away again, sweat beading on her forehead as her eyes rolled beneath closed eyelids, Lena hummed faintly at the back of her throat. “She’ll be here soon.”

     

     

                Kara had spent the rest of the day on that ice floe, her wet clothes drying stiffly on her body as the water froze in the cold temperature of the Arctic Circle, recharging in the sunlight as it lingered. She was fortunate it was summer, and that the midnight sun meant that it stayed light all through the night, the radiation fuelling her as she sat alone on the ice and patiently waited until she felt strong enough to lift the prison.

     

                The only problem was that as the radiation suffused her starved body, it took more energy to sustain her, and with the meagre rations she’d been on before, and the carefully managed caloric intake for the last eighteen years before that, Kara found herself ravenous. Even though the diet of prison food had been bland and sufficient enough to only cover her body’s needs, as depleted as her powers had been underneath the red sun lamps, Kara had never starved, never felt a hunger like the one she felt then. Despite three months of slim rations, barely a few mouthfuls a day, dwindling to one - if that - was not as bad as the gnawing in her stomach that evening as the sudden influx of strength and power demanded more of her than she had ever had to give before.

     

                It was almost midnight when she couldn’t help herself, sitting up from her splayed position and then climbing to her feet. There was that strange lightness that she felt again, knowing that she would be able to simply shoot through the sky if she dared to try it, deep in her bones, her body knowing her limits better than she did. Kara had never flown before, not properly, managing barely more than hovering before she’d been locked in a cell and cut off from her abilities. But that awareness was there as her powers came back, like an itch that she couldn’t shake, although she could have tapped into it, tapped into her full potential if she’d wanted to. And she did, but Kara knew she didn’t have the control necessary to manage such a thing.

     

                But she was starving and she was expecting to lift an entire prison from beneath the sea the next day - she wouldn’t wait any longer than that - so she had to try. She wouldn’t have the strength to do what needed to be done on an empty stomach, and it was that thought alone that led her to her feet, squaring her shoulders as she stared at the ships, their flashing lights beckoning her. Of course, they’d be just as likely to blast her out of the sky and back into the water if they thought her a threat, but there were other ships around. She could hear them, miles away in the distance, lurking near enough to not be a nuisance but intrigued and using the guise of fishing to stay within the vicinity. 

     

                Kara decided to take a chance on one of them and clenched her jaw as she inhaled deeply, muscles tightening as she coiled to spring. With a leap, she was air bound - not much, maybe fifteen feet in the air as she blinded thirty feet forward - before gravity claimed her and her feet clipped the surface of the sea, soaking into her canvas shoes as her composure wobbled. Arms windmilling, Kara was obstinate as she staggered onwards, kicking waves but staying somewhat afloat as she tried again. 

     

                In fits and starts, she covered a few hundred feet before she really got going, shooting skywards with her arms stretched before her, body parallel to the water below. The surface glimmered in the light of the midnight sun and she heated the shouts of amazement from the decks of various vessels as those on night shift caught sight of her flight. It was thrilling as much as it was terrifying, and Kara wobbled as she shot forward, slowly getting the hang of it as she picked up speed.

     

                Her first flight was clumsy and slow compared to what her potential was, although she was barely more than a grey streak to anyone watching, but Kara was just grateful she didn’t pitch herself headfirst back into the sea. She wasn’t sure she’d have the momentum to take off again whilst treading water. Spared that difficulty, she pinpointed the first boat outside of the convergence of government-owned vessels and streaked towards it as quickly as she dared, setting down on the deck with a thud before she staggered a few steps, unbalanced and still moving quickly. 

     

                Barrelling straight into the side of the cabin on the deck, Kara winced at her clumsiness and took a second to run her fingers over the riveted metal, making sure she hadn’t left a person-sized dent in the side. She could hear the sounds of voices below and was wary as she crept towards the unlatched door to the cabin and the depths of the fishing vessel beyond. It was a sensory nightmare on that vessel, even more so than on the aircraft carrier, the smell of fish so nauseating, mingling with the all too familiar coppery tang of blood, the air thick with it as she breathed shallowly, worried about being caught, the taste caught at the back of her throat.

     

                It was a clean ship though, the ropes tied off or neatly coiled, the deck rinsed of the blood from their catch, nets stored away. It made it easier for Kara to pick her way to the door without incident, slipping inside without a sound and descending a ladder into the bowels of the ship. It was utilitarian in its appearance, but there was a full kitchen and the clutter of the crew from their weeks at sea. 

     

                Making for the fridge first, mindful of the quiet voices in the rooms off the main area, Kara gingerly eased it open, baring her teeth in a wince as she tried to be quiet. Cans of beer rattled slightly in the door but she got it open with little fuss and plucked a few things that looked ready-made or would be filling at any rate. Pickles, packets of smoked ham and bacon, a block of half-used cheese, cured sausages, bread rolls and little yoghurt cups. Piling her findings on the counter, she pillaged the cupboards next, half a box of cereal, unopened packets of cookies and chips, sacks of flour and rice - which she left untouched - and root vegetables that were vaguely familiar to her, even if she’d only eaten them in other forms. Grabbing the sack of potatoes, two bags of carrots and a bag of onions, Kara searched around for something to carry it all in.

     

                Finding a canvas sack, she quickly transferred her goods to the sack and then stole a few cans of soda and some beers for good measure, not knowing what they were but knowing she’d need a drink. Slipping out again, feeling as if she should have been caught, as bright as it was at midnight, Kara took off with her bounty clutched tightly to her chest. If the crew wondered where a chunk of their remaining food supplies had gone when they got up the next morning, they’d have no idea an alien had stolen in and taken it all. 

     

                It was a slower flight back, unbalanced by the extra weight of her food, but Kara was getting the hang of it now, was not quite so unsteady, as if she was going to fall out of the sky at any moment. When the sight of the ships and aircraft carriers loomed into view - miles away, given her vision - it was something of a relief and she zeroed in on Lena’s heartbeat the moment she could make out the noise. Still beating, still alive.

     

                Setting back down on her ice floe, Kara opened the bag and pulled out the first thing she got her hands on. Eating her way through a packet of cookies, she was delighted by the sight of them, reminding her of the little packets Eliza had given her after routine blood tests. The next items up were the raw potatoes, and Kara wrinkled her nose as she bit into one, a starchy mouthful entirely unpleasant after the sweetness of the cookies. Still, she needed her energy and it was edible, so she forced down half a bag of them as quickly as possible before chugging a beer and peering at the label as the sour taste filled her mouth. That wasn’t any better.

     

                She enjoyed the chips, the raw carrots weren’t half bad, and the cheese, sausage and ham went down a treat with a couple of withering apples - Kara was familiar with them - the varying flavours of the yoghurt cups and three sodas. Reserving some of her goods for later, Kara was pleasantly full and lay stretched out on the ice as she left her body to metabolise it all. It wasn’t the most nutritious, but she needed calories then, and her thieving had done the trick. What she needed then, was sleep.

     

                As much as she wished she was ready to retrieve the prison, she knew she needed rest before she could try it. Being tired wouldn’t help her, and she would only have so many shots at this, depleting her energy and powers with the exertion, so Kara didn’t want to waste any opportunities. A few hours of sleep in exchange for a quicker rescue was logical but Kara still had to stamp down her frustration at the thought of delaying getting Lena out of there even by a few hours. The truth was she just wasn’t strong enough yet, needed at least another good day of pure sunlight to feel her true potential, but she couldn’t wait that long, didn’t want to wait that long.

     

                Stretched out on the ice, she closed her eyes and eventually found sleep, after a restless hour of trying to block out the noise. It was everywhere, so overwhelming that she couldn’t blot it out; the sea, the ice, the ships, engines, voices, heartbeats, footsteps, even beneath the sea with the prison and all the noise that encompassed that. Eventually, her exhaustion gave out and she slept like the dead, hours passing by as the sunlight brightened with what should have been the approaching dawn, although the sky had never darkened to begin with. 

     

                It wasn’t until the whine of an engine interrupted her sleep that Kara woke, blinking at the brightness as she sat up, her sack of food tucked in at her side as she looked around. The ice floe was high enough above sea level for her to not be at risk of the tide sweeping her off it, but it almost meant she was high enough to have a safe vantage point of her surroundings. That also benefited her as she watched a little black inflatable boat, like the one the divers had been in when she’d surfaced from the prison, skim towards her. The engine whined and it was filled with five sailors, making a beeline for her.

     

                As it neared, she was glad she was six feet above them, but she didn’t move closer to the edge of the ice out of concern for her safety. Planting herself in the middle of it, she fished out a packet of chips and tore it open, eating as she listened to the little boat approach before the engine was killed.

     

                “Kara Zor-El, you’ve been ordered to surrender yourself to the custody of the United States Navy. If you do, no harm will come to you. No charges will be raised against you. It’s in your own best interests-”

     

                “No, thank you,” she called back.

     

                The voice fell silent for a moment before they tried again. “I urge you to reconsider the Captain’s generous offer. If you intend to interfere with a naval operation, the consequences will be-”

     

                “I said no, thank you.”

     

                “Miss Zor-El-”

     

                On her feet then, Kara moved to the edge of the ice in a flash, her hands balled into fists, pulverising her bag of chips as she bristled with frustration. She didn’t know it but her eyes were glowing a dangerous red as she hunched her shoulders, frightened and angry, so many years of mistreatment making it hard for her to believe a word any human said. Any human but Lena, but her friends, the family she’d made in the prison. Kara swore by their good intentions, as clouded as her judgement was, as naïve as she could be at times, still that little girl who’d been put into a cell with no hope of escape. Except there she was, the breeze of the Arctic ruffling her hair as the ice floe drifted with the current.

     

                “Leave me alone,” Kara ground out through her teeth, five bone-white faces staring back at her with wide eyes as they took in the glowing eyes. “Now.”

     

                She didn’t know how to control her powers then, the anger building as she rose from the ice, her hair drifting around her in the breeze as her glowing eyes brightened. Beams of bright blue scored through the surface of the bitterly cold water, Kara shocked herself as the water hissed and bubbled, steam rising from wherever her heat vision touched. The beams guttered as she tried to rein it in and she accidentally nicked the hull of the inflatable boat before her feet landed firmly on the ice and she squeezed her eyes shut.

     

                Voice trembling as her throat tightened, Kara felt flushed with panic. “Leave, now. Please. I don’t want to hurt you.”

     

                The engine gunned to life and they quickly started to depart as Kara kept her eyes squeezed shut, breathing slowly through her nose as she tried to quell the parts of herself that she didn’t understand. Despite these people, what they could do and had tried to do to her, they weren’t bad and Kara didn’t want to hurt them. She didn’t want to hurt anyone; she just wanted to be free.

     

                “Lieutenant, we’re losing pressure.”

     

                Eyes snapping open at the frantic words and the hiss of air leaking out of the melted rupture point in their boat, Kara winced and dropped her bag of chips before she jumped off the side of the ice and into the water without thinking. There were panicked shouts from the sailors that had been keeping a close eye on her and she resurfaced at the rear of their boat to even more panic.

     

                She hadn’t realised they were armed until one of the sailors unholstered a pistol as the five of them scrambled towards the bow. Piled on top of each other, the one closest to her tried to aim, hand shaking terribly as he aimed the pistol at her and shot, the sound ringing out across the quiet sea. The bullet pinged harmlessly off Kara’s forehead and she scowled as she grabbed the engine. Mindful of the propellor as she let her legs float behind her, she started to kick, spurring the boat back towards the aircraft carrier. 

     

                The sailors didn’t relax, the one with the gun still pointing it in her direction in a trembling grasp, but they were silent and still as she guided them back to safety. They stared at her in disbelief, as if they’d been expecting her to rip them apart, especially after shooting at her, but Kara was merely fed up and impatient to save her friends. She didn’t have time for anything else. 

     

                Reaching the near vicinity of the aircraft carrier, she let go of the boat and started treading water, keeping her head above the lapping waves as she bobbed with the current. Raising her voice to be heard over the sound, her tone left no room for misunderstanding. 

     

                “Don’t come for me again.”

     

                Turning, she tore through the water as she made her way back to the ice, climbing up on top with ease and picking up her packet of crushed chips. As the water froze in her clothes, she ate her fill and tried to sleep a little bit more. It was almost noon and she knew she would have to try soon, that she couldn’t sit there for much longer without trying. Soaking up as much sunlight as she could, Kara grew increasingly more agitated as time passed by. And then, with no signal, nothing that let her know she could do it, Kara decided it was time.

     

                Climbing to her feet, she stood on the edge of the ice and drew in deep breaths as she steeled herself for what had to be done. Without confidence in herself, she would never believe she could do it, but she had to, and more importantly, perhaps, Lena believed she could do it. That was enough for her to try. Launching herself into the water before she could second-guess herself, Kara fought against the current as she quickly descended, moving quicker than a fish as her powerful muscles smoothly went through the motions.

     

                Her biggest issue would be oxygen, and she knew that her inhuman speed was the only thing that was going to help her there. The quicker she went, the quicker it would be done, and then she’d be able to breathe again. Of course, if the Navy had helped, as she’d anticipated, she’d have diving gear to spend up to hours down there, but Kara didn’t want hours. She would do it quickly by relying on herself; that was the only way to get it done.

     

                Diving twenty metres and then some, her eyesight able to make out the shadowed shape of the prison as she neared it, cutting through the sea at an angle, Kara ended up beneath the mass of metal and concrete. It was disorienting to hear all the heartbeats above her and nothing below but sea creatures that didn’t want to be disturbed. Even with her eyesight allowing her to see what she was doing, there wasn’t much to see, and Kara felt a strange pang of loneliness as she positioned herself beneath what she roughly estimated to be the middle of the prison. 

     

                Rising quickly, she planted her palms against the underside of the prison and heaved with all her might. One thing not to be overlooked was that as much as the prison weighted in the water, which was too much for a single ship to winch up to the surface, that was nothing to what it would weigh for Kara to lift it out of the water. Yet she tried, the water pressure and the current making it slow progress as she strained her muscles and kicked her feet as she pushed them towards the surface.

     

                Then her lungs were aching badly and she knew she wasn’t going to make it before she ran out of oxygen, and Kara was forced to abandon her first attempt. Quickly swimming out from beneath the prison, she darted skywards and burst through the water to drink in grateful lungfuls of air. Waiting until she’d caught her breath, barely a minute, she sucked in a deep breath and descended again, going quicker this time, the prison not quite having the chance to sink as far as it had been, which was something at least. If she could raise the prison in increments, that would at least give her a better chance to get it out of the water, where the only thing that would matter would be whether or not she was strong enough to hold it.

     

                Jamming her shoulder against the underside of the prison, she pushed with all her might, teeth bared as her face furrowed with the effort. Pushing upwards against the pressure of the water, Kara lifted the prison, rising foot by foot as her lungs ached, until she had to duck out again for more air. Panting as she paddled in the water, her hair brassy as it clung to her face, she found herself growing frustrated at her own limitations, knowing that if she had more time, had more sun exposure, she’d be able to do it with relative ease. It might be the extent of her abilities but it wouldn’t be quite the struggle it was then. Either way, she had to do it, then and there. There was no room for limitations or struggles.

     

                With another deep breath, she dived down again and found herself determined this time. Honing in on Lena’s heartbeat, she swam to it, off-centre to the middle of the prison but an anchoring point for her, a beacon calling to her. Lena was just above her, a few feet of steel and concrete separating them, and Kara’s throat tightened at the blatant desperation to see her, to wrap her in a fierce hug and never let her go. They were going to get ice cream together and eat it on the beach. It was everything she’d ever wanted and so she did what needed to be done.

     

                Pushing with all of her might, beyond what she thought she had the strength for then, she drove the prison up and up, until she could feel how close she was, the water tinged cerulean instead of deep navy as sunlight filtered through the surface of the ocean. It was there, just a few more metres away, and Kara’s lungs were on fire as she gouged handprints into the algae-slick metal sheeting above her. She was running out of air but she was so close.

     

                So close to saving Lena, to everyone’s freedom, and she didn’t want to stop, didn’t want to lose that momentum again. Straining against tens of thousands of tonnes pressing down on her, muscles aching and tendons taut as she gritted her teeth, Kara forced herself to keep going. She saw black spots, fighting the urge to suck in a lungful of seawater, and with a final, desperate attempt to breach the surface, she let out a wordless cry, bubbles streaming out of her mouth as all the oxygen she had left spilt out of her.

     

                And as she threw all of her remaining energy into trying, the sailors on the USS Ford watched as the surface of the ocean churned and the deck of Fort Rozz made its first appearance in three months. But it didn’t stop there, rising inch by inch out of the sea until it fully emerged, and beneath it all, an impossible sight as one soaking wet woman held the weight of the prison in the palms of her hands, rising from the ocean like some god from the old myths.

     

                There were mutters of awe from the aircraft carrier but Kara didn’t hear a thing, her heartbeat pounding in her ears as the blood rushed through her, her whole body straining beneath the effort. She felt like she might pass out, sucking in great lungfuls of oxygen, spitting out the taste of salt as seawater ran off her in rivulets. But she had Fort Rozz in her hands and she was above the water, staring across the glimmering expanse of sea as she marvelled at her own strength. It was a feat that no human could have done and she felt adrenaline rush through her, elated at the surprise of her own capacity, the good she could do with what had been given to her on Earth. It didn’t all have to be death and destruction at her hands; it could be salvation too.

     

                What came after lifting the prison from the depths of the ocean was another thing entirely. Kara faltered as she hung five feet above the waves, holding a prison aloft as her arms started to tremble and the radiation she was still absorbing, still metabolising, tried to offset the sheer output of energy it was taking for her to keep it up. She wasn’t sure what the next stage of Lena’s plan had been beyond Kara lifting the prison out, but the ships didn’t have the capacity to hold Fort Rozz afloat with their winches, which meant Kara had to find some other way to keep the prison above sea level so the various military branches could rescue the prisoners.

     

                The only viable option she could see was the ice. From her swimming, she could see that the ice went deeper than it looked from the surface, but even the ice floe she was on was only three metres thick and maybe twice that in diameter. She’d need to find a bigger stretch of ice, a patch that was triple or quadruple the size of the prison and a dozen metres thick, still frozen solid even as summer melted off the smaller ice caps. 

     

                Pushing herself to climb higher in the sky, Kara scanned the horizon and headed northwards, knowing that the further north she went, the colder it would be, the thicker the ice caps and the better her chances. Still, she couldn’t go too far and it had to be somewhere the prisoners could be rescued, whether by sea or air, a sense of urgency gripping her as she shouldered the burden and flew until a solid expanse of white filled her field of view.

     

                She had no way of knowing if the ice was thick enough but Kara was starting to flag, each minute that passed by with the weight of it pressing down on her leaching more of her strength. Trying to land slowly as she descended on her chosen patch of blinding whiteness, Kara’s feet skittered as she hit the ice, dropping to a knee as her legs buckled beneath the weight. Gritting her teeth, she strained with the effort as she fell to the other knee, skidding forward, carving a furrow in the ice as she tried to maintain the precariously balanced prison on her palms. 

     

                As she slowed, losing momentum, Kara carefully tipped the prison so the front end of it grazed the ice, before she slowly started to shuffle backwards on her knees, retreating to the rear of the prison as she tried to stay low so that the prisoners trapped inside weren’t too unbalanced by the movement. Walking her palms back and back on the underside of the prison, she reached the end of it and ducked out from beneath the mass of metal and concrete until she was holding it in her hands. Slowly lowering the weight of it to the ice, she let it go and there was a booming shake as ice cracked and sank lower into the ocean at the sudden weight. 

     

                Her hands nervously flitted around as she listened to the stress fractures in the ice, wondering if she was about to submerge them again. It held, although she wasn’t convinced, and Kara knew that it would have to be everyone for themselves while she got Lena out. Only once she was safe would she be able to help the others, which meant she needed to get a move on. 

     

                Finding a service ladder on the side of the prison, she hauled herself up, algae and rust covering her hands, before she was on the concrete deck, her socks slipping on the saturated surface as she sprinted for the elevator hatch. It would have been easier to make a hole in the side of the prison, but Kara erred on the side of caution, not quite sure that the ice would hold the prison for long. In the case that they were all plunged into the ocean again, a hole in the walls wouldn’t be ideal and would probably ensure at least all of the humans died. As cold and difficult as it would be, swimming was the safest option for them all.

     

                A second later, she was in the water, moving faster than she ever had, her lungs full of air as she dived down, cutting through the dark water and through the hallway. She could have punched out a ceiling panel then but Kara kept going, dodging bodies and debris as she forged onwards as quickly as possible, frustrated by her sluggish movements in the water, even if it was faster than she’d been able to swim before, even with fins and an oxygen tank.

     

                Coming up in the ceiling panel, she crawled through the ceiling space and dropped down into a foot of water. The turbulence of moving the prison and then setting it down on the ice had shifted more water through the section she’d just come through and water ran down the stained walls as she splashed down the hallway, avoiding ceiling panels that had rotted through as they fell out of their frames. 

     

                Saturated with radiation, she moved quickly, at the doors to her cell block in a heartbeat, tearing them open and pausing in the doorway to look around with a wild-eyed look of desperation on her face. The cell block was in disarray, supplies strewn around the place from all of the movement, and a few dozen frightened faces stared back at her as she honed in on the sound of a heartbeat tucked away in the corner of what had been her cell until a day ago.

     

                “Everyone out. Now. On your feet!” Kara ordered, her voice hoarse as she stepped over people. Even though she’d only been gone a day, it was still surprising for them to see her in their midst again so soon. “If you can swim, leave now.”

     

                Rounding the corner of her cell, her sight latched onto Lena, stretched out with blankets piled on top. Her dark hair was plastered to her sweaty face, so pale that her skin seemed almost greyish, eyelashes fluttering as her lips moved soundlessly. Kara wasn’t imagining things when she thought she made out the shape of her name. 

     

                Moving swiftly to her side, she sank to a knee and reached out to brush Lena’s hair back, a cold hand touching her feverishly warm cheek. “Hey. Hey, it’s me. I’m here.”

     

                “Kara,” Lena murmured, a thin smile crossing her face as her expression slackened.

     

                “I’m here. I’m going to get you out, okay?”

     

                She didn’t wait for a response, gathering Lena up into her arms and turning, her eyes finding J’onn’s as he gave her a questioning look. Crossing over to him, Kara swallowed thickly, nodding. “Lead them out. I’ll come back as soon as I can, alright? We’re on ice; I don’t know how long it’ll hold but the way is clear as long as they can swim through the sections.”

     

                “I’ll help them as best as I can.”

     

                “Round up any of the others you find.”

     

                He turned and touched Nia and Querl’s arms, gesturing them onwards before he started to usher the others into motion. They’d all heard Kara’s orders but were at a loss of what to do and she didn’t have time to sit around waiting to round up and shepherd a few hundred people out safely. Not waiting for anyone at all, Kara lurched into motion, cradling Lena’s limp form carefully in her arms as she ran down the hallway, nothing more than a streak of grey to the curious inmates and staff that poked their heads out of their hiding spots.

     

                She was up in the ceiling with little issue as she floated them through to the crawl space and laid Lena down gently on the steel beams. “I need you to crawl with me,” she softly urged her. “Please, Lena, I need you to crawl now. We’re almost there.”

     

                Exhausted, her breaths shallow and quick, Lena pushed herself to all fours as Kara kept a hand on her waist, trailing after her as they inched forward. It was slow going and when Lena’s arms buckled and she couldn’t push herself up, her face a mask of pain as the wound in her side flared up, Kara scooted in front of her and grabbed her arm, trying to be gentle but not knowing her own strength as she started to drag her. 

     

                She went beyond the usual panel they’d removed to slip in and out of the water, dragging Lena all the way to the end of the section, where they met the concrete and steel wall encircling the entirety of the middle chamber. Lena cried out softly in pain every few feet as Kara breathlessly apologised, strangled sobs caught in her chest as tears wet her cheeks and she continued to drag her friend along. Barely clinging to consciousness, as feverishly weak and injured as she was, Lena was like a rag doll as Kara pressed right up against the concrete wall and held onto her tightly before smashing her elbow into the ceiling panel beneath her.

     

                Working her legs through the hole, she braced herself on the edge of the hole and guided Lena into the water as well, a sharp exhale of surprise escaping her friend’s bloodless lips at the sudden stinging cold that enveloped her legs. Submerging them deeper, up to their chests as she gripped the edge and kept an arm tightly around Lena, Kara stiffened at the ragged cry of pain that tore from Lena’s throat as the saltwater soaked into her wound, so painful that Lena saw white.

     

                “I’m sorry, I’m sorry,” Kara babbled into her hair as she held onto her tightly, trying to stop her thrashing. “Shh, it’s okay, it’s almost over, okay? I know it hurts but you’ve done so well. I’m so sorry. I just need you to hold on a little bit longer and then we’ll be out of here for good.”

     

                It felt like twisting a knife in her chest, her throat tightening around the urge to cry as Lena breathlessly sobbed, nothing to be done for the agony of salt in the open wound, but Kara just whispered reassurances to her as she waited for Lena to calm down enough to continue. Breathing slowly as she tried to retain her own composure, Kara gently shushed her as she pressed her face into Lena’s hair, listening to their twin heartbeats pattering wildly.

     

                “Come on, we’re almost there. I just need you to take a deep breath for me, okay? One deep breath and then trust me - I’ll get us out of here in no time.”

     

                Breaths frantic as her fear of water and the pain of her wound got the better of her, Lena tried her best to draw in a deep breath. When she finally managed one that Kara thought would last her to the surface, she sucked in her own deep breath and dragged them both under. Her arm braced across Lena’s chest, she towed her through the parted airlock doors as quickly as she could, cursing the sluggish nature of moving through the water, which wasn’t helped by the unwieldy limbs of her friend.

     

                Still, it was all going fine as Kara led them into the cavernous central chamber and aimed upwards to the square of white light overhead, dodging bodies as she kept a firm grip on Lena. It was all going fine until Kara adjusted her grip on Lena, the water making it hard to keep her steady, her fingers pressing down on her shoulder, her forearm across her chest like a seatbelt, and her left elbow having the unfortunate placement of being right near Lena’s stab wound. As she accidentally pressed her elbow into Lena’s bandaged side, Lena couldn’t stop the wordless shout that escaped her with a stream of bubbles as all of her oxygen was forced from her lungs.

     

                Stomach jolting, Kara watched as Lena went limp, her head lolling back against Kara’s shoulder as she passed out, lips parting as the last few bubbles were expelled. Knowing that Lena would inhale a lungful of water without even meaning to, having no air and no conscious ability to stop herself, Kara swiftly turned her in her embrace and pressed her mouth to Lena’s, breathing her air into her lungs as she wrapped her arms around her, one hand cupping the back of her head as she fed her oxygen, the other secured around her waist, Kara furiously kicked upwards.

     

                Grateful for her strength, even if her swimming was rather clumsy, Kara guided them to the open elevator hatch as her lungs burned without the air she’d given away. They came up for air, Kara gasping as she bobbed in the shifting water, pushing Lena up, trying to get her out first as she got her limp form over the lip of the elevator shaft, before hauling herself up, spluttering as she splashed water everywhere.

     

                Rolling Lena over, Kara cradled her in her lap, a lump in her throat as she gently patted her cheek, willing her to wake up. She could hear Lena’s heartbeat, still erratic but strong, and while Kara knew it had been perhaps a minute in the water, she still feared she might have already inhaled water before she’d tried to save her. The searing warmth of her burrowed into Lena’s cold form as she shivered in her soaked clothes, and her eyelashes fluttered a moment later as she curled in towards Kara, to nestle closer to the heat radiating from her, drawing in a rattling breath before she let out a hacking cough, choking up seawater.

     

                “We’re out,” Kara whispered, wiping strands of hair out of Lena’s face as he held her closely, eyes darting from her pale face to the stretch of ice and water and sky. “We’re out, it’ll be okay now. I’m going to get you help, okay? I’ll take you to a doctor.”

     

                Lena’s lips moved but Kara couldn’t make out the word, leaning down, trying not to drip water onto Lena’s pallid cheeks. Head lolling, Lena drew in another breath, heaving a sigh as her body slackened. 

     

                “My mom.”

     

                “Your mom? I met your mom.”

     

                “She’s … a doctor.”

     

                Reassured that Lena was okay now, at least conscious and breathing, Kara didn’t waste any more time as she climbed to her feet with Lena cradled to her chest and took off. The wind whipped around them and Kara looked to the naval vessels in the distance, slowly moving northwards to where she had gone with the prison, picking up speed as she redoubled her efforts, relief and elation washing over her as she pushed herself as hard as she could.

     

                A couple of minutes later, she was landing on the top deck of the aircraft carrier as helicopters and cargo planes were being prepared for takeoff, a few dozen sailors, pilots and technicians pausing to look at her as she dropped down in the midst of them all. Soaking wet, dirt and blood dried hard on her skin, ice forming in her tangled hair, Kara looked feral as she touched down and didn’t miss a beat in her stride as she walked onwards.

     

                “Where’s the Captain?” Kara shouted, eyes darting around.

     

                The nearest ones were frozen mid-task, staring at her with disbelief, with awe, some fear and panic, and she moved towards the building with stairs disappearing down to the other decks. Bypassing the steps, she vaulted over the railing and dropped straight down, slowing to a hover two decks down, where she remembered the command deck being. Kicking open the door, she barged into the hallway and followed the sound of congregated heartbeats, sailors getting out of her way as she passed by in a streak and came to a stop in the middle of the room.

     

                “Where’s Lillian Luthor?” Kara asked the Captain without preamble.

     

                He looked at her with surprise, then down at Lena and back up to Kara’s face again. Mouth opening and closing, he faltered for a moment. “Mrs Luthor is being detained.”

     

                “Release her. Now. Her daughter’s been injured-”

     

                “We have doctors-”

     

                “She wants her mother.”

     

                “That-”

     

                “If you want my assistance rescuing the prisoners, get her mother here now. We’re wasting time, Captain.”

     

                Slowly nodding, his eyes on Lena again, he gestured to some of the milling sailors. Two of them broke off and rushed out of the room and the Captain ran a hand over his weary face before he shooed Kara away.

     

                “They’ll take you to the medical bay. Leave me be.”

     

                “Thank you,” Kara stiffly replied, turning and stalking out quicker than her escorts.

     

                It was an effort to stick to a human pace as she was led through the hallways, down a set of stairs and down another hallway, smelling the sickly sharp tang of antibacterial disinfectants before they made it to the medical bay. They escorted Kara inside and she set Lena down on the bed they directed her to, relinquishing her hold on her in exchange for her hand. Kara wouldn’t leave until Lillian was there, the only person her daughter knew on board, the only person Lena would even semi- trust, the only person Kara would semi- entrust her safety to.

     

                It was another ten minutes before Lillian appeared, Kara’s fierce stare keeping the doctors at bay as they kept trying to hook Lena up to machines, set up a central line and some fluids. Looking none the worse for wear, Lillian breezed inside in her borrowed fatigues, her eyes landing on her daughter as she dismissed Kara from her attention, bearing down on the bed with a severe look on her face.

     

                “What happened?”

     

                “An iron pipe went into her side,” Kara rasped, guilt threatening to overwhelm her as she stared down at Lena’s pale, clammy face. “She asked for you.”

     

                Mild surprise crossed Lillian’s face and she cast Kara a brief glance. If she’d thought the alien looked dishevelled when she’d first barged into the command deck the day before, she looked even worse then. Clearing her throat, Lillian nodded her eyes glancing over the machinery and equipment. She started hooking Lena up, the beeping of the heart rate monitor replicating what Kara could hear with her own ears.

     

                “I’ll take it from here,” Lillian declared.

     

                Wanting to stay but knowing there were lives at risk and she’d done what she could for Lena, Kara swallowed thickly, sinking to a knee as she pressed Lena’s hand to her cheek. Unconscious already, whether from exhaustion or pain, Lena was oblivious to it all. 

     

                “I’m sorry,” Kara whispered. “You weren’t supposed to get hurt. You’ll be okay though, alright? Your mom’s here, and I’ll be right back. I promise. Once you’re better, we’ll get that ice cream.”

     

                She kissed the palm of Lena’s hand and then gently set it down on the mattress before rising to her feet. Lingering a moment longer, Kara dashed out of the room and went to save the prisoners inside Fort Rozz, while Lena stayed behind to be saved by her mother.

    Chapter 26

                Waking slowly, head thick like it had been stuffed with cotton wool, Lena’s heavy eyelids parted slightly before closing, taking a few seconds before she managed to open them again, fighting for consciousness. Heaving a sigh, her head lolled on pillows and she could smell the commercial sterility of hospitals and dental practices as she scrambled to make sense of things. Sluggish, she was slow to connect the series of events that had transpired however many days ago, dimly aware that she had been drugged and that she was not inside the prison any longer.

     

                Managing to get her eyes open long enough to catch a glimpse of a blonde woman sitting at her bedside, Lena frowned as her eyes slid closed again. Prison grey covered in blood, long legs stretched out before her as she tried to sit comfortably, Kara quietly watched Lena come around. Opening her eyes again, Lena kept them open this time, staring at Kara as their new reality slowly started to sink in.

     

                “Kara,” Lena whispered, her fingers twitching on the bed as if she were trying to reach for her.

     

                Tucking her legs in as she straightened, Kara shifted the chair closer to the bed and slowly reached out. Her hand was warm as it enveloped Lena’s, gentle as she feared her own strength. Eyelids fluttering, Lena smiled thinly.

     

                “Hey, you,” Kara murmured, hunching over slightly.

     

                “Is it over?”

     

                “Yes, it’s over.”

     

                “You got them out?”

     

                “I got them out.”

     

                “Good. That’s good.”

     

                There was a brief pause, the sound of the machines and monitors filling the silence, and Lena swallowed thickly. Her eyes were open again, a muddled green as she tried to focus through the haze of what she was grasping was painkillers, not the sedative she’d been given by Eliza. 

     

                “You look tired.”

     

                Kara smiled crookedly, dark shadows beneath her eyes as she hummed at the back of her throat. “I’m okay.”

     

                “You should sleep.”

                

                Chewing on her lip, Kara’s eyes strayed downwards, away from Lena’s searching gaze. She slowly shook her head. “No, I don’t want to do that.”

     

                “Why not?”

     

                Running a hand over her face, still flecked with blood and dirt, Kara closed her eyes, a tense set to her shoulders. “You should rest. Don’t worry about anything else, alright? Your mom did a good job patching you up but you need to rest.”

     

                Alarm spiked through Lena at the evident avoidance of Kara telling her something. It cut through the fog in her mind and Lena struggled to sit up slightly, blinking rapidly as she tried to focus

     

                “What’s wrong?”

     

                “Nothing’s wrong. We’re two days out from port. It’ll all be fine soon.”

     

                “No, something’s wrong. I might not have spent a lot of time looking at you but … I listened a lot and you sound like you’re not telling me the whole truth. Can you just- can you tell me, please? I feel all … uncomfortable. God, these sheets are itchy. Can they get me out of here? I don’t want to be here,” Lena babbled as she got frustrated, overstimulated by the confusion, the heaviness of her body as she slowly scrabbled at the blankets, dropping Kara’s hand.

     

                Halfway rising from her seat, Kara pressed down against Lena’s shoulders, keeping her pinned to the hospital bed. Despite her gentleness, she was an immovable rock as Lena struggled to sit again, and Kara let out a soft sigh, leaning in to press their foreheads together.

     

                “Lena, be still. Please. You’re going to hurt yourself; you’ll rip your stitches.”

     

                Making a low sound of frustration, the fight fled her and she sank back against the pillows. Hand straying to her left side, Lena had the vague sensation of pain, muffled now with the painkillers but the ghost of it nagging at the back of her mind. Kara sounded horribly guilty and Lena remembered her spearing Mon-El on a piece of lead, getting caught in the crossfire as she was pressed against the wall. 

     

                Truthfully, Lena didn’t remember any of the pain, not until she’d been stretched out on a desk having the edges stitched together. Then it was a feverish haze of agony that all blurred together into a nothing day spent drifting in and out of sleep in a packed room, and then Kara’s arms around her, the shock of cold water and then, blissfully, nothing. And now it didn’t hurt at all, the feeling of surgical bandages through the thin hospital gown she was wearing, her arms prickling with goosebumps in the cold, save for the burrowing warmth of Kara’s forehead pressed against her own.

     

                “What’s the matter?” Lena quietly asked, her voice small and frightened.

     

                “They’re detaining everyone,” Kara whispered, trembling with rage and worry. “They said it’s for everyone’s own safety, until we make it back to US soil but … I don’t know. I don’t like this one bit; it feels- it feels exactly the same as before.”

     

                Eyes closed, she reached up to cup Kara’s face in her hands. “Why aren’t you-”

     

                She didn’t get to finish her sentence, Kara letting out a quiet bark of laughter, withdrawing slightly and settling on the edge of the bed. “They’re frightened of me. I guess … seeing me lift the prison out of the water, they saw what I could do. And after their last attempt to detain me went so badly, they didn’t try it when I told them I wouldn’t be moving from your side.”

     

                “Is that why you haven’t slept?”

     

                Falling silent, Kara anxiously chewed her lip as she stared at Lena with wide, fearful eyes. “Mostly. I just- I don’t … want to be locked up again. And I don’t want to be too far away from you to reach you. They- your mom broke me out last time-“

     

                “My mom?” Lena hoarsely exclaimed, jolting as if she’d been shocked, her surprise was so keen. 

     

                Lips twitching with a faint smile, Kara dipped her chin in a shallow nod. “They locked her up too, once she was finished here. Um ... I don’t think they’re good people, Lena. I mean, they came to save us but … I don’t trust them. I don’t want to fall asleep because I’m not sure I’ll wake up again.”

     

                Reaching out, scrambling to make sense of things, Lena’s fingertips brushed the back of Kara’s hand. “It’s okay. I won’t let anything bad happen to you again. I promise. We’ve got the whole world watching; we’ll be alright now. You can sleep.”

     

                Closing her eyes, Kara swiped her thumb and finger across her eyelids as she let out a resigned sigh. Swallowing thickly, she was slow to reply. “I just- if I take my eyes off you … I’m afraid I won’t see you again.”

     

                Lena’s heart wrenched in her chest at the worry clouding her friend's words, the pinched look of fear on Kara’s face. Hands balled into fists in her lap, Kara stared down at them, her shoulders taut as she tried to stop her chin from wobbling.

     

                “And I’m- I’m afraid to look at you as well because … I don’t feel like myself anymore and I- it’s so confusing. I’m scared I’m going to accidentally burn a hole right through you or- or I’ll crush your skull if I touch your face too carelessly. On Krypton, we didn’t have powers, and then I had powers for a couple of hours and then … I was in jail and I was- I was stronger than I should’ve been but there were red lamps and- and kryptonite and I just- now there’s nothing and I’m scared. I don’t know what’s going to happen to me when we dock. I don’t know if I- it’s really bad. It’s so bad, Lena, but I can’t stop thinking about it.”

     

                “It’s okay.”

     

                “No, no, it’s not. I killed a lot of people, didn’t I? And then I killed Mon-El too. And I just- for the last two days all I’ve been thinking about is going back. It- it was so easy to go back last time because … the others were still in there and I had to- to save them but … we’re all out now and I still want to go back. I don’t want to do the things I do. I’m not safe for you to be around.”

     

                Her body going slack as she slowly exhaled, Lena stroked Kara’s knee and gave her an agonised look. “Come here.”

     

                Haltingly shaking her head, Kara kept her eyes on her lap, fiddling with her fingers as she fought back tears. Lena knew it by the sound of her voice, trying to swallow the roughness of it, and her heart ached in her chest as her mouth thinned.

     

                “Come on,” she murmured, a soft sigh. “Come here.”

     

                “I don’t want to hurt you.”

     

                “You won’t hurt me.”

     

                Kara let out a choked laugh, reaching out to lightly place her hand over the surgical bandages. Her mouth twisted derisively and she wiped her nose on her sleeve, sniffing as she gritted her teeth. 

     

                “It’s cold and you’re so warm. Lay down with me and sleep,” Lena continued, “keep me warm and I’ll keep you safe.”

     

                Hesitating, a long minute passing by, Kara eventually shifted, and Lena wasn’t sure if it was the slight tremor as she became more aware of the cold that made her friend move or whether Kara made that decision for herself, but she was relieved either way. Shifting over on the thin bed, Lena made room for her and Kara stretched herself out on top of the blankets. Even with the layers between them, her body heat was feverish and Lena couldn’t stop herself from turning in on her, burrowing closer.

     

                It should have felt awkward, being so close to someone she’d never had much physical contact with before. They’d existed on opposite sides of a wall for so many months, then across from each other. There had been fleeting touches at socials and that kiss once they were on the deck, a few more since then after Lena had broken back into the prison, but this was the first time they had been in such close proximity without any sense of urgency. And it was comforting, a sense of safety and relief as Kara pressed her face into Lena’s dark hair.

     

                “I think we’re all going to be okay,” Lena whispered into her sweatshirt, feeling Kara shudder as she started to cry.

     

                Murmuring soft reassurances to her as she buried her face in Kara’s chest, Lena was grateful she’d been pumped with a load of painkillers so she didn’t have to try to make sense of it all. She imagined when the cotton wool feeling of drifting inside her own body vanished, she’d be left with that same confused fear as well. For so long, the driving force in her life had been getting out and then getting Kara out, and she would have to confront her new reality of readjusting back to normal life while managing the trauma that came with it.

     

                They fell asleep together, Kara exhausted from a lack of sleep and Lena still wrapped in the pleasant haze of drugs, and neither of them stirred for hours. Even Kara and her heightened sensitivity from yellow sun exposure didn’t respond to the constant hum of noise, inside the medical bay and beyond the aircraft carrier, sleeping like the dead as a doctor came to check on Lena and found her sharing the bed with an alien. The doctor had just twitched the curtain back into place and left them to sleep.

     

                When Lena finally woke, it was eight hours later to the sound of the curtain being jerked aside again, this time her light sleep dragging her back to consciousness as she blinked slowly. Her body felt heavy and aching as she stretched and came to, blearily staring at the doctor at the foot of the bed filling out a clipboard. Letting out a rough sigh, she closed her eyes as her face furrowed, feeling the dull ache of her injury as she tried to make herself more comfortable.

     

                “Miss Luthor, how are you feeling?”

     

                Grumbling softly, Lena propped herself up a bit higher on the pillows. “Don’t wake her.”

     

                More alert now, Lena raked a hand through her lank hair and rubbed her gritty eyes as the doctor studied her. The woman was silent for a moment before she repeated herself. “How do you feel?”

     

                “That’s secondary to the cause; how long until we dock?”

     

                “I’m asking so we can administer more pain medication.”

     

                “Thanks but no thanks. I don’t want anything else pumped through me. You can write that down on your clipboard.”

     

                “That would be unwise,” the doctor said with faint amusement. “But I’ll withhold your next dose for the time being if you aren’t in any pain.”

     

                Smiling thinly, her face a shocking shade of white that belied her dismissive attitude towards her pain, Lena turned her head to the side slightly. Kara was fast asleep, lips slightly parted, eyelashes fluttering, and Lena couldn’t resist touching her, trying to be gentle so she didn’t disturb her friend.

     

                “Actually … can you get me something?” Lena asked, her attention moving back to the doctor.

     

                “Is it health-related?”

     

                “Sort of. Just- I haven’t eaten in days. I was hoping maybe I could get something to eat, maybe a change of clothes and a shower. For both of us.”

     

                She tacked on the last bit with a coy look in her eyes, wondering if she could get away with requesting things for the two of them, knowing that Kara wouldn’t part from her to seek it out on her own. The doctor hesitated, setting the clipboard back down and deliberating before she sighed and relented.

     

                “I’ll pass your request on.”

     

                “Thanks.”

                

                “Other than that, you’re recovering well.”

     

                Nodding, Lena closed her eyes against the bright lights overhead, breathing shallowly through her nose as the antiseptic smell of the medical bay made her feel faintly nauseous. She kept her eyes closed and listened to the sound of the doctor moving about until the curtain rattled as it was yanked across.

     

                Wide awake, Lena was still and silent as she tried to sift through her memories and get things straight. It had been a whirlwind of a few days and she wasn’t sure how long she’d been out for, or how much longer of the two days they had left, or even where they were docking, but Lena at least knew that she was with Kara.

     

                Making sure not to do anything to disturb her friend, Lena lay beside her until the curtain was jerked aside again almost forty minutes later. A man had a rattling trolley with two trays and bundles of clothes, setting the latter down on Kara’s vacated seat and then the first tray with a clatter.

     

                Lena wasn’t even aware of Kara waking up, only that her friend was suddenly on her feet, hand around the sailor’s throat as she breathed heavily. The noise had startled her awake and Lena could see Kara’s tense shoulders rising and falling quickly with her rapid breaths. It was only a brief moment before she let go of him and turned around, and Lena saw that her eyes were screwed shut, a pinched look of panic on her face.

     

                Setting the other tray down with an even louder rattle, the sailor muttered something unpleasant beneath his breath as he rubbed his throat. Gripping the trolley, he made a quick exit and Lena sat up, reaching out to touch Kara’s hand.

     

                Jumping at the contact, Kara winced, hunching her shoulders as she pulled her hands back, nervously wringing them. Lena cringed at her tactlessness, withdrawing her hands and balling them on top of the blankets as she looked at Kara with aching concern.

     

                “It’s alright.”

     

                Eyelashes fluttering as she warily opened her eyes, Kara gave her an uncertain look. “Good morning.”

     

                Letting out a small laugh, Lena’s lips twitched with amusement and she sank back against the pillows. “Hi.”

     

                There was a long pause and Lena cleared her throat, gesturing to the trays of food. “You should eat.”

     

                “So should you.”

     

                “No, I’m not hungry. You have them; when was the last time you even ate anything?”

     

                Kara shrugged indifferently, nervously hovering, and Lena patted the bed and gave her a softly pleading smile.

     

                “Come on. Sit and eat. Then we can shower and change our clothes. We’ll feel like new people then.”

     

                Giving her a dubious look, Kara sank onto the bed and looked at the trays of food. She hesitated before reaching out, eyeing the canned boiled potatoes and three-bean salad, corned beef and jello for dessert. It wasn’t that dissimilar from the first week of meals after a new shipment inside Fort Rozz and Kara made no complaints as she ate everything on both trays once Lena reassured her once more she wouldn’t be eating any of it.

     

                Lena hasn’t been lying about her lack of appetite, feeling gritty and unwashed as she languished in bed for days, unconscious and pumped full of drugs. She could wait until her hunger came back, even if it was to ensure Kara ate enough to sustain her fast metabolism, but she couldn’t wait any longer for a shower. Climbing out of bed, she stripped off anything attaching her to machines and the IV drip and gathered up the armful of clothes as Kara hovered around her, looking sheepish and alarmed, hands fluttering nervously as if anticipating Lena passing out.

     

                Tearing back the curtain, Lena looked around, feeling a little unsteady on her feet but haughty enough to get away with being out of bed, unadvised. “Bathroom?” she asked the first person she saw.

     

                Directed to a door at the end of the ward, she set off towards it with Kara on her heels and opened the door to reveal the dismal sight of the bathroom. It wasn’t the luxury of the Waldorf but it would have to do, switching on the light to cast a garish glow over the bleached tiles and spotted metal of the rails situated at varying spots. They had towels as well and Lena set the bundles down away from the shower and turned to Kara.

     

                “You go first, I think I need to … sit.”

     

                Feeling slightly light-headed, Lena sank onto the closed lid of the toilet and kneaded her forehead as Kara made for the shower. Neither of them wanted to be parted from the other, a small comfort amid so much uncertainty, confined to an aircraft carrier with however many strangers who did not have their best interests at heart. Patiently awaiting her turn, Lena rubbed her arms as the frigid air slowly warmed with the heat of Kara’s shower. At least they had hot water.

     

                For her turn, Lena stripped off her hospital gown and left the dressing on her wound in place before she stepped under the stream of water. Kara had left it running to ensure it was hot the second she stepped in, and Lena closed her eyes as it ran over her shoulders and down her back, dousing her in its warmth. She could have stayed in there for hours, letting it work away the stiffness in her joints and muscles, washing away the grime and smell of the prison, but she didn’t linger nearly as long as she’d wanted to. Washing and scrubbing her hair, she shut off the water and wrapped herself in the worn towel she’d been given, rubbing her face dry with the corner and huddling for warmth as she walked over to the clothes.

     

                Kara was already dressed in her borrowed clothes, the same pants and t-shirt Lena had been given before, looking markedly better without the blood and dirt of her rescue mission. She looked more human too, her long wet hair falling around her shoulders and blue eyes vulnerable and wary. Lena dressed quickly in identical clothes, pulling on the jacket as well, needing the warmth of it, wrapping her hair in the towel to squeeze out the extra moisture before she made a pile of their old clothes and towels.

     

                Turning to Kara, she studied her for a long moment as they looked at each other, a few feet separating them, and then Lena stepped in and wrapped her arms around her. She’d never had time to notice it, but Kara was a few inches taller than her average height, and Lena pressed her cheeks against hers, eyes closed, and held onto her tightly. It took Kara a few seconds to let her muscles unclench and hesitantly wrap her arms around Lena in return, burying her face in her shoulder. 

     

                “I missed you,” Lena whispered, her hand cupping the back of Kara’s head, her voice still cracking a little even as she tried to keep it steady.

     

                “I missed you too.”

     

                They stayed that way for a minute, neither of them wanting to let go first, the safety and comfort of each other’s embrace too precious to let go of. They did have to let go though, coming apart but remaining so close to each other, the heat radiating off Kara, making Lena want to sink right back into her, to never feel the cold again. Meeting her gaze, she gave her a small smile and reached up to touch her cheek, Kara’s eyelashes fluttering as she leaned into her touch.

     

                “We should find out what’s going on.”

     

                “They won’t tell us anything,” Kara sighed as Lena made for the door, stepping back into the ward. She stepped up close behind her and lowered her voice. “But I’ve eavesdropped enough.”

     

                Pausing, Lena glanced over her shoulder and gave Kara a look of surprised delight, lips twitching with a smile as she reached behind her and found Kara’s hand. Squeezing gently, Lena led her back to her bed, tucked away in the corner near the door to the ward, and tried not to wince as she eased herself up onto the mattress. Her wound was starting to ache now but not enough for her to regret saying no to the painkillers just yet.

     

                Kara started from the beginning, filling her in on everything that happened from the moment she’d left Lena inside Fort Rozz until she’d regained consciousness hours ago.
