It was a lot of information and Kara kept her voice low, keeping an ear out for anyone approaching, and they sat on the bed together, so close their thighs touched, heads ducked together as their damp hair slowly dried and Kara kept on talking. Lena didn’t know how to feel about it all, relieved that everyone had been rescued, angry that the prisoners had been locked up again, even if only until they docked, unsure of what came next and whether she should try to help. Some had helped her along the way, people who had kept her sane, in addition to Kara, and those who had helped Kara for the long decades Lena hadn’t been imprisoned, so Lena felt like she owed them on Kara’s behalf, but at the same time, she just wanted to leave it all behind and never think about them again. Was it selfish to disappear on everyone and leave them to their fate?

     

                Running a hand through her hair, she closed her eyes and exhaled heavily. “Two more days you said?”

     

                “Something like that.”

     

                “We should wait and see, shouldn’t we?”

     

                “I would like to; if you want off this ship, I’ll fly you home myself. I would understand why you feel that way and I’d come back to you afterwards.”

     

                “But you’d like me to stay?”

     

                “I would. For my peace of mind. I’m sorry.”

     

                Giving her a small smile, Lena squeezed her leg. “Don’t be sorry. I’ll stay.”

     

                Kara’s shoulders went faintly slack and she leaned into Lena, touching their heads together briefly before she sighed. “So … when do I get to hear about what happened to all of you?”

     

                “Oh, um, there’s not much to say. I flew us to the black site, we stayed there a couple of weeks. I flew out a few more times to find you but … nothing. Um … and then I contacted my mom and she got it to the news so we had to leave because they were onto us. We got to my safe house in Anchorage and stayed there for a few weeks until we got news that they were sending the defence force to rescue you. We turned ourselves in then and, um, we got taken to Washington. The President stepped down so I got a pardon from the new President. Then my mom got us clearance to head out to the carrier so … I came straight back.”

     

                “You’re leaving out a lot of details.”

     

                “Some, yes,” Lena hedged, giving Kara a weak smile as her stomach twisted uneasily.

     

                The thought of telling her about the others, about the uncertainty of their circumstances, wasn’t a pleasant prospect, and Lena had been hoping she could avoid it as long as possible. Even now, she hoped to delay it.

     

                “I’m a bit tired,” she suddenly announced, feigning a yawn as she covered her mouth. “I think I might sleep some more. You should too.”

     

                “Lena,” Kara softly sighed, her voice filled with wary impatience. “Tell me everything.”

     

                Rubbing her eyes, Lena hummed at the back of her throat as her mouth thinned. “Like what?”

     

                “They’re not here with you; where are they? Is- is everyone okay?”

     

                Cringing as she turned her head away, Lena’s shoulders were taut as Kara pressed a hand against her back, gently insistent. Chewing on her words for a moment as she tried to break the news to her gently, Lena rubbed the back of her neck and stared down at her lap. She couldn’t look Kara in the eye and tell her.

     

                “They’re all alive. Um … obviously Alex was- was shot, but she pulled through. Eliza got the bullet out. There weren’t any other health issues, so … there’s that.”

     

                “And then?”

     

                Swallowing thickly, Lena squeezed her eyes shut briefly before she sighed, her shoulders slumping. “They wouldn’t do anything. No matter what we told them or the few documents we sent them, nothing was happening . We argued a lot about turning ourselves in but … Alex did in the end. She snuck out one night. I, um, I heard her. I went after her. I … I didn’t stop her though. I think we were the only two who knew that it was the only way; Kelly and Eliza never would have let her go. I did - for you.”

     

                Kara sucked in a sharp breath but didn’t say anything, Lena pausing momentarily to wait for an accusation, a question, anything. When no response was forthcoming, she pressed on.

     

                “Um … we had to wait until there was news of her. Eventually, she was everywhere as well, the whistleblower for the DEO. It gained traction and that’s the reason why they decided to do something, having undeniable proof in the form of an employee. The thing is … even though she was telling them about the bad shit the DEO was doing … she was still a whistleblower so … the stuff that she knew, all of the government side of it, um … well, there’s an espionage act. She’s been in custody, awaiting trial for it. Maybe for the last month now?”

     

                Kara got off the bed, pacing a few steps away as she absorbed Lena’s recount of events, her hands balled into fists and her head tipped back. She had her eyes closed, face to the ceiling, and breathed slowly as she turned and paced back, and then forth again. 

     

                “The others?”

     

                “We all handed ourselves in together. My mom got me a pardon but … well, I never did anything wrong so … they let me go. But Eliza and Kelly … they’re being held in custody too. Um … I’m not sure what’s going on with them, I haven’t seen them since or- or heard anything but … they were complicit, you know? They were employees .”

     

                “No, no, no,” Kara whispered as she turned again, pacing back as she ran her hands through her hair in a distressed manner, shoulders hunched, expression slack with disbelief and panic. “No, that’s not right. They- they didn’t mean to. They’ll let them go, right? All of them?”

     

                Her eyes were suddenly on Lena’s face, glassy with tears as she looked ghostly pale in the harsh light of the medical bay. Wincing slightly, Lena held out a hand to her and Kara quickly crossed over to her side, urgently taking her hand as she gave her an expectant look of hope.

     

                “Kara …”

     

                Faltering, Lena let out a resigned sigh, her mouth turning down at the corners as she gave Kara a pitying look. Squeezing her hand, Lena covered it with her other one and drew in a shaky breath as she met her eyes.

     

                “They’re all … awaiting trial. I’m not sure how long it will take, or what the outcome will be but … it’s not good for them. It’s not going to be good for any of the staff. I need you to- to understand that … they’re probably going to do some time, and I’m sorry to upset you - I know how- how … you feel about them - but … there’s not really much we can do about it. I’m sorry.”

     

                “But … they helped us,” Kara slowly said, her face furrowing with confusion. “They’re my- my friends. The only reason I’m alive is because of them. I- they’re not like the others, you know that, don’t you? I’ll tell them. I’ll- I’ll tell the judge, the- the President. We can get pardons for them too, right?”

     

                She sounded so hopeful, her expression so pleading, that it cut deep as Lena slowly closed her eyes. Cradling Kara’s hand in her own, she hesitated and swallowed thickly. Unable to meet her gaze, Lena softly exhaled.

     

                “They’re not good people. You understand that, right?”

     

                She said it slowly as if speaking to a child, and Kara let out a choked sound of disbelief. Sinking to her knees, Kara grasped a fistful of Lena’s pants in her free hand as she pressed her face into her thigh. Her shoulders shook slightly and her words were thick and wavering when she spoke.

     

                “No, I- you don’t know them like I do. They’re good - they’re good. I promise you they’re not bad. If you- if you can help them-“

     

                Guilt clawed at Lena but she knew in her gut that she wouldn’t be able to make herself go out of her way to help them. Sure, they’d all used each other to escape from prison and been forced into close proximity while they were fugitives, but she would never feel anything more than cordial towards the other three women in their escape party. 

     

                “I can’t. I’m sorry. It’s- it’s out of my hands. The best I can do is give them my lawyers and pay their legal fees but … that’s all.”

     

                “But … we’re supposed to be free.”

     

                “They are free - from Fort Rozz. Normal prisons … they’re- they’re similar to that in some ways but … they’ll be treated better than we were treated. They’ll be fed properly and they’ll be able to go outside for a bit every day, um, and there will be books and commissary where they can buy things, and you’ll be able to write letters and call them and- and send gift packages. It’ll be a prison but it- it won’t be like our prison. It won’t be the same for them, and … I don’t know, maybe it’ll only be a few years for them. I’ll pay their way, as promised and- and Alex … she asked me to tell you where she is so you can visit her.”

     

                Pausing, Lena’s silence was filled with the quiet sounds of Kara’s sobs and she swallowed the lump in her throat as she covered her blonde hair with a hand. Lena didn’t know how to comfort her, so torn with her own feelings on the people Kara had clung to out of necessity and desperation for more than half of her life. She felt sorry for her, for not being able to see past the codependency born in such a bleak place, and she felt sorry for the women who’d been locked away there too to provide a service to the prison, but it didn’t change anything about the reality of what had happened.

     

                “Once we’re back,” Lena continued, her voice a weary rasp, “I’ll find that out for you and see if they’ll let you visit. Eliza and Kelly too if- if they’re still locked up. Um … I don’t know, I just- I’m sorry, Kara. Really, I am, but … it’ll be okay. I can promise you that. You are going to get through it and you are going to be fine.”

     

                She let Kara cry until she exhausted herself, cheeks blotchy and eyes a raw red when she finally glanced up at Lena, and Lena softly clicked her tongue as she cupped her face in her hands. Brushing away a few errant tears, Lena felt such keen sympathy cut through her that she felt if she’d hated the others just a little bit less, she would have given in and promised to do everything in her power to free them. 

     

                As it was, she wanted justice, and while she wouldn’t step in to defend them, she knew she wouldn’t testify against them either, removing herself from it and remaining neutral. It was perhaps cowardly and wrong to omit herself from it but it was too personal and she didn’t want to hurt Kara any further. It would already be a blow to her friend to have lost the majority of the people she’d spent all of her time on Earth with.

     

                “You can’t leave me too,” Kara rasped after a pause, almost as if reading Lena’s mind. “Please promise me we’re going to stay together. I don’t want to … lose anyone else.”

     

                “I’m not leaving you.”

     

                “Thank you. For everything. I- I know … it hasn’t been easy for you, I know you don’t- I wish it had been different. Thank you for- for giving them their freedom for a little while.”

     

                Lena felt her stomach twist with regret, knowing it hadn’t been much of a freedom at that. They’d been cooped up in a black site and a safe house, damp and cold and tense, unable to go anywhere, feeding off each other’s irritability and negativity. They’d feared discovery at any moment and a different cell, and only saving Kara had kept them together, focused on their task. It hadn’t been fun for any of them.

     

                Eyes prickling with tears, Lena gave her a thin smile as guilt welled up in her chest, thumb brushing over Kara’s cheek. “Of course.”

     

                She didn’t know what else to say, didn’t have anything to say in defence of the three women she’d spent a few months living alongside, aside from a lukewarm commendation for their loyalty to Kara that had kept them working at Lena’s side to free her. Other than that, it would be empty reassurances and Lena didn’t want to lie to Kara. If she’d wanted to lie, she wouldn’t have told her the truth about their imprisonment in the first place, and sugarcoating it to someone who’d spent more than half of her life in prison would have been insulting. The best she could offer was an overview of ordinary human prisons, a glimpse of the reality that Kara’s friends were facing, but Lena still felt guilt twinge in her stomach at not being able to offer anything more than that cold comfort that at least they were alive and would be treated fairly.

     

                Remaining on the edge of the bed, Lena let Kara keep her cheek pressed to her knees as she remained on the floor, running her fingers through her blonde locks as she silently soothed her. It was a heavy silence that cloaked them and Lena didn’t know what else to say, no words to comfort her friend when their opinions on the matter differed so greatly. Lena could only feel slight sympathy for the women who’d been forced to work in the prison, and only then for the circumstances that had given them a life sentence, the same as it had for Lena. Anything beyond their mutual imprisonment was where Lena drew the line; they didn’t have to do their jobs, they didn’t have to lock the prisoners away, they didn’t have to take their blood and inject them with medications, they didn’t have to restrain them or make them shower in freezing water, they didn’t have to starve them and leave them to their own minds and the all-consuming boredom and insanity of imprisonment. If they’d had any backbone or morals, they could have joined the prisoners in a cell and served out their imprisonment without dirtying their hands for their captors. If Lena had been given the choice, she knew she would have chosen a cell. 

     

                Of course, she would never know for sure, her resolve never tested in such a manner, no alternative presented to her to to tempt her into turning on her fellow inmates. Lena was steadfast in her conviction that she would not have turned her back on innocent people though. She was many things but a coward wasn’t one of them, and she truly believed it was cowardice that had led to the many employees imprisoned in Fort Rozz to go about their day, prepping food and mopping floors and brutalising inmates, never speaking out against the actions of those that had fully succumbed to the power of being a rung up on the ladder of the prison hierarchy. Others, such as Kara, may not have begrudged them for doing what they could to improve their own circumstances and help the inmates what little they could from their position outside of a cell, but Lena did. 

     

                It wasn’t out of any sense of revenge that she refused to lift a finger in turn, aside from her intention to foot the hefty bill for legal fees for the three women who’d helped her free Kara, otherwise, Lena would have planned to testify against them. It was out of indifference that she removed herself from what happened next. Lena hoped they got what they deserved, but she didn’t plan on being the one to determine what that was. There was a very good chance they would all do some time, and she strongly believed they deserved that, but she wouldn’t cause Kara any further pain by aiding that decision, so she saved her revenge for the likes of the Warden and the Deputy. Not that she had any plans to testify against them either.

     

                As soon as she was off the carrier, Lena was flying as far away as possible, maybe even out of the country if she could get Kara out with her, and becoming a recluse who indulged in anything she deigned to. Anything to fill the bleak pit that the last year had caused, anything to forget that it happened and try to recover from what had been done to her. Preferably somewhere warm, of course, although Lena had never been too fond of the heat before. 

     

                The rest of the day passed by without any further talk of what had happened and what would happen, the two of them so tired that they stretched out beside each other on the bed in silence. It was companionable, and Lena felt oddly nervous as the right side of her body pressed against Kara’s left, her palpable warmth almost electrifying through the layers of their clothes, the firmness of her alien body that looked so human making her pulse stutter and stomach clench whenever she became hyper-aware of Kara’s presence. They dozed in and out of sleep, both of them tired and restless and impatient.

     

                By evening, a doctor had checked on Lena twice more and they were brought dinner, eating silently as Lena palmed off her banana pudding to Kara and picked at her powdered mashed potatoes and ground beef. She was offered more pain medication, and while Lena knew she should accept it, the discomfort of the ache in her abdomen hard to ignore, but she rejected the offer and spent a fitful night trying to sleep some more as Kara similarly found herself unable to sleep, every sound rousing her with the fear that someone was coming to imprison her again. It was a comfort to each of them to find themselves beside each other whenever they woke, and Lena was glad the doctor hadn’t said a word about making Kara leave. She didn’t think anyone could have made Kara do it if she didn’t want to, and Lena was glad that she didn’t.

                

                The next day felt extraordinarily long as well, the hours passing by with agonising slowness, and Lena idly passed the time filling Kara in on geography and political news, cultural aspects of America and other trivial facts and snippets of information she might not have learned in prison. While she’d been educated alongside Alex, there were gaps in Kara’s knowledge, especially when it came to foreign affairs. Lena gave long-winded explanations about the international waters they sailed through and which coastal countries had offered their aid in the search and rescue of Fort Rozz. Kara seemed riveted by any and every piece of information gleaned from their talks and it helped pass the time so Lena didn’t stop.

     

                They fell silent whenever anyone approached the curtain surrounding Lena’s bed, and their brooding wariness made for an uncomfortable atmosphere as the nurses made their rounds and left quickly until the two of them were left alone again. Lena preferred it that way, just her and Kara as they tried to make sense of things, to adjust to their somewhat newfound freedom and the uninhibited proximity to each other. It still felt so strange to Lena that she could have endured so much inside the prison and come out of it with someone she cared for more than she’d ever cared for someone else before, but she did. 

     

                After eight months, she cared about Kara more than she’d ever cared about the family she’d known for almost her entire life, and it went beyond the unchartered territory of their kiss and what it would bring, something fiercer than that tying them together. Maybe it would take years of therapy to understand the bond between them, what had cemented it so solidly to ensure that they would loyally stick by each other’s side through whatever came next, but Lena would never give someone the opportunity to poke around in her head again to find out what it all meant.

     

                “We should ask questions,” Lena murmured as the afternoon dragged on. “I think we deserve some answers about what happens next.”

     

                Kara’s fingers brushed the back of Lena’s hand, “I don’t think they’ll let you leave the ward.”

     

                “Are we prisoners here too?”

     

                “No, but you’re a patient. They probably don’t want you wandering around the carrier so soon.”

     

                “I don’t think they want me wandering around the carrier at all - physical fitness aside. The last thing the Captain would want is another Luthor poking around in classified defence operations. Especially after my mom freed you; I’m surprised she hasn’t weaselled her way out of wherever they’re holding her yet. She’s a crafty woman.”

     

                “You take after her then,” Kara commented with a crooked smile.

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena shifted into a more comfortable position. “Don’t insult me like that. I like you, you know? I’ll have to change my opinion if you compare me to my family.”

     

                “As much of a joke as it was, I actually think it would be a compliment. I don’t know her, of course, but she freed me to come and save you. And she helped you to save me-”

     

                “Yeah, I’m still not sure what her ulterior motives are.”

     

                “Have you considered that there aren’t any?”

     

                “I have , yes, but there has to be.”

     

                “Why?”

     

                “Because she’s my mom. I’m intimately familiar with how she operates. She’s not prone to selflessness.”

     

                “You’re her daughter.”

     

                “That doesn’t score me any brownie points. Why? Did your mom love you a lot? She must have, sending you away to safety.”

     

                Shrugging slightly, Kara frowned up at the ceiling. “I think she did, in her own way. We didn’t express feelings the same way on Krypton, it was all very … what’s the word?”

     

                “Aloof?”

     

                “Sure, aloof. I like to think if she was alive, she’d miss me, and maybe she thought she was doing the right thing to help give me a future, but … it never felt like that. It wasn’t the future she wanted for me. I resented my parents for a while, for sending me here. I could have died with them but I was stuck in prison instead. But … I think she did it selflessly because she loved me. There were no ulterior motives.”

     

                “I don’t think my mom loves me, Kara. She says she does, but people lie.”

     

                “Well, if she doesn’t, I love you, and I would never lie to you, so it’s okay.”

     

                “Liar,” Lena said with a thin smile, glancing sideways at Kara. “You’ve told a few white lies already.”

     

                Drawing in a quick breath and then hesitating, Kara let out a sheepish laugh. “Okay, maybe I have, but I’m not lying this time. As long as I’m around, you’ll always have someone who cares about you.”

     

                Turning her hand over, Lena splayed her fingers, waiting for Kara to weave hers through, and then squeezed firmly. “You’re the best friend I’ve ever had, did you know that?”

     

                “Well …”

     

                “Well …”

     

                They both smiled wryly, their shoulders pressed together, fingers laced together and a strange sense of uncertainty for the future, which could only be better than their shared past so far. There would be time to figure it out, time to untangle the mess of things that prison had made, trying to find some truth amidst the confusion of their new reality. Lena found herself wondering if what had drawn them together was sheer proximity and desperation for some sort of connection or if it was something that could exist outside of prison too. It was a nerve-wracking thought that it could all be fabricated, a false impression of closeness that simply wasn’t real beyond the walls of their cells, but Lena couldn’t even begin to explain how she felt anyway. Only that she was drawn to Kara’s company like a moon revolving around a sun, the gravitational pull of her so strong that Lena would follow her anywhere, apparently even back into prison if it meant freeing her.

     

                “Can I ask you something?” Kara softly asked, her voice light but wary as she tried not to let her doubts cloud their time together. 

     

                At Lena’s hum of consent, Kara continued, teeth anxiously pulling at her lower lip. “What if- what if it doesn’t work out? I mean … what if we go somewhere and it’s just- I’m me , and I’m not human and I don’t know- you’re so- so-”

     

                “So?”

     

                “Fragile.”

     

                Letting out a muffled laugh of surprise, Lena turned her head to glance at Kara, taking in the furrowed look of concern. “I’m more durable than I seem. Harder to kill than a cockroach, apparently. And I’m not afraid of you.”

     

                “I know that. It wouldn’t be so scary if you were . But what if we go somewhere … what if we’re at the beach, enjoying the day with some ice cream, and I … if I forget, if I move too quickly, if I- if I touched you too thoughtlessly … I could kill you in a heartbeat.”

     

                “I could kill you too. I have … so much kryptonite in my lab, it’s not even funny. Inherited from my brother, of course, and his obsession with learning more about aliens but … well, I could kill you.”

     

                “That would be intentional. I could kill you accidentally and I would never forgive myself if I did. I’m not … used to myself. It all feels like too much.”

     

                “We’ll go somewhere away from people and you can- you can practise. You can learn all about your powers and how to control them and it’ll just be me and you. You’re a gentle person, Kara,” Lena murmured, squeezing their joined hands to prove her point. “You would never hurt me.”

     

                “Except I did,” Kara gravelly replied, reaching over to touch Lena’s side, fingers ghosting just above the wound. “If I had been any stronger at the time … I would have skewered you to the wall.”

     

                “But you didn’t.”

     

                “But now I could.”

     

                “You’re holding my hand right now. My fingers are fine, you haven’t broken them. It doesn’t hurt.”

     

                “I could crush your hand in a heartbeat.”

     

                “Then do it.”

     

                Kara let out a quiet scoff, closing her eyes. Her lips twitched, equal parts worry and amusement, and her fingers flexed slightly around Lena’s. Rolling into her, their bodies flush, Lena kept her voice quiet as the tip of her nose brushed Kara’s cheek.

     

                “Squeeze my hand.”

     

                Turning her head towards her, Kara hesitated, Lena’s breath warm against her cheek, and she faltered for a moment, stomach swooping with uncertainty, before she ever so slightly tightened her hold on her hand. As close as they were, she still watched Lena like a hawk, waiting for a ripple of pain or some other sign that she was hurting her, but Kara had been around humans for years, and even if she wasn’t as strong as she was now, she knew how to be careful, how to rein in her strength, even if she didn’t realise it.

     

                “See? Doesn’t hurt a bit.”

     

                “I’m paying attention. What happens when I’m not? What happens when we’re in public and I accidentally burn a crowd of people in half with my eyes? Or- or I clap my hands and burst everyone’s eardrums, or I blow an eyelash off your cheek and send you flying across the room?”

     

                “They’re all hypothetical scenarios. It’s a lot more likely I’ll get struck by lightning or shot. Probably a hell of a lot more likely I’d wind up in prison again, the way this has all gone down.”

     

                “I’d break you out if they did.”

     

                “Thanks. My point is that anything can happen at any time and I know who you are and what you can do and I’m not afraid. I’m not scared of you, Kara, regardless of what happens. What I am scared of is going back to having no one and having to navigate … all of this shit,” Lena said, waving a hand as her expression clouded. “I know I’d rather run the risk of an accident than lose you on purpose. Besides, I still owe you that ice cream.”

     

                Cracking a thin smile, Kara touched her forehead to Lena’s. “You know, if we say it enough times, maybe one day it’ll actually happen.”

    Chapter 27

                Docking the next day, Lena finally attempted to leave the medical bay and wasn’t stopped as she stepped over the threshold, Kara shadowing her with a fiercely protective look on her face, as if daring someone to lay a finger on her friend. She felt better than she had in days, despite her reluctance to accept some painkillers, which meant she felt the ever-present ache of her injury, which she could have done without. The doctor had assured her earlier that morning that it was healing well though, no sign of infection in the neat row of stitches as a clean surgical bandage was placed over it.

     

                They finished off their breakfast before taking their leave, both of them dressed in their naval fatigues, which suited Kara’s lanky form a lot better than Lena’s. Making their way down the hallway, they were stopped by a trio of sailors before they could get very far, bid to follow them as they turned on their heels and retraced their steps, up to the command deck, where the Captain was overseeing the mooring and subsequent disembarkment plans. There were a lot of detained would-be prisoners that they had to deal with, which would be a feat in and of itself, not to mention the hundreds of sailors to manage.

     

                “Captain,” Lena haughtily greeted him, folding her arms over her chest. 

     

                “Miss Luthor, Miss Zor-El.”

     

                He gestured to a desk with a couple of office chairs in front of it, Kara sitting on one as Lena hovered uneasily at her side, stubborn to the end. When it became apparent that Lena was going to sit, the Captain took the other seat and stretched his legs out in front of her.

     

                “Now, you and your mother have caused a few problems for me, but considering the circumstances, and your mother’s friends in high places, we’ll put it behind us and there won’t be any further action taken against you. Your mother’s being released as we speak and the two of you will be amongst the first to disembark.”

     

                “Two?” Lena echoed, her gaze hard as she stared at him.

     

                He ran a hand over his close-cropped hair and gruffly cleared his throat. “I’m afraid that Miss Zor-El is to be held in the custody of the United States Government until further notice, until she’s pardoned of any and all crimes and granted citizenship, or detained for a fair trial.”

     

                There was a momentary silence as Lena slowly absorbed the words, unsure whether she was hearing things correctly or if it was someone’s idea of a bad joke. Blinking as she slowly unfolded her arms, Lena’s mouth opened and closed and her expression furrowed as she made sense of it all.

     

                “No,” she slowly replied. “No, she’s coming with me. She’s free and she’s leaving with me.”

     

                “That’s not for you to decide.”

     

                “I don’t give a shit who gets to decide, I’m telling you it’s happening.”

     

                “Miss Luthor, you have to understand that she is an illegal immigrant on US soil-”

     

                Turning to Kara as she ignored whatever else the Captain had to say in his defence, Lena reached out and cupped Kara’s cheeks in her cold hands, her face gone white with fear at the thought of her friend in another prison, in some place waiting out the long process of granting her a visa and identity documents or finding out if she’d wind up in a different prison. It was supposed to be over by now and Lena felt her throat close up, a shakiness in her chest as she stared at Kara with desperation.

     

                “Go. Now. Please.”

     

                Reaching up to cover Lena’s hand with her own, Kara was loyal to a fault, her face softening with aching sadness as her shoulders slumped. “I’m sorry, I can’t.”

     

                “You can get away from here,” Lena quietly hissed, her eyes stinging. “They can’t stop you; I’ll find you after.”

     

                “You know that I can’t leave my friends behind. I can’t leave them to suffer the same thing you want me to run from. I’m sorry,” Kara murmured, leaning in closer as she kept her voice down, wrapping Lena in a gentle hug.

     

                “Don’t do this to me again,” Lena pleaded, her vision blurring as she gritted her teeth, trying not to let the tears fall. “I’m not leaving you.”

     

                Rubbing her back, Kara shushed her, lips brushing Lena’s temple. “It’s okay. I’m not going anywhere.”

     

                Climbing to his feet, the Captain cleared his throat and gestured to two sailors, who stepped forward, casting dubious glances at the alien who could have ripped them apart with her bare hands. Surely they had seen what she’d done to the prison, had heard what she could do at the very least, but they were there to escort her at their Captain’s command and Lena wouldn’t let them take her without causing a scene.

     

                “If you will go with them, Miss Zor-El. Peacefully would be preferable.”

     

                “If you take her, you’re taking me too,” Lena declared, standing in front of Kara as she reached behind her, grabbing fistfuls of her clothes. 

     

                There was a stubborn set to her jaw and she stared down the two sailors. No one moved for a second, the sailors glancing to the Captain for instruction and Lena’s gaze moving to his face as well, her stare defiant as she bristled with anger. Shrugging indifferently, he gestured to the two women and started walking off.

     

                “If she’d like to be detained, then detain her as well.”

     

                Taking Kara’s hand in her own, Lena shied into her, frowning as she clung to her friend. They followed after the sailors and found themselves in one of the berths, teeming with the other prisoners - some familiar, some from other cell blocks - and any prison staff conspicuously absent as they kept them separate for safety’s sake. From their own cell block, only Nia and J’onn were there and the four of them huddled together on the bottom mattresses of two facing bunks, Kara’s hand still in Lena’s.

     

                They were happy to see Lena was doing better and couldn’t offer much intel after being locked inside the berth for the majority of the three days, as Kara and Lena similarly could only offer up snippets, most of them eavesdropped by the alien while Lena was unconscious. As they sat on the beds, Kara listened to the sounds of activity, narrating it for the other three as they anxiously awaited their fates. Lena couldn’t help but feel frustrated, knowing she should be walking off the aircraft carrier and going home, wherever she decided to make that, but they wouldn’t let Kara go with her, and that made all the difference in the world to her freedom. She wished Kara would fight, run, anything , but she also understood why she couldn’t do that. It would have gone against Kara’s morals, the fabric of her being, and would have undermined the effort they had both gone through to get everyone out of the prison the first time Kara had stayed behind.

     

                It was hours before anyone came to fetch them, leaving the four of them to talk quietly or ruminate on their fate, wondering if they would remain together or be separated again. They started taking inmates in groups of ten, leading them off the aircraft carrier in small quantities so that they could control the process. When a sailor gestured to the four of them to stand and follow, they stayed close together, Lena holding Kara’s hand tightly as she feared they might intentionally split them up out of spite. They didn’t though, and they filed out with the other six inmates making up their group, two guards leading them with another two bringing up the rear as they were shepherded through the hallways.

     

                The wind buffeted Lena as she stepped over the threshold of the exit, the salt air of the port refreshing after the stifling air conditioning pumped through the carrier's vents, and she quickly assessed the situation. There were more sailors standing guard and other military personnel on the ground, creating a perimeter as they cut the prisoners off from the rest of the naval base. Lena was mostly concerned with the rifles held in the hands of the military below as she shielded her face with a hand as the wind made her eyes stream.

     

                Stiff beside her, overwhelmed by the noise and the people and the vastness of the base, Kara stumbled along as they were prodded off the carrier. As soon as their feet hit the asphalt, soldiers stepped in, taking each of them by the elbow, Lena holding onto Kara’s hand tightly as she tried to keep them together. Fortunately, if Kara didn’t want to be moved, it was hard for them to move her, and she squared her shoulders and dug her heels in, staying at Lena’s side so the soldier gripping her arm was forced to move with her.

     

                A few of the other prisoners wouldn’t go as peacefully though, one of them shaking off his soldier and trying to make a run for it. Shouts broke out, guns raised, and Kara broke the grasp of her soldier and dropped Lena’s hand, moving quickly to try and calm the situation. The speed she moved and the obvious strength she displayed only served to cause a bigger panic, the soldiers yelling at her as she held her hands up in surrender, trying to reason with them. Lena’s heart leapt into her throat and she pulled against her own soldier’s grip, wanting to go to Kara and make sure that they weren’t parted, no matter what.

     

                A shout tore from Lena’s mouth as the grip on her tightened, both hands grabbing her then, shoving her forward towards the black van, where Nia and J’onn had already been stowed, the former arguing with the soldier at the open back doors as she gestured heatedly to Kara. Lena tried to go limp in her escort’s grasp, sinking to the floor before the man sighed impatiently and lifted her. Struggling, Lena could feel herself panicking now, unable to see Kara as she tried to crane her neck to look over the man’s shoulder. 

     

                “Kara!”

     

                Placed into the back of the van, Lena almost immediately lunged back out but was pushed back in, the door slamming into place. A muffled shout of outrage passed her gritted teeth as she banged her hands against the door.

     

                “Open the door! Open the fucking door!”

     

                Gentle hands rested on her shoulder, her arm, urging her back as she breathed rapidly, tears smarting her eyes as her palms stung. J’onn guided her down onto one of the benches lining the interior of the van and crouched in front of her, his hand a reassuring presence on her knee.

     

                “Lena, she’s fine. It’s alright, they’re bringing her now.”

     

                Raking her hands through her hair and then burying her face in her palms, Lena drew in ragged breaths as she waited, her heartbeat pounding in her ears, before the doors opened again an agonising length of time later. It wouldn’t have even been a minute but Lena couldn’t shake that panic that they would be separated again, until they were shoving Kara into the back of the van, the other prisoners quickly following after her. 

     

                They were pushed to the back of the van, the ten of them crammed in together, and Lena all but fell on Kara’s lap as she grabbed a fistful of her shirt. Anger washed through her as she struggled to process her worry, unable to express her emotions properly as her cheeks reddened.

     

                “Why would you do that? You can’t- it’s not your job to save everyone,” Lena hoarsely said, raising her voice a little, a strangled sound escaping her.

     

                Eyes wide, lips parting slightly, Kara reached up to cover Lena’s hand with her own, looking surprised and somewhat chastened by her friend’s words. Apologetically meek, Kara’s voice was soft as she thumbed the back of Lena’s knuckles, the idling engine of the truck roaring to life as they took off.

     

                “I’m sorry. I’m sorry, I was just trying to help. Everyone’s fine, everyone’s okay, I’m just- I can’t let them hurt them, I-”

     

                “I know,” Lena breathlessly replied as relief started to steal over her.

     

                Her frantic tension diminished as the adrenaline waned, leaving her shaky and clammy as she pulled back and heavily sat in the narrow portion of the bench left to her. Running a hand over her face, she swallowed thickly and closed her eyes, the van too quiet as she slowed her breaths.

     

                “Sorry,” she blurted out after a moment, a headache at her temples as she frowned.

     

                Feeling the bump of Kara’s knee against hers as her legs filled the space between benches, Lena looked up, a sulky expression on her face. Leaning back against the van wall, Kara looked defeated and drained, her eyes mournful in the dark, but that stab of relief filled Lena again, that they were still together - even better that two other friends of Kara’s were there too. J’onn had aided them in multiple ways throughout their escape and well-being, and Nia was close to Kara, but that only served to make Kara even more stubbornly insistent that she rescue all of her friends. It was a double-edged sword; either they never would have escaped alive without the help of other people, or they had to develop a strong enough attachment to the people they trusted to help them, and end up loyal enough to help them in turn. 

     

                No one else spoke for the remainder of the drive, jostling with the movements as they were driven through the city, and Lena closed her eyes, breathing slowly as she focused on the warm touch of Kara’s knee pressed against her thigh, trying to reassure herself. No matter how badly Lena wished she had walked off the carrier with her mother, she would never have been able to do it, knowing Kara would be detained, and she resigned herself to being stuck in the van and enduring whatever came next. As free as she was, pardoned of any crime, including the murder that hadn’t been revealed, Lena had made her choice to suffer the same fate as her friend, until things had been ironed out.

     

                They travelled for hours in the van, well past the city limits, and the prisoners started to grow restless, the confined space warm with so many people crammed into it. Lena couldn’t complain about that though, not after so many months of cold, and her recent bout in the Arctic Circle not able to be considered warm, despite being summer. Drowsy after the first hour, she slept intermittently, although it was far from comfortable, and she felt groggy and surly when the van finally came to a stop.

     

                It was a few minutes before they continued onwards again, their pace slower now, and then they stopped again, the engine cut and the sound of doors opening and closing. Sudden bright sunlight made them all wince after so long in the gloom of the van and Lena shielded her eyes as they streamed, blinking rapidly as she tried to get her bearings while the others filed out. Kara’s warm hands urged her up and towards the open doors and the rough hands of soldiers lifted her down to the packed earth.

     

                “If you’ll all follow me,” a soldier wearily ordered them, setting off without explanation.

     

                Sticking to Kara’s side, Lena looked around at the hastily constructed detention centre. It was essentially a prison, with chain-link fences enclosing the acres of land dedicated to the camp, barbed wire on top and demountable buildings set in neat rows. The day was sunny though and Lena had to concede that if they were going to be detained for a while, at least it was outdoors in the fresh summer air, even if she had no desire to be in Virginia. 

     

                It was very similar to the process of being imprisoned the first and second times, taken through as a group to have their photos taken and whatever information they could provide written down, clean prison scrubs handed to them in their nearest sizes - beige this time - and a quick rundown of the facilities before they were taken to one of the demountables, where another group of ten were already sitting on their chosen beds. 

     

                Querl was in that group of ten and perked up at the sight of familiar friends, the four of them taking beds as close to each other as possible, Kara taking the top bunk and Lena on the bottom. The building was quite cramped and not well insulated so Lena hoped it wouldn’t be too cold at night as she lay on the thin mattress, Kara at her feet, feeling wrung out by the long day. It was already mid-afternoon and it wasn’t shaping up to be what she’d expected the day to be, but she didn’t feel as if she was any worse off, being moved from one place to another, to another, a seemingly endless relocation as she waited for this nightmare to be over.

     

                Lena napped a while as the others talked in low voices and woke to them being ordered to line up for dinner. Rubbing the sleep from her eyes, she climbed to her feet and fell into the group, forty of them now allocated to the two rows of ten bunk beds, stepping outside into the late afternoon, the sun slowly starting to set, although it wouldn’t be dark for hours yet. She had no concept of what time it was but her stomach was growling and the ache in her side was making itself known.

     

                Walking to a mess hall, bigger than the other buildings, they found five rows of tables and benches, each row long enough for twenty to sit at each side of the tables, accommodating their cohort. Three of the tables were already mostly filled, a few empty spaces as the detainees moved along the line to have their lunch trays filled. Directed to join the back of the queue, they waited their turn and assessed the room. Lena saw a few familiar faces amongst the crowd - Imra sitting at the second table beside Psi, a few of the others that she’d only briefly seen when she’d been holed up in the cell block with them upon her return to the prison - but they didn’t make any attempt to speak to each other.

     

                The food was somewhat better than the prison food, on account of it being relatively fresh, but she had no appetite for what was dished onto her metal tray, picking at it until she nudged it to Kara, who tried to convince her to eat it herself before sheepishly finishing it off. Restless with unease, Lena didn’t want to be there. She imagined everyone else felt the same, but she really didn’t have to be there, and the knowledge that she would have to wait this out until Kara was as free as she was didn’t make her feel any better about her freedom. After dinner, they were escorted back to their demountable quarters and Lena went straight to bed.

     

                The next two days followed a similar structure. They were led to three meals a day, hot showers and clean clothes, allowed to walk around the cracked asphalt of an old parking lot re-purposed for recreational use as they drank in the sunlight, a basketball procured from somewhere with a hoop set up to keep the more actively inclined detainees entertained. There were a few recreational rooms with sofas, flat-screen TVs and sealed decks of cards, new-release paperbacks and a couple of gaming consoles. It was just a more modern prison with looser restrictions, although when a fight broke out between two of their fellow inmates, they were swiftly led away and weren’t seen again. Lena imagined some sort of solitary confinement for them.

     

                For her part, she ate little, spoke even less and didn’t feel like walking, taking the painkillers that were doled out to those who were given medical attention for varying injuries. Each day, a doctor checked on her stab wound and reassured her it was healing fine. The staff weren’t inhumane, they didn’t forcibly restrain anyone unless necessary, they didn’t lock shock collars around their necks or taunt them for amusement, they were just bored and stoic, manning the guard stations along the perimeter of the multi-levels of chainlink fencing penning them in. No one objected much, not after the newfound freedom they had in comparison to sitting in a cell virtually all day. 

     

                They had lawyers and case managers for the aliens and metahumans as well, those who were already US citizens not needing to plead their case for residency but to clear their name of any charges, while Kara had spent a few hours within those two days speaking to various people about Krypton and her time in prison so they could determine the outcome of her detention. On the morning of the third day, they were both summoned together by a guard after breakfast, following after him instead of returning with their cohort. 

     

                Exchanging wary glances, they quickly followed on his heels, Kara reaching out to take Lena’s hand to comfort her. Kara had been plagued with headaches from the sensory overload of being at full power around so many people but Lena watched as she tried to concentrate, to tune out the overwhelming noise to see if she could figure out what was happening, why they had been singled out. Giving Lena’s hand a quick squeeze, Kara’s face clouded with confusion but it was short-lived as they found themselves in the same office building they’d been processed inside.

     

                “Right, well, you are free to go,” a woman brusquely told Lena with a dismissive glance before turning to Kara, “and you’re Kara Zor-El - did you want to stick with that name?”

     

                “Sorry?”

     

                “For your identity documents. They’ll lodge whatever you put down as your legal name.”

     

                “Um …”

     

                She glanced at Lena who quietly explained to her that American surnames weren’t typically patronymic unless it was a relic of Eastern European ancestors, and her friend frowned for a moment. Kara didn’t have any other name for herself, and Lena hesitated, mouth opening as Kara beat her to it.

     

                “Oh … I guess Kara … Danvers?”

     

                Her voice hitched slightly as if in question but the woman at the desk just nodded, penning it in. Knowing what the mother and daughter meant to Kara didn’t make it any less disgruntling for Lena to hear her pick their surname for her own. She would have offered up Luthor to her if she’d thought Kara would take it, but things between them were still murky and could Lena fault her for taking the surname of people she’d known half of her life, who had been as close to a family as she’d had on Earth?

     

                “Right, well, Kara Danvers , you’re now a US citizen. They’ll have to formally issue you your green card before you can get any identity documents and a social security number but here’s your paperwork. You’re good to go.”

     

                “I- wait, I’m- I can … leave?”

     

                “A presidential pardon came through for you just before breakfast. You’re the first of the lot, on account of your friends in high places,” the woman indifferently explained, her eyes sliding to Lena. “If you head out that door, they’ll process your release.”

     

                Mouth opening and closing as she held her new paperwork in hand, Kara looked a little stunned. “Um … what about the others?”

     

                “Their cases will be processed in accordance to their risk level and priority.”

     

                “My friends-”

     

                “Sorry, that’s not my job. You’ll have to talk to immigration or law enforcement if you’re looking to get them settled. Good luck.”

     

                Lena grabbed Kara’s arm, tugging insistently on her sleeve as she lowered her voice. “Let’s go. We’ll be able to help them from outside. We can stay in Virginia until they’re free, I promise.”

     

                “You’ll stay?” Kara asked, hopeful as she gave Lena an aching look.

     

                “Where you go, I go, remember?”

     

                “I have to help them all .”

     

                Smiling thinly at Kara’s earnest insistence, Lena nodded slightly, happy to agree to anything to get her to leave as a free woman. “I know. I’ll help too. I just- we can do more out there, you’ll see. I mean it. We’ll help Alex, Kelly and Eliza too.”

     

                “Okay. Okay, thank you,” she directed the last part to the woman who waved a careless hand, stamping the documents she’d just finished filling out for Kara.

     

                Taking her hand, Lena quickly made for the door and stepped outside, a guard falling into step as they were escorted to the building near the armed gates, where they’d first been processed upon arrival. It was a reversal of that, quickly letting them through the levels of security as they were checked in the system and then led through a door that freed them to the last chainlink fence, before the gate was opened and an idling black car waited for them. 

     

                Lena already knew it was for them, and who she would find in the cool interior of the back, opening the door and sliding in first. Kara followed her inside, looking around with interest at the car, which Lena realised she must not have ridden in before, or not for a long time - the van didn’t count - and the three of them were silent for a moment. Sitting across from her mother, Lena cleared her throat as she took in Lillian’s polished appearance, rid of her naval fatigues and looking no worse for wear for her brief imprisonment on the aircraft carrier.

     

                “I’m assuming you had a hand in all of this?”

     

                “Of course. What’s the point in money and power if you can’t pull a few strings here and there?” Lillian smugly responded before her expression turned disgruntled. Eyes sharp, she arched an eyebrow. “The next time you decide to hand yourself over to the authorities, I might just leave you there. Securing your freedom twice is enough, don’t you agree?”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena sank into her seat, relief washing over her as she closed her eyes for a brief moment and then opened them to look at Kara. Her friend was toying with her hands in her lap, surprise in the wideness of her eyes as she looked down at the papers as the car drove off. Looking back at Lillian, Lena’s lips twitched slightly with faint amusement.

     

                “Thank you.”

     

                “Right, yes, thank you, Mrs Luthor,” Kara said in a daze, raising her gaze from the papers to give Lillian a quick smile. “I don’t know how I can ever repay you.”

     

                As Lillian opened her mouth, Lena quickly interrupted, reaching out to touch Kara’s knee as she gave her mother a look of warning. “There’s nothing to repay. This was for my benefit, so whatever debt there is is for me to sort out.”

     

                Lillian clicked her tongue, her smile sharp. “A little trust, Lena. Surely I’m owed that by now.”

     

                Raking a hand through her hair, Lena tipped her head back, closing her eyes. “Please, let’s not start this again. I’m too tired for your mind games so just be honest. This is all over now, and I’m genuinely grateful, so what’s it cost me?”

     

                “The price wasn’t negotiated with you. I made a deal elsewhere; freeing you just lined up with my interests in it all - and I might add that I’m your mother, so there is some love to be factored into my decision.”

     

                “What deal?”

     

                Eyes sliding to Kara for a brief moment, a look that made Lena’s blood run cold, Lillian cleared her throat and shifted in her seat. “We can discuss this later.”

     

                About to object but thinking better of it, Lena’s jaw tightened and she leaned against the door, pressing her fingertips to her temple as she tried to figure out what to do next. The three of them were silent and she could sense Kara’s restlessness as the car drove back towards Norfolk, where the naval base was situated, wishing her mother wasn’t there so they could talk, so she could comfort her and keep her away from Lillian’s ulterior motives. Kara would believe the best of her mother out of naïvety but Lena wasn’t about to let that happen, no matter how relieved she was to be free once more.

     

                “So … shall I have the jet readied immediately or would you like a hotel for the night?” Lillian asked after a long silence.

     

                “We’ll be staying in Norfolk.”

     

                “Staying? What on earth for?”

     

                “To help Kara’s friends.”

     

                There was that flicker in her mother’s gaze again, too cunning for Lena’s liking, at her response and Lena felt the prickle of wary suspicion steal over her again. Mouth tightening at the corners, Lillian arched an eyebrow. Softly sighing, Lena wearily waved a hand in her direction.

     

                “What?”

     

                “For the sake of peace, I’ll keep my opinions to myself. I’ll book you a hotel room - two hotel rooms?”

     

                “One is fine,” Lena stiffly replied.

     

                Nodding, Lillian made a brief call to an assistant and they resumed their silence. It was an awkward silence, the tension between mother and daughter making it uncomfortable, while Kara’s was an agitated silence, with Lena wondering if they should have just refused the ride and had Kara fly them back to Norfolk. It would have been quicker, if not as inconspicuous - and they wouldn’t have had her mother’s bank account to rely on and Lena didn’t have access to any of her own at present.

     

                The ride back felt mercifully quicker, and without the stifling heat or too many bodies packed into the windowless back of the van, it was a lot more pleasant as well. Once they hit the outer limits of the city, Lena felt a little more at ease with the thought of a hotel waiting for her, a proper rest and good food, away from the purgatory of waiting to be free. They slowed with the traffic and Lena glanced at Kara as she watched her friend move towards the window, looking outside with fascination. Lena had to wonder if this was her first glimpse of a city on Earth, and what they had looked like on Krypton.

     

                Lillian’s assistant had called back and her mother had relayed an address to the driver through the partition, which led them to the curb outside the Hilton. Following her mother out, Lena kept her head down as she stepped onto the sidewalk, turning to the car as she watched Kara climb out, her expression going slack with wonder as she looked around and then wrinkled her nose, covering her ears with her hands. Reaching out, Lena put an arm around her back, palm urging her onward as they followed Lillian to the door and into the cool lobby.

     

                Lena shepherded Kara to the elevators and they tucked themselves away in a corner, turned inwards towards the wall to avoid any chances of recognition. Checking them in, Lillian approached with two room keys, jamming her thumb into the button and stepping into the elevator as the doors parted. 

     

                They rode the elevator up to their floor, and they parted ways without speaking, her mother handing her the key card and then unlocking her door. Lena unlocked the door to their suite and stepped over the threshold with Kara following after, the door clicking shut and locking behind them as they were left alone in the cool air-conditioned room. Wandering through the small suite, Lena closed the curtains and walked through to the bedroom, two queen beds beside each other, and flopped down onto one. Covering her face with her hands, she let out a forceful sigh and didn’t think she’d be able to muster the energy to move again for the rest of the day. It was already past lunch as it was, and when the mattress jostled with the weight of Kara sitting beside her, Lena realised they hadn’t eaten lunch yet.

     

                “Are you hungry?” she asked.

     

                Kara let out a strained laugh, clutching her papers in her hands as she tried to take stock of her new surroundings. “Always.”

     

                Kicking off her shoes, Lena shuffled up to the bedside table set between the two beds and checked the menu and the call list for room service. Ordering burgers, steak, two pizzas, a variety of drinks and all of the desserts, she set the receiver back down and stared up at the ceiling. Kicking off her own shoes, Kara moved up to lay beside Lena, close enough to not be touching, until she reached out with her pinky to graze the back of Lena’s hand.

     

                “You alright?”

     

                “No,” Lena unevenly replied. “You?”

     

                “No.”

     

                Nodding, Lena’s mouth thinned and she closed her eyes. She was tired and thought a nap might help resolve some of the tension, some of her anger and frustration, but the truth was it would take a long time before any of it was resolved. It wouldn’t make a difference how long she slept, not when there was so much to come to terms with. But at least she wouldn’t have to dwell on any of it, ruminate over the awful things that had happened, for a while if she was asleep. She would only have dreams to contend with then.

     

                “Hey, do you want a bath?” Lena suggested as she opened her eyes and pushed herself up onto her elbows. A weak smile crossed her face as she looked down at Kara. “I imagine you haven’t had one of those since you wound up on this planet.”

     

                “A bath? Really? They have one here?”

     

                “In a suite, I bet they do. Come on, I’ll run you one and then you can stay in there for as long as you want and eat your room service.”

     

                Lena’s enthusiasm wasn’t feigned, it was something for her to cling to, making the most of this situation as she tried to indulge Kara. She might have felt like crying but at least if she was too preoccupied with making her friend feel comfortable in the overwhelming strangeness of their new environment and the relative luxury of a presidential hotel suite, she wouldn’t have time to brood in her pit of despair. 

     

                On her feet, Lena walked through to the bathroom, a deep tub situated in the middle of the large space, and put the plug in. Running the hot water, she added in some of the body wash to make bubbles, the room quickly steaming with the heat as Kara watched her with a look of eagerness on her face. Once the tub was full enough, Lena tested the temperature, finding it just a little too hot but in a pleasant way - not that it made much difference to Kara, considering the water wouldn’t scald her anyway - and then gestured to it, giving her friend a quick smile.

     

                “Take your time.”

     

                “Thank you,” Kara said with a quick grin before she started stripping off her clothes without any self-consciousness.

     

                Pausing a moment, mouth opening and closing as she wondered whether she should leave or look away, Lena moved over to the stack of towels and set one beside the tub as Kara tossed her scrubs aside. Moving over to the vanity, Lena leaned back against the sink as she watched her friend climb into the bath, folding her lean form as she sank into the hot water with relief, closing her eyes and tipping her head back against the rim.

     

                “This feels so nice,” Kara murmured.

     

                “Well, get used to it. You’ll be able to take as many baths as you want.”

     

                “Don’t tempt me; I might never get out.”

     

                Softly chuckling, Lena gave her a crooked smile. “Take your time. I’ll bring the food in once it arrives.”

     

                “Thank you.”

     

                Nodding, Lena pushed off the vanity and walked out of the bathroom, easing the door shut behind her, and made her way out to the living room. Sinking onto the sofa, she turned on the TV and flicked through the news channels out of curiosity, wondering if there would be any coverage about the aircraft carrier docking in Norfolk. There wasn’t much, merely a five-minute segment with the news anchor raising more questions than providing information, and Lena ended up turning it off, leaving her to listen to the muffled sounds of splashing in the bathroom as Kara basked in the tub. 

     

                A knock signalled the arrival of their room service ten minutes later and she warily rose to her feet, checking the peephole before she opened the door. A laden trolley was wheeled inside and a multitude of trays were unloaded, Lena directing them to the table, which was big enough to seat ten and ended up full by the time they finished setting everything down. It was overkill but she wanted Kara to try everything, to feel full for the first time in years, to enjoy freshly cooked food and desserts and indulge in something that wasn’t slop served on a tray.

     

                Balancing two plates and a milkshake, Lena carried them through to the bathroom, not bothering to knock with Kara’s sensitive hearing picking up on her every movement inside the suite anyway, and set down the milkshake on the edge of the vanity as she juggled the plates and cutlery. She went to fetch a couple more of the dishes as well, pouring a can of Coke on ice and taking the bottle of champagne from the bucket of ice and tucking that one under her arm for herself, before she stepped back into the bathroom and started to arrange things.

     

                Taking a swig of champagne, she set it down and cleared her throat. “Okay, fries first before they go soggy,” she declared, picking up the plate with the beef burger and the milkshake as well.

     

                She perched on the damp edge of the tub and held out the milkshake to Kara, who took a sip, her dubious expression quickly turning to one of delighted surprise. Quickly looking up at Lena, her blue eyes innocently wide, Kara took another sip and then eyed the glass and its pink contents.

     

                “What is this?”

     

                “Strawberry milkshake. Have you ever tried strawberries? No? Oh, well, you know, it’s a fruit and, um, it’s got ice cream in it and some milk and then they … well, they blend it all together.”

     

                “So this is what ice cream tastes like?”

     

                “Kind of. It’s like the liquid version of it. And these, fries, are made from potatoes.”

     

                Taking one from the plate Lena offered up, Kara chewed thoughtfully and swallowed, her brows pinching together in confusion before she sceptically looked up. “These are made from the same potatoes as our mashed potatoes?”

     

                “Well … I wouldn’t go that far. What we were given was powder, so that’s like … the bottom tier of how good potatoes are. These are good though, right?”

     

                “Really good.”

     

                Smiling, Lena made her try the burger and more of the fries before she swapped it for the pepperoni pizza, the bottle of champagne in her hand as she swigged from it in between explanations to Kara, who only knew what a lot of foods were in theory. There had been long hours spent reminiscing over favourite meals for those who had spent enough time on Earth, or been born there, to experience the food and miss certain things. While Lena had her own vices, the main one was alcohol, and even though she was sure she would’ve been able to get a good bottle of whisky if she’d asked, the champagne was good enough as she sipped it on an empty stomach, lacking any appetite as she made Kara try dish after dish. 

     

                Once Kara had eaten enough for the time being, Lena left her to finish her bath, taking her champagne with her as she walked back out to the living room and then hesitated. She was feeling the softening of the alcohol at the corners of her mind, having drunk more than half of it already, and hesitated a moment before she fetched the spare keycard and stepped outside without fetching her shoes, crossing the hallway to knock on her mother’s door.

     

                Lillian opened a few minutes later, looking surprised to see her. “Oh.”

     

                “And who else were you expecting?”

     

                “I hired a personal shopper to pick you up some things. Clothes and the like. Just until you’re back home.”

     

                “That might be a while.”

     

                “You can’t stay in Virginia,” Lillian exasperatedly replied as she stepped away from the door to let her daughter inside.

     

                “Sure I can. Now, tell me about the deal.”

     

                “Oh, that’s why you’re here. Of course. I bet it’s been eating away at you since this morning, hasn’t it?”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena folded her arms over her chest. “I want to know what the price was.”

     

                “How about it’s none of your concern? It’s best that you don’t know.”

     

                “Tell me.”

     

                Letting out a scoff of laughter, Lillian turned and continued to walk further into her suite, waving a hand dismissively. “You are pushing the boundaries of my patience. You have what you wanted; surely I’ve fulfilled every obligation to you already. I think I’ve gone above and beyond what most mothers would do. And now, leave me to my end of the bargain. It doesn’t concern you. You should be content with the freedom of you and your … friend.”

     

                “I am content with that, but she is not. We’re staying in Virginia until they’re all freed. She won’t leave without them.”

     

                “Well, I’m afraid it will be an unfortunately long wait if that’s the case.”

     

                “And what do you mean by that?”

     

                Sighing, Lillian started to make a fuss, “Lena-”

     

                “Tell me.”

     

                Her mother fell silent for a brief moment, lips pressed into a flat line as she turned to face her daughter, pale eyes shrewdly narrowed. “I’ve been given permission by President Brayden to take those deemed too much of a threat into the custody of Cadmus. For research purposes.”

     

                “You’re going to experiment on them?” Lena said, aghast.

     

                “Research. It’s in the interest of the United States for us to know how our enemies-”

     

                “They are not our enemies.”

     

                “Behave and what they can do, what their weaknesses are. How else are we supposed to defend ourselves from them?”

     

                “Mom-”

     

                “Look, Lena, I did what I had to do to get you a pardon, and you weren’t satisfied with that because she didn’t have a pardon, so I made a deal that would get her a pardon and solve the problem of what to do with the rest of them. Now, you and I both know you don’t really care about the others - you only care about her - so run along and tell her everything’s going to be okay and her friends will be just fine, and then put all of this behind you.”

     

                Staring at her mother with unbridled horror as nausea blossomed in her stomach, Lena was deathly pale as she was struck speechless. Lillian spoke matter-of-factly, her tone cool and unbothered as she slowly walked towards her daughter, pausing in from of her to caress her cheek, giving her a grim look.

     

                “You can’t win them all, you know. And this is the price to pay for your freedom; it’s their lives for your two. Is that not a fair trade in your eyes?”

     

                Stiff with anger, Lena jerked her face away from her mother’s touch and didn’t say a word as she turned and started back towards the door. Lillian clicked her tongue with annoyance behind her but didn’t pursue it, leaving her words to follow after Lena instead.

     

                “Nothing I do is never good enough for you, is it? Can you not be grateful for anything?”

     

                Opening the door, Lena stepped outside and quickly jerked it shut behind her. She was trembling with shock as she slapped the keycard against her door and let herself back in, trying in vain to swallow the lump in her throat as she moved in a daze, feeling stiff and uncoordinated as she walked through the suite to the bedroom, where Kara was wearing a hotel robe, damp hair falling around her shoulders.

     

                “My mom’s sold them out,” Lena raggedly told her. 

     

                Before she could even finish speaking, Lena was blinking in surprise, her feet off the ground, the enveloping warmth of Kara’s body around her as she was swept off her feet in a bear hug. Despite her worries, Kara was gentle even in her urgency, cupping the back of Lena’s head in a hand as she buried her face in her shoulder.

     

                “Thank you for telling me,” Kara murmured as her urgency dimmed, setting Lena back down on her feet and giving her a wavering smile.

     

                Blinking in surprise, Lena raised her eyebrows a fraction. “You were eavesdropping.”

     

                “Only accidentally, but yes. I heard everything.”

     

                A flicker of hurt ran through Lena as she pulled back slightly, green eyes wounded as she swallowed with some difficulty. “You didn’t think I would tell you, did you?”

     

                Looking sheepish, Kara ducked her head and raked back her damp hair before sinking onto the mattress. “I- your mom is right. You only ever cared about getting me out, didn’t you? So how could I blame you for not being honest about the deal if it means you get what you want? It would make all of this end, and we could go somewhere together and … I wouldn’t be able to do that if I- if I knew about the deal.”

     

                Stumbling forward a step, Lena sank to her knees in front of Kara, giving her a furrowed look of determination. “I would never lie to you about something like that, okay? I want you to trust me-”

     

                “I do.”

     

                “You’re right though, and so is she - I only cared about your freedom. It’s selfish of me, I know, but … I got the word out so they could be rescued, and that was enough for me. Now they’re out and waiting for their case to be seen, and I would be content with that if they weren’t going to be sold off as my mother’s experiment subjects. But I know that you wouldn’t be content with that, regardless of the deal or not, and I said I would help you, so I will. I would never make your decision for you, Kara. I know you haven’t had much say in the matter before, but you’re allowed to decide what you want.”

     

                Hesitating, Kara leaned in and kissed Lena. Her lips were soft and warm, a firm press against Lena’s mouth as she caressed her cheek. Eyelashes fluttering, Lena closed her eyes and sank into it for a brief moment before she cut it off. Turning her head to the side, so that Kara’s forehead rested against her temple, Lena pressed her lips together and Kara slowly drew back. Clearing her throat, Lena touched Kara’s bare knee, even that seeming too much for the way things were between them. 

     

                Mouth opening and closing, Lena raised her eyes and gave Kara a faint smile. “We need to talk about that.”

     

                “Oh. Did you not … like being kissed?”

     

                “No, I- that’s not- things are going to be … complicated for a while. We, uh, we became friends inside a prison and I depended on you a lot , and that’s not- that’s not really healthy and, um, I care about you a lot but I don’t know what that looks like for us on the outside. You will always be my friend and I’ll look after you for the rest of our lives, but whether that means you and I- where we go from here … I think we need to figure some things out first. You’ve spent most of your life in a cell and that’s- you don’t even know what you like, Kara. Am I the first person you’ve kissed? In prison, did they- did anyone … force you to do things? I-”

     

                “No,” Kara murmured, covering Lena’s hand with her own. “No, they didn’t make me do anything. But I’m not- I do know how things work, you know? I know what I want.”

     

                “I’m not trying to be condescending here, or a bitch,” Lena said with an awkward laugh, her cheek shallowly dimpling, “but you think you know but that’s because you’ve never had a real choice. I’m not saying you don’t know how things work in theory, but in practice is another thing entirely, and you’re just- you’re going to be really naïve in a brand new world. There’s a lot of trauma that you need to work through - and so do I - and that can- that can mess with your brain a lot. It can make you like people you should hate, it can make you think things are okay that aren’t okay, that you like being treated a certain way when you shouldn’t. None of what … happened to us is okay.”

     

                “I know that, but I know I like you too, and that’s not made up because we were in prison together. And I know that’s true because I didn’t feel that way about anyone else I was in prison with, and I was with some of them for more than a decade. But it’s okay if we’re just friends; you’d be the best friend I’ve ever had.”

     

                Shoulders slumping, even more confused about her feelings now, Lena reached up to cup the side of Kara’s face and plant a kiss on her cheek. There was a sense of relief there too, after so many months since Kara had kissed her and said things and then vanished back into the prison, leaving Lena to wonder about it all, and as confusing as it all still was, it felt good to at least talk about it. Although, Lena imagined it would take many more conversations to work things out, and they had different priorities at the moment to focus on.

     

                “You’d be mine too,” she told Kara before climbing to her feet and holding out her hand. “Now, do you trust me?”

     

                “Of course,” Kara readily agreed, taking her hand.

     

                Tugging on her hand to urge her to her feet, Lena looked a little nervous as she smiled thinly. “I need you to get dressed and then come with me. There’s also chocolate cake on the dining table if you wanted that first, but we’re not staying here tonight.”
