                Confused, Kara started for the bathroom, shedding her robe and changing back into her scrubs. Lena would have to do something about their clothes herself but that could wait until later. Dressed again, both of them putting on their shoes, they walked out to the dining table where an assortment of desserts waited, and Lena gestured to the chocolate cake.

     

                “Go on. Nothing’s going to get sorted right now so you may as well enjoy it before it goes to waste.”

     

                Pulling out a chair, Kara eyed the slice of cake with interest. “So this is chocolate?”

     

                “Mhm, those little shavings on top are from a chocolate bar. You had chocolate chip cookies in there, right? This will be richer than that.”

     

                Taking a bite of the cake, Kara’s eyes widened and she had another bite before looking up at Lena. “Do you want some?”

     

                “No, thank you. I’m not a big fan of chocolate cake.”

     

                “How can you not be? This is the best thing I’ve ever tasted!” she enthusiastically responded, scooping up another bite and savouring the chocolate frosting. “I could eat this every day.”

                

                Quietly laughing, Lena folded her arms over her chest. “Then I’ll buy you one every day.”

     

                Smiling around a mouthful of cake, Kara’s eyes creased at the corners and Lena felt a tug of warmth in her chest as she laughed again. It all felt so surreal, in a hotel room with Kara, eating cake. It was just past lunchtime and at breakfast they’d still been detained in an off-grid camp, and she didn’t know how to reconcile that with the whiplash of freedom once again. She hadn’t felt settled in a long time, and in a sickening way she missed the monotony of the months in prison, knowing what to expect each day. Since she’d escaped the prison, she had felt like her body was fuelled by anxiety, the stress of the unknown and unpredictability of her situation leaving her incapable of relaxing, of pausing to take stock of things.

     

                It still wasn’t over, not until Kara was satisfied that she’d helped everyone enough, but at least Lena could feel reassured that they were in the clear. At the very least, she had her freedom and she had Kara’s too. However, there was a nagging uneasiness at the back of her mind as she wondered whether Kara’s freedom would be rescinded if the deal didn’t go through with Cadmus. Could President Brayden undo a pardon? Or would they just come up with some false charges instead? The thought didn’t sit well with Lena but she kept silent about her concerns, letting Kara enjoy her cake in peace.

     

                “So … where are we going?” Kara eventually asked, setting down her spoon and finishing off the glass of Coke she’d started sipping halfway through.

     

                “Right, so … you have to trust me on this one-”

     

                “I do.”

     

                “I need you to fly us to Metropolis.”

     

                “Metropolis? That’s the city you live in, right?”

     

                “Yes. It’s north of Virginia - a few hours by plane - and it’s also where my company is.”

     

                “L-Corp?”

     

                “Yes. I need you to take me home, and then I’ll make some calls and in the morning we’ll head to L-Corp for a press conference. Everyone will come. I haven’t spoken directly to the media so they’ll all be dying to hear from me, and we’ll just … tell them. I’ll expose it all. And you can speak as well and say your bit. We’ll get the jump on the whole thing and the President won’t be able to save face.”

     

                “Oh. I guess that’s the diplomatic way to do it, yes. But how long will it take?”

     

                “Well … that depends. That’s where you need to trust me. I’m not just trying to trick you into leaving this state and running away with me, but I don’t know how quickly the rest of it will happen after that. But the press is the key; that’s how the prison got round in the first place.”

     

                “Okay. Okay, I trust you. Are we- are we going now?”

     

                “Yeah, let’s go now,” Lena said with a small smile, a little scared at the prospect of flying in Kara’s arms. Last time she’d been delirious with pain, but this time she’d be conscious of the hundreds of feet of empty air below them. “We’ll be able to rest a while then. Have a proper sleep, put on some real clothes.”

     

                “Real clothes,” Kara hummed. “I’m curious to see what that entails.”

     

                Holding out her hand again, Lena gave Kara’s hand a quick squeeze as she took it and then pulled her to her feet. “Let’s go.”

     

                They had to go down to the lobby because there was no balcony, their beige scrubs making Lena cringe at how conspicuous they were, and they stepped out onto the street hand-in-hand. Leading them around the corner of the building, she looked at Kara and stepped in close, wrapping her arms around her neck. Closing her eyes as she breathed in the clean smell of soap, feeling warm as Kara’s arms wrapped around her waist, Lena tried not to tense up too much.

     

                “Lena, I-” Kara faltered. “I’m not very good at this yet.”

     

                “It’s okay; I trust you. Just head north.”

     

                Lips brushing her temple, Kara set her jaw and swallowed thickly. “Okay.”

     

                Lena’s stomach swooped a moment later as Kara shot them both into the sky, the city immediately shrinking below them as they cleared the tops of the tallest buildings in a mere second. The wind was strong and Lena clutched Kara as panic knifed through her, feeling her friend’s arms shift to hold her more securely.

     

                She wasn’t sure how long it took, keeping her eyes squeezed tightly shut, Kara’s warmth keeping the cold at bay, even as the wind dragged at her clothes, but the miles passed by quickly. Kara set them down twice, once in Washington and a second time in Gotham, Lena checking their bearings on the nearest newspaper stand or landmark, ignoring the shouts of surprise from pedestrians and drivers. She informed Kara to keep going until she saw an entire island of buildings, knowing that if they reached New York, they wouldn’t be that far from Metropolis. 

     

                Once they flew in over Manhattan, Lena had her fly lower, reluctantly opening her eyes as she tried to guide them to Metropolis. Fortunately, it was a clear day, and they still had the afternoon sunlight for her to see by, although Lena’s fear of heights made her wish that she couldn’t see just how high they were, the lanes of traffic and tiny crowds of people making her stomach turn. They left the city behind and it was five more minutes of wobbly flying before Lena pointed out the mass of steel and glass of the high-rise buildings and the glimpse of water. Descending, Kara’s voice was low in her ear as she asked where to set them down.

     

                Pointing out one building in particular, Lena had her set them down on the balcony of the penthouse. Feeling as if her legs were going to buckle as she found her feet on the concrete floor, Lena held onto Kara for a moment, dazed and windswept as her heart pounded. Then she let go and walked over to the balcony door, turning the handle and stepping over the threshold of her home for the first time in almost a year.

     

                “Um … should we have knocked?” Kara nervously asked as she followed Lena inside, casting a worried glance at the unlocked door. Of course, it wouldn’t have been locked; how many people could fly to the top of a high-rise building?

     

                “No,” Lena said, weak with a sudden feeling of home that swept over her as she turned in the dusty interior of her apartment. Giving Kara a wavering smile, she gestured around. “This is my home.”

     

                Looking around with renewed interest, Kara shut the balcony door and quickly walked further inside. “Oh.”

     

                Walking over to a panel of lights, Lena tested one and softly swore as the lights didn’t turn on. The electric, water, gas and internet must have been cut off when her bank accounts had been frozen. All of her electronics had been taken too, so Lena didn’t even have a phone to call someone from. It was evident that her housekeeper, cleaner and assistant had clearly found employment elsewhere, or been banned from entering the premises at all, and Lena didn’t know who to contact to fix things, to have her penthouse back in working order again, with a fridge filled with food and running hot water.

     

                Pausing to think for a moment, she made a quick dash to her bedroom, bypassing the dust-covered sheets and making for her closet. The clothes were untouched and she dragged off a pair of tailored pants and a shirt, shedding her scrubs and dragging on the pants as Kara hovered in the doorway. Glancing at her, she paused with her shirt in hand and then turned to the rows of hangers. Grabbing a pair of pants she vaguely remembered being too long for her to wear without heels, Lena handed them off to Kara and then snagged a cotton shirt as well. They would have to do.

     

                Both of them changed into the clothes, a faint smell of dust clinging to them, they made their way back out to the open living space and Lena walked over to the balcony door, jerking it open and stepping outside. Turning to Kara, who was rolling up the too-short sleeves of her borrowed shirt, looking rather ordinarily corporate - save for the slip-on shoes she had to wear - Lena gave her a grim look.

     

                “So, change of plans. We’ll need to go to L-Corp today so I can sort some things out.”

     

                “Right. Where’s that?”

     

                “The building with the giant L on its side,” Lena said with a sheepish smile, gesturing to the tall building in the distance. 

     

                Snorting, Kara picked her up and pushed off from the balcony. It only took her a minute to fly the distance, and Lena had her set them down on the balcony there too, leading right into her would-be office, now commandeered by as close to a friend as Lena used to have. At the sound of the door opening, Sam turned and then turned a shocking shade of white as she lurched to her feet.

     

                “Lena? My God, what the-” Sam babbled, crossing the short distance to the door, falling silent at the sight of Kara, her face furrowed with confusion. 

     

                “Sam,” Lena rasped, giving her a thin smile as she reached out to squeeze her acting-CEO’s arm, “it’s good to see you.”

     

                “It’s good to see me?” Sam exclaimed, stepping in to give her a tight hug, an act that caught Lena off-guard, unused to anything but warm professionalism between the two of them. “It’s good to see you. All this stuff in the news, I don’t even know where to begin. Is it all true? You vanished without a word.”

     

                “It’s true. Um … this is Kara. She’s my … friend. We’ve just gotten back to Metropolis and, well, things are a bit of a mess right now. I may need to use some of the facilities here, so I do apologise for the disruption.”

     

                “I- of course, I mean, it’s your office.”

     

                Opening her mouth, Lena paused a moment and then cleared her throat. “My mother ensures me you’ve been taking good care of the business.”

     

                “I’ve been trying my hardest.”

     

                “Well, the position is yours. Indefinitely.”

     

                “Excuse me?”

     

                Silent for a moment as she walked over to the sofa, Lena sat down and sank back against the cushions, tipping her head back as she inhaled slowly. Nothing had changed in the office - not even the type of floral arrangements brought in fresh every week - and she felt a pang of longing in her chest. Opening her eyes, she looked at Sam, who was still rooted to the spot, mouth slack with surprise and hazel eyes confused.

     

                “I’m not coming back to work, so this is your office now. You’re my permanent CEO. Whatever salary you want to negotiate to take it on for good, just let me know and I’ll sign the paperwork myself. As for me … I’m going on a very, very long sabbatical and I’m not planning on coming back from it so … anyway, does Eve Tessmacher still work here?”

     

                “Your assistant? Yes, she’s in Research and Development now as a lab assistant.”

     

                “Can you please have her brought up here for me?”

     

                “Of course, right away.”

     

                As Sam walked back to the desk, dialling her assistant and relaying the message, Lena patted the space beside her on the sofa and gave Kara a small smile. Crossing over to her, Kara sat close beside her and briefly touched Lena’s knee. Hanging up the phone, Sam cleared her throat and wrung her hands as she looked at them.

     

                “Tea? Coffee?”

     

                “Do you still have my liquor collection?” Lena asked, running a hand over her face, the softened edge of the champagne having already waned. 

     

                Hesitating, Sam walked over to the wall and opened one of the hidden panels, getting clean glasses and a bottle of top-shelf scotch and carrying them over to the coffee table. She set it down and sank onto the ottoman across from the two women, shakily pouring scotch for them all, feeling a little unbalanced herself. Lena knocked hers back in a mouthful and reached for the bottle, filling the glass two-thirds of the way full that time. Swallowing a good portion of that in another mouthful, she closed her eyes, savouring the honeyed taste after longing for it for months. 

     

                Taking a sip of her own, Kara coughed and spluttered, wrinkling her nose as she licked her lips. “What is that?”

     

                “Scotch,” Lena replied, taking another pull of hers. “Alcohol.”

     

                “Well … it’s not as good as the milkshake was.”

     

                With a quiet laugh, Lena finished off her glass and poured more. If left to it, she would sit there and drink the whole bottle as quickly as she could but Sam topped off her own and added a little more to Kara’s before she screwed the bottle cap back on and returned it to the cupboard. Lena smiled at that, as if Sam would try to stop her if she walked over to the cupboard and refilled her glass again.

     

                “Lena, what-” Sam started and then trailed off, unsure where to begin.

     

                “Do you have any Aspirin or Tylenol?” Lena said after a silent pause.

     

                Climbing to her feet, Sam walked over to her desk and rummaged through her handbag, coming up with a packet of pills and then fetching a bottle of water from a fridge hidden in one of the wall compartments. Handing them off to Lena, she sat back down. Popping two pills from the packet, Lena unscrewed the bottle of water and knocked them both back before handing the bottle to Kara and taking the scotch from her, tipping the contents into her glass.

     

                “Thanks.”

     

                “What the hell is going on?” Sam sighed after a moment. “I mean … they drag you off to prison in the middle of the night, no one hears from you for eight months and then you’re here somehow. I’ve been following the news, I know that carrier docked in Norfolk last night but-”

     

                Swiping a thumb over her eyes, Lena made a low sound at the back of her throat. “I really don’t have the energy to talk about it right now. I’m sorry. I just came here because … I have no power, no water, no food or- or any way to call anyone at home, and I just want to go to bed and not think about it all until tomorrow. And tomorrow, I need to call the press here because they might actually listen so I’m sorry for the shit show I’m about to bring your way, but I don’t have a lot of resources at the moment-” 

     

                “The company’s yours to do with as you please. You’re still the majority shareholder; I can step down as CEO-”

     

                “No. That’s the last thing I want. I just- I don’t want to tank the stock or cause a media storm for the company but I’m going to be here tomorrow, regardless of the mess it’s going to cause, so I’m sorry for that. But until then … I don’t want to talk about it.”

     

                “Right, of course. If there’s anything you need from me …”

     

                “Thank you, Sam.”

     

                They sat in silence for a few minutes, Kara tense as she sipped the water, while Lena sipped her scotch, until there was a knock on the door. Sam climbed to her feet, calling out for the person to enter, and Lena looked to the door as Eve stepped inside, wary curiosity turning to outright shock as her eyes moved from Sam to Lena. Mouth falling open, Eve couldn’t even speak.

     

                Clearing her throat, Lena set down her class and stood. “Eve. I need your help with a few things; it seems my utilities have been cut off, and I’m assuming my internet provider too. My assets should be unfrozen by now but I’m not sure if they’ve cancelled my credit cards, so if you can look into that, that would be great. Also, the penthouse looks like no one has stepped foot inside for months, so can you arrange a cleaner to go there as soon as possible and take care of that? And a grocery delivery as well - just my usual items, and chocolate cake as well. Thank you.”

     

                “I, uh,” Eve stammered before composing herself. “Yes, Miss Luthor. I shall do that … right now.”

     

                “Thank you, Eve. If you could also track down a new cell phone and laptop, that would be great too. A spare work one will be fine if you don’t have time to pick up a new one today.”

                

                Nodding, looking alarmed and dazed, Eve backed up to the door and slipped back outside. Kara let out a quiet laugh a moment later, glancing at Lena. “You’re very bossy.”

     

                “Well,” Lena shrugged, gesturing helplessly. “I was the boss.”

     

                “The secret will be out very soon; she’s already telling the woman sitting out there.”

     

                Sam let out a quiet sound of indignation, hurrying to the door and sticking her head out. Kara let out another muffled laugh as they listened to Sam hiss instructions to keep everything confidential for now, and Lena crookedly smiled, the scotch easing some of her tension and the painkillers already numbing the edge of pain in her abdomen.

     

                “Sorry, Sam, I may need to commandeer this sofa until the cleaners are finished with my place. I can’t stand the thought of going to another hotel now that I’ve been back home, and here. God, I’ve missed this place.”

     

                “That’s not surprising, given the amount of hours you spent here.”

     

                “Mm, well, it will be a long time before I think about doing that again.”

     

                Lapsing into silence, they were all left to their thoughts for a few minutes and then Sam cleared her throat, elbows on her thighs as she leaned forward, a burning look of curiosity in her eyes. “Sorry, um … I just- the balcony …”

     

                “Right, well, Kara can fly,” Lena wearily stated, gesturing to her friend. “She’s actually the one who lifted the prison.”

     

                Sceptical, Sam gave Kara a dubious glance. “By yourself?”

     

                Shifting under the attention, Kara gave her a weak smile and shrugged half-heartedly. “It wouldn’t have been possible without Lena’s help.”

     

                “Right, but you lifted the prison by yourself? Like, alone?”

     

                “Yes. I’m, uh, I’m from Krypton. Do you know where that is? No? Oh. Um … well, it’s a planet and it exploded so my- my parents sent me here.”

     

                “You’re the one who’s been in there since they were a child,” Sam said with recognition, a look of pity crossing her face as her shoulders sagged slightly. “I can’t even imagine that. You know, that’s almost the same age as my daughter. I hate to even picture her in a place like that. You poor thing, this all must seem so … strange to you.”

     

                Shrugging again, Kara toyed with her fingers in her lap. It was strange to Lena and that wasn’t even factoring in an entirely different culture, people, world or surroundings. Reaching out, Lena gave Kara’s hand a quick squeeze of reassurance, and when no one spoke after a few minutes, Sam climbed to her feet. Clearing her throat, she glanced down at her watch.

     

                “Well … I’m supposed to be in a meeting right about now, so I’ll give you both some privacy. I haven’t changed anything so everything is still where it should be. They, uh, they did seize a few things - I thought you’d just taken them with you when you vanished but I guess not - but everything else is where it should be. If you need anything, here’s my number,” Sam babbled as she crossed over to her desk, jotting down her number on a note and leaving it on the desk, before grabbing her laptop, bag and phone.

     

                “Thanks, Sam,” Lena murmured, tired but glad to be in familiar surroundings, with familiar people.

     

                Even though she’d spent an inordinate amount of time with her mother over the last few days, it was unusual. Lillian was familiar, of course, but only as a remnant of Lena’s childhood; Sam was familiar in a day-to-day manner, a permanent fixture in Lena’s work life as the CFO to her CEO, and it felt more ordinary to be sitting in her office with Sam than trekking it to the Arctic Circle with her mother.

     

                “It’s good to see you, boss.”

     

                Giving her a small smile, Lena nodded, watching her move towards the door. As soon as they were alone, Lena reached for the scotch and finished off the dregs of her glass before kicking off her shoes and tipping onto her side on the sofa, on her back with her knees bent. Sighing, she dug the heels of her palms into her eyes. There was a warm presence on her thigh and Lena lifted one hand to peer at Kara, who was looking at her with concern.

     

                “Are you alright?”

     

                “It’s all a bit much, is all. I’ll be okay though. And you?”

     

                Mouth turning down at the corners, Kara shrugged. “I don’t know how to feel. This is all- I mean … I was in there for so long . I don’t even know what to expect or- or how to … get used to this. Yes, it’s all a bit much.”

     

                Holding out a hand, Lena gave her a sad smile and waited for Kara to place her hand in her grasp. Squeezing her fingers, Lena swallowed thickly. “You’re doing very well.”

     

                With a huff of laughter, Kara’s face furrowed. “Am I? It’s taking everything in me not to fly back to that camp and tear it to pieces. I could do it, couldn’t I? Easily, I think. I feel so- so strong and they’re all in there and I just feel- I could free them all in minutes. But I shouldn’t do that, because that would be wrong, but what they’re doing is wrong, so which one is worse? I don’t want to be a bad person.”

     

                Her voice was a low rumble as she vocalised her conflicted feelings and Lena squeezed her hand again. “That wouldn’t make you a bad person to anyone with a conscience. Unfortunately, that excludes the government. I’m sorry it’s not what we expected, I’m sorry I couldn’t get you out without all of … this.”

     

                “You have done more than enough for me. I’ll be grateful for the rest of my life that I met you, even if I wish you’d never had to suffer through what you did. I would have gladly stayed in there too if it meant you never had to be imprisoned.”

     

                “Don’t say that.”

     

                “It’s true. You get used to it after a while when it’s all you’ve known for over half of your life. Today would have been just another day if you hadn’t shown up there. What would you have been doing if today was just another day and none of it had happened?”

     

                Craning her head back to look at the desk behind her, she shifted her free hand to gesture towards it. “I’d be sitting there. My assistant would have brought me my lunch and a coffee from my favourite café down the block. I’d have back-to-back meetings in the morning, phone calls, emails, spreadsheets and paperwork in the afternoon. Sometimes I’d have a business dinner or a gala or some charity event in the evening, but more often, I’d stay here and work in the lab until late and then I’d go home to my apartment by myself and eat the dinner my chef had left in the fridge for me and I’d go to bed alone.”

     

                Lena was silent for a moment after she finished her brief overview of her days before being imprisoned. Chewing on her lip, a serious look clouded her face. Drawing in a shallow breath, she swallowed thickly.

     

                “I’m glad I met you. I’m not glad the rest of it happened but I’m glad I met you - I haven’t really felt alone since then.”

     

                Squeezing her hand in return, Kara slumped on the sofa, unwinding now that it was just the two of them alone. It was evident they would be there for a while and they both lapsed into silence, getting comfortable on the sofa. Lena wished she was in bed, could sleep a while, the pills dampening her headache and the pain in her side, while the scotch did the rest, making her tired and limp.

     

                After a while, Kara was so restless that she got up and started to pace, while Lena had to blink back the dryness in her eyes, the building urge to cry pressing behind them, so wrung out that she felt nothing but frustration. She wished she could have napped on the sofa but she didn’t have it in her, her mind too busy as she tried to fine-tune her sudden plan, trying to plan for different outcomes, different eventualities. Lena had led many work conferences and had no fear of public speaking, knowing the questions to expect and rarely getting caught off-guard with one, but she felt out of her depths at the idea of speaking to the press about the detained aliens and metahumans and the President’s plan to sell them off to her mother. 

     

                Perhaps it was just because she was so tired, or maybe it was nerves at speaking to a crowd of reporters with cameras trained on her after such a long absence, but Lena felt anxious about the whole thing. Chewing her lower lip as she ran through scenarios, envisioning herself in front of a podium in the courtyard outside of the building, trying to put together an appropriate outfit, wondering whether she should play up the wrongfully imprisoned by making her makeup minimal and her outfit drab. She would have to find clothes that fit better for Kara as well. With so many things to organise and little energy to do it, Lena felt like she was drowning a little.

     

                It was a few hours later when there was a knock on the door. Sitting up on the sofa, Lena glanced at Kara, who nodded and murmured, “it’s the blonde woman who was here earlier.”

     

                “Come in,” Lena called out, smoothing down her hair.

     

                Eve warily stepped into the room with an armful, giving her old boss a cautious smile. “Miss Luthor, I’ve contacted your banks and they’re reissuing new credit cards for you. In the meantime, I have a digital version in the wallet of your new phone.”

     

                Handing a phone over to Lena, Eve then set down a new laptop and a set of keys, which Lena recognised as her assistant’s set to the penthouse, and continued to babble. “Your utilities have been switched back on and your internet provider will be sending out a new modem, but your old one should work fine until that arrives tomorrow. The cleaners will be finishing up shortly and groceries are scheduled for delivery in an hour. Was there anything else I can do for you or would you like me to arrange a driver to take you home?”

     

                “Thank you,” Lena said with a sigh of relief, climbing to her feet and moving over to the desk. “If you can arrange a driver for fifteen minutes, that would be great.”

     

                Reading the number stuck to Sam’s desk, Lena punched it into the desk phone and waited as it rang. It only rang twice before the call was picked up, Sam’s voice an anxious murmur on the other end.

     

                “How can I help?”

     

                “Can you come back up here once you’re done?”

     

                “I’ll be right there.”

     

                Gently setting the phone down on the receiver, Lena rounded the desk and took a seat in the one for visitors. Slumping, she closed her eyes and listened to Kara’s quiet footsteps come to a stop behind her, warm hands resting on her shoulders.

     

                “You must have been very important before,” Kara mused. “You have all of these people so eager to please you.”

     

                “Mm, I’d almost forgotten how nice it is to be disgustingly rich and powerful.”

     

                “Is that what your life was like before? Everyone just did what you asked them to? Everything was done for you?”

     

                “To an extent. I’m a solitary person by nature so I spent most of my time working on my projects or in the office, so I had other people to pick up the slack. You know, my laundry and cleaning, my shopping and cooking. I grew up that way so I’ve been very lucky.”

     

                Humming, Kara gave Lena’s shoulders a gentle squeeze. “I grew up quite similar. We weren’t as rich or powerful as you but my family was one of the most well-respected on Krypton. Our legacy stretched back thousands of years, but … well, it sort of fell out of favour a couple of generations ago and then my uncle, Jor-El, he kind of ruined whatever respect was left after stirring up trouble about our depleted resources. Anyway, I guess he was right in the end because I wound up here and they’re all … gone.”

     

                She didn’t say dead but they both knew that was the truth of the situation, and Lena reached up to cover one of Kara’s hands with her own. Smoothing her thumb over her knuckles, Lena swallowed thickly.

     

                “Well, my family reputation has gone the same way, and I plan on taking a sledgehammer to my mother’s public persona tomorrow, but … well, it’s no House of El, and I know you picked Danvers as your new last name because you already chose a new family when you were in prison … but this is all yours too. Everything at my disposal. If you want it, it’s yours. If I can’t get it for you, I will make it myself.”

     

                Leaning down, Kara kissed the top of her head. “I just want to stay with you. That’s all. I don’t need money or power; I just want you to be my friend, no matter what.”

     

                Smiling slightly, Lena leaned back against her. “Now that you already have.”

     

                Before they could say anything else, the door opened and Kara withdrew her touch, taking an almost guiltily quick step away from Lena as she turned to the door. Turning in the seat, taking in Kara’s hands, clasped behind her back as she fiddled, Lena let her gaze travel to Sam, who stepped back inside with concern etched on her face.

     

                “Is everything okay?”

     

                “I need you to call a press conference for me tomorrow morning. Shall we say ten or eleven? I’d like to sleep in, I think. I’d also like for you to be there to handle any business-related questions. I understand you’ll need to consult with HR and Comms but this will largely be a personal statement. I won’t be announcing any resumption of my role within the business, it’s just a method for me to garner enough public interest in what I have to say.”

     

                “Oh. Oh, yes, right, of course. For the business side of it, shall we stick with something standard? I can give a similar statement as when I assumed the title of acting CEO; all of the generic things. That will be easy enough to arrange with the departments. Is there anything ugly I need to prepare them for?”

     

                “No, nothing that should impact the business. Unless- tell me, what’s the general public’s sentiment towards aliens at the moment?”

     

                Shrugging slightly, Sam looked perplexed. “As positive as can be expected. Of course, all of this has stirred up a lot of fuss, and a few extremists and radicals are fear-mongering in online spaces, but I’d say generally quite supportive.”

     

                “Right, well, I’d maybe prepare for a negative backlash, just to be safe. Again, it’s all personal but I understand anything I say might harm the company. I’m not trying to tank your stock-“

     

                “Your stock.”

     

                “I want nothing to do with it. Not now, not for at least a long while. And it will be better for the company that I won’t be standing there tomorrow as CEO. That would make it too personal to separate my statement from the values of the business.”

     

                “Right. If you’re sure …”

     

                “Yes. I’ll just need cameras and eyes on me.”

     

                Pausing, Sam pressed her lips together. “You’re not … going to get yourself in trouble again … are you?”

     

                Giving her a quick grin as she climbed to her feet, Lena arched an eyebrow. “Oh, undoubtedly. I imagine it’ll piss off a lot of people, my mother included, but it’s what must be done for the greater good. I’m just sorry to show up here out of the blue and lay this all on you.”

     

                “No, no, please don’t think anything of it. It’s your company; anything you need is just a call away. Not just as your employee, but as a friend too.”

     

                A little off guard at that description, having not considered that Sam might see her as a friend, even if she was the only person Lena had considered as such before Kara came along, she smiled quickly. 

     

                “Right, thank you. For everything.”

     

                Waving a hand dismissively, Sam gave her a small smile, hazel eyes full of worry.

     

                “We’ll leave you to your work,” Lena said, crossing over to the coffee table and gathering up her things.

     

                “Shall I call security for an escort?”

     

                Glancing at Kara, Lena bit back a laugh. “No need, thank you.”

     

                Nodding, Sam walked to the door, silently following them out of the office and over to the bank of elevators. Lena didn’t try to dissuade her from accompanying them downstairs and was even glad for her presence when the elevator started to descend and employees climbed on as they stopped at other levels. Sam and Kara were both quite tall and Lena purposely stood behind them, head ducked down to remain unnoticed, keeping out of sight until they made it to the lobby. 

     

                It wasn’t particularly busy in the lobby but it was harder for her to remain unnoticed as she led the trio across the marble floor, glances and then double-takes at the sight of her, seemingly appearing out of thin air after a year away from L-Corp. It wasn’t the impression Lena had hoped to make upon her eventual first sighting in public but she couldn’t be too prideful, given the circumstances.

     

                Outside, she hurried to the car parked on the side of the road, Eve hovering beside it and then perking up at the sight of Lena. The driver opened the back door and Lena directed Kara into the back before giving Sam a nod in thanks and following her inside. The door was closed behind her and she held her new belongings in her lap, feeling a little more in control of her life with some financial independence and access to her things.

     

                The ride back to her building was slow, the pre-rush hour traffic already clogging the streets, but forty minutes later they were pulling up outside. The doorman blanched at the sight of her, so surprised she thought the older man might keel over, but he greeted her as per usual and held the door for her as she swept into the foyer. Riding the elevator up to her penthouse, Lena opened the front door to the faint smell of bleach and air freshener.

     

                Moving further into her apartment, she found the balcony door open to air out the stale rooms, all of the surfaces and floors gleaming and dust-free. Flicking on some lights, she was glad to see the electricity was back on, setting her things down on the kitchen counters and then walking over to the fridge. Opening it, she found it fully stocked with her usual favourites, plus a white bakery box with a cake in it. Smiling, she tapped the box as she glanced over her shoulder at Kara.

     

                “Your chocolate cake.”

     

                “Thank you,” Kara said with a shy smile, wringing her hands as she looked about with curiosity, now afforded the opportunity to take it all in properly. 

     

                “What do you want to do now?”

     

                “Um … I don’t know. What is there to do?”

     

                “Well, you can watch TV, I can make us some food, I have a lot of books, and a chess set as well, if you’d like to play with real pieces for a change.” 

     

                Brown furrowing with a serious look as her mouth thinned at the edges, Kara gripped the edge of the island countertop. “You should eat something.”

     

                “Me? I’m fine, but if you-”

     

                Moving quickly, fast enough to make Lena jump slightly as Kara was suddenly around the island and gently cupping her arms. “Lena, you need to eat. You haven’t had anything since breakfast, and to be honest, I’m not sure you even really ate breakfast. Or any of your meals really.”

     

                Wrinkling her nose faintly, Lena averted her gaze as she mumbled some unintelligible excuse before trailing off into a sigh. “Alright, fine. How about steak?”

     

                “Was that the cow you fed me earlier?”

     

                “Yes.”

     

                “It was good,” Kara conceded. 

     

                “Great, steak it is.”

     

                Hesitating after a moment, as Lena turned to the fridge to raid it, Kara looked a little wary. “Can you cook?”

     

                Rolling her eyes as she scoffed, taking out the scotch fillets and some butter and garlic, Lena gave her friend a withering look. “Can I cook?”

     

                “You did say you have people to do that for you.”

     

                “Out of time management necessities, not from a lack of skill. Would you like to learn?”

     

                Shrugging nonchalantly, Kara stepped up beside her at the counters. “Sure.”

     

                Lena fetched potatoes and set Kara to peel them as she fished out other vegetables from the fridge and then opened a bottle of red wine from her collection. She poured Kara a glass too, unsure whether the alcohol would even affect her, but at the look of disgust after the first sip, Lena got her a seltzer instead and polished off both glasses of wine herself. It softened the edges, taking over from the waning scotch she’d had earlier.

     

                Soon enough, the potatoes were boiling on the stove and Lena was grilling some garlic mushrooms with broccolini and was setting the steaks in a pan. Kara hovered nearby, uncertain of herself after breaking one of the knives when she accidentally chopped her finger, which obviously survived unscathed, and then startled Lena when she gently submerged her entire hand in the pot of boiling water to nestle the chopped potatoes in it without splashing water everywhere. She was still coming to terms with just how apparent their differences were now that she had full access to her powers.

     

                Still, when Lena set her to mash the potatoes, Kara took to the task enthusiastically. A little too enthusiastic about it as she ended up crumpling the handle of the masher in her tight fist, and Lena found the entire thing very endearing as she tried to hide her smile, reassuring Kara that it was completely fine and she would have someone replace it. She could still sense Kara’s dejected mood at how little self-control she exhibited at times, but she had only ever touched Lena with tenderness, so Lena didn’t feel even the slightest bit wary of her friend hurting her. 

     

                In short order, Lena was plating up their dinner and they sat side by side on the stools along the other side of the island counter. Eating slowly to savour the meal, Lena felt so off about the whole thing. How could she be eating the finest cuts of steak in her apartment after so long away? With Kara beside her, as if she’d always been there, instead of being the alien Lena had brought home with her. It was all so surreal that she still couldn’t wrap her head around it as they ate in relative silence.

     

                After dinner, she showed Kara the dishwasher as she loaded it herself, explaining what it was for and how it worked, and then moved over to the curved sofa to turn on the TV. Curling up on it, she let Kara flick through the channels faster than she could keep track of, biting the cuticles of her nails as she zoned out, preoccupied with her thoughts of tomorrow. Kara ended up on the Discovery Channel, watching a documentary about wildlife with rapt attention and wonder at the different species she had no concept of until now. It was so strange to Lena that someone could not know about pandas or giraffes, that Kara hadn’t even known about something so simple as a seagull until she’d landed on Earth.

     

                Once it was late enough, Lena decided to have a bath and excused herself, telling Kara to help herself to the contents of the fridge or pantry, to feel free to explore the multitude of rooms in the penthouse and call out to Lena if she needed anything else. Slipping into her spotless bathroom, Lena ran a hot bath with bubbles and stripped off her clothes before stepping into the tub. It was a luxury that was not taken for granted, and she thought she might fall asleep in the tub as she lingered for a long time, soaking up the heat and then making herself wash her hair and scrub herself clean.

     

                After she was out, she put on silk pyjamas and carried a pair out to Kara as well. She found her friend on the balcony, listening to the sounds of the city as she stared out at the glow of lights amidst the dark, the wind ruffling her hair. At the sound of Lena’s arrival, Kara turned to face her.

     

                “You look less tense.”

     

                “That obvious, huh?” Lena asked with an uneven smile, raising the bundle. “I brought you some pyjamas. I can, uh, I can show you where one of the spare rooms is, if you wanted to sleep in there.”

     

                She didn’t mean for her words to sound so suggestive but Kara readily agreed to the offer of the spare room and Lena felt a small stab of disappointment. Leading her inside, she walked to a closed door only a few rooms from her own bedroom and opened it up to reveal a spacious bedroom with a queen-sized bed and tall windows looking out over the city. Kara stepped onto the fluffy carpet and looked around.

     

                “I can have this whole room?”

     

                “Mhm, for as long as we’re here - or as long as you’d like.”

     

                “This is … a lot better than a cell,” Kara thickly replied. 

     

                Throat closing up, a spasm of pain ran across Lena’s face and it took her a moment to speak. “Yeah. Um … well, this is all yours so … make yourself at home. Take or use anything you want, please. If you need anything, just ask as well.”

     

                “Thank you, Lena.”

     

                “Right, well, I think I might go to bed now, if that’s okay.”

     

                “Of course, yes, you should- you should sleep. I think I might as well; it’s been a long day.”

     

                “Yes, it has,” Lena wearily sighed, running a hand over her face. “Well, sleep tight.”

     

                “You too. And thank you again, for all of it.”

     

                Giving her a tender smile, Lena stepped forward, her eyes stinging as she reached out to squeeze her friend’s hand. “Thank you.”

     

                Kara’s answering smile wavered slightly and she wrinkled her nose sweetly, holding the pyjamas to her chest with one hand as she held onto Lena’s hand a moment longer before releasing it. Stepping out of the room, Lena walked down the hallway to her own, the dimness of it making her realise how quiet the place was, no sounds of other people, no fear of being caught, no worrying about Kara. She was alone in her bedroom and Lena suddenly felt weak with the relief of being home after such a long time. The homesickness slammed into her so heavily that she had to clamp her lips shut to stifle the whimper that worked up her throat.

     

                Stumbling over to the curtains, she dragged them across the windows, letting out a quiet gasp and then drawing in a shallow breath. It was all too much, had been too much for such a long time that she didn’t think she could bottle it up any longer. Standing in the middle of her room, she buried her face in her hands, stifling a pitiful sob as she couldn’t hold back the tears any longer. Tired and vulnerable, Lena couldn’t help the emotions that poured out of her, the dam breaking as a year’s worth of pain, grief and worry flooded out of her.

     

                She couldn’t bring herself to move from her spot, to climb into bed and sob into her pillows, and she didn’t hear the door either, silently opening. The only thing Lena was aware of was warm arms winding around her as Kara hugged her from behind, her voice gently comforting her as Lena let out a ragged sound of agony, loud in the silence of the room. 

     

                “It’s okay,” Kara murmured as Lena turned in her arms, grabbing fistfuls of the silk pyjamas and burying her face in her shoulder.

     

                It just made Lena cry harder, her tears soaking into the fabric, her sobs hitching and broken as she sagged into Kara’s chest, kept on her feet by her friend’s strength alone. It felt like she might never stop and after a minute, Kara gently lifted her and carried her to the bed, setting her down and crawling onto the mattress beside her. 

     

                Gathering Lena up into her arms again, she held her tightly to her chest and let Lena cry it out, shushing her breathless apologies and stroking her hair until her friend’s breaths started to even out. The quiet whimpers tapered off and the occasional shudder of a hitching breath stopped as Kara gently rubbed Lena’s back, her breaths turning slow and deep as she eventually slipped into sleep in the safety of her embrace. Kara was quick to follow and neither of them moved an inch the entire night, comforted by the warmth of each other’s presence and the thump of their hearts as their exhaustion won out.

    Chapter 28

                Lena was restless as the elevator descended through L-Corp, running her hands over the grey wool pants, tugging down the cuffs of her spotless white shirt, feeling a little unsteady in her teetering Louboutins after so long without wearing heels. Her feet were already aching and there was a pit in her stomach, nausea blooming in anticipation of the crowd of reporters, journalists and photographers outside. Kara stood at her side and extended her pinky to gently brush the side of Lena’s hand in reassurance.

     

                “Ready?” Sam asked, staring down at her phone, a leather portfolio under one arm and a stern expression on her face.

     

                “I’m not sure that matters,” Lena said with a thin smile.

     

                The elevator slowed and softly chimed as they reached the ground floor, doors parting to reveal the spacious lobby. The marble floors made the open room cool and Lena’s palms felt clammy as she tried to feign easy confidence, shoulders back, chin up, walking towards the glass doors, where she could see through to the courtyard separating L-Corp and the office building next door. Two steps descended to a paved square, perpetually in the shade of the tall buildings, and usually occupied by a coffee cart, while employees got a breath of fresh air, eating lunch or making phone calls.

     

                Today, everyone was neatly packed in and a podium was situated at the top of the steps outside L-Corp’s doors and Lena stepped outside, the day quite mild as the blue sky was partially clouded white and a breeze swept through Metropolis. Immediately, camera flashes assaulted her vision, black spots momentarily blinding her, and she felt, rather than saw, Kara shrink in on herself, covering her ears as she ducked her head, the sounds of so many clamouring voices too much sensory overload for the alien. Hell, it was too much for Lena as well, and she’d done this a hundred times before - perhaps with less rabid interest.

     

                Sam turned her back to the crowd and gently touched Lena’s arm as she leaned in to make herself heard over the noise. “Are you sure you want to do this?”

     

                Tersely nodding, Lena’s mouth tightened at the corners and she stepped past her CEO and up to the podium. Gripping the sides of it, she glanced down and wished she’d prepared a speech. She’d never needed them before, her articulation and regular presentations, talking to crowds of hundreds - sometimes thousands - giving her an ease with public speaking, her drafted notes rehearsed in front of mirrors or pacing in her office, picked over by her PR and Marketing teams before presented meaning that she relied on muscle memory when it came to the act. Except this time Lena hadn’t rehearsed anything, had no drafted notes, nothing but the burning anger for her mother’s betrayal and the government’s lies to fuel her.

     

                Clearing her throat, she raised her eyes, her stare hard as looked out at the dozens of faces, more camera flashes dazing her, and clutched the side of the podium tighter. Leaning in slightly to the mics, Lena drew in a slow breath.

     

                “Good morning. I’d like to thank you all for coming on such short notice. I know-” she faltered, swallowing thickly before forging onwards. “I know you all have questions, but I’ve arranged this press conference for a more pressing matter. I’ll cut right to the chase; a deal has been made in secret for the detained prisoners of Fort Rozz to be handed over to the custody of the bioengineering company, Cadmus, for illegal testing and experimentation on aliens and metahumans. As many of you will be aware, the CEO and owner of Cadmus is my mother, Lillian Luthor. I’m holding this press conference today to shed some light on the illegal trafficking that has been sanctioned by the government of the United States, and call on the White House to address this matter and release the prisoners from the detention camp they’re currently being held in.”

     

                Pausing, Lena pressed her lips into a flat line as she frowned at the podium, glancing behind her to meet Kara’s mournful blue eyes, before turning back to her audience. Shoulders set and back stiff, Lena drew in another breath and continued.

     

                “There is a systematic failure within our government that has allowed the illegal imprisonment of aliens, metahumans and humans to be discreetly authorised, and while there has been some progress in retrieving them from Fort Rozz - a place I, myself, was a prisoner of - their efforts are insufficient. While I am afforded my freedom, there are hundreds more who are being detained until they can be turned over to my mother by President Brayden, to imprison them elsewhere. The government has deemed them a threat to society, but under President Marsden, and the Alien Amnesty Act in 2016, there was not a single instance of a threat from any alien or metahuman. I know this Act was repealed by President Baker, but is the opinion of a morally bankrupt President, who was impeached for his own involvement in the unlawful imprisonment sanctioned by the DEO, what we should be following? Today, I am calling for the immediate release of all Fort Rozz prisoners, as well as the reinstatement of the Alien Amnesty Act, so that all aliens can be afforded the same rights as humans.”

     

                Falling silent for a second, Lena glanced back over at Kara and gestured to her. “This is Kara Zor-El. She was imprisoned inside Fort Rozz for eighteen years. She arrived on Earth as a thirteen-year-old child and was forcibly detained and sentenced to life in prison without a trial. This is a violation of America’s judicial system and human rights upheld in the Constitution. We need to fix that, and it’s not going to be fixed by shifting a bunch of aliens to a different form of imprisonment so they can be experimented on like animals. I won’t allow it, and I won’t allow myself to be silenced, or my silence to be bought. I’m asking that people use their voices and contact their local representatives, their state Senators and United States Congressmen and call for immediate action against this ongoing injustice, for the freedom of all inhumanely imprisoned aliens, metahumans and humans. Thank you for your time.”

     

                With a slight nod, as she fell silent, Lena turned and walked over to Kara, a stormy look on her face, and heard Sam scramble to take over as raised voices overlapped with questions hurled at Lena’s retreating back. Falling into step beside her as they walked into the lobby, Kara reached for Lena’s hand, enveloping it in her warmth, and squeezed gently. Quickly crossing the lobby, Lena jammed her thumb into the elevator button and waited for the doors to part, stepping inside and pressing the button for the top floor before falling back against the metal wall as she closed her eyes and let out a weary sigh.

     

                “You did very well,” Kara said as they started to rise.

     

                Cracking open an eye, Lena gave her a wry smile. “A lot of people are going to be angry.”

     

                “At you? Why?”

     

                “Ah, well, there’s this whole … anti-alien sentiment. When someone gets on camera and likens them to humans, it won’t go over very well with them. Especially considering my family. I think throwing my mom under the bus is my only saving grace to come off as ethical and unbiased. Although, how can I be unbiased when they lumped me in with the rest of the prisoners? It’s a shit show but I can be very stubborn and have enough money to make a nuisance of myself, so … we’ll see what happens.”

     

                “Thank you. For your help, for everything. I know- I know it’s making it harder for you, stopping you from moving on, from getting the help you need. I just- I’m very grateful to you, Lena. I’d say I don’t know where I’d be without you, but I do know and I’m glad I’m not without you. Not only for what you’ve done and what you’re doing but … how you make me feel.”

     

                The elevator door chimed and parted and Lena pushed off the wall, her shoulders sagging as she walked through the wide hallway, past reception and into Sam’s office. Lena collapsed onto the sofa and pinched the bridge of her nose and stretched her legs out before her, glancing up at Kara.

     

                “How do you feel?”

     

                Sinking onto the sofa beside her, Kara gave her an aching smile. “Happy.”

     

                “Happy?”

     

                “Not … about all of this,” Kara waved a hand, “but yes, you make me feel happy. Safe.”

     

                “That’s funny; the only time I feel safe now is when I’m with you.”

     

                “Are you alright? Last night-”

     

                “I’m fine. Last night was just … it all caught up to me. I’m fine now. Better once I can put all of this behind me. Do you think we’re on the news yet?”

     

                To distract herself, Lena climbed to her feet, stooping to pick up the remote and switching on the TV. She clicked through channels as she crossed over to the hidden panel, pouring herself whisky as she kept her eyes on the screen, finding a news channel with Sam’s face on the screen. Taking her glass and a bottle of water for Kara, Lena strayed back to her friend and handed off the bottle, while she remained standing, nursing her glass as she turned up the volume.

     

                “-you be stepping down?”

     

                “At present, I will be retaining my position as CEO of L-Corp, but we, as a company, are committed to supporting Miss Luthor through this challenging time.”

     

                “Miss Arias-”

     

                “That’s all the questions I have time for today. Thank you.”

     

                It went back to the reporter for a quick word and Lena lowered the volume, lips pursed as she narrowed her eyes at the screen. Sipping her whisky, she crossed over to the arm of the sofa and perched on the edge, wondering what the general consensus would be. She anticipated much the same as the initial revelation that the government was imprisoning aliens - protests, conspiracy theories, reruns in the news and think pieces in magazines and posted on blogs - and just hoped it would be enough to keep the momentum going. Once people lost interest, which they very quickly would if she remained out of sight, now a free woman, she would lose a portion of her power to the general public’s indifference.

     

                Running a hand over her face, mostly bare of any makeup in an effort to appear as haggard and vulnerably soft as possible, Lena closed her eyes and rolled the honeyed taste of her whisky on her tongue. Aside from the murmur of the TV, back to the studio now, it was quiet in the office, cold air pumping out of the HVAC’s vent, and it was a few minutes before footsteps clicked closer to the door. Opening her eyes, Lena glanced at Kara, who was watching the door without any visible tension in her body, and then turned her attention to the door without any apprehension as Sam opened it and stepped inside.

     

                Heavily sighing, her CEO closed the door behind herself and ran a hand through her hair, striding forward to toss her portfolio and phone onto the sofa. “God, they’re rabid. Is ten-thirty too early to have a drink?” Her eyes landed on Lena, who was tipping her glass back. “Oh.”

     

                Pouring herself one and offering one to Kara, who politely declined, Sam refilled Lena’s and clinked their glasses together. Swallowing a mouthful, Lena gave her an apologetic smile. “Sorry.”

     

                “Ah, it’ll be fine. You might have politicised it a bit too much for my liking, from a company perspective, but our stocks can take a hit without too much to worry about. I’d be more wary about a defamation suit from Brayden if I were you. Baker too, if he’s still bitter about his resignation. Are your family lawyers-”

     

                “I’m sure I can poach them from Lillian, even after dragging her through the mud.”

     

                “I don’t envy that phone call.”

     

                “Mm, well, that’s chess. I think she’ll be almost impressed. Thank you, again.”

     

                Waving a hand, Sam smiled and sipped her whisky as she trailed back to her desk, taking a seat behind it. Kara softly cleared her throat, her bottle of water anxiously rolled between her palms as she looked at Lena with wide eyes.

     

                “How long do you think …?”

     

                “It’s hard to say,” Lena diplomatically replied. “It’ll be picked up by every major news channel as an update on the ongoing situation, but whether the government backtracks or doubles down is unknown. Something will have to give at some point, and it won’t be me.”

     

                Nodding, although there was an impatient tautness to her shoulders, Kara unscrewed her water and took a sip as she considered that. They lingered a short while until Lena had taken a dizzying peek over the balcony to ensure the streets below were as busy as usual, with no extra crowds or reporters lurking about, and then had a driver take them home. It would have been easier for Kara to fly them to Lena’s penthouse, but they wanted to keep a low profile, which meant the agonisingly slow drive through midday traffic.

     

                Walking through the door of her apartment, Lena let her handbag dangle from one hand as she started shrugging off her coat, pausing to kick off her heels, the soles of her feet aching as she padded onwards barefoot. Discarding her handbag on a kitchen stool and draping her coat over the back of it, she smoothed her hair out of her face and sharply exhaled.

     

                “Right, well, that’s done; I should call my mother,” Lena stated, turning to her bag and rifling through the contents. 

     

                Kara hovered with uncertainty and Lena started dialling her mother’s number from memory as she paced away, tension knotted in her chest as she chewed her lower lip. It rang five times before it was eventually picked up and Lena managed to gather her aloof composure by the time she heard her mother’s voice.

     

                “Hello?”

     

                “It’s me.”

     

                “Oh. I’ve just seen the news - calling to gloat?”

     

                Snorting, Lena rolled her eyes. “No. I thought I owed you the courtesy of a call, though.”

     

                “Yes, after you’ve sabotaged my plans. That’s very appreciated,” her mother sarcastically responded, an edge of steel to her voice.

     

                “You can’t possibly think I would have let you do this.”

     

                “I thought for her you might.”

     

                Considering that, Lena swallowed thickly. “Yeah, maybe you’re right. Still doesn’t make it right, at the end of the day.”

     

                “There’s a difference between what’s right and what you want.”

     

                “I know. And clearly, for you, that doesn’t matter, but it does to me. Can I ask you something?” Lena paused, lips pressed together before she asked the question she wasn’t sure she wanted to. “Was this the deal from the beginning? Was that your motivation to help the whole time?”

     

                The silence dragged on and Lena would have thought her mother had hung up if she couldn’t hear the static silence on the line. With a withering sigh, Lillian’s response was irate and haughty. “President Brayden was still VP when you first came to me for help.”

     

                “So? What, you … played the long game and cut a deal with her, knowing she’d take Baker’s spot eventually and want that problem dealt with?”

     

                “No,” Lillian curtly replied, stiff but somewhat wounded as she continued. “There was no deal. My motivation was you, and only you.”

     

                Lena was silent as she tried to process her mother’s words, even now doubting her honesty.

     

                “All of it has been for you. You think I care about that girl, about what happened to her? This whole time, I’ve done it for you. And you still doubt that.”

     

                “Yes, I do,” Lena whispered.

     

                “I don’t deny the rest of it but I made that deal after I’d helped free you. Believe me or not, that’s the truth, I swear.”

     

                Swallowing thickly, conflicted by her mother’s words, unable to determine whether she was being honest or not, Lena clenched and unclenched her empty hand. Stomach knotting with unease as the tension in her shoulders made the base of her head ache, her eyelids fluttered shut and she let out a long breath. Things with her mother had never been easy, had always been frustratingly complicated, and Lena knew Lillian wouldn’t hesitate to lie to her, but she couldn’t see how it would benefit her to make Lena think that the deal hadn’t been cut until after she’d helped free her daughter. Sure, it might have warmed Lena to her mother, but they both knew as soon as Lillian had confessed to the deal she’d struck with President Brayden, in direct opposition to Lena’s efforts, any chances of anything beyond gratitude would have been snuffed out, becoming irrelevant in comparison to the resentment.

     

                “You know I’ll always be grateful for your help. I can never repay you for that-”

     

                “I’m not asking you to.”

     

                “But I can’t look past this. I’m sorry, really, I am - I hoped maybe things would be different this time, but you haven’t changed and I can’t knowingly let you do this.”

     

                “That’s no great surprise; I knew you’d try to stop me the moment I decided to tell you,” Lillian said with amusement. “Whether you do is an entirely different matter, and remains to be seen. At the very least, you’ll have her, so I hope you’ll be content with that as a consolation prize. Don’t say I never did anything for you.”

     

                With a quiet scoff, Lena’s mouth twisted wryly. “Right, well, I’m sure this won’t be the last I hear from you.”

     

                “No, I very much doubt it will be. But if you need anything … just call.”

     

                “Maybe. I guess we’ll see.”

     

                “Take care, Lena.”

     

                Her mother hung up the phone and Lena rubbed her eyes, keyed up and wishing things were easier. Despite her freedom, nothing seemed resolved and it was making it difficult for her to feel relieved or content. Tossing her phone onto the sofa, she sighed heavily and rounded on Kara, giving her a grim smile.

     

                “Come here.”

     

                Drawn forward at the gentle command, Kara looked at her with serious blue eyes, slowing a foot from her. The space was reduced to nothing as Lena stepped forward and wrapped her in a tight hug, burying her face in Kara’s shoulder as she frowned, seeking comfort in her embrace. Kara’s arms wound around her and held her gently, hands splayed over her back as warmth radiated through Lena’s back. After a prolonged moment of silence, Lena drew back.

     

                “You alright?” Kara murmured.

     

                “Mm, I’ll manage. It’s not ideal though.”

     

                “Thank you.”

     

                “For what?”

     

                Biting her lip, Kara looked down, her hands cupping the back of Lena’s arms as she stopped her from retreating too far. “I heard what she said and I know it’s not what you wanted but … you’re a good person. You’re being very selfless and I- it means a lot to me. I know what it’s costing you and I’m sorry but I’m also very grateful.”

     

                Giving her a small smile, Lena briefly touched Kara’s cheek. “It wouldn’t be right if I didn’t help. I wish I could compromise my morals, and I think a few months ago I would have - if you’d come with me when we escaped, I think I would never have looked back - but now that I know … I have to see it through, even if I don’t want to.”

     

                “I may not have a lot of good experiences with humans,” Kara murmured, a wry smile on her face as she cupped Lena’s chin in her hand. “But you must be the best of them. I’m sure of that.”

     

                With a quiet huff of laughter, Lena turned out of Kara’s touch and slowly paced away, digging the heels of her hands into her eyes as she tipped her head back. “Maybe the smartest of them, I’ll claim that.”

     

                “You downplay how much you care.”

     

                “Do I?”

     

                “Yes. Why?”

     

                “I don’t know,” Lena mused, turning to face her again, an uneven smile on her lips. “Maybe I just don’t want people to know so they can’t take advantage of that. Maybe I don’t actually care that much.”

     

                “Yes, you do. You care even more because you don’t want to be like your family.”

     

                “Mm, maybe you’re right. Maybe I’m just in a shit mood because I’m hungry. Shall I order food? Big Belly Burger?”

     

                “Um … whatever that is, sure.”

     

                Lena laughed, her broodiness abating somewhat as her eyes creased at the corners. “Cheeseburgers, fries and milkshakes.”

     

                “Milkshakes?” Kara perked up with delight.

     

                Placing an order to UberEats their food to her apartment, Lena collapsed onto the sofa with exhaustion and they lingered in silence until their food showed up twenty minutes later. Reluctant to go downstairs, Lena buzzed them up to the penthouse and forked over some cash as a tip, keeping her head ducked low as she handed off a tray of drinks to Kara and cradled three bags in her arms before nudging the door shut with her foot. Setting it all down on the coffee table, Lena sat cross-legged on the rug and tore open a bag, laying everything out on top of it as she gestured to it.

     

                “Dig in.”

     

                Cautiously eating a few fries and unwrapping a cheeseburger, Kara cleared her throat, looking a little nervous as she kept her eyes on the coffee table of food. Leaning back against the base of the sofa, Lena raised her eyebrows, taking a sip of Coke and setting the paper cup back down, ice clinking and a ring mark soaking into the brown paper bag.

     

                “So … I was thinking,” Kara haltingly started. “I don’t think you’ll like it …”

     

                Taking a couple of fries from her carton, Lena chewed slowly as she waited for Kara to continue, her expression clouded as wariness flickered in her green eyes. Setting down her burger, Kara gestured off-handedly, her cheeks slightly flushed.

     

                “I’d like to visit the others, if- if you could tell me where they are.”

     

                Licking salt off her fingers, Lena swallowed and softly cleared her throat, brows furrowed together. “Alex and the others?”

     

                “Yes.”

     

                “Oh, um, yeah, well, it doesn’t matter if I like it, so … sure, I can tell you where they are. I know- I know you would want to see them, and they’d want to see you too, so … um, well, it might be easier if I came with you, if we took my jet. Just because you wouldn’t really know what you’re looking for, geographically speaking.”

     

                Blinking in surprise, Kara straightened slightly, her eyebrows rising as she reached for her burger again. “Really? You’ll help?”

     

                Softening, Lena gave her an aching look as her shoulders slumped. “Of course I will. I know you feel differently about them and Alex asked me to ask you to visit her before she turned herself in so … debts repaid and all of that. If we- if we could maybe give it a couple of days … I just- I would like to rest a bit. Try to get things in order, you know?”

     

                “Of course,” Kara readily agreed, reaching across the coffee table to touch Lena’s hand. “And hey, thank you.”

     

                Nodding, Lena gave her a small smile. “Sure.”

     

                They finished eating, Kara inhaling half a dozen cheeseburgers with fries to match, and Lena dumped the mess into the trash before opening a bottle of wine and pouring two glasses. Kara liked it more than the scotch but sipped it warily as they changed into pyjamas and nestled on the sofa, sitting so close to each other that Lena could feel Kara’s body heat radiating from her in the few inches between their almost-touching knees. 

     

                The wine made Lena sleepy, her eyes growing heavy before she had even finished the bottle, and she found herself yawning as they watched episodes of Gilmore Girls back-to-back on the TV. Kara watched with rapt attention, leaning forward as she questioned Lena relentlessly on small-town habits, pop culture references and whether typical American life was like that. She shyly confessed to wanting to live somewhere like that and Lena watched her watch the TV, a tender look on her face as she took in the way Kara leaned forward slightly, drinking it all in with a wistful expression on her face. She swore then that she’d hunt down a small town just like Stars Hollow for her and buy them a house there.

     

                When she didn’t think she could keep her eyes open any longer, Lena fought back another yawn and mumbled she was off to bed. Despite her insistence that Kara could stay up as long as she wanted, and to treat Lena’s apartment as her own, Kara trailed her to her bedroom and followed Lena inside. Closing the door behind her, plunging them both into darkness, Kara could still see clearly and stopped when Lena paused in the middle of the room.

     

                “You don’t have to-” Lena rasped, cutting off as she pressed her lips into a thin line.

     

                She felt Kara’s fingertips brush the back of her pyjama shirt, warm through the silk. “I know. Truthfully, I don’t want to be alone either. I can- I can still hear you, but I slept with someone on the other side of the wall from me for eighteen years. Two feet away, if that. It feels … lonely without it. Your house is too big.”

     

                Kara let out a short laugh, faintly embarrassed as she rubbed the side of her nose, and Lena turned to blindly face her, unable to make out anything more than a vague shadow standing before her. Reaching out, she felt warm silk and let her hands glide over the fabric as she tried to make sense of what part of Kara she was touching, until she reached her shoulders, feeling the radiating heat from Kara’s neck as she cupped the side of it, feeling her pulse against her palm.

     

                “Sleep next to me then.”

     

                She felt Kara’s head turn, the soft brush of lips against the base of her thumb, eliciting a gentle swooping sensation in her stomach, and Lena’s eyelids fluttered shut. They’d talked about this, about the concerns of getting in over their heads without time to work things out in the outside world, but Lena would be lying if she said she didn’t feel the desperate need for someone. They moved closer without any conscious decision to and she could feel Kara’s warm breath on her cheek, the anticipation of what came next knotting her stomach, but Lena turned away before it could go that far. They’d talked about this.

     

                The bedroom felt cold as she stepped away from Kara’s body heat and Lena cleared her throat as she raked a hand through her hair. Tossing decorative pillows aside and pulling back the covers, she climbed into bed and pulled the covers over her. Kara warily sank down onto the other side of the mattress, on top of the blankets, and left a good two feet between them, as effective as a cell wall as Lena stared up at the dark ceiling and swallowed thickly.

     

                “Goodnight,” Kara whispered, and Lena likewise replied before rolling over and trying her best to sleep.

     

                Unfortunately, all of her exhaustion had given way to tension and it was a long while before she slept. Beside her, Kara’s breaths were slow and even and Lena was left alone with her thoughts, trying to lay it all out straight. She felt fiercely protective of her friend, so attached to her that it was frightening, and Lena had never felt that way about anyone before, so it was confusing and concerning as she wondered whether her own feelings were real. Would she have felt similarly if they’d met normally, or was this fixation merely a side effect of imprisonment? She didn’t want to believe that they’d purely bonded over the trauma of what had happened to them, and Kara similarly didn’t have that same attachment to anyone but the guard, doctor and, later, psychologist, so what did that say? It was undeniable that they’d gravitated to each other, albeit with little choice in the matter with their adjoining cells, but they’d talked about everything and anything in a way that Lena had never been so open about before. Surely that wasn’t purely because they’d shared the same vent in a prison wall. 

     

                She ended up falling asleep later than anticipated as she ruminated on her puzzling feelings, so keyed up that she thought maybe she should download Tinder or take up some adrenaline-fuelled activity to vent some of her bottled-up feelings. For the amount of crying she’d done recently, Lena was still shockingly brimming with so many unspent emotions. She didn’t think a one-night stand would cut it, and truthfully couldn’t even fathom feeling comfortable enough around a stranger to be that vulnerable, and with her fear of heights and water, that ruled out a fair few activities geared towards adrenaline junkies. Instead, she would have to stamp it all down and forge onwards until she reached a point of complete and utter defeat, or found a way to compartmentalise and process it all bit by bit, preferably in a healthy way. Neither seemed like a viable option.

     

                The next few days were uneventful and quiet. In some ways, it was almost like being in prison; they didn’t do anything productive, didn’t do anything except eat at meal times, or whenever they grew hungry, sleep whenever they grew tired, wash and change into clean pyjamas and sit idly beside each other on the sofa. Of course, it was in stark contrast to prison in many ways; better quality clothes, good food, a bed with a large, comfortable mattress, hot baths and unlimited access to TV and alcohol. They watched so many episodes of Gilmore Girls that Lena lost track of time.

     

                It was peaceful though, a few days of nothing that allowed them to make up for a busy week or so. Lena hadn’t really felt so aimless since she’d still been a prisoner inside Fort Rozz and it was disconcerting but well-needed after the months on the run or being shuttled about in her crusade to rescue her friend. The wound in her side was healing well and it almost felt like it could’ve been the holidays, a few days where she was holed up inside her penthouse to dither about until the office opened back up, except Lena wasn’t doing any work and there was an alien parked up on her sofa with her. It was surreal but also the most normal her life had felt in a long time.

     

                “We can leave tomorrow if you’d like,” Lena announced as she cut a slice of chocolate cake for Kara, the coffee machine behind her dripping fresh espresso into cups for them and a peaceful evening ahead.
