                They’d already had dinner, a selection of salads and vegetables to sate Lena’s craving for something fresh , and the muffled sounds of the city beyond the cracked open balcony door were soothing. The sky was a deep blue, a thousand windows illuminated by yellow light, and a warm breeze crept in as they lingered in the peace they’d carved out for themselves. If every day could be like that, Lena thought she would be able to move on quite quickly. 

     

                Glancing over at her, Kara’s eyebrows rose with mild surprise. “Tomorrow?”

     

                Nodding, Lena gave her a ghost of a smile, not particularly thrilled to be doing it for her but resolutely following through on her promise to Alex. Perking right up, Kara gave her a sweet smile as her cheeks dimpled, and Lena carried their coffee and the slice of cake over to the sofa, setting the cups down on the coffee table and passing the plate off to Kara. Resting a hand on her friend’s knee, Lena gave her a serious look.

     

                “I need you to promise me you won’t make matters worse and try to free them. I understand it’s- it’s difficult for you but … they’re in custody, awaiting trial, and it’s- I don’t know if they’re going to be as lucky as we are. But you have to let them deal with the consequences. Please-“

     

                “I won’t do anything to endanger you,” Kara softly promised, covering Lena’s hand with her own and gently squeezing.

                

                Mouth opening and closing, Lena looked down at her lap. “It’s not me I’m worried about.”

     

                “I know that … they helped them do bad things, so they must have done bad things too. I don’t think they’re bad though, and they’re my family-“

     

                “I know they are,” Lena sighed as her shoulders slumped. 

     

                “I just- I want to be able to see them. If they’re going away for a while … I want to be able to visit them. I know you don’t want to see any of them, and you don’t have to, and you don’t have to help them or- or anything else, and I won’t fight anyone on the charges, even if I disagree. I think … all the time they were onboard Fort Rozz should have been a long enough sentence already served, but … it’s not up to me, so I’ll accept whatever comes next. But I won’t abandon them; I’ll never do that. They didn’t give up on me, they did the best that they could, and I’ll do the same for them. You don’t have to like it-“

     

                “I don’t like it. One bit. But you’re free now, Kara. Free to do whatever you want, whether I agree with you or not. I just don’t want to see you end up a fugitive or worse. But if all you want to do is see them while they’re put away … I’ll make it happen for you. And you’re right, I don't have to help them, or maybe I do for all the help they gave me outside, I don’t know, but either way … I’ll help them for you. I already told you my lawyers will help them, and I won’t go back on my word.”

     

                Raising Lena’s hand, Kara kissed her knuckles, giving her a small smile. “I know you want them to do time, but thank you. I’m putting you in an awkward place but … I’m lucky to have you. I won’t do anything to mess that up. I wouldn’t know what to do if I didn’t have you.”

     

                Exhaling softly, Lena touched her fingertips to Kara’s cheek as she gave her a weary smile, barely more than a twitch of her lips. “There’s nothing you could do to lose me.”

     

                Hesitating, Kara reached up to cover Lena’s hand with her own. Her cheeks were slightly pink, and if she wasn’t already feverishly warm, Lena would have noticed the way she flushed, a little flustered as she stammered.

     

                “When we- when we get back … would you- could we- do you want to go on a date?”

     

                Surprise flashed across Lena’s face as she straightened, sitting back with her hand still held beneath Kara’s, pressed to her cheek. “A date?”

     

                Gesturing towards the TV, where the current episode continued to play, Kara gave her an uncertain smile. “Like on the TV. That’s what you do when you like someone, right? Flowers and- and food. Or is it coffee? Lorelai gets coffee …” Kara’s eyes strayed to the coffee on the table and then back to Lena, her expression crumpling. “Does that mean that we’ve already -”

     

                “A date can be whatever,” Lena interrupted before Kara could go down a rabbit hole of musing about human customs, or what she thought she knew about them, from a prison and a few hours of TV. “You just pick something both people would enjoy and do it on that date. Um … it’s usually dinner but it can be anything - it can be a movie or bowling, or ice cream on a beach somewhere.”

     

                Kara cocked her head to the side. “So ice cream on the beach … was that-”

     

                Leaning in, Lena touched their foreheads together, grimacing slightly at how complicated it was all getting. “I don’t know. It was just … something to cling to.”

     

                “Oh.”

     

                “But now we’re out, and I’m still clinging to it, and I would really like to go on a date with you. Just … maybe not right now.”

     

                “Oh, okay,” Kara said, perking back up again as she freed Lena’s hand and gave her a quick grin. “So … you do like me?”

     

                Softly groaning, Lena rubbed her eyes and laughed, shaking her head. “I like you, I love you, I- I don’t know. I just want to have you around; I’m not sure in which way yet though.”

     

                “Okay, well, you decide which way and then let me know. I already know how I feel but I know it’s not that simple for you.”

     

                “It shouldn’t be that simple for you either. You know how you would have those sessions with Kelly? Talk about your thoughts and feelings? I don’t think it would be a bad idea for you to do that with someone outside , just to help you … adjust. Things might change a lot for you now. It might not be that simple anymore. There’s a lot of trauma associated with what you went through, and it was for such a long time, I-”

     

                “Okay,” Kara whispered, reaching out to touch Lena’s knee as she fell silent. “Sure, Lena, I’ll talk to someone. But they’re not going to change my mind.”

     

                Nodding, Lena smiled faintly as she closed her eyes. Patting Kara’s hand, she cleared her throat and jerked her chin towards the plate balancing in Kara’s lap. “Eat your cake.”

     

                They put any further conversation about tense topics to bed for the remainder of the evening, Lena drinking her coffee and migrating to something stronger to medicate the prickle of unease, the unrelenting worry about what would happen next, which led to memories of what had happened to easily resurface at night as they manifested as nightmares. At least with a few drinks it made her mind sluggish and soothed the panic a little, further aided by the warmth of Kara as she unconsciously shifted across the mattress each night. It didn’t matter how much space was between them when they went to bed - Lena always awoke pressed up against Kara, or with Kara’s arm slung across her waist. 

     

                It was no different that night, going to bed together just after ten o’clock, Kara stretching out on what had unequivocally become her side of the bed in Lena’s room, and Lena slept as peacefully as she could. It was better than she had been sleeping, some part of her mind aware that she was home and aware of Kara, but it was a restless sort of sleep, even at the best of times. The worst of times were snatches of nightmares that woke her in the middle of the night, Kara blinking owlishly beside her as she reached for her, soothing her. Kara never had nightmares; Lena didn’t understand how.

     

                The next morning, after conversing with Eve on the details of the flight she’d arranged on a private jet, Lena showered and dressed and compiled a few necessities into an overnight bag, procuring a small suitcase for Kara to likewise pack a few borrowed clothes. They had paperwork and documents and a book each to read on the flight, a tablet with ten episodes of Gilmore Girls downloaded for Kara to watch if she fancied it, and a hotel booked on the other end. Lena resented the need to return to hotels so soon after finally coming home, but she wouldn’t be able to buy an apartment in DC overnight, even with her fortune, so they had to make do and she resigned herself to a new unfamiliar setting. 

     

                A car came to pick them up, the ride slow but they weren’t in much of a rush, and Kara was fascinated by the interior of the private jet as they took their seats, their things packed away and a selection of sparkling water, nuts and fruit laid alongside recent magazines and newspapers. Lena watched her with amusement, wondering if she should book a seat in economy for the trip back, just for Kara to have a better understanding of more common airfare. As the jet took off, she rapidly explained to Lena how the aircraft on Krypton differed from the aircraft on Earth, and even though she’d been about to settle in with the New York Times crossword, Lena set the newspaper aside and probed for more information on Krypton. All too willing to oblige, Kara animatedly talked and occasionally drew a rough sketch on a monogrammed notepad set on the sideboard of the jet, highlighting the major differences and advancements in their technology. Lena wondered if she could replicate some of it and found her mind turning back to her work, something that she hadn’t done in a year, something that she’d sorely missed.

     

                The flight time to DC wasn’t very long and they touched down before Lena could even settle in properly, their conversation taking up most of the hour and a bit it took for them to descend to the private airstrip. A car was waiting for them and whisked them away to the Waldorf, the penthouse booked out for Lena again, disorientingly familiar as she stepped over the threshold of the suite with a nauseous look on her face.

     

                “Last time I was in this room, I’d just been pardoned and you were still in Fort Rozz,” Lena rasped as she looked around.

     

                Kara’s hand brushed her back as she passed her and then turned in the middle of the suite to give Lena an uneven smile. “Look how much has changed in so little time.”

     

                Running a hand over her face, Lena hummed, dropping her bag to the floor. Her hands shook slightly and she curled them into fists, hating the drawn-out process of fixing things and not knowing where to begin. Sure, she had Kara with her now, which was the most important thing to Lena, but she still felt like she was back to square one in many ways.

     

                “We’ll sort the rest of it too,” Kara confidently said, giving Lena a bright smile. “I’m sure of it. We can do anything if we work together, we’ve already proven that.”

     

                “Right,” Lena doubtfully replied, falling silent for a moment before she wearily sighed. “I think I need to call my mom.”

     

                She really didn’t want to but Kara was hopefully optimistic that things would work out and Lena didn’t want to be the one to burst her bubble. Truthfully, she had no contacts in the government and no leverage, the news over the last few days filled with nothing but doubts about whether her press conference had been factual - President Brayden had denounced any deal with Cadmus and played it off as the PTSD and paranoia of a recently freed woman trying to adjust back to society - and Lena didn’t know where to begin finding out what the latest status was with Alex, Kelly and Eliza. Not exactly on the best terms with Lillian, she was all Lena had to fall back on, so well connected with her web of contacts and hidden secrets for blackmail and bribery. 

     

                Pulling out her phone, Lena sighed again as she punched Lillian’s number in and waited for the call to connect. It didn’t take as long for Lillian to answer this time, recognising the number and sounding annoyingly smug as her voice came through.

     

                “Well, that didn’t take as long as I expected.”

     

                “I’m in DC,” Lena sulkily replied. “We’d like to visit the others but … I don’t have any contacts with the prisons or know where they’re being kept. If you could help … that would be very appreciated.”

     

                “I’m sure it would be. But, you know, I’m getting a bit tired of offering up my help with nothing in return. Especially when there’s a lack of trust.”

     

                Pinching the bridge of her nose, Lena grimaced. “Okay, we’re not doing this. I told you I don’t agree with the choice you made, that’s that, it’s done, let’s move on. If you don’t want to help, that’s fine, but you told me to call you if I needed anything so I’m calling. Whether you decide to help is entirely up to you but … if there’s something I can do for you in exchange, just let me know.”

     

                She hated to put herself at her mother’s mercy but it was the only way she could envision getting the information she needed. It didn’t seem a worthy sacrifice for the sake of the people who had been on the opposite side of a cell to her, but it was worth it for Kara’s sake. She just wished her friend wouldn’t squander any deals Lena made on people she didn’t think deserved it.

     

                “As a matter of fact, there is something you can do for me.”

     

                “What?”

     

                “Where are you?”

     

                “At a hotel,” Lena airily replied.

     

                “Which one?”

     

                “Why?”

     

                “I’m going to send a car for you. We can talk when you get here.”

     

                Growing impatient now, Lena bit back a huff. “Get where?”

     

                “Well, that’s the deal, that’s what I want from you. You get in the car and come and meet me here, and you’ll leave with the most up-to-date information on your little friends, and visitation privileges if I have enough time to make some calls. Whether or not I do have the time will depend on how long you insist on prolonging this call.”

     

                “We’re at the Waldorf.”

     

                Hanging up without another word, Lena groaned softly and tucked her phone into her pocket. Giving Kara an exasperated look, she rolled her eyes. “Looks like we’re not hanging around for as long as I’d thought. I’m assuming you caught all of that?”

     

                “Yes.”

     

                “Right, well … until then, I might take a nap.”

     

                Walking through to the bedroom, Lena paused to kick off her shoes and shed her coat and then toppled onto the mattress, dragging a pillow into a comfortable position and burying her face in it. Kara didn’t follow after her and Lena soon heard the muffled sound of Gilmore Girls coming from the living room as Kara tuned in on the tablet they’d brought, passing the time in her own way. Still existing in a state of near-permanent exhaustion, Lena did manage to lightly doze, until Kara gently shook her awake, startling her nonetheless, and sheepishly informed her there was a car idling downstairs and a driver on the phone held in Kara’s hand.

     

                Taking her time as she slipped on her heels and belted her coat, Lena gathered up her handbag and took a moment to apply fresh lipstick before snagging the hotel room key and taking the elevator downstairs. She warily eyed the two suited men waiting beside the black town car and only felt comfortable enough climbing into the back because she had Kara with her, and unless they had a surprise stash of green kryptonite stowed inside, she was sure her friend would handle any troubling situations.

     

                The drive was silent and neither of the men in the front seats offered up any explanation of where they were going, although Lena noticed the earpieces and thought she should have expected their destination when she caught a glimpse of where they were. It seemed the most logical explanation and she stifled a groan of annoyance as five minutes later they neared the gated expanse of the White House. Disgruntled, Lena was helpless to be ferried the rest of the way there, the car idling at security as they were all cleared and then directed through. It occurred to Lena that the men who had come to fetch her were, in fact, the Secret Service, which made her instantly suspicious about her mother’s scheming.

     

                Climbing out of the car, she smoothed out her coat and tossed her hair back, handbag in the crook of her arm as she walked ahead of Kara, escorted inside with a vague sense of familiarity. It wasn’t her first time at the White House, although it was the first time she was there against her will, and Lena was already weary of it by the time she was ushered into the Oval Office with Kara, finding her mother sipping tea with President Brayden.

     

                Pausing just inside the threshold, with Kara hovering behind her, brimming with nervous energy, Lena arched an eyebrow as she folded her arms over her chest. Setting her teacup and saucer down on the tray, Lillian turned her full attention to her daughter and faintly smirked as President Brayden gestured to the empty spots on the sofas.

     

                “Ah, good, Miss Luthor, please take a seat. And you must be Kara Zor-El - I hear I have you to thank for retrieving Fort Rozz.”

     

                Lena was wary as she crept closer and stiffly perched on the edge of the sofa, at the opposite end of her mother. Kara refused to sit, taking up a protective stance at Lena’s elbow, her alien strength and power hidden behind the restlessness of her darting eyes and fidgeting fingers, unsure of what was going on.

     

                “To what do I owe the pleasure?” Lena sarcastically asked.

     

                “I requested your presence here so we could sort this out amicably and without further involvement of the press,” President Brayden said, reaching for the teapot. “Tea? Miss Zor-El?”

     

                Uncomfortable with the situation, Kara leapt at the offer of tea, if only to give her something else to fiddle with. She nursed her cup and gave the saucer a puzzled look as she held onto it, while Lena left the cup slid across the coffee table for her untouched, waiting for further explanation.

     

                “I thought we might come to an understanding, of a sort.”

     

                “You mean you want to know the price of my silence?”

     

                “If your silence could be bought, I wouldn’t have heard a peep out of you since you left for college,” Lillian witheringly retorted. “Instead, you insist on making trouble for me. Throwing your own mother to the wolves, really?”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena’s mouth twitched with a faint smile at the theatrics. “Don’t pretend to be surprised. You already admitted you knew I wouldn’t agree when you decided to tell me. Now, can we cut to the chase? I believe you have the information I wanted, and I’d rather not drag this out any longer than necessary.”

     

                “Well, I’ll put it plainly, Lena,” Brayden said, shifting forward, sliding a manila envelope towards Lena. “You sign this agreement and NDA, and in return, I’ll give you the opportunity to provide me with a list of names of prisoners who will walk free.”

     

                Swallowing thickly, Lena’s fingers hovered over the envelope. “And the rest of them?”

     

                Shrugging helplessly and splaying her hands, Brayden blew the air out of her cheeks. “I’m afraid I can’t risk that many potential hostiles out amongst the public.”

     

                Glancing up at Kara, Lena met her eyes and saw the way the corners of her mouth tightened, the minute shake of her head. Clearing her throat, Lena crossed her legs and leaned forward, scooting the envelope away without even opening the contents.

     

                “No deal, I’m afraid. It’s all of them or nothing.”

     

                “By all means, let’s empty all of the human prisons while they’re at it. Dangerous criminals free to do what they please,” Lillian scoffed.

     

                “It’s innocent until proven guilty in this country,” Lena snarkily responded. “Something that I was denied, just like everyone else in the prison. Including the human staff, I might add. What’s going to happen to them? I bet you’ll let them walk, right? It doesn’t matter if they were more cruel than any of the aliens or metahumans. You don’t care about the things they could do to the general public because that doesn’t fit your ideology.”

     

                Climbing to her feet, Lena picked up her handbag and smoothed down her coat, stepping around the coffee table and letting her hand brush against Kara’s arm. “Burn it.”

     

                With a quick glance at her, Kara turned her attention to the envelope on the table. She didn’t so much as blink before her heat vision burned a hole right through it, and then on a less than ideal note, right through the coffee table too, the carpet smoking as she staggered back, blinking as she tried to stop herself. Cringing slightly, Lena smoothed a hand over Kara’s back and suppressed a groan as she watched Kara blow to put out the flames, flapping her hands to dispel the smoke, and sending the entire tea tray and decorative coffee table pieces flying off the other end of the table.

     

                She did take care of the fire threat though, looking meek as she shrank in on herself, shoulders hunched as Lena patted her shoulder. Lillian was cradling her cup and saucer again and just arched an eyebrow, eyeing the mess and clicking her tongue as she leaned forward to set her cup down on the now-bare coffee table.

     

                “A prime example of what we’re trying to avoid,” Lillian pointed out.

     

                Frowning, a little flustered at the unfolding events, Lena cleared her throat. “She’s already been freed and she’s not caused any problems.”

     

                President Brayden leaned back against the sofa cushions. “Yet.”

     

                Lena’s attention slid to her, expression cool and aloof, and she folded her arms over her chest. There was a brief moment of silence before the President beckoned her back to the sofas. 

     

                “Sit. Let’s sort this out so we can come to an agreement and put it past us.”

     

                “There’s no agreement that we can make that will give me what I want.”

     

                “Sit and let’s talk about it. I won’t lie to you, Lena, you have a lot of power at the moment with the media’s interest in you, which is making things very difficult for me. I’d prefer it if we could avoid any further public accusations.”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena quietly scoffed, her lips twitching contemptuously as her green eyes shone with anger. “They’re not accusations if they’re true. And I have no patience for politicking - I didn’t intend to be brought here, so if we can resolve this quickly, that would be great.”

     

                “Take a seat.”

     

                Hesitating a moment, the obstinate side of her wanting to remain standing, to not give in to the whims of the most powerful person in the country, Lena reluctantly sat down again. With a haughty jut of her chin, she propped her elbow on the arm of the sofa and rested her chin in her palm, arching her eyebrow with a derisive look on her face.

     

                “Well?”

     

                “An NDA will be an absolute.”

     

                “And a public apology, of course,” Lillian added, Lena’s eyes cutting sideways to her mother as she silently fumed. “To President Brayden, and perhaps your mother if you can find it within yourself.”

     

                “And why should I apologise for the truth?”

     

                “Because I’ll cut you a sweeter deal than I’d like to,” Brayden stated, spreading her hands in an amenable manner, a maddeningly serene smile on her face as Lena stewed on it. “What do you want?”

     

                “Justice. For everyone . I want the staff in jail; I want the prisoners free. That’s how it should have been, not the other way around.”

     

                “And you won’t settle for a list of names? It can be a lengthy one, I’ll grant you that.”

     

                “No.”

     

                “How about a compromise? No, hear me out; you want them all to walk free but that’s a big risk - you didn’t see half of what’s inside that prison, what kinds of aliens and powers are in there - and I’m not willing to ruin my approval ratings to please someone who got mixed up in this by my predecessor’s mistaken choices.” 

     

                “How are we supposed to compromise on a human rights issue?”

     

                “Now, the way I see it, we could stick to the original story we released to the public - they’re being detained until they’ve been approved to settle. That would rely on the risk factor of approving them.” 

     

                “What about due process? A fair hearing? They shouldn’t have been imprisoned in the first place with that. They haven’t committed any crimes.”

     

                Clearing her throat, Brayden deliberated and conceded. “I admit, it was badly handled. I tell you this in confidence, but we’re still in the midst of looking into the formation of the DEO and how it evolved into its present-day form. Obviously, there are a, ah, few legalities to take into consideration. I hope you can understand that I will never be able to condemn a branch of the government, even one such as the DEO, and that leaves me in a difficult place. To admit that they were imprisoned without a trial would entail the condemnation of the DEO. The best I can offer is processing them on a case-by-case basis of their powers and threat to society.”

     

                “And what else?”

     

                “As for the staff … well, I had intended to release most of them but a similar process could be implemented for them as well. A case-by-case review of their position and, ah, influence within the prison. Obviously, there are a few higher-ranking employees who would take the brunt of the blame for any unfortunate deeds committed. We would make an example out of them. How does that sound?”

     

                Eyes flitting to Kara, Lena shifted on the sofa, clearing her throat and drawing in a slightly shaky breath. “Could we have a moment to discuss things?”

     

                “By all means. Lillian, why don’t we discuss our business elsewhere for a few minutes?”

     

                The two women left in conversation and Lena hated the familiarity of the way her mother spoke to the President, as if they were on equal footing, both opportunistic and allied with each other. It made her not want to trust a word either of them said, knowing they would both be manipulating her for mutual gain. However, as soon as the door closed behind them, she turned to Kara.

     

                Sinking onto the vacated sofa across from her, Kara clasped her hands, elbows on thighs, and frowned as she puzzled over it. Lena gave her a few moments to think about it before prompting her opinion.

     

                “Do you think that’s fair? I mean, we were expecting to fight to have their applications processed quicker anyway, and at least we can guarantee they won’t be experimented on.”

     

                “But what about the ones deemed a threat? How do we know they won’t say they’re all a threat. Or experiment only on the ones that are threats.”

     

                “A very good point. If we had some guarantee though … if we used what we know as leverage to hold them to their word or we go public, surely that would be a better deal than what they were planning on doing. I just- I don’t think we’re going to get them all free without using force. And I don’t think that’s a good thing to do either. You know more about aliens than I do; are there some you wouldn’t want running around free?”

     

                “Well, fifth-dimensional imps,” Kara confessed. “Although, I’m certain there wasn’t one of those in the prison or we probably could’ve been out a lot sooner. But I agree there are certain species that could be very dangerous. I just think there should also be a chance to prove themselves, right? I’m more dangerous than any of them but I’m being given a chance.”

     

                Opening her mouth, Lena clamped it shut again and grimaced, a shallow furrow between her eyebrows. “Kara … I’ll be honest, I don’t know if they’d be giving you a chance without my mum helping to negotiate it for me. And I think part of that deal was you in exchange for the rest of them.”

     

                “I know,” Kara forlornly murmured, running a hand through her hair. “I know that I’d be the last one they’d want to free if it hadn’t been for you. That’s why I’m so grateful - I know what my life would be like without you. I’ve lived it for so long and I know it wouldn’t have changed.”

     

                “What about the staff?”

     

                Cheeks dimpling as her mouth flattened, Kara shrugged indifferently. “You know that I- it doesn’t matter to me what happens to them. I’m not … vengeful.”

     

                Letting out a small laugh, Lena smiled crookedly. “Do you think I am?”

     

                Pausing, Kara floundered for a moment. “No. No, I don’t think you’re vengeful . That means … you want to- to hurt them back , right? You just want justice. There’s nothing wrong with justice.”

     

                “But … don’t you want that?” Lena desperately asked, wanting to understand Kara, wanting Kara to understand her . “You, more than anyone, know the evil they inflicted. The kryptonite collar, the straitjacket, I mean … that deserves justice.”

     

                A ghost of a smile crossed Kara’s face as she shrugged. “I don’t know. The things I want … they’re all good things, things that will make me happy. I’m not sure justice would make me happy. Being free and living a good life will make me happy.”

     

                Rising to her feet, Lena rounded the coffee table and sank to her knees as she reached out to cup Kara’s hands in her own. Looking up at her with a pained look on her face, Lena’s eyes were aching and pleading. She softly sighed, her shoulders caving, and Kara’s face furrowed with gentle confusion.

     

                “I will make your life happy, but we need to decide together what happens next. I know what I would do but … I don’t know if it’s something we should agree to. And I won’t decide for you.”

     

                “I’ve never had to make any real decisions,” Kara weakly laughed with a wavering smile.

     

                “I know, I know, but now you do. So … what do you want to do?”

     

                Chewing her lip, Kara stared down at their hands, the way Lena’s thumbs ghosted over her wrists, the slight tremor in her hands. Swallowing thickly, Kara raised her eyes to meet Lena’s, guilt and panic welling up in the innocent blue.

     

                “I want to … give them a list,” she whispered, “with the names of my friends on it, and the names of the people who hurt us. And they can process the rest of them in their own time. But they’re not experimenting on any of them.”

     

                Nodding, Lena slowly exhaled and shifted back. “Okay. I can live with that. We just have to hope they can.”

     

                She was seated back on her sofa and a few minutes of anxious-filled silence passed by before the President and her mother stepped back in, first a little hesitant and then boldly as they saw them sitting in silence. Once everyone was comfortably seated again, Lillian raised her eyebrows as she looked at her daughter.

     

                “Well?”

     

                Lena had procured a pen and a sheet of paper from President Brayden’s desk and made two separate lists at Kara’s word - one for her friends and one for the staff - and handed them over to Lillian with a cutting look. Taking the page, Lillian’s eyes ran over the names and she shrugged her shoulders and gave Lena an expectant look.

     

                “The first is a non-negotiable list of detainees we’d like released. The second is, ideally, a list of the high-priority staff to be sentenced.”

     

                She explained it matter-of-factly, trying to swallow her dislike for the names of three women on the list of Kara’s friends. Clearing her throat, Lena rolled her eyes as she gestured to the page.

     

                “If you agree to that, then I’ll make whatever public statement you want. We’re also expecting you to actually process the rest of them - prisoners and staff - according to their risk level and crimes.”

     

                “What about those who are too risky to be released?” Lillian asked.

     

                The President leaned in to add her bit too, looking disgruntled. “I need a way to keep them out of the way, Miss Luthor, I hope you can understand that. Cadmus was the optimal solution, for everyone’s benefit.”

     

                “And it was going to help us understand them more.”

     

                Giving her mother an exasperated look, Lena wearily sighed. “If they’re a genuine risk, then by all means keep them safely tucked away somewhere. In more humane conditions though.”

     

                Lillian laughed, her mouth twitching at the corners as her eyes shone. “So you’re fine with a humane prison? Isn’t that a bit counter-productive to your ethos?”

     

                “You and I both know I’m not going to get my own way here, so I have to make sacrifices somewhere. Unfortunately, it will have to be them, as the rest is non-negotiable, of course.”

     

                “Of course. I can assure you, my conditions will be humane,” Lillian smiled sharply.

     

                “Experimentation is non-negotiable,” Lena coldly replied.

     

                “Your mother is right; understanding these creatures is our best hope for keeping America, and the rest of the world, safe from invasion.”

     

                Eyes shifting to President Brayden, Lena’s lip curled derisively. “If they wanted to invade, they would have. That’s very obvious, considering there are already hundreds that have been imprisoned by the government. How many are hidden? How many live overseas in other countries? They haven’t been a threat so far.”

     

                “So far is not good enough, I’m afraid. I can compromise on that though, if it helps us come to an agreement,” Brayden said with a condescending smile. “How about Cadmus takes possession of them for experimentation after they’re deceased?”

     

                “How do I know you’re not going to purposely kill them for that reason?”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lillian gave her daughter a withering look. “Your imagination is a bleak place.”

     

                “I’m trying to meet you in the middle, Lena,” Brayden said with an edge of desperation.

     

                Raising her eyebrows as she folded her arms, Lena gave her a sceptical look. “Why? Why are you trying to cut a deal with me? Surely you’re not afraid of a little bit of bad press? I’m not that powerful.”

     

                “No, you’re not.”

     

                The implication in her voice, coupled with the way her eyes furtively darted to Kara and back, made Lena let out a surprised bark of laughter. Grinning, she cocked her head to the side, eyes creasing at the corners as she looked at Kara and then back to the President.

     

                “Oh, I see. It’s not me you’re trying to please.”

     

                “No, it isn’t,” Brayden brittly replied.

     

                “You have plenty of kryptonite, I’m sure. Why are you so afraid?”

     

                Kara blinked, catching up to the conversation as she looked around at all three women, her eyes widening with surprise as her face paled a little. Her knuckles whitened as she clenched her hands into fists in her lap, trying to shrink in on herself, to look smaller, harmless. Lena felt a pang of tenderness and sympathy for the alien.

     

                “It didn’t seem to be that effective last time.”

     

                Lena didn’t mention all the ways it was agonising for Kara, even if she was able to forge onwards through smaller doses. She didn’t want to give them any more information about her friend than they already had, didn’t want to highlight Kara’s vulnerabilities. Instead, she’d use this newfound fear of the Kryptonian as leverage to benefit them. It was almost a relief to know that there was a straightforward reason they were being so accommodating, instead of having to work out what new scheme was unfolding, and Lena fought back a bigger smile.

     

                “Well, let’s continue,” she said with thinly veiled delight. “Kara, what else would you like?”

     

                Mouth parting as all eyes fell on her, Kara was speechless for a moment as she started fiddling with her hands, meek and uncertain as her cheeks turned pink. Her eyes met Lena’s, who nodded, and she softly cleared her throat.

     

                “Um … I don’t know if- if it’s honourable to the dead to experiment on them.”

     

                “It’s an Earth custom to donate your bodies to science,” Lillian tried to reason.

     

                Scoffing, Lena shook her head. “It’s not a custom. Some people do it but they consent.”

     

                “Um … we could maybe ask them then,” Kara optimistically ventured.

     

                The two older women shared a look and President Brayden shifted awkwardly. “I’m afraid this will be non-negotiable for us. We need to know what we’re working with here, how to counteract any terrorist attacks, keep people safe. We already have an extensive dossier on the prisoners of Fort Rozz but Cadmus will be able to take that a step further with scientific research on corpses.”

     

                “Of course, live subjects would yield better results,” Lillian sighed, “but I’ll take what I can get.”

     

                Lena waited for Kara to respond and it was a tense few minutes of silence before the Kryptonian grimaced and nodded with a look of pain in her eyes. “Okay. Fine. Only when they’re deceased - but you’ll give them proper funeral rites afterwards.”

     

                “Sure,” Lillian flippantly agreed. “Anything else?”

     

                “That Alien Amnesty Act thing … I want it reinstated.”

     

                Lillian glanced over at the President. “Susan?”

     

                Mouth thinning, there was a moment as she deliberated over it. “That’s not entirely up to me. And it’s something public , something that could damage my approval ratings, so I can’t make any guarantees with that one. My administration will need to assess it before making a decision. Hell, for all we know, it could actually benefit me, but I don’t know that yet and there’s already been so much upheaval in this country’s politics recently. I’d rather not be the next ousted President so soon.”

     

                “That’s fair,” Kara relented. “There’s just one more thing.”

     

                All eyes were trained on her and Lena watched the way her soft features hardened, her jaw clenched and eyes flat as her stare drilled into President Brayden’s face. Lena didn’t know what thought had triggered such a change in Kara’s gentle demeanour but she felt her stomach lurch, rooted to her seat as she felt her pulse quicken, wondering if things were about to take a disastrous turn. After watching Kara’s rogue heat vision carve through the table and set the carpet smoking, she was half-paralysed with the fear that Kara was about to melt the face off the President. 

     

                “What happened to my cousin?”

     

                Lena’s stomach dropped and she opened her mouth to try and mediate. It wasn’t for the sake of the other women but for Kara’s sake. She didn’t want her to know the truth, didn’t want to hear something that would upset her, which it undoubtedly would. Before she could speak, the President beat her to it.

     

                “Your cousin? Who’s your cousin?”

     

                “Kal-El. He should’ve been here, should’ve landed on Earth shortly before me. They told me he was dead. I want to know how. I want to know what happened to my only living family, my baby cousin. What they did to him, who did it to him, who was capable of killing a little baby.”

     

                Looking a little grey at the brimming fury in the alien’s voice, Brayden’s response was shaky as she curled her hands into fists to stop them from shaking. “I’m unfamiliar with your cousin but … I will do everything within my power to find out that information for you. There should be … records. I’ll have the DEO archives scoured for any mention of him.”

     

                “Thank you,” Kara tightly replied, climbing to her feet. “That’s all.”

     

                Relief made them all weak as the tension let up somewhat, and Lena hurriedly climbed to her feet, rounding the coffee table to take Kara’s hand, giving it a tight squeeze. The squeeze she received in return was almost hard enough to be painful, and she knew it would have taken an excessive amount of self-control from Kara. 

     

                “Good. I’m glad we could come to an agreement. My staff will ready the necessary documents, and we’ll need new NDAs-”

     

                “I’ll give you your public apology,” Lena cut her off, her stare hard and words full of contempt. “But we’re not signing a damn thing.”

     

                “But-”

     

                “As my mother mentioned, if my silence could be bought, it would have happened long ago. I won’t give up my leverage, and if you expect me to then you don’t know who you’re dealing with. But rest assured, as long as your end of the bargain is upheld, I’ll keep my mouth shut.”

     

                “I’m afraid that’s not good enough.”

     

                “Well, I’m afraid that’s all you’ll get. Take it or leave it. Now, we have places to be so, if you don’t mind, we’ll take our leave and the information we came here to get,” Lena haughty replied, her eyes glancing to her mother. 

     

                Lillian’s lips twitched with a smile, and Lena thought she read a hint of pride in it, shrugging nonchalantly. “I’ll have my driver take you there. The three of them are being held in the same place now.”

     

                “Thank you.

     

                Turning her attention back to the President, Lena gave her a curt nod, her expression smoothing out to one of blank indifference. “You have our terms and the promise of our silence; if you’re happy to agree, you know how to reach me.”

     

                Without another word, still clinging to Kara’s hand, Lena turned and started towing her friend to the door. They were escorted out by silent men in dark suits and Lena could feel her palms getting clammy as her heart pounded, wondering with every stop if they were about to be stopped. But they walked out of there free and were soon being picked up by Lillian’s driver, silent as they sat pressed up against each other in the back seat, their hands still entwined, both of them tense and brooding.

     

                They arrived at the prison where the three women were being held, awaiting trial, and as much as Lena didn’t want to go in and see them, she wanted to be parted from Kara even less. She couldn’t bring herself to wait in the sterile, corporate waiting room on a cheap folding chair so she endured the security checkpoint as her things were pawed through and kept for the time being, her clothes being checked and a metal detector walked through, sticking close to Kara as her stomach plummeted at the unease of familiarity. She didn’t like how much it made her skin prickle and clam up, how they all seemed the same, no matter what prison it was, reminding her of the months locked away. 

     

                Directed to an open space with scattered tables and chairs, they picked a table and took a seat. The air had that air-conditioned stale chill and the floors were stained linoleum, laminated infographics on the walls and the windows of the doors and walls reinforced with a metal grille. Kara was jittery beside her and Lena placed a hand on her knee to try to comfort her. 

     

                It was a long eight minutes of waiting before the sound of footsteps and jingling equipment of the guards reached their ears. Kara had gone white, leaning forward in anticipation as she heard Alex’s heartbeat approach, and Lena watched as the door opened. It had been a few months since she’d last seen the ex-guard, looking scared as she put on a brave face to sneak out and hand herself in, and Lena had to admit that she looked better than the last time they’d been face-to-face.

     

                Dressed in beige prison clothes, her hair longer, cheeks fuller with a faint tan from her mandated outdoor time, Alex was led into the room, her shoulders sagging as her wary expression went slack. Kara was on her feet and moving quickly, wrapping her friend up in a tight hug as she almost bowled Alex over.

     

                “No touching,” a bored guard stated.

     

                Kara held on a moment longer before she let go, her eyes wet as she tearfully laughed, holding onto Alex’s arms. They separated as Kara gave her a wavering smile, stepping back. 

     

                “Kara,” Alex said with quiet amazement. “You’re free.”

     

                “I am,” Kara laughed. “We made it.”

    Chapter 29

                They stayed for hours at the prison, their time uninterrupted as Kara beamed through her tears, animatedly talking with Alex as Lena removed herself to a table in the corner, where she could be comforted by the sight of her but didn’t have to involve herself in the conversation. Aside from a cordial nod and mutual gratitude, she and Alex had nothing to say to each other. The same could be said for Eliza and Kelly when they were cluelessly walked from their cells to the communal space, repeating everything a second and third time, until Kara’s face was blotchy and her eyes bloodshot.

     

                Eventually, they had to leave and Lena rose from her plastic chair and held a hand out to Kara, who rose from her seat, making promises to visit again soon, before she slipped her hand into Lena’s. Expression coolly indifferent, Lena nodded to Kelly in parting and squeezed Kara’s hand reassuringly as the guards came to take Kelly back to her cell. Tugging on her hand, Lena towed Kara towards the exit and reversed the trip they’d made, collecting her things and stepping outside. A car waited for them but Lena paused to wrap Kara in a hug, holding her tightly as she rubbed her back.

     

                “It’ll be okay. They’re being looked after.”

     

                Nodding as she pulled back, fingers wiping at damp eyes, Kara sniffed and cleared her throat. “Thank you. For making it happen, for coming with me.”

     

                Mouth thinning at the corners, Lena nodded as she gave Kara an aching look, her arms cupping the backs of her arms. She leaned in and kissed her cheek, touching her forehead to Kara’s temple for a brief moment before stepping away and turning to the driver, who was holding the door open.

     

                Ushering Kara inside first, Lena slid in after her and buckled her seatbelt, sitting as close to her friend as she could get, coaxing Kara’s head onto her shoulder as the driver climbed into the front and started the engine. Letting out a long, soft sigh, Lena was too tired to think about anything else for the rest of the day, itching for a drink and a bath, wishing she was at home but willing to compromise for what the hotel offered on account of helping Kara. She still hadn’t heard back from her mother, although a few hours was too soon to expect negotiations to have been agreed upon, and she rechecked her phone as the car moved into traffic.

     

                Back at the hotel, she turned the lock and kicked off her heels, shedding her coat and leaving a trail of belongings in her wake. Making for the mini-fridge, with its small supply of liquor, Lena twisted the caps off them one by one and drained them in quick succession. The alcohol hit her empty stomach and she willed it to work quickly, to blunt the frustration and anger that seethed inside her. She could feel Kara’s eyes on her and as she lowered the little bottle of tequila, empty as the taste of it stuck to the back of her throat, she met her gaze.

     

                “I wish this worked for you too,” Lena said, a faint smile twitching the corner of her mouth, her voice gravelly and uneven. “I’m sure you could use a drink more than any of us.”

     

                Shrugging as she smiled slightly, toying with her hands, Kara stepped forward. “I wouldn’t know what it feels like to be drunk so I’m not sure if I’d want it or not.”

     

                “You would. Trust me, you would if you knew how it would … make the pain softer.”

     

                “I don’t feel pain.”

     

                Lena gave her a sceptical look, raking a hand through her hair and cocking her head to the side. “What do you feel?”

     

                “I don’t know. Nothing. It all just feels … numb. I wish things weren’t the way they are but … once they’re not, I think I’ll be okay. I’m just … lost.”

     

                Expression crumpling with pain and an ache for her friend, palpable in her chest, Lena’s shoulders sagged. “Kara-”

     

                “I’m not like you, Lena,” she quickly cut her off. “I was born knowing things, I was born to be as genetically perfect as possible, I- my life hasn’t turned out perfectly - far from it - but I … I don’t feel broken.”

     

                Crossing the space between them, Lena grabbed fistfuls of the jacket Kara was wearing, looking at her with confusion and no small amount of desperation. “You are like me. You’re the only one who- who understands. You’re just- you got used to it and you grew to love them and you forgot what it’s like-”

     

                “I haven’t forgotten a thing.”

     

                Fingers brushing over her cheeks, her shoulders and neck, Lena felt the tightness in her throat as her eyes stung with bitter tears. “You shouldn’t have to remember all of that. The things they did to you- it-”

     

                Cutting off, Lena gritted her teeth as she tipped her head back. Breathing shallowly for a moment, her chest rose and fell quickly. “It’s not right . You should be … angry. You should want to tear the whole world apart. Don’t you feel … anything?”

     

                Cupping Lena’s face in her hands, Kara grimaced, her soft expression resigned. “Yes. I feel relieved and I feel scared. And I feel love. That’s enough for me because … if I let myself feel more than that … I think I’d do exactly what you said.”

     

                “Then be angry. You’re allowed to be. Tear this whole suite apart - I’ll pay the damages.”

     

                Kara pressed her lips to Lena’s in a hard kiss, holding her tightly. After a moment, she pulled back, breathing quickly, while Lena similarly reacted. “I don’t want to be angry. I don’t want to dwell on the- the things that were done. What I want is … you. I just want the good things now.”

     

                Despite her previous reservations, Lena kissed her back. The alcohol was getting to her now, blurring the lines between reason and desire, knowing that she did want Kara, on so many levels, and it would soothe the pain, even just a little, to give in to that. It wouldn’t be right or fair to use her, especially knowing it was something new for Kara, but Lena kissed her back and felt Kara’s arms wrap around her, a hand in her hair, fingers splayed over her spine. 

     

                Feeling a little unsteady as the liquor smoothed over the frustration, making Lena’s mind go blank as she basked in the peace of Kara’s touch, she could feel the frantic edge to the way they held each other. It was an effort to pull herself back, stammering with pink cheeks and glassy eyes, her lips already swelling slightly and her heart hammering, but she did manage it. She managed to not fuck up this one thing.

     

                “I’m sorry, we can’t-”

     

                “It’s okay,” Kara whispered, reaching for her, fingers sliding over Lena’s skin as she drank in the sight of her, her eyes plainly needy.

     

                Eyelids closing as she leaned into her palm, Lena reached up to cover Kara’s hand with her own, her voice shaking as she whispered, “no, no, it’s not, it’s- it would be for all the wrong reasons. I don’t want to have sex with you because I’m angry; I would want to do it the right way.”

     

                “Oh. Okay. I’m sorry-”

     

                “No,” Lena quickly reassured her, stepping in closer and taking Kara’s face in her hands. She couldn’t stop herself from leaning in to kiss her, soft and lingering, three presses of her lips to hers. “No, don’t- I don’t want to … use you. I care about you, I just- I can’t use you to fix me. It’s not fair.”

     

                “I wouldn’t mind,” Kara softly admitted.

     

                It broke something in Lena’s chest to hear that, to know that Kara wouldn’t care how badly she was used, how often she’d been mistreated in prison, that it was something she’d grown accustomed to. A soft cry escaped Lena’s lips as her throat tightened around it and then tears were spilling down her cheeks as she came apart. 

     

                Kara’s arms came around her and Lena buried her face into her shoulder as she quietly sobbed, angry and hurt and not nearly drunk enough to blunt it fully. It only left her more vulnerable, more confused and unable to manage it all well enough to keep it from spilling out. Lena barely felt it as Kara lifted her ever so slightly and whisked her into the bedroom, putting her down on the bed with carefully controlled movements and softly shushing her as she tried to encourage her to take deep breaths, the same way Eliza had used to coach her through various meltdowns in the early days of prison.

     

                Head between her knees, dark hair cascading towards the floor, Lena pushed the heels of her palms into her eyes as she tried to even out her breathing. Kara rubbed her back and knelt on the carpeted floor in front of her, hand on her knee, taking her cold hands in her warm ones, and brushing her dark hair back. It made her heart beat quickly with panic to watch Lena cry, nervously hovering around her, unsure how to comfort her or how to make things right.

     

                “It’s alright, it’s okay,” Kara murmured to her. “I know it’s a lot but it’s all going to work out and then you and I … we’re going to go somewhere where we can do whatever you want to do. Because I don’t mind what we do, as long as I’m with you.”

     

                “I just … want it to be over,” Lena whispered, voice hitching as she raised her head slightly. “How are we out and … nothing is fixed?”

     

                “It almost is, I promise.”

     

                Cheeks flushing with anger, Lena’s voice was hoarse as she sat up, eyes wet and face furrowed into a scowl. “We shouldn’t have to fix it. This isn’t our mess to fix. I never wanted any of this; I just wanted to go home.”

     

                Wincing, Kara smoothed her hands over Lena’s shoulders. “Okay, okay, I’ll take you home.”

     

                “No,” Lena roughly replied.

     

                “What can I do? Tell me what you want me to do, please.”

     

                Lena drew in a shuddering breath, wiping her face with her hands as Kara’s pleas knifed through her. “I don’t know,” she listlessly replied. “There’s nothing to do, I just- I’m fed up. And I’m angry- I’m angry at my mom. She was supposed to help me but she just- she did it again, the same thing she always does, and I’m so sick of it. Why do my family’s mistakes always fall back onto me to fix?”

     

                “You don’t have to fix anything. I’ll- I’ll fly you to wherever you want to be. You can be done with it all.”

     

                Scowling, her cheeks blotchy as her mouth twisted with annoyance, Lena wiped away an errant tear. “And you won’t come with me. You won’t give up; you wouldn’t even leave them there to start with.”

     

                Mouth opening and closing, Kara meekly withdrew, sitting back on her haunches. “I’m sorry.”

     

                “I don’t want you to be sorry.”

     

                After a moment of silence, Lena felt her cheeks warm as her biting anger was directed at the wrong person, she rubbed her face and climbed to her feet, a little unsteady but not nearly as drunk as she wished to be. Kara was still crouching and tipped her head to look up at her with open concern.

     

                “Sorry,” Lena rasped. “I think- I’m going to … take a bath.”

     

                Nodding, Kara silently rose to her feet and let her hand brush against Lena’s arm as her friend brushed past her. Throat tight, Lena made her way into the bathroom and quietly shut the door behind herself before resting her forehead against it momentarily, letting out a weary sigh. After a second, she turned to the bath and started filling it with hot water, using the body wash to make it foam with bubbles, and stripped off her clothes.

     

                She felt cold and tense and the water was too hot but she stepped in anyway, sinking down as she let the tub continue to fill as the taps poured over her stomach and the water level rose. The heat of the bath fogged up the bathroom and turned her skin pink as she brooded, her expression mournful and stony. It warmed her though and she blinked back tears as she lingered until the water started to cool, before removing the plug and filling it again with more hot water.

     

                Kara knocked on the door after she turned the taps off again, hesitating only a few seconds before she opened the unlocked door and invited herself inside. Closing the door, Kara gave Lena an appraising look of concern, her shoulders sloped with weariness. Crossing over to the bath, Kara sank to a crouch at the side of it and gave Lena an aching look that softened her face.

     

                “How’re you feeling?”

     

                “Fine,” Lena mumbled, her mouth barely above the water.

     

                “Here, let me wash your hair.”

     

                Lena didn’t bother objecting, just closed her eyes as she sat up a little straighter, drawing her knees to her chest and wrapping her arms around them. Her dark hair stuck to her wet back and she closed her eyes, listening to Kara’s movements. The gentle touch of her fingers in her hair made some of the tension bleed out of Lena and she bowed her head, brow resting on her folded arms, and let Kara lather up the shampoo.

     

                Slipping beneath the water, she rinsed the suds herself and then resurfaced, sluicing water down her face and leaning against the rim of the tub. Sighing heavily, she let her head loll to the side and gave Kara a grim smile. Reaching up, she stroked wet fingers over her chin.

     

                “I’m sorry for snapping at you.”

     

                Kara encircled her fingers with her own and squeezed gently, pressing a kiss to Lena’s palm. “It’s alright. You’re overwhelmed and it’s- nothing feels like it’s going right, except for the two of us being free.”

     

                Nodding, Lena swallowed thickly, tipping her head back against the rim as she closed her eyes, the steamy air caressing her cheeks. After a moment, she roused herself enough to quickly condition and wash her pink skin before pulling the plug and standing. Water streamed off her and she wrapped herself in a towel. Kara vanished into the bedroom and brought back pyjamas for her from Lena’s duffel, and she gave her a crooked smile.

     

                “I ordered food.”

     

                “You ordered food?”

     

                “Mhm. On the phone,” Kara said, pleased with herself. “They said they only had double cheeseburgers but I don’t know what else you like - except steak, but when I asked for steak they kept saying beef tenderloin and I didn’t know if that was the same sort of cow. I’m not sure how many types of cows there are-” 

     

                Swallowing a laugh, Lena’s bleak expression softened with amusement as her mouth twitched with a smile. “Any meat that comes from a cow is beef. They’re all the same cows, it just depends on which part it’s from.”

     

                “Oh. The tenderloin is a different muscle?”

     

                “Yes, below the ribs, like this,” Lena tried to explain with her waist. “Thank you.”

     

                Nodding, Kara hovered with uncertainty and then turned to give Lena some privacy. She dried off and dressed in her pyjamas, the sound of a knock at the suite’s door making her slow as she folded her worn clothes away, an uptick in her pulse as she listened. It was only room service but Lena couldn’t shake the feeling of being hunted down, still so wrapped up in the months on the run, or the months of listening to the thump of heavy boots as she expected another beating from a guard. But no, it was just their room service that Kara had ordered for her, trying to look after Lena the way Lena had looked after her.

     

                Still, she waited for the front door to close before she stepped out of the bedroom, her hair damp around her shoulders and some colour in her cheeks from the heat of the bath. She looked softer and younger, not quite so hard and angry after shedding some of it with her crying jag and lurking in the hot water for a while. It didn’t particularly make her feel any better but at least she’d spent some of her building frustration.

     

                Their dinner was spread over the dining table and Kara was neatly arranging the collection of plates, looking up with a quick smile on her lips before she sat at the table, crossing her legs on the chair and picking up a milkshake. She took a sip and hummed appreciatively and Lena smiled faintly as she took the adjoining seat at the head of the table. Removing the pickles from her own burger, she picked up a couple of fries and listlessly took a bite. She was surprised that she actually was hungry, the alcohol kindling it in her stomach, and she ate slowly with mouthfuls of the Coke Kara had ordered for her. After polishing off one double cheeseburger and a serving of fries, exchanging the plates, Kara cleared her throat.

     

                “So … while you were in the bath … I also used the phone to make another call.”

     

                Lena set down her burger, her eyebrows rising slightly in an expectant look. She chewed quickly and swallowed, wiping her hands on the napkin. “Oh. Who’d you call?”

     

                “Your mother.”

     

                “My mother?”

     

                “Yes. I memorised her number, so, um … well, I wanted to help work out the deal.”

     

                Blood running cold, Lena straightened in her seat, her whole body stiffening. “What did you do?”

     

                “It’s okay, I just- they’re worried about what happens if they let them all out and they start attacking people. Well, I don’t want any humans to die either, and … I’m the strongest alien in the world, right? And I’m the one that wants them to be freed, so if anything happens … I should be the one to stop them.”

     

                “Kara, you’re not a hero. That’s not for you to do. I mean … what if you get hurt?”

     

                “That’s pretty hard to do without kryptonite.”

     

                “Yes, but … why would you offer to do that?”

     

                “It seemed the best thing to offer them. That way they don’t have to worry about stopping anyone, because I’ll be able to do that.”

     

                Scrubbing her hands over her face, Lena let out a low sound of frustration. After a moment, she dropped her hands and gave Kara an exasperated look. “What did she say?”

     

                “She said she’d pass that along to President Brayden, but she didn’t see how that benefited her.”

     

                “And what did you say?”

     

                Anxiously chewing on her lip, Kara kept her eyes on her food as she shrugged her shoulders. “That maybe I could offer something that benefited her too.”

     

                Biting back another groan, Lena squeezed her eyes shut as she clenched her teeth. “Like what?”

     

                “My body.”

     

                “What?”

     

                “I’ll give her my body if I die. So she can study and experiment on it. You know, for research.”

     

                Rubbing her forehead, Lena sighed as she thought for a moment. “Okay, that’s- that’s fine, I’ll call her and tell her no-”

     

                “No, you won’t,” Kara softly told her.

     

                Expression aghast, Lena gave her an incredulous look. “Kara. I’m not letting you-”

     

                “You said I’m free now, which means I’m free to make my own decisions. Well, I have decided. I decided this by myself - no one talked me into it, and no one can talk me out of it. I want to help people - aliens and humans - and make it so we can coexist together in peace so I will do whatever I can to make that happen. And you know, on Krypton we send our dead out to deep space in a pod, kind of like the one I was sent here on. My dad … he was a part of the Science Guild, and I was going to follow in his footsteps. It would’ve made me the youngest member of the Science Guild in history. But I didn’t, I came here instead and had to learn Earth science in a prison, so … I don’t think it’s a bad thing to donate my corpse to science. I think I like the sound of that more than being sent back out into space again, alone.”

     

                Floundering for a moment, feeling chastened, Lena blinked in surprise as she sat back. “Oh. Well, alright then. If that’s your decision.”

     

                “It is,” Kara firmly replied.

     

                Nodding, still grim-faced but accepting of her friend's wishes, Lena took a sip of Coke and cleared her throat. “Well, I guess we’ll just wait for them to get back to us.”

     

                They finished eating in mostly silence and then Lena called to order coffee and cake sent up to the room, the remainder of their evening spent on the sofa, watching Gilmore Girls together while she picked at her cake and gave the rest to Kara. Having an early night, so spent from the flight, the meeting at the White House and then the trip to the prison, Lena crawled into bed and her body sagged against the soft mattress. 

     

                Kara slipped in beside her, the bed wide enough for them both to not touch but she inched closer anyway. Her arms wrapped Lena in her warm embrace and her face pressed into the back of her neck as her face furrowed with the determined look of someone trying to impress as much of her love onto her friend as possible. Wrapped up in her arms, back to Kara’s chest, Lena could have fallen asleep instantly. 

     

                Her mind was too alert though, even the softened edge of liquor worn away after so many hours, and as Kara fell asleep, the weight of her arm across Lena’s waist growing heavy, she couldn’t find escape in the same. Laying still so she didn’t wake her friend, Lena saw both sides of midnight before she dozed off into a restless sleep of dark dreams, replaying memories of prison as her mind twisted them into even worse nightmares than their origin. 

     

                Waking to the dimness of the pre-dawn morning, she looked over at Kara, sleeping peacefully on her back, and then slipped out of bed. Padding out into the living room, she paced for a few minutes before fetching her phone. It was just past six o’clock and she knew her mother rose early so didn’t hesitate at the thought of it being too early to call her before she called her number. 

     

                “I’m surprised it took you this long to call.”

     

                “It’s not to try and undo the little deal she cut with you, if that’s what you think,” Lena scoffed, her hackles already rising.

     

                “Then I’m doubly surprised.”

     

                “Do we have an agreement then, with what she offered?”

     

                “I’m not sure yet. We’ll have to wait for President Brayden’s response.”

     

                Lena gritted her teeth with frustration. “I don’t have time to sit around waiting at her leisure.”

     

                “You’re still angry.”

     

                “Of course I’m still angry.”

     

                “At me,” her mother deduced.

     

                Throat closing up, Lena faltered for a moment and her voice was uneven when she managed to force out a response. “Yes. Yes, I’m angry at you. You were supposed to help, but you just- you did what you always do and I was too stupid to see it this time.”

     

                “You need help, Lena. I tried to spare you from all of this; if only you’d stayed out of it.”

     

                Tears stung her eyes and she swallowed thickly. “You had the chance to help me, to make this easier for me, but instead you made it so you benefited from it. And now you want to pretend like it was all for my best interests that you kept me out of it. It was never about you caring for me; I bet the second you got that phone call from me at the black site, you leapt at the opportunity to see what you could get from it.”

     

                “I’m tired of rehashing this argument over and over. I never pretended there was nothing in it for me, but it was merely a byproduct of helping you. If I could get a cut of the pie while carrying out your wishes, why not take it? As it is, I wish I’d never picked up that call at all. Any goodwill it earned me has gone down the drain now, so what was the point in it all? Clearly, your freedom isn’t worth as much to you as it was to me.”

     

                Rolling her eyes at her mother’s faux-wounded words, Lena’s lips twitched with a bitter smile. “Fine, if you say so. But if that wasn’t your intention, why are you going against me now?”

     

                “It’s business, and any good businesswoman needs to know when to cut their losses or when a risk looks like it’ll pay off. Unfortunately, what you want is a risk that doesn’t look like it’ll pay off, so I’m cutting my losses. So should you.”

     

                “This isn’t business, mom. This is family. And you’re all I have left of it; doesn’t that earn me some loyalty? Some trust?”

     

                “Is that what you want from me? Loyalty, trust?”

     

                “I guess even that’s asking for too much. Never mind. I was only calling to see if you’d received a response but you haven’t, so … that’s all there is. Call me once you hear.”

     

                Hanging up, she sank onto the sofa and sighed heavily, a brooding look on her face as she ran a hand over it. She briefly closed her eyes and when she opened them again she found Kara standing in the doorway of the bedroom, rubbing her tired eyes. Brooding expression softening to a smile, Lena held her arms open and Kara plodded over to her, collapsing beside her and wrapping her in a warm hug as Lena pressed her face into the crook of her neck.

     

                “Everything is shit,” she grumbled.

     

                “It’s still not a no.”

     

                She should have known Kara would be eavesdropping in some capacity but Lena still felt defeated, despite her optimism. Pulling back, she gave her a droll look and curled her legs up beneath her. 

     

                “Breakfast?”

     

                “Sure.”

     

                Ordering room service, they both showered as they waited and dressed in preparation for visiting the jail again, Lena knowing that Kara would want to see as much of her friends as she could. She picked at her eggs but made herself eat, knowing she’d been eating too little over the last few days, and drank two cups of coffee before scooting her chair back and going to finish getting ready. 

     

                Ordering an Uber, she waited until they were only a block away before heading downstairs, a large pair of sunglasses hiding most of her face, and quickly got into the back of the car, the driver setting off towards the address she’d found on Maps the day before, while they’d still been at the detention centre. Preoccupied with her thoughts, she had little time to dwell on visiting the people she’d thought she’d be rid of a lot sooner, and was quiet as they were ushered through the security checks inside the centre before Alex was brought out again first.

     

                They were allowed coffee this time - their cups white, Alex’s brown - and Lena sat at her own table in the corner, milling things over as she tuned out the conversation until her name was called out. Blinking as she came back to the present, her head turned to the two women and she saw Kara half-twisted on her chair, eyebrows raised.

     

                “Lena?”

     

                “Hm?”

     

                “We were just talking about your mom. Alex has an opinion.”

     

                “Does she?” Lena derisively replied, her eyes flitting over the prisoner.

     

                Giving her a weak smile, Kara pulled the chair out next to her and patted the seat. “Come sit.”

     

                Helpless to her friend’s earnest optimism, Lena bit back a sigh and rose to her feet with her cup of coffee. It was lukewarm now and bitterly cheap but she took a sip and slowly wove through the other tables and chairs to take the seat beside Kara.

     

                “What’s your opinion, then?”

     

                “You’re wasting your time,” Alex softly said as she fixed Lena with a firm stare. “This deal … it’s pointless. We all know it.”

     

                “That’s the only way.”

     

                “No, it’s not. You have a freed Kryptonian sitting right next to you-“

     

                “No.”

     

                “Kara,” Alex sighed, her attention moving from Lena to fix Kara with an exasperated look. “Do everyone a favour and tear down the doors and let everyone out. Let them loose and disappear.”

     

                “I can’t do that,” Kara whispered, sitting rigidly in her chair.

     

                “Yes, you can. If anyone can, it’s you.”

     

                “I can’t. Lena could get hurt. And what about you? What about Eliza and Kelly? I won’t be able to visit, I-“

     

                Leaning forward, Alex covered Kara’s hands with her own and gave her a wavering smile. “I know, and I’ll miss you, but I’ll be okay. They won’t be okay without your help. At best they’ll end up in another jail, maybe with fewer restrictions, but that’s not what you want for them, is it?”

     

                “No,” Kara whispered, her eyes brimming with tears as she gripped her sister’s hands tightly. “No, but … I can free you too. We can all-“

     

                “No. No, I’m fine. I’ll be okay. It’s- look, we all knew I’d do some time. And my mom and Kelly too. We helped do things that … whether we had a choice or not, we all knew it was wrong, so … don’t worry about us. You help people who need it, okay? You got everyone out of one prison so this one should be a piece of cake, right?”

     

                Wiping her cheeks, Kara nodded, her chin dimpling with how torn she was. Lena was wooden beside her, her heart beating quickly at the panic of how much danger they’d be putting themselves in again. She didn’t want to be a fugitive again, she wanted to be somewhere safe and warm without the fear of being caught hounding their every footstep.

     

                “It’s alright,” Lena murmured as she stroked Kara’s arm, swallowing thickly as her stomach sank. 

     

                She could already feel Kara swaying towards Alex’s insistent words, making her believe that was the easiest way. And Lena knew that she was right - that would be the easiest way. But only the easiest way to free them. The ramifications once they were free would be more than she was willing to bargain. There would be arrest warrants, this time with probable cause, and she'd have no access to her money or any hope of one day going back to work. It would uproot Lena’s life entirely.

     

                But then hadn’t it already been entirely uprooted? Hadn’t she already confessed to having no desire to return to work? Hadn’t she already made a contingency plan to head overseas somewhere, to live out life in a quiet place where they would be able to fly beneath the radar? She had fake IDs and passports, she had overseas bank accounts linked to shell companies and houses in the names of her fake identities, so it was all possible. Lena just needed to decide to commit to giving up being Lena Luthor. After all the misfortune her family had brought her, was that really so difficult?

     

                She needed time away somewhere, to think and heal and live slowly, without the pressure of the media or her job. As much as Lena thrived off of research and manufacturing new things, she had gone so long without it and felt no motivation to jump back into it yet. It wouldn’t be as if she was giving up much, not when she hadn’t recovered so much of herself and her life yet. It would be choosing a new path instead of trying to slot back into her past as if none of it had happened.

     

                Wrapped up in her thoughts, she rubbed her forehead and felt her heart pound in her chest. After a moment, she lurched to her feet, the chair skittering backwards, and swallowed thickly. “We should go.”

     

                “I- but … we haven’t talked to Eliza or Kelly yet,” Kara said, her expression surprised and pleading as she looked up at Lena, Alex’s hands still in hers.

     

                Waving a hand dismissively at her, feeling clammy and agitated, Lena couldn’t look at her, or at Alex. “You stay. I need … I need fresh air.”

     

                What she really needed was the guarantee that it would all be okay, that if she did what Alex said and had Kara free everyone, they’d be okay. Lena didn’t give a shit about seeing any of them again, although she knew that would be hard on Kara, but it was still a lot to give up in other areas. Stalking out of the room with the guard escorting her, she rubbed her eyes and tried to stifle the frustration rising in her chest. She was so tired and felt so helpless.
