Wouldn’t it be easier to put a stop to it once and for all? They could free them all and leave them to their own devices, and wasn’t that what they’d been partitioning for anyway? If they got caught, then oh well, but at least if they had the opportunity to run and be free, it would be better than nothing.

     

                And this way Lena would owe no one and wouldn’t be reliant on any government to uphold a deal. A deal that would be made under the table and easily deniable if President Brayden was ever made to acknowledge it. Softly hissing through her teeth as she cursed the woman and the institution, she paced in the lobby and then took a seat on a chair, closing her eyes and thinking as she tried to scramble a plan together. For what eventuality, she wasn’t sure yet.

     

                She waited in the reception area for two hours as Kara talked to Eliza and Kelly before she was escorted back out to Lena. Pale-faced and quiet, she crossed over to Lena, who climbed to her feet and reached for her phone to order an Uber, and they lingered inside for fifteen minutes until the car pulled up outside before piling into the back of it. It was a silent ride back to their hotel.

     

                Once safely locked back inside their suite, they still didn’t say anything, an unfamiliar sort of tension stretching out between them as Lena slowly undressed in the bedroom and changed into something more comfortable, while Kara hovered in the doorway with uncertainty. Ordering a bottle of wine and some food up to the room, Lena sat at the table and drank three glasses in succession while Kara ate three meals, including Lena’s one that remained untouched, and the day wore on.

     

                Eventually, Lena had to ask. Clearing her throat, she sat curled up on the sofa as she ran her finger around the rim of her glass, a distant, brooding look in her eyes as she avoided looking at Kara.

     

                “Kara?” she murmured. “About what Alex said … is that what you want to do?”

     

                Looking away from the TV, Kara stared at her for a moment before pausing her episode. Sitting forward on the sofa, she nervously ran her palms over her thighs.

     

                “I don’t know. I think … if things were different, then yes, I would but …”

     

                “If what was different?”

     

                Wincing slightly, Kara looked down at her lap. “Alex told me they’d be fine in prison, that it’s where they need to be, and Eliza and Kelly said pretty similar things when I told them what Alex said. So they’d all be fine if I- if I broke everyone else out and couldn’t visit them. I’d miss them so bad , I really would, but I think I would be okay with that but … I wouldn’t be okay with leaving you. I think I’d be so alone without you too and I made a promise that we’d stick together and I don’t want to leave you all by yourself.”

     

                Lena’s face crumpled with an agonised ache as she exhaled softly. Hesitating, she reached across the gap between them and covered Kara’s hand with her own, a lump forming in her throat.

     

                “But … I’d come with you.”

     

                Looking up as surprise flashed across her face, Kara’s blue eyes were grave as she stared at Lena. It took her a moment to reply. “I couldn’t ask you to do that.”

     

                “You’re not.”

     

                “But I- it would be putting you at risk, putting a target on you again and … you just got your life back. I can’t let you give all of that up.”

     

                Letting out a small laugh, Lena felt her heart twinge with longing for what was lost. “Truthfully, Kara, I haven’t gotten my life back. This is- this is not what my life was like. And I can’t go back, as much as I wish I could, and … I hate the way things are but it’s just- it’s different and it’s not going to feel the same, even if I did exactly the same things I used to every day. So, I know I said you couldn’t do this because it was too dangerous, but if- if you wanted to you could break them all out and I’d come with you. We could go anywhere.”

     

                “Really?”

     

                Pausing for only a split second, Lena firmly nodded. “It would be the right thing to do.”

     

                “You don’t always have to do the right thing. Sometimes … you can just do what you want to do.”

     

                Sighing, Lena raked a hand through her hair and nodded. “Okay, it’s not what I want to do, it’s- I just think that we have to do it. My life feels like it’s at a standstill right now, and nothing’s going to give and nothing feels right and I’d rather do what’s right and figure out something new with you than stick my head in the sand and live with this- this anger that I can’t do anything about without pissing off some very powerful people. I’m walking on eggshells and it doesn’t feel good, so why not blow it all up and start fresh?”

     

                “I- well, it’s very risky,” Kara cautiously replied, wariness in her eyes.

     

                “It is,” Lena conceded. “And it’ll take a bit of planning. A few days, at least. Rushing would only make it easier for us to get caught in our escape, leaving a more obvious trail for them to follow. I just- if- if we do this … I need you to promise me that you’ll come with me this time. No more staying behind or being the hero. I don’t want a hero; I just want you.”

     

                “Think about it for a few days. If you want to free them and run, we’ll free them and run. If you want to stay and make it a public spectacle, we’ll stay and make it a public spectacle. Either way, we’ll be together, I promise.”

     

                “Okay. Okay, Kara, I’ll think about it. But you think about it too. I’m not the only one who’ll be giving up something.”

     

                “But I won’t be giving up a life.”

     

                “Just a family.”

     

                “I did that before and survived it. And at least this time I’ll see them again someday, I’m sure of that. It’s easier to bear it when I have that to hold onto.”

     

                “Just think about it anyway, okay?”

     

                Giving Lena’s hand a quick squeeze, Kara gave her a quick smile. “Sure, I’ll think about it. But either way, it’s you and me, right? That’s what we always said would happen when we were out, that we’d stick together. Regardless of what we decide, I’m not losing you too.”

     

                “You and me,” Lena murmured, a longing ache in her voice as she gave Kara a yearning look, worried that for all their talk of togetherness, it would all go awry once more. “I won’t leave you behind this time, and you can’t make me go without you.”

     

                “The only thing that could take me away from you now is death itself.”

     

                “Don’t say that. I’m scared to lose you; I don’t know what I’d do with myself anymore. I’ve relied on you for so long.”

     

                “No, you’ve relied on yourself. From the moment they brought you to the prison, you fought for your freedom, you believed in yourself. You have yourself, no matter what.”

     

                “Maybe, but you know what? None of that was worth a damn without you there to help me.”

     

                “It was. We wouldn’t be sitting here right now if you hadn’t been so persistent. If there’s one thing I know, you will always do what needs to be done. For yourself and others. So … regardless of what happens next, believe in yourself and believe in me. What we’ve done is already a testament to what a Luthor and a Kryptonian can do together - imagine what else we could do if we believed we could. We could free them all, we could change the world. ”

                

                “I used to want to change the world, but not anymore. Now, I just want a quiet life.”

     

                “But doesn’t that shred of good we can do make it all … I don’t know, at least a little bit worth it?”

     

                Face oddly blank, Lena swallowed thickly as she stared ahead, her stomach sinking. “No. No, I don’t think anything in the world was worth all of that. Except maybe you. You’re the only good to come out of what happened, and even then … I wish so badly you had never come to Earth. You’d have been better off on any other planet, you’d have been better off drifting through space for a thousand years, unconscious but left alone.”

     

                “But then I wouldn’t have met you.”

     

                “I could live with that.”

     

                Kara gave her a weak smile. “I couldn’t. I would pick Earth every time, knowing every ounce of pain it would cost me, if I got to meet you. Over and over again. I love you, Lena, and I know you don’t think it’s right, or … I don’t know, you don’t believe me anyway, but I do. I love you as much as I’ve ever loved anyone, so even if you don’t love me back, I’ll always be your friend.”

     

                Groaning softly, Lena shifted closer to cup Kara’s face in her hands. “God, you beautiful idiot. Of course I love you back. I have had so little cause for love in my life that I know without a shadow of a doubt that what I feel for you is more than I’ve ever felt for anyone. I just- I wish it was simpler, I really do, because I love you too and that scares me more than anything else ever has. And I don’t think it’s a good thing and I’m sorry for that.”

     

                “How can love ever not be a good thing?”

     

                “I don’t know,” Lena said with a hollow laugh, “but I’m yet to find out how it’s good.”

     

                “Don’t worry, I’ll show you how. If you let me.”

    Chapter 30

                Four days later, Lena’s phone rang with an incoming call from her mother. They’d been online shopping, accumulating a plethora of things they might need to leave at a moment’s notice - sturdy hiking boots, puffy jackets and thick cotton shirts, a first-aid kit and meal rations bundled into backpacks with their fake passports and IDs, all of it bought from Patagonia or Kathmandu - adding to their supplies to ensure they would be able to survive a few days on the run at least, if it came to it. It wouldn’t be so difficult for them with Kara’s abilities; she’d be able to fly to a town and steal supplies before anyone caught her, but Lena didn’t want to run the risk of them being seen if they could avoid it. And that was assuming it would be necessary to run.

     

                Unfortunately, Lena knew her mother and anticipated bad news the moment her phone started ringing. Climbing to her feet and moving away from the sofa, she sighed and answered, pressing it to her ear. Already, she was on the defensive, her stomach clenched with unease.

     

                “Hello?”

     

                “I won’t beat around the bush.”

     

                “Ah.” 

     

                “It’s going to be a no on all fronts, I’m afraid.”

     

                “I thought that might be the case.” Silent for a moment, Lena let out a resigned sigh. “What won’t she bend on?”

     

                “The lack of an NDA. She’d give you everything if you agreed to sign.”

     

                “Yeah, and then I have a gag order on me. There’s too much at stake for me to silence myself.”

     

                “I know. I know you hoped for a different answer, but … well, the risk is too high. And, to make the President’s position on it brief, you’re not a big enough threat to warrant folding to.”

     

                “And Kara?”

     

                “Well … they’d prefer her not to be.”

     

                “Right. Well, I guess they’ll find out.”

     

                “Don’t do anything rash , Lena,” her mother harshly warned her.

     

                “I won’t. Thank you for letting me know.”

     

                It wasn’t rash. They’d been planning for this eventuality, although they hadn’t yet decided to do it. Hanging up the phone, Lena’s mind was made up though. 

     

                Kara had heard it all, sitting on the sofa with Lena’s laptop on her knees, deliberating over which brand of socks they should add to their cart. Glancing over at her, Lena felt guilt shoot through her at failing so miserably to secure a deal with the White House. Not that she’d anticipated much, but she’d hoped they might be lucky enough to gain some ground, and bide their time to build a better case. Instead, they were left with nothing, not even the facts around what had happened to Kara’s baby cousin.

     

                In the wake of the rejection of any deal from the White House, Lena paced in their hotel room as she tried to arrange her thoughts. She hadn’t been that optimistic that it would go in their favour, knowing they didn’t have much to leverage and the public interest already waning after months of this ongoing political drama, so it wasn’t a devastating disappointment to be left with nothing. Especially not when they’d been planning for it anyway, making the necessary arrangements as if it had already been decided. Perhaps it had, a part of her knowing that this was the most likely outcome and planning accordingly.

     

                It was almost an hour of silent pacing before Kara cleared her throat, having heard every word of the phone call. “We should talk about what happens next.”

     

                Nodding, Lena quickly stopped pacing and crossed over to the sofa, sitting beside her and reaching out to take Kara’s hands. She squeezed her fingers quickly, meeting Kara’s eyes as she drew in a deep breath.

     

                “I’ve thought about it some more,” Lena informed her. “I’m all in if you still are.”

     

                “You mean … you want to do it? Go on the run?”

     

                Giving her a faint smile, Lena nodded as her throat tightened. “I think … it’s the best thing for us now. We’ve already got it half-sorted but I’ll need a few days to finalise some arrangements. Um … it should be relatively easy.”

     

                Kara looked softly surprised but relieved, all the same, her eyebrows rising as a smile curled the corners of her mouth. “Really?”

     

                “Mhm. I don’t think either of us will be able to rest until they’re all free, and this is the only way to do it, so let’s do it. There’s no point dragging it out longer. That won’t bring peace to anyone, and I just- I want it to be over. I want to stay somewhere for a while, without worrying about anything.”

     

                “Where will we go?”

     

                Lena gave her a small smile, squeezing her hands again. “I already have a safe house in the northwest of Australia, so I think that would be our best bet to get as far away as possible for a while. Not long-term, but just for a while. It’s remote, which will be good, and it’ll be hot but it’s near the beach too. Then we could maybe go to Ireland, once it all dies down. I have another safe house there too, in the town my mom grew up in.”

     

                Nodding, on board for anything, Kara raised her eyebrows a fraction. “When do we leave?”

     

                “Give me a few days. That’s all I’ll need. And then we just need to figure out how we can break them all out of the prison and get away before we’re caught.”

     

                “That’ll be easy,” Kara assured her. “Brute strength will do it. It didn’t look too difficult to break out of while we were in there. And they won’t be expecting anyone to break in , so maybe it’ll be easier this time.”

     

                Lena felt uneasiness steal over her, mouth a flat line as her brows furrowed together. “Unless that’s exactly what they’re expecting. They could all be armed with kryptonite, for all we know. I don’t want you to get hurt.”

     

                Grinning, Kara draped an arm over the back of the sofa, around Lena’s shoulders. “You underestimate me.”

     

                Fixing her with a level stare, the corners of Lena’s mouth twitched. “No, I don’t underestimate you - I overestimate. I’m … expecting you to sacrifice yourself for them all. I’m scared that you won’t stop, no matter how hurt you are or if you reach your limit. It’s the one thing that makes me want to say no to this whole thing, but instead, I’m just trying to prepare myself to expect the worst.”

     

                She tried to keep the bitterness out of her voice, already grieving the possibility of losing more than just her old life in this jailbreak attempt. But she’d gone along with the plan anyway, getting her affairs in order and purchasing everything they’d need, because she knew it was what Kara wanted to do, and Kara had had little say in her actions until recently. Lena wouldn’t be the one to hold her back, even if she wished things could be different. She just hoped her worst fears wouldn’t become reality.

     

                Kara wanted to convince her of the same, shuffling closer on the sofa with a mild look of panic on her face. She removed her arm from the back of the sofa and reached out to Lena, her hands anxiously fluttering about, touching the back of her hand, her knee, her arm as she tried to reassure her.

     

                “No, I- I won’t do that. I made you a promise that this time I wouldn’t leave you alone. I’ll help them the best that I can but if I get hurt … I’ll leave. I promise .”

     

                Giving her a weak smile, Lena nodded, unconvinced. It wasn’t that she didn’t believe Kara’s intentions, but that could easily change in the moment when confronted by dozens of imprisoned aliens and metahumans she’d been in close quarters with for decades. Perhaps the heroism of rescuing them all would go to her head, her Kryptonian abilities making her think she was more invincible than she was. She would be if they didn’t have green kryptonite on hand, but who was to say they wouldn’t?

     

                “Okay,” Lena whispered.

     

                “Don’t say okay,” Kara said with a strained laugh. “I want you to believe me.”

     

                Lena smiled slightly at the insistent command, rolling her eyes as Kara gave her hand a playful tug. “Okay, I believe you.”

     

                “Say it like you mean it.”

     

                "Or what?”

     

                Kara raised her eyebrows and carefully pulled her closer, a quick flicker of uncertainty on her face as if she expected to yank Lena’s arm out of its socket, before she wrapped her arms around Lena’s waist. She keeled over on the sofa and Lena sprawled on top of her, a surprised laugh escaping her as struggled to extract herself but was held fast. It felt good to laugh, Kara joining in as Lena writhed in her arms and then fell limply on her chest, pink-cheeked and slightly breathless.

     

                “Okay, okay, I mean it, I believe you.”

     

                “You believe me?” Kara murmured, raising her head slightly off the sofa.

     

                “Yeah, I do. In a few days, we’re going to be far away from here, sunbathing in Broome. Well, maybe not sunbathing - it’s their winter right now - but, you know, we’ll be together.”

                

                “Good.”

     

                She let her go, arms unwinding, and Lena pushed herself up slowly, her stomach jolting as she looked down at Kara, their faces a foot apart as she hovered over her. Hesitating, lips parted, Lena felt her pulse pick up and Kara frowned, reaching up to press a hand to the side of Lena’s neck.

     

                “You alright? Your heart just went all funny.”

     

                “I’m fine,” Lena murmured, scooting off Kara’s lap and raking her hair out of her face.

     

                It would have been so easy to cave to what she wanted and kiss Kara, but she didn’t, withholding from crossing that line until they were away somewhere where they could be alone together and get to know who they were outside of prison. Not just together, but individually as well. Lena felt so out of touch with herself that it would be nice to be able to sit for a while and mull things over, see what had changed, reassess her needs in life now. Sitting beside Kara, folding her legs and reaching for the laptop, Lena patted the spot beside her and moved on, resuming their online shopping.

     

                She’d remained sober for the four days it had taken to get a response from her mother, carefully planning, sleeping and eating as much as she could while she could. Kara likewise rested and ate as much as she could and spent a decent amount of time meditating while she softly chanted Kryptonian scripture. When questioned on it, she informed Lena she was trying to learn self-control, still not quite certain of herself. That was evident in the amount of door handles they were now missing in their suite, the bedroom door off its hinges and resting against the wall, the splintered chair leg where Kara had stubbed her toe, and a slight dent in the wall where she’d sneezed and flown backwards into it. Lena was unbothered by them, insisting the damages would just get charged to the credit card on file, but Kara always looked slightly terrified after breaking something, pale-faced as she looked at Lena with wide eyes, clearly envisioning it being her that was broken instead of a piece of furniture.

     

                It was hard on her, trying to exist with her newly discovered abilities, and Lena felt a pang of pity for her whenever she watched her move carefully, the cautious calculating of her speed and strength, the way her face gingerly creased as she held her knife and fork or a glass. She was overly cautious but Lena didn’t try to interfere - she couldn’t say how it felt to know you could crush the bones in someone’s body just by touching them. It was better that Kara knew how to control her abilities so that she knew what her limits were and what going beyond them meant. In a few days, she’d have to cross that carefully discovered limit to free everyone from the detention camp.

     

                Even that didn’t frighten Lena. She’d seen Kara covered in blood as she pummelled someone, rammed a pipe through Mon-El, carved a path through the prison guards to free them, and she still found herself curious to know what it would be like to be held and touched by such strong hands. The fact that Kara could tear her to pieces only added a certain thrill to it but she knew it wasn’t the time to be entertaining such thoughts. 

     

                With their decision made and a list of things that needed to be sorted, Lena paid for express shipping for their online orders and then made a list of things they needed to get from a local drugstore. She sent Kara, a baseball cap and unassuming clothes - a plaid shirt, washed jeans, corduroy jacket and Chelsea boots - making her easily blend in. At the very least, she would be more instantly unrecognisable than Lena, who had been in the public eye for a long time.

     

                It was a long hour, fraught with worry as she bit her nails and paced, waiting for the room phone to call. She’d given Kara her cell phone, just in case she got lost or needed to call about something on the list. Lena could have saved herself the worry by going with her, but it was an exercise in independence as well - they couldn’t be joined at the hip for the rest of their lives - and if she was recognised, it would bring unwanted attention to them. Anything that could overstimulate Kara, beyond the expected noise, sights and smells of the city, was to be avoided on the off-chance she wrecked a city block with her heat vision alone. It would also help Kara to learn how to do human things she had never done before.

     

                Still, Lena was grateful when she was back, unlocking the hotel room door and stepping inside with two bags full of supplies. Beaming, Kara was pink-cheeked with excitement, talking animatedly as she set her bags down. She’d called Lena on the hotel phone six times on the trip, letting her know she’d arrived, checking items on the list and certain brands, letting Lena know she was leaving, so Lena hadn’t been too sick with worry but she still felt the keen relief and comfort as she listened to Kara babble.

     

                “Okay, so I know it wasn’t on the list but I just had to get these. Look! The perfect disguise. Don’t you think they suit me?” Kara asked as she fished out a pair of plastic-rimmed glasses and slipped them on her face, smiling.

     

                Lena couldn’t help but laugh, moving in closer to reach up and fix the slightly crooked frames on her face. “Yeah, they really do suit you. Good choice.”

     

                “I got the hair dye too! I thought maybe we could just swap, but, I don’t know, you just don’t strike me as a blonde, so I got you this one as well, just in case.”

     

                Rummaging through the bags, she came up with a box, carefully fumbling with it until she displayed the auburn-haired woman on the front. Lena’s stomach jolted at the colour, so similar to what she remembered her mom’s hair like when she was younger. She took it from Kara and smiled slightly.

     

                “Another good choice. What did you pick for you?”

     

                “A dark brown. But it says it has warm undertones . It’s kind of like my mom’s hair colour.”

     

                She said it with a sad smile, old grief welling up, and Lena was surprised at the shared feeling, unexpected over something as trivial as hair dye . But then she had always felt more understood by Kara in ten months of knowing each other than in all the years she’d known anyone else. Swallowing thickly, Lena put her box of hair dye down on the table and craned her neck.

     

                “What else did you buy?”

     

                “Okay, so … a book each. This one sounded interesting,” Kara explained, gesturing with a thick trade paperback and then setting it down on top of another one. 

     

                They looked like any historical romances one might find in a drugstore and Lena didn’t ruin Kara’s excitement, nodding as she forged on. She had toothpaste and toothbrushes, deodorant, a pair of scissors, tampons, Clif Bars and a plastic BIC lighter. There were a few other essentials in there as well, to go with the things Lena had ordered online, and she nodded approvingly and told Kara she’d done a great job, an answering warmth in her chest at the way her friend perked up with delight. 

     

                Packing everything away into the bags they’d half-filled, Lena took stock of it all and worried over the next few days. Even though she’d promised Kara they’d be in Broome soon, she was still apprehensive about the whole thing. They needed to be careful and she had a bad feeling in the pit of her stomach. 

     

                She couldn’t shake the feeling for the rest of the day, chalking it up to nerves, now that they’d made their choice, but she felt queasy as she cut her steak into squares, forcing the food down, not wanting to pass up the chance for a meal. They watched Gilmore Girls for the remainder of the evening and Lena was too preoccupied with her thoughts to pay much attention to it, brooding and worrying over the next steps as she curled up on the sofa beside Kara, taking comfort in the knowledge that she at least had her.

     

                They went to bed relatively early, Lena’s face pressed against Kara’s back as she burrowed into her body heat, trying to make her mind slow so she could sleep. It took a while, turning thoughts over as she tried to wind down, her body too tense for her to relax, but eventually, it came. But not for long.

     

                It was a few hours past midnight and Lena groggily woke to a disturbance. Head coming up off the pillow, she looked around, disoriented by being dragged from sleep as she blearily tried to make sense of the incessant buzzing. Her whole body was tense with confusion, and Kara was awake beside her as well, neither of them able to rest easily at any disturbance. As Lena got her bearings, it became apparent that it was her phone buzzing on the nightstand, one glance at the screen revealing her mom as the caller. Being so late, it didn’t bode well and Lena felt dread settle heavily in her stomach as she reached for it.

     

                Her voice was raspy with sleep as she answered the call. “Hello?”

     

                “Get out of there. Now.”

     

                Lena bolted out of bed, dragging Kara’s arm with her as her friend kicked off the blankets. She’d heard every word, of course, and cocked her head to the side, her expression too shadowed for Lena to make out in the dark.

     

                “There are twelve of them in the elevator,” she murmured. “A floor down.”

     

                Heart hammering in her chest, Lena didn’t even bother attempting to change, just grabbed the phone charger from the wall, staggered over to their packed bags and jammed it in before she slung a bag on her back. Kara was beside her, the considerably heavier bag slung over her shoulder as she looked at Lena.

     

                “What’s the plan?”

     

                Hesitating only a brief moment, Lena slipped her bag off and pushed it into Kara’s arms. “Get out of here. Take our things and stash them somewhere. Break them out and come back for me, okay? You heard my mom - I’m not a big enough threat-”

     

                “I’m not leaving you,” Kara hissed, her eyes straying to the open doorway. “They’re almost at the door. Am I- am I fighting them or are we running or-“

     

                “We can’t run,” Lena groaned, “you need to free everyone and say goodbye to your family. We both know you won’t leave before you do that.”

     

                Kara swallowed audibly. “Let me get you somewhere safe first.”

     

                “No, you’re not leaving me behind. I can’t- I need to know what’s happening.”

     

                “Lena,” Kara said, her voice wheedling as she bounced on the tips of her toes.

     

                She knew they were running out of time, what little warning her mother had given them not enough to come to an agreement. They were surely on the other side of the door now, getting into position, and Lena winced as she bit her lip. Reaching out, she slipped Kara’s bag off her shoulder and bore the weight of it as well as her own.

     

                “Once you free the prisoners, it makes no difference what we do. We’ll be fugitives, so … we may as well start now.”

     

                Slowly nodding, Kara looked frightened, her shoulders tense. Reaching out, she cupped Lena’s elbow and gently steered her towards the bathroom door. Halfway across the distance, she went rigid, the quietest click as the door to their suite was opened, picked up by her sensitive hearing. Lena didn’t hear it, or the soft sound of a metal canister rolling across the floor, hissing. Kara continued to push her towards the bathroom with more urgency.

                

                “Stay in there. Lock the door, okay?”

     

                “But-”

     

                “I’ll be fine. I just- I don’t want to accidentally hurt you and-”

     

                “Okay, okay,” Lena whispered. She dropped the bags to the floor and pressed her fingers to Kara’s cheek, eyes wide with worry as her stomach tied itself into knots. “Stay safe.”

     

                Hesitating, Kara leaned in an inch before she swayed back, parted lips pressing together. She eased the door shut, no door handle on the outside, and locked it as her heart thundered in her chest. It was silent beyond the door, and she strained her ears to listen, the seconds seeming infinitely longer until there was noise. There was a shout first and then the shots of a gun and Lena’s heart leapt into her throat.

     

     

                Kara had eased the broken door over the doorway to deter any of the agents from entering the master bedroom and trying the bathroom door, which she’d heard Lena lock, and turned to the sight of thick smoke pouring out of a little gas canister. Another canister followed and she frowned, confused by the sight of it until the first lungful of poisoned air hit her. Green kryptonite.

     

                The breath burned her lungs and she quickly clamped her mouth shut, holding onto the air already inhaled as she tried to limit the damage, surprise quickly turning to anger. Confident in their toxic smoke cover, the first of the SWAT agents filed into the room, rifle held aloft, a red laser darting around as they scoped out the place, the others filing in after and fanning out. Only three of them made it inside before she was on them.

     

                Grabbing the barrel of the rifle, Kara jerked it out of the agent’s hands, crushing it in her grasp as she reached out with her other hand to drag the man closer by his tactical vest. He let out a panicked shout and she tossed him across the room like a ragdoll, the stuttering of rifles firing following his exclamation. Kara felt them ping off her skin harmlessly, barely even felt, let alone hurt her, and she moved in a blur, dragging rifles from hands and her eyes intermittently shooting off beams of heat vision, shearing through furniture, tactical gear, the walls, floor and ceiling. 

     

                It was chaos for a few minutes, trying not to kill anyone but second-guessing the force behind her body as she tossed them about, the snapping of bones making her falter a few times, the smell of blood triggering memories of the prison, of the others she’d hurt. Despite how quickly she was able to decimate them, all twelve knocked out cold and nursing injuries, she still suffered a decent amount of green kryptonite inhalation, purely through the accidental reflex of breathing. 

     

                As soon as the last one slumped unconscious in her grip, she let him drop to the floor in a crumpled heap and staggered over to the bedroom door, which was largely unscathed, save for a bullet hole that knocked it off-kilter. Shouldering through it, the door thudding to the floor as it tipped over, Kara made straight for the window and punched through the glass. Sticking her head outside, Kara dragged in rasping lungfuls of air, her eyes, nose and mouth all burning from the smoke, the faint taste of gasoline and dust on the breeze a welcome balm to it.

     

                After a minute, eyes streaming, green veins tracing over her skin, Kara drew back inside and ran her sleeve over her face. Darting across the room, she jerked the door handle to break the lock and stepped inside, hearing Lena’s heartbeat from the corner.

     

                “It’s me,” Kara rasped, her voice hoarse and uneven.

     

                Lena rushed towards her, heart hammering in her chest, and stumbled into Kara’s arms. She hugged her tightly for a moment before reaching for the light switch, green eyes flitting over her face as she tried to reassure herself that Kara was fine. 

     

                “Are you okay? I- they had kryptonite?”

     

                Tracing the web of green as she swallowed thickly, Lena’s eyes dipped lower as she held Kara at arm’s length, checking for any other injuries. There were bullet holes in Kara’s clothes but no blood, and she only let Lena give a perfunctory glance before she cupped her chin and urged her eyes back up to Kara’s firm stare.

     

                “I’m fine. We need to go.”

     

                Nodding, Lena ducked to pick up their backs and Kara relieved her of them, one on each shoulder and her friend swept up in her arms. Before Lena could even respond, they were through the broken window and she felt the wind tug at her clothes as Kara shot skywards. It would be hours until dawn and Kara had dealt with the immediate problem, but she wasn’t confident more trouble wouldn’t follow. Not just with the President, but at the prison too. She wondered if they knew what they’d been planning, or whether it was just them being cautious, trying to contain a possible threat. Either way, it made no difference now.

     

                She flew them ten miles out of the city, setting them down in a thicket of trees along a highway. It was a cool night and pitch black to Lena’s human eyes, and she felt her friend cling to her with uncertainty, even after her feet had been set down on grass. Smoothing a hand over her hair, Kara felt an ache in her chest as she pressed her lips to Lena’s temple.

     

                “It’s okay. We’re safe for now. You need to tell me what’s next.”

     

                “Next? I don’t know. It’s too late - or too early, I-”

     

                Falling silent, Lena let go of Kara and moved to her left. Turning with her, eyes scanning the area for something her hearing had mortifyingly missed, Kara looked around with a wary expression on her face. Lena just clicked her tongue in annoyance and kept circling until she jerked a zipper on one of the backpacks open and fished out her cell phone. With a huff of sheepish laughter, Kara shifted from foot to foot as Lena fumbled with the phone, her hands shaking horribly.

     

                She managed to call her mother and Kara listened to it ring as she watched Lena press the phone to her ear. Anxiously biting her lip, Lena looked everywhere, and sometimes at Kara, as her eyes restlessly moved around. It rang five times before Lillian picked up the call.

     

                “Are you safe?”

     

                “Am I-” Lena started, her voice breaking as a hysterical laugh worked up her throat. “What the fuck was that?”

     

                “I had a bad feeling so I had someone watch the Waldorf for me. I got the call as they entered the building.”

     

                Lena couldn’t speak for a moment, pacing away from Kara with her hand clapped to her forehead, brimming with adrenaline and panic and confusion. Curling and uncurling her bloody fingers, Kara bounced on the tips of her toes as she watched her, restless with unease.

     

                “What- I- I thought you and I were done.”

     

                “We will never truly be done. Yes, I lied to you for my own gain, just like you made your little press conference for your own gain, but I will not let them have you again. You should’ve taken my advice the first time and vanished when you could. I might have to do the same; it looks like we’ve both exhausted our use to the President. She pulled the deal with Cadmus.”

     

                Mouth opening and closing, Lena swallowed her anger. “I can’t say I feel bad about that. What are you going to do now?”

     

                “Oh, you know me. I have my ways of staying hidden when I want to be.”

     

                “Okay. We’re going too. Once we wrap things up here.”

     

                “Lena, don’t-”

     

                “If you know anything … about the camp they’re being detained in, if they have kryptonite or- or anything that can hurt her … please tell me.”

     

                “You and I both know they wouldn’t entrust that information to me. If I knew, I would tell you.”

     

                Kara didn’t know Lillian well, but she knew Lena, even if she didn’t know her expressions well yet, and she could tell that her friend believed her mother. Chin wobbling as she squeezed her eyes shut, Lena swallowed thickly.

     

                “Okay, thank you.”

     

                “You should go now. Good luck to you both, whatever you decide. And … please know I had your best interests at heart - I always have.”

     

                Eyes smarting with tears, Lena turned around, her back to Kara. Wanting to comfort her but understanding she was intentionally putting space between them, Kara stayed where she was. There was a prolonged moment of silence, filled with the sound of rustling leaves and the occasional car passing on the highway, before Lena spoke, her voice wavering.

     

                “Thank you for all of your help,” Lena hoarsely murmured. “I really appreciate it, I- things between us … I wish there was more time.” 

     

                “I know.”

     

                “I’ll never forget what you did for me.”

     

                “This won’t be forever. Someday, maybe we can sit down together, and you and I can patch things up properly.”

     

                “Maybe,” Lena whispered in agreement, a smile in her voice. “Well … I've got to go now.”

     

                “Let me know when you’re somewhere safe. You don’t have to say where , but … just so I know.”

     

                “Sure. I’ll do that.”

     

                “I won’t say it - you never seem to believe me when I do - but be safe, my girl.”

     

                “Bye, mom.”

     

                Her goodbye was barely a whisper and Lena held the phone to her ear for a beat longer before she turned to look at Kara. Eyes bright in the dark, Lena cleared her throat and sniffed before she crossed the few feet separating them and held her phone out to Kara.

     

                “Can you break that, please?”

     

                Confused, Kara hesitated a moment before taking the phone from Lena and crushing it in her grasp. It was an easy thing to do but Kara didn’t understand why until Lena took it back and tossed it carelessly aside. Looking at Kara, Lena’s clouded expression softened with worry and she stepped in to reach up and touch Kara’s cheek. There were still traces of green but she was already breathing better, her body healing quickly.

     

                “Are you alright?” Lena asked.

     

                “Yes. Are you?”

     

                “I’ll live.”

     

                Nodding, Kara paused, pressing her lips together before she exhaled. “I’m sorry about your mom.”

     

                Brow furrowing together, Lena smiled slightly. “It’s alright, I’m not losing much. Just … what could have been, maybe. But it’ll be alright.”

     

                “What now?”

     

                Kara was jittery with nerves, her eyes darting around as her body hummed with energy, and Lena smoothed her hands down her arms, trying to calm her. “We need to get out of here. We stick to the plan; you free them and then we go to Australia.”

     

                Wincing slightly, Kara raked a hand through her hair. “I- can I say goodbye first?”

     

                Mouth opening and closing, Lena desperately wanted to say no, but she knew that closure was the least she could afford Kara. She was taking her away from people she’d known for most of her life, far longer than she’d known Lena, and despite the complex nature of things, of her own feelings on the matter, Kara cared for them, even if Lena wished she wouldn’t. She paused a second too long and awkwardly cleared her throat.

     

                “Yes. Yes, of course. But … we can’t wait for word to spread through the channels about what just happened. They’ll be hunting us so … we go now, and you break in and do it quickly. I wish you could have had more time, I’m sorry, but it needs to be quick. And … maybe not all of them.”

     

                Kara’s expression was pained but she nodded with understanding. “Okay. Thank you. I- I’ll be quick, I’ll- you stay here, okay? Stay hidden and I’ll be right back. Are you- are you warm enough? Do you need anything first, or-”

     

                Cutting her off with the touch of a hand, Lena gave her a pitying look. “I’m fine. I’ll be right here. Just … stay safe.”

     

                Nodding quickly, Kara slipped the backpacks off and set them at the base of a tree and gave Lena a lingering parting look before she shot off into the air. She was still getting the hang of flying, and wasn’t familiar with DC, or the aerial view of it, but she was familiar with the three heartbeats located within the same building as she set off through the dark. Out of the three women, it was Alex who knew her the best, Alex who she’d spent the most time with and had been raised alongside as much as possible, given the circumstances, so it was only natural that she went to her. Honing in on Alex’s heartbeat, Kara came to a shaky stop as close as she could get to Alex without breaking down the walls between them, hovering midair outside the detention centre as she considered her options.

     

                They were already in trouble, and they were already being hunted, so Kara didn’t give it much thought before she punched through the brick and plaster. No one was on the other side, so she didn’t have to hurt anyone, shouldering her way into the building and then through a door and two more walls before she was inside Alex’s cell. Her friend was crouched near the cell door, protecting her head, a dusting of plaster and brick coating her prison uniform, and she looked at Kara with shock.

     

                Hurrying to kneel at her side, Kara swallowed thickly. “Alex, we don’t have much time.”

     

                “Kara, I- wha-”

     

                Tugging insistently on her arm, Kara derailed her intention to say goodbye as she listened to alarms start blaring and decided to free her friends as well. “We need to go. Now. I don’t have much time, I can’t- I can’t go with you all, but-”

     

                Pulling her arm free from Kara’s gentle grasp, Alex shook her head. “No. No, no, you need to go . You need to go right now.”

     

                “Let me get you out. I can give you a chance-”

     

                “No. This is where I need to be. Look, we’re going to be fine , okay? We’re going to be fine but you … you need to go. I wish it was different, trust me, I do. You and I … I never had a sister, but if I’d gotten to choose, I would’ve picked you. I wish you’d landed in our backyard and we got to grow up as real sisters, and maybe in another life that would’ve been true, but not in this one, so I need you to listen to her and go and live your life and … know what kind of person you are and what it’s like to be free. The rest of us … we’ll be okay, and who knows, maybe in a few years- in a few years, we’ll be out of here and you can come and find us again.”

     

                Eyes filling with tears, Kara’s chin dimpled as her face crumpled. “But you can be free too.”

     

                “I know, but … my whole life was ruined the day my mom and I were sent to Fort Rozz; I don’t want to ruin the rest of it by going on the run. One day, when I’m out of here, I want it all to be normal again, so that means, for now, just for a little while, I need to stay here and do my time. It won’t be forever this time.”

     

                Alex wiped Kara’s wet cheeks for her, her brown eyes bright with tears as well, and Kara had to force the lump in her throat down as she nodded. It was the last thing she wanted to do, leave the three of them there, even though that had always been the plan, and she could hear boots thudding on the linoleum floor as guards rushed towards Alex’s cell, their time together reduced to less than a minute. Wrapping her in a hug, Kara kissed her cheek and gently squeezed her.

     

                “It’s not forever but I’ll miss you anyway. Be well, all of you.”

     

                Pulling back, Alex cupped Kara’s face in her hands and smiled warmly. The guards were at the cell door now, barking orders, shouting as they took in the hole Kara had made in the walls, footsteps on the other side of it as well as they tried to pen her in. Hearing the key scrape in the lock, Kara gave her one last squeeze and let her go.

                

                “You too - both of you. Make sure she looks after you.”

     

                Letting out a choked laugh, Kara nodded, backing away. “And tell your mom and Kelly-”

     

                “I will,” Alex assured her, not needing her to say what it was she needed to tell them. “Go.”

     

                At the soft command, Kara turned, knocking over the first guard to reach the hole in her haste to leave, and darted out into the night. She was nothing more than a streak before the guards got their bearings, got the cell door unlocked and figured out what was happening. Even as she left, Kara listened, making sure that Alex was safe before she committed to her decision to leave, to not turn around again.

     

                Within minutes, she was skidding through the dirt as she clumsily landed, a deep furrow in the ground before she got her balance and dashed through the trees to Lena’s side. She appeared so suddenly that Lena let out a startled yelp, clapping a hand over her mouth as her heart went wild. Quickly reassuring her, Kara’s voice was hoarse as she spoke, and Lena couldn’t see her bloodshot eyes in the dark.

     

                “Time to go.”

                

                Scooping up the bags and then holding a hand out to Lena, Kara picked her up and held her safely before sending them skywards so quickly that Lena’s stomach dropped. Cradling the back of her head as she kept Lena’s face pressed against her chest, shielded from the brunt of the rough wind as they rocketed through the sky, they quickly left DC behind.

     

                There was a certain thrill to knowing she had already outpaced anyone pursuing them, knowing that if she kept going, they would be untraceable and it would all be okay. But they had to stop, they had to go to the detention centre so she could free the others, and that would ruin any chances they had of knowing peace. The US government wouldn’t take kindly to a few hundred prisoners loosed into the world, all of them aliens or metahumans, powerful enough to cause destruction if their minds turned that way. Kara hoped it wouldn’t, that they would all be happy with their freedom and a fresh start, but they at least deserved a chance to prove her wrong instead of being condemned for their mere existence.

     

                Twenty miles out from the remote detention camp, Kara set Lena down in a secluded spot where she could safely go unnoticed and set the bags down with her. Feeling nervous now, so much riding on her getting everyone out safely, getting Lena away safely, Kara gave her a wavering smile.

     

                “Alright, well, wish me luck. I’ll be right back, okay?”

     

                “Be safe,” Lena ordered her, voice shaking slightly as she put her hands on Kara’s shoulders, and touched her cheek, her neck, and her arms, reassuring herself that she was okay for now. “Don’t sacrifice yourself for them. Please.”

     

                “Hey,” Kara murmured, her smile crooked and her eyes bright in the dark, barely holding it together after the mad rush of their night coming apart. “I thought you believed me.”

     

                With a huff of laughter, Lena rolled her eyes and then suddenly cupped her face in her hands, firmly pressing her lips to Kara’s in a quick kiss. “I believe you, now go on. Come back to me soon.”

     

                A little dazed from the unexpected kiss, Kara nodded and backed away with her eyes on Lena before she turned and sped off into the dark, her heart pounding as adrenaline flooded through her, so much anger, sadness and fear building in her chest that it fuelled her motivation. She could do this, and she could do it without killing anyone. She’d free her friends and keep them safe and then she’d vanish without a trace, to the country on the other side of the world she’d seen on maps in old textbooks.

     

                In less than a minute, she was hovering above the prison, too high for anyone to have noticed her, but hopefully within earshot of her old friend. Swallowing thickly, stomach knotted with nervous anticipation, Kara cleared her throat and shouted to the night.

     

                “J’onn? J’onn , it’s Kara. Are you awake?”

     

                Spending years inside a prison, she knew that one adjusted to sleeping with the noise of so many people around, but she also knew that any slight disturbance was enough to rouse you too. The cell block doors opening, the sound of footsteps down a parallel hallway, the sound of an inmate shouting on the next cell block over. She knew he would hear her, unconsciously aware of his surroundings and always alert for something unexpected.

     

                “Kara?”

     

                “We don’t have much time. You need to wake everyone up and keep them quiet.”

     

                “What’s the plan?”

     

                “I’m going to tear down the fences and disable the guards. You need to run for it - all of you. Get everyone ready to run as soon as the fence is down. Tell them not to stop until they’re far enough away to disappear. Everyone on our block … please help them.”

     

                “Querl is here with me. I’ll find the others before I go.”

     

                “Thank you.”

     

                “And you?”

     

                “Lena is nearby. We’re going as well, once you’re out, I just- I couldn’t leave without getting you all out first. Don’t trust the government, alright? Make sure you don’t get into any trouble; they’ll be looking for you all. Head overseas if you can.”

     

                “Thank you for coming back for us.”

     

                “Get ready.”

     

                Without another word, she dropped like a stone, landing on the pitted asphalt outside the fence and cracking it beneath her feet as she slammed down hard enough to make the earth tremble. There was an undercurrent of unease through the camp as guards muttered at the disturbance, spotlights moving slowly as the night shift was suddenly alert, wary of any intruders. She was too quick for it though, moving in a blur as she made for the front gate and yanked it clean off with ease. 

     

                As the guards responded to the act, she was already inside the first tower, crumpling rifles into scrap metal like they were balls of paper, bullets pinging harmlessly off her skin as a quick thinker unholstered a pistol and started emptying it into her, thinking it would do any good. She had the three guards knocked out in a minute and leapt across to the next tower, following the same process as they barely had time to realise she was there and fire off a shot before they were out cold, one sporting a possibly broken nose, even though she’d tried to be gentle.

     

                The gunshots had garnered some attention though and alarms started blaring, the whole camp waking up as the wailing filled the silence and everything was illuminated in sections as they first assumed a detainee trying to escape was the cause of the trouble. Of course, they weren’t expecting someone to break them out, and it bought Kara a few more minutes as she picked up the pace, disarming the entire perimeter of the guard towers before they even realised she was there.

     

                Within the camp, there was a barrage of motion and noise, J’onn instructing everyone to run as aliens and metahumans warily stepped outside at the commotion. The first to flee was Leslie Willis, cutting the power as she sprinted through the dark unseen until she reached the fence, trying to scale the chain link before she realised she wouldn’t be able to get through the ceiling of the giant cage they were essentially penned inside. A few feet off the ground as she swore loudly, she was startled by the sudden appearance of the Kryptonian on the other side, shredding the metal mesh without so much as a thought, creating a hole that widened to let the woman out and then kept growing as Kara tore down the whole section. 

     

                “Thanks, blondie,” Leslie said with a wink before she set off into the night.

     

                Smiling now, Kara slipped inside and watched as a guard fired shots at the next few aliens braving their chance to escape, and she was between them in a flash, snatching bullets in her palms and shooting off a beam of heat vision that melted the rifle in the woman’s hands. Ushering the detainees to continue with their escape, Kara covered their fleeing as she zipped back and forth, bowling guards over as she blew a gust of wind at them, tore an AC unit off the side of a demountable and launched it at another two that ran at her in a panic.

     

                Around her, hundreds of her fellow inmates streamed towards the fencing, some of them trying their own hand at tearing through the metal mesh. A few faces were recognisable but none of them were her friends as she listened to their heartbeats as they congregated near the middle. They were trying to suppress the guards as well and she ran to them, fear tightening her throat as she ran. She hadn’t managed to save everyone, running past a few bodies in prison beige with regret, and she saw a few of the more unsavoury aliens already making good on their chances to seek revenge, mauling prison guards or fighting back. She left them to it as she sought out her friends.

     

                “J’onn!” she bellowed as she skidded to a halt, beckoning him.

     

                Nia and Querl were with him, holding hands for dear life, and J’onn had teamed up with M’gann, a White Martian he’d never been friendly with, as they fended off a few guards. Andrea was there with Imra and Psi, the Saturnian telekinetically juggling a few jagged pieces of metal like they were throwing knives while the latter stalked down a gaggle of guards who were quaking with fear as Psi’s psychic ability made them falter in their task.

     

                They all flocked to Kara with a few stragglers, scared and eager to escape unscathed, and they made a formidable group as they carved a path of destruction through the detention camp. It would have been possible for them to do it before, of course, but no one wanted to be the one to instigate trouble without the possibility of escape. They’d all been beaten and cowed inside Fort Rozz, with no hope available to them until Kara had made that decision for them. She would get them out safely, she would free her friends and part ways knowing she’d done the right thing, even if it meant a life on the run for them all. A life on the run was still a life lived freely.

     

                The gunfire came to a stuttering halt as the few remaining guards gave up or were killed by the more vengeful inmates, and she ushered her cellmates out through a destroyed fence, covering their escape from the rear. The inmates of Fort Rozz were all free with minimal casualties, and only a few minor scrapes and bruises for her friends, and Kara felt relief keenly cut through her chest as she let out a ragged breath, laughter bubbling up as she didn’t know how to manage her emotions.

     

                “Go! Run!” she urged them, staying behind as she made sure any stragglers got out fine, made sure no one went after them.

     

                What little time she had before she had to go to Lena and whisk her away to safety, she would spend giving her friends the best chance she could so they could run as far away as possible. Querl clapped her on the shoulder as he passed her by, Nia hugging her before taking his hand and letting him drag her off, and the others gave her terse nods, grateful and stoic, until it was just J’onn left. 

     

                He’d been there the longest with Kara, and there was a weighted moment of understanding between the two of them, the moment poignant as they realised this was goodbye, that they’d made it out free. It was almost as cutting as her goodbye with Alex, and Kara threw herself into his arms, holding onto him tightly as he chuckled deep in his chest, elated and surprised at the sudden turn of his luck. Patting her back, he lifted her off the ground for a brief moment and then set her down, Kara holding onto him for a moment longer. She would miss so many people now that she was free, and it was mildly terrifying and lonely, but she wouldn’t have changed a thing.

     

                “Goodbye, old friend.”

     

                Swallowing thickly, Kara closed her eyes and drew in a shaky breath. “You’ve been a good friend, J’onn J’onnz. I’m glad to have known you.”

     

                “And you, Kara Zor-El. You’ve made your family proud, I know that much. Have a happy life.”

     

                Eyes wet, she nodded as she pulled away and he softly smiled before they parted ways. Breathing heavily as she turned, Kara listened to the sounds of the detention camp, the frightened whispers of guards as they tried to radio the nearby naval base, those still alive quietly picking their way through the ruined buildings and mess she’d helped make. She stayed until she was sure everyone who wanted to flee had done so, aware of a few aliens who had remained inside, whether because of the comfort of routine or to seek revenge, and then made her departure.

     

     

                Lena was anxiously pacing when Kara returned. Staggering as she landed, Kara forged onwards, engulfing her in a hug as she started to cry. Lena let out a strangled sound of panic, fearing her hurt or the attempt failed, her arms going around Kara as she held her tightly.

     

                “Are you okay?” she asked, her voice breaking. “What happened? What-”

     

                “I’m fine, I’m fine,” Kara babbled through her tears, drawing in a hitching breath. “They’re out. They’re free, we did it, we-”

     

                “Oh. Oh, okay, it’s okay now, it’s done.”

     

                “It’s done.”

     

                Lena could hear the exhausted relief in Kara’s voice before she let out a breathless sob, pulling back and wiping her face, her shirt riddled with bullet holes and plaster dust. Sniffing as her mouth turned down at the corners, Kara ducked her head as she toyed with her fingers. Her shoulders were hunched and pity knifed through Lena as she watched her.

     

                “We can’t stay here,” Lena said, a ripple of guilt passing her face as she reached out to touch Kara’s arm.

     

                Nodding, Kara swallowed the next sob as she tried to pull herself together, and Lena picked up their backpacks and went to her, pulling her into a hug and rubbing her back. After a moment, Kara tightened her grip on Lena and set off with her. They couldn’t go to Australia yet, broad daylight making their arrival more obvious if anyone was watching, so Lena had her fly them to Vegas, forking over some cash for a sleazy motel. It was early hours of the morning and with the number of drunks about, leaving casinos and nightclubs, they just looked like two dishevelled women looking for a place to spend the rest of their night together.

     

                Inside the motel, Lena locked and bolted the door and dragged Kara over to the bed, pushing her down onto the mattress. Bags slipping off her shoulders, Kara let out a ragged gasp as her expression crumpled again, hot tears in her eyes as she scrubbed them away. Sinking to her knees before her, Lena gave her an aching look as she cupped Kara’s hands in her own.

     

                “Hey, hey, it’s okay, you’re alright.”

     

                “Yeah,” Kara pitifully murmured, swallowing thickly as more tears welled up and spilt down her cheeks. “I just- I’m going to miss everyone.”

     

                “Oh. Right.”

     

                She knew Kara was so attached to the people who had gotten her through the worst years of her life, keeping her going as she clung to their companionship, ever hopeful and eager to befriend the new inmates, but she hadn’t considered the depth of her sacrifice for their freedom too. It wasn’t just getting them out of the detention camp, but cutting them loose from the bonds they’d made inside the prison as well, and in that regard, Kara was giving up a lot more than just the three women she was closest too, and an equally big sacrifice as Lena, who was giving up her life as much as Kara was giving up the only life she’d known. Stomach lurching with dismay as she wondered whether they’d made the right choice, her shoulders slumped.

     

                “I’m sorry. I know it’s difficult but …”

     

                No words to comfort her, knowing that she didn’t have any real experience with missing anyone, except for Kara when she’d had to leave her behind, Lena trailed off into silence. Quietly crying for a few more minutes, Kara finally heaved a resigned sigh and touched Lena’s cheek, giving her a grim smile.

     

                “But it’s for the best. We’re all free; the best we can do now is live.”

     

                “Yes. We should get some sleep as well, while we can.”

     

                Shaking her head, Kara grimaced. “I don’t think I’ll be able to sleep tonight.”

     

                “Alright, well … let’s watch some TV and then once it hits around … five o’clock western time, we can head off. It’s winter in Australia, so it should be dark by seven o'clock their time. No one will see us coming then, and hopefully, no one will see us leave here .”

     

                Nodding, Kara sighed again and then flopped back on the bed. Lena turned the TV on, reruns of Judge Judy filling the screen, and she moved over to the clunky phone on the nightstand and thumbed through a worn Yellow Pages until she found a number for a Big Belly Burger chain nearby. It was a twenty-four-hour store and she called and placed a huge order for delivery, giving a fake name and telling them to come straight to their room upon arrival before hanging up. Crawling onto the bed beside Kara, Lena let her body go limp as she stared up at the speckled ceiling and heard the faint sound of noises they could have done without as Kara grabbed the TV remote and upped the volume a bit.

     

                Their food took an hour to arrive, and by that point, it was two o’clock in Vegas, both of them gritty-eyed and tense as the delivery guy knocked on the door. Kara answered it as a precaution, handing over a few folded bills with a decent tip and coming back to bed with two bulging bags and a cup tray precariously balanced. They both leaned against the headboard in the shitty motel room and ate their greasy food as they watched Judge Judy in silence, the solid warmth of the other a comforting presence as they pressed up against each other, knowing that it was done now and they had each other. Lena couldn’t begin to describe how grateful she was that Kara had kept her word and had come back to her. She wouldn’t have been able to follow through with the next part without her.

     

                Once the digital alarm clock on the nightstand hit five o’clock, they bundled up their trash and put it in the trash can, grabbed their bags and the room key, and checked out without a word to the woman at reception. Heading out into the garishly neon city, they slipped down one of the seedier alleyways behind their motel and Kara picked her up once more, for the last leg of their trip. Australia. 

     

                It was thousands of miles away and Kara didn’t know her limits yet but was wary of them, not wanting to push herself too hard in case Lena suffered for it, so it took them a lot longer than Lena guessed it should have. If Kara was alone, flying at her full capacity, Lena thought she would have been able to make the trip within minutes, but it took them almost forty, Kara’s body heat keeping her warm as she kept her eyes closed, face pressed into her shoulder as strong arms held her securely. Still, she felt stiff and it was a relief when Kara hit the eastern coast of Australia, although it was another five minutes of flying across the expansive desert and bushland before she said she could see the ocean on the other side. That meant they were within range of their destination, residing somewhere within Western Australia, although Lena had no clue where . 

     

                After forty-five minutes of flying, Kara set them down on the outskirts of a cluster of lights denoting a small town, and it took a few minutes of creeping closer to determine they were a few hundred kilometres south of where they needed to be. In that fashion, it took another ten minutes of slowly drawing in on their location, hitting too far north, they were just a touch too south before Lena was satisfied that they were close to her safe house. She had fifty acres an hour north of Broome, not too big to be noticed but enough land to give the demountable chalet situated on the beachfront a wide berth by anyone passing nearby. The entire area was red dirt and bushland, inhabited by kangaroos, wallabies and other wildlife, the red dirt giving way to golden beaches and the blue of the Indian Ocean. Lena had been there once, merely to set everything up, setting up cameras around the entire perimeter to alert for any intruders, getting the demountable set up, and two generators installed with a plumbing system and solar panels to power everything. She had a battered Toyota Land Cruiser that wouldn’t look out of place on trips into Broome, and enough rifles with the serial numbers filed off and stashed cash to get her through any trouble. As long as nothing had been touched, they should have almost everything they needed.

     

                Kara set them down once more and Lena had to rely on the Kryptonian’s eyesight to guide them through the dark, a chill to the endless bushland as they trekked the few remaining miles to the borders of Lena’s land. Nothing disturbed the night, save for the sound of the wind and the rustling of the trees and scrubs, and the occasional snap of a twig that could have been any number of creatures that made their home there. Before long, they could hear the sea as well.

     

                “I can see a shack ahead,” Kara informed her as they picked their way across the land. “Is that it?”

     

                “Should be.”

     

                “Alright, hold on.”

     

                Before Lena could speak, she was in Kara’s arms, feeling as if the wind had picked up for a brief moment, before she felt solid ground beneath her feet again. Using the wan moonlight peeking between heavy cloud cover, Lena’s eyes adjusted enough to make out the chalet. Corrugated iron, galvanised but slowly worn to the salt-laced air where it faced the ocean, made up the walls and roof of the safe house, slightly elevated with a small shaded verandah situated at the front. It was nothing special but Lena was grateful to be there as they rounded the building and reached the front door.

     

                Lena hurried up the few short steps and reached up to the eaves of the verandah to take down a hidden key. Unlocking the security screen and then the front door, she stepped into the dark chalet. The solar panels had a battery to feed into, which meant that when she flicked on the lights, a warm glow suffused the space and Lena stepped aside to let Kara in before locking both doors behind them. Not that she anticipated anyone near enough to notice the sudden lights, but it never hurt to be safe.

     

                “Welcome home,” she said as she rounded on Kara.

     

                Slipping off the backpacks, Kara looked around. It wasn’t much to look at; tiled floors, kitchen cabinets with a metal table and two folding chairs. One door led to a small bathroom and another to a bedroom with a camp bed - fortunately a double - a safe in the corner with Lena’s cash and documents, and a trunk beneath the bed with her rifles. The main living area had a boxy TV, a stereo system and VHS player, and a small bookshelf with old paperbacks, cassette tapes and videos, and a battered deck of cards to pass the time. This was one of her last resort safe houses, remote and fully off-grid, so there was nothing modern about it and only a few things to help pass the time. 

     

                “Here, we should get this done first,” Lena murmured, rummaging through her backpack and finding the boxes of hair dye. 

     

                She left her backpack in the kitchen and switched the light on in the bathroom. There was a shower stall, toilet and a sink set in a cabinet. A more in-depth first aid kit, toiletries and towels were stowed in there and she removed the latter and a bottle of shampoo before gesturing for Kara to take a seat on the toilet.

     

                “We should cut it as well,” Lena regretfully said as she unboxed the bottles of hair dye and plastic gloves.

     

                Kara’s blonde hair was long enough to reach her lower back, too many years imprisoned and not enough haircuts, and Lena loved it, was loath to cut and colour it, but it would make her recognisable, and that was too big of a risk. Looking up at her, Kara smiled, eyes creasing at the corners, and shrugged indifferently.

     

                “Makes no difference to me.”

     

                Nodding, she mixed the bottles of dye and put on the gloves, a towel around Kara’s shoulders to protect her clothes, and got to work. Working the dye into her roots, Lena methodically worked her way in sections until she ran out and picked up the second one and moved on to the length of Kara’s hair, taking off a chunk with the scissors so she didn’t waste time and dye on it, and made sure she didn’t miss any spots. Massaging it in properly, she peeled the gloves off and put them in the trash before smiling at Kara.

     

                “Alright, you just need to keep that on for a bit and then wash it off and I’ll cut it for you.”

     

                “Is it your turn?”

     

                “Mhm. Do you want to give it a go?”

     

                “Me? Um … I don’t know, I- what if it hurts?”

     

                Briefly cupping Kara’s chin, she smiled. “It won’t hurt. You just need to rub it in everywhere, like you’re massaging my head.”

     

                “What if I massage too hard?”

     

                “Then I’ll tell you.”

     

                Hesitant, Kara rose from the toilet seat and nodded as she decided to give it a go. Taking her spot, Lena draped a towel around her shoulders and watched as Kara mixed the bottles of hair dye and donned her gloves before getting to work. Her touch was so featherlight that Lena wanted to laugh, assuring her that she could be more vigorous with it as she rubbed it into her roots. She had the unfortunate need to bleach her dark locks first before they could go in with the coppery colour Kara had picked for her, and Lena double-checked Kara’s work once she’d finished, making sure she hadn’t missed any patches that might make the rushed dye job look too obvious when they went into town. 

     

                Both of them stayed cooped up in the bathroom as the colours developed, until Lena told Kara she could wash hers off and left her to it. Shutting the bathroom door behind herself, Lena set about making some coffee, a tin of sealed coffee grounds in a cupboard, enamel cups beside it and the pipes groaning a little from disuse as she filled a kettle with water to boil. 

     

                Listening to the sputtering water, Lena was filled with another belated surge of adrenaline, it all feeling surreal that she was on the other side of the world with someone she’d met inside a prison ten months ago. In less than a year, her upper-class lifestyle and career in the tech industry had been completely ruined, and Lena was struggling to wrap her head around it. She wouldn’t have changed anything - except maybe being fugitives - and knew it was what she needed now, that time out of the spotlight, unrecognisable and without the pressure of running a billion-dollar business and pretending like it hadn’t happened. It was another thing to actually put into action the thing she needed and she knew it would take a few days for the reality of her new life to sink in.

     

                Once the water stopped, she waited for Kara to change and crack the bathroom door open, looking a little surprised, her hair dark as it hung in a wet, tangled mess. Leaving the kettle to boil, Lena made her way into the bathroom as Kara took a seat on the toilet again and picked up the scissors. Making Kara tuck her chin in, she started cutting. Lena let Kara pick the length, just a little longer than her shoulders and tried to cut it evenly as she snipped off inches, after already cutting off a decent amount before she’d dyed it. It was such a drastic change and Lena felt a pang of regret but couldn’t deny that it suited Kara, beautiful no matter what colour or length her hair was.

     

                Kara had her cut a fringe in too, a more uneasy prospect for Lena as she squatted in front of Kara and tried her best to give her curtain bangs, sheepish as she gingerly tried to make it even. She didn’t think she’d done too bad a job, but they wouldn’t know for sure until Kara’s hair was air-dried. Lena smiled as she gently ruffled the fringe, especially when Kara plucked her plastic glasses from her shirt pocket and put them on, raising her eyebrows expectantly.

     

                “Like a whole new person,” Lena assured her, cupping her chin. “We’ll get you a fake ID sorted and no one will suspect a thing.”

     

                Climbing to her feet, Kara studied herself in the mirror and seemed pleased with it, smiling as she toyed with the short ends of her damp hair. Leaving her to take in her new appearance, Lena slipped out and made their coffee, the kettle whistling on the stove as it started to boil itself dry, and then gave it another five minutes before she washed her hair. Emerging from the shower, her dark tresses were a ghastly orange from the bleach and she towel-dried it before she had Kara go in with the bottle of copper dye and repeat the process.

     

                Sipping coffee at the kitchen table, the two of them were relatively silent, exhausted from the chaos of the day but glad for the quiet reprieve in their little hiding spot. Lena just hoped that no one had spotted their arrival, that satellite images hadn’t picked up on Kara streaking to Western Australia, or the locals didn’t notice. She knew any chances of sleep over the next week would be scarce, too worried about being discovered leaving her too keyed up to rest. As she let the hair dye develop, she brooded over the possibilities of the next forty-eight hours. 

     

                Taking another shower to wash out the dye, Lena stepped out and towel-dried her hair, staining it orange in the process, and looked at her wan expression in the mirror. Kara knocked on the door a few minutes later before opening it, and Lena caught sight of her surprised expression in the mirror.

     

                “Do you like it?”

     

                “I look like my mom,” Lena said with a pang of sadness, looking at herself like she was seeing a ghost. “My birth mom. Um, she had red hair. And bangs.”

     

                Touching her own, Kara smiled faintly. “Well, you know, bangs wouldn’t be a bad idea.”

     

                Lena let out a huff of laughter and shrugged with feigned nonchalance. She wasn’t sure she would be able to face looking like her mom, catching sight of herself in the mirror every day, but then again, the multitude of fake IDs she had stored in every safe house always had one of a redhead with the name Elizabeth Walsh on it.
