Picking up the scissors, Lena hacked off the ends of her hair, until it was almost of a length with Kara’s, just past her shoulders, and then brushed a section forward and cut straight across. It was blunter than Kara’s curtain bangs and Lena felt her stomach lurch as she fussed with the slightly uneven ends, trimming them until it was decently straight.

     

                Setting the scissors down and leaving the mess of cut hair, stained gloves and boxes for the morning, Lena turned and cupped Kara’s face in her hand, the small bathroom not affording much space, and gently stroked her thumb over her cheek.

     

                “Come on, let’s have some dinner.”

     

                Making another cup of coffee for them both, Lena also fished out every tin of soup she had stored, clearing out the supplies with Kara’s appetite in mind as she checked the date on her old supplies and considered two months past expiry decent enough. It had been years since she’d set up the safe house, so everything had a layer of dust and red dirt, and some of the shelf stable supplies were reaching the last legs of their expiry dates. Still, it was hot and filling and she heated tin after tin in the saucepan as Kara wolfed down her dinner without complaint. It wasn’t up to the standard of the food they’d been ordering through room service at the Waldorf, but it was food.

     

                Dumping the empty tins in the trash, Lena set their dirty bowls in the sink and left them for the morning before she turned to Kara and gestured to the bedroom door. “You should rest.”

     

                “And you.”

     

                Wrinkling her nose as she smiled slightly, Lena toyed with her fingers. “I don’t think I’ll get much sleep done tonight. And you need it more than I do after everything; you must be exhausted.”

     

                “I am,” Kara agreed, climbing to her feet and cocking her head to the side as she studied Lena’s face. “But so are you. You didn’t get much sleep last night either.”

     

                “I’ll sleep when you’re awake. I just- I’d like to be sure we weren’t tracked.”

     

                “We’re pretty far away from any major cities, and if the government tells Australia we’re here, I’m sure that gives us at least a few hours of sleep before they show up here. I’ll hear them coming; I’ll protect us. Just … come to bed. Get some rest.”

     

                Lena felt so drained that she wanted to cry, all the worry and fear sitting heavily in her chest making her vulnerable to Kara’s caring pleas. Rubbing her eyes, feeling the blunt bangs, which made her feel so unlike herself, Lena let out a heavy sigh and then nodded. She was too tired to protest, and if she was too tired for that, it didn’t matter who came for them, she’d be too tired to resist them anyway. Kara would always be her best bet for dealing with any trouble, and she just hoped it would steer clear.

     

                Crawling into bed, taking the spot against the wall, Lena shifted on the mattress as she tried to get comfortable. The air was stale and dusty and despite being so far north, it was cool and the chalet wasn’t well insulated, which left her pressed up against Kara’s back for warmth, an arm thrown across her waist as if it was the most natural thing in the world for them. They whispered goodnight to each other and Lena laid awake for another hour at least before exhaustion won out and she sank into grateful sleep.

     

                Waking to bright daylight seeping in around the roller blind, Lena slowly sat up and rubbed her gritty eyes before she looked down at Kara, who was still fast asleep beside her. Disoriented and a little panicked, Lena’s eyes shot to the door and she strained her ears for any sounds of intruders before easing herself out of bed and then unlocking the bedroom door and peering into the chalet. It was as they’d left it last night and she let out a slow breath before quietly closing the door and moving over to the front door. Unlocking it, she stared through the security screen and couldn’t see anyone outside either, but was sure to check the security footage on a clunky, encrypted laptop to make sure none of the cameras or sensors had been tripped. 

     

                Reassured, Lena took a minute to send her mother an email and let her know she was safe, ensuring it would be untraceable, although Lena thought she and her mother were past that now. Powering it down, she set water on to boil and then fetched powdered eggs for breakfast, with a tin of baked beans and sausages. She had to make a large portion again, going through five of the tins and the whole container of powdered eggs, and Lena was starting to think it would be a lot easier for them to starve than she’d anticipated with bringing Kara along. Her safe homes had been designed for emergency use for one person and she knew that the stock-piled cash would only last for so long. Of course, she would have ways of accessing more money, but she wondered how long they’d be able to survive before they needed to stock up on supplies that were supposed to last a few weeks at least.

     

                Kara was roused from bed a short while later and Lena reheated the food for her and made them both some tea - black because they had no milk - feeling better after making it through the first night unscathed. They’d slept for almost ten hours each and it was already past mid-morning, the day grey and a strong wind coming in off the coast. Lena suggested a walk to the beach, the roaring ocean not even twenty metres from the front door and audible through the security screen. All too eager to take a look around, Kara wolfed down her food and drained her tea before fetching her boots. 

     

                They could just see a glimmer of the Indian Ocean through the shrubs and trees, the low woodland predominantly made up of short acacias and white woods with long grass, dry even in the middle of winter. Beneath it all was red dirt and rock and they trampled through it until the rock sloped down to the beach, the sand a patchy orange and tan and water blue as small waves rolled in. It was peaceful and Lena shaded her eyes as she took in the Silver Gulls on the sand and a few pelicans bobbing just beyond the surf.

     

                “Look how big those birds are!” Kara exclaimed with delight as she smiled brightly. “Pelicans, right?”

     

                “Yes.”

     

                “I didn’t know they were so big!”

     

                Lena couldn’t help but smile, watching Kara with a tender look in her eyes. It suddenly felt like the right decision to make, bringing them there, if only to see her on the sand, watching birds. It might not have been a sunset and there was no ice cream, but it would do for now to just be there with her, free. 

     

                “Go on,” Lena urged her, indulging Kara in her freedom. “Take your shoes off. Go in the water.”

     

                “Really? I can?”

     

                “Mhm. You can do whatever you want now.”

     

                Grinning like a kid, reminding Lena that so much of her childhood had been stripped away, Kara kicked off her shoes and stripped off her socks before she took off across the sand, moving so quickly she barely left a mark in the sand before she was splashing through the surf. Her laughter drifted back to Lena, who stayed safely on the sand, quietly joining in with her friend’s laughter as it eased some of the tension in her chest. She wouldn’t go in the water, already frightened of it enough before she’d been subjected to the bitter cold of the Arctic, but she watched as Kara frolicked through the waves, soaking her pants and scaring off some of the birds as she basked in her freedom. It healed something in Lena to watch her, knowing that no matter what became of her, she’d done some good in the world by freeing someone who should never have known imprisonment. It was the greatest achievement of her life. 

     

                Sinking to the sand, she stretched her legs out before her and similarly revelled in her own freedom, enjoying the peace and solitude of her private stretch of the beach, and content to do that every day for the foreseeable future, until they grew sick of it. If ever a day came, one trip down memory lane would surely right that, and Lena knew she’d never take for granted again the simple act of a slow life and living at her leisure. There was no one to make demands of her, no one to require her time, and it was perhaps the first time in her life that she had no obligations to anyone else. Except maybe Kara.

     

                Kara ended up swimming around for a bit as well, stripping off her clothes and bobbing in the waves, still within Lena’s line of sight, and Lena lightly dozed on the beach. It wasn’t a warm day but the fresh, salt-laced air was refreshing and she waited there until her friend came splashing back out of the sea, picking up her scattered clothes and grinning like a madwoman as she met her at the top of the beach. They went back into the chalet and Kara showered as Lena rummaged around in the chest freezer tucked in the corner to cook some frozen meals for lunch.

     

                They had lasagna and drank tap water, tasting stagnant but refreshing, and Kara picked a cassette from the bookshelf and figured out the stereo, listening to Britney Spears with rapt attention as they ate. Afterwards, they dusted off a chess set and spent the afternoon playing each other before it was time for dinner and then an early night, tucked in bed together as they quietly talked.

     

                The following few days unfolded the same way for the most part, eating breakfast with black coffee or tea, Kara swimming in the ocean as Lena occupied herself with a novel, before they showered off the sand and had lunch. Lena taught her card games and they watched movies on the VHS player and boxy TV, sitting on the small sofa together as they whittled away at the afternoon before making dinner and sleeping. Mostly, they preferred to be outside though, too much time cooped up in cells leaving them eager to explore the coastline or Lena’s fifty acres, which was much the same but interesting to Kara all the same, bright-eyed the first time they spotted a kangaroo, and pointing out any bird she caught flitting through the trees as she recalled their names from the bird guide she’d read in prison. It was peaceful but they were tense, waiting for it to blow over before they ventured further than their new home, and Kara was prone to bouts of strong emotion as her sadness and grief caught up with her, all of it so confusing after so long inside a prison that she wasn’t sure how to process it. Lena felt helpless as well, not knowing what to do, how to guide her through it or make it better when the people she missed were in cells on the other side of the world. Still, they coped and they managed and made it through the following few days.

     

                By the end of the week, making it through a decent chunk of the MREs they’d packed with them, as well as Lena’s stockpiled foods, she declared they’d kept a low enough profile to venture into Broome for a restock. They needed to pad out what she’d kept stocked up, and some fresh food as well, and Lena methodically went through all of their supplies that morning before she informed Kara they’d drive into town for a shopping trip that afternoon.

     

                It was three o’clock when they left, dressed unassumingly, their new haircuts and colours an effective disguise, and she had the Land Cruiser engine running for a little while before they left, having changed the battery and filled the fuel tank from the canisters. She had Kara lug those into the trunk for her so she could refill them at a gas station while they were there, and eventually deemed them ready to go.

     

                Buckled in, she adjusted her mirrors and put the car into gear, while Kara looked around the vehicle with interest. She hadn’t been in the front of a car before and Lena cast her a bewildered look for a moment as she watched Kara study the different dials, before she set off. Clearing her throat, she gripped the steering wheel and glanced over at Kara again. 

     

                “Alright, just to go over it all again, your name is Linda Lee, and mine is Elizabeth Walsh. We’re Canadian tourists travelling around Australia in a caravan. You’re very interested in birdwatching and I can’t wait to ride a camel on Cable Beach,” Lena rattled off as she drove down the bumpy access road and Kara fiddled with the staticky radio. 

     

                “And why are we travelling together?”

     

                “We’re friends. Girlfriends. Whatever you’d like.”

     

                “Girlfriends,” Kara quickly decided.

     

                Lena rolled her eyes and fought back a smile. “Sure, you’re my girlfriend. We met at UBC - that’s the University of British Columbia in Vancouver. You studied biology and I studied anthropology.”

     

                “Right, and how long have we been together?”

     

                “Eight years.”

     

                “Shouldn’t we be married?”

     

                “No, you don’t have to- I- sure, we’re … thinking of eloping on our trip.”

     

                “Who asked who?”

     

                Laughing, Lena gave her a sideways glance and shook her head. “We don’t need to go into that much detail. It’s just to cover our bases if we get caught in conversation with anyone.”

     

                “Okay. But what if-“

     

                “Just lie.”

     

                “Okay. And how old are we?”

     

                Rummaging for the licence she’d set in the cup holder, Lena glanced at the date of birth. “I’m thirty-two. You can be thirty-four. Keep your birthday though. It’s good to stick to facts when you can, so you don’t slip up.”

     

                Kara nodded as she committed everything to memory, following up on a few tidbits she deemed important as Lena indulged her in their cover stories. The hour it took to reach Broome passed by quickly, the radio eventually getting reception as music poured through the speakers and Kara flicked through the different stations, delighted by the songs, and Lena fine-tuned her mental list of supplies they needed. They wouldn’t be able to come into town often with their flimsy cover story of just passing through, and with the amount that Kara ate, the food wouldn’t last as long as she hoped, which meant they would need to go a bit overboard and stock up on as much as they could while they could. 

     

                Finding a shopping centre, Lena pulled into a parking bay and cut the engine. Climbing out, she looked around as she shut the door, Kara climbing out on the other side, and she met her at the front of the car, leading her towards the doors of the centre. Looking around with interest, Kara’s eyebrows drew together as she pressed closer to Lena and ducked her head in.

     

                “Why do they sound like that?” Kara asked, keeping her voice low as she wrinkled her nose.

     

                “What? They’re Australian; that’s what their accent sounds like.”

     

                “Oh. I like yours better.”

     

                Lips twitching with a smile, Lena took her hand and led her to Woolworths before dropping it for a shopping cart. Kara insisted on pushing it, enjoying the novelty of the grocery store as she gingerly wheeled the cart around, going slowly until Lena hurried her up with a look and a hand motion. Grabbing predominantly as many shelf-stable things - cured meats, pasta, jars and tins of fruits and vegetables, rice and lentils - Lena was quick but not obviously so, trying not to attract attention to their overflowing cart. Kara was more of a problem, quietly questioning things as she pointed them out on shelves, lifting a 24-pack of water off the shelf with more ease than she should’ve, and Lena was quick to check them out, feeding notes into the machine and setting off with the cart as Kara scrambled to follow.

     

                She made a stop in Kmart as well, finding sunglasses and baseball caps for them and checking out. Anything that wasn’t a necessity, like more clothes to pad out their slim wardrobe, was postponed for the time being as she had them in and out. Breaking the tags off, she made Kara swap her glasses for the sunglasses and then tugged a cap down on her dark hair as an added precaution, before she did the same. Making another stop for a carton of Coronas and six bottles of wine, Lena had them outside and stacking everything into the trunk of the car in short order before they drove to the Ampol across the road to fill up the Land Cruiser and the extra containers Lena had grabbed.

     

                Paying as she made Kara wait in the car, Lena stepped outside and climbed behind the wheel before gunning the engine to life. The Land Cruiser wasn’t out of place at all and no one glanced twice at them, which made her bold enough to warrant a treat. Placing an order for four pizzas at a nearby Domino’s, she had Kara go in separately and order six more, trying to remain inconspicuous by ordering separately, and they loitered around outside for a bit as Kara excitedly recounted her ordering experience. It was going to be a while until their order was ready and Lena bit her bottom lip until she relented to her idea, instructing her to get back in the car.

     

                Driving them to a general goods store on the beachfront of Cable Beach, Lena was smiling as she led Kara inside. It was a typical deli, a display of candy, chips and sodas in the shopfront with batteries, sim cards, band-aids and other necessities, and a full kitchen beyond, the smell of fryer oil hitting them as they went inside. It was an old store, the till clunky, everything slightly worn and peeling, but it served its purpose as Lena walked over to a long counter with a dozen tubs of ice cream behind the glass. A woman came through from the kitchen at the sound of a bell chiming at their arrival and Lena pulled out some cash.

     

                “Can I please get two cones with a double scoop of the chocolate and a double with strawberry and vanilla, thanks.”

     

                Standing beside her, Kara smiled as she realised what the tubs were, and reached out to let her fingers brush the back of Lena’s hand. Silent, Lena hooked a finger with hers as a smile faintly graced her lips. They were handed their cones and she paid for their ice creams before they slipped back outside and she took Kara’s hand, dragging her across the road as they stepped onto the wide expanse of pale golden sand. 

     

                The sky was cloudy and the sunset wasn’t so great as it quickly settled in, six o’clock in the afternoon with a bitter wind blowing in off the rough surf, but it was everything they’d wanted. Trudging across damp sand, they found a spot a safe distance from the rough waves running up the shore and took a seat, savouring their ice creams as they watched shrieking seagulls wheel about overhead, a few fighting over the scraps of chips from the deli.

     

                “So … this is chocolate ice cream,” Kara hummed with relish as she held her cone out before her to inspect it.

     

                “Mhm. Is it everything you’d hoped it would be?”

     

                Taking off her sunglasses, Kara gave her a radiant smile, stretching across her face as her eyes crinkled at the corners. They might have dyed and cut her hair, but those eyes were exactly the same, and as she spoke, it was her voice, her words, that reminded Lena of what she’d first loved about Kara, her earnest warmth and hope.

     

                “It’s even better because it’s real. I know we always said, but … there were so many times along the way when I thought it would just be some … fantasy. But here we are.”

     

                Reaching out, Lena covered Kara’s hand with her own and she let herself breathe a little easier. “Thank you for being here with me.”

     

                It wasn’t much, and they couldn’t stay long, but for a little while, they weren’t fugitives and they weren’t looking over their shoulders, they were just two women following through on a promise they’d made to each other a long time ago. And it wasn’t a date - not really - but if it had been, it would have been perfect.

    Chapter 31

                They stayed in Australia far longer than either of them anticipated. Lena had always liked the idea of going to Ireland, living in the same home her mother had lived in before going to America, but the idea all but vanished in her mind when she saw how happy Kara was. The winter was mild that far north but when the weather started to warm, it brought boiling hot days, dry and windless, and Kara basked in the sunshine in their hidden spot on the coast. As the weeks passed by into months, three months dragging by with the unhurried and well-earned respite from the world, her friend spent an inordinate amount of time outdoors, her pale skin developing a deep tan as she went swimming every day, growing better and better, spent hours on the beach with a rod cast further than a human should have been able to, reeling in fresh fish, which padded out their food stores, and pleading for a used kayak they’d seen for sale on someone’s driveway on a supply run into Broome. 

     

                Lena always watched from the beach, her worries eventually fading the longer they went undetected there, although she never truly let her guard down. She bought the kayak, drank beer in the shade as she watched Kara paddle back and forth, waving to her whenever she was in sight. They had a pair of binoculars and would go birdwatching together on the shore or in the bush, and Kara came back one day with a bright look in her eyes, clothes tattered, muddy and damp as she excitedly told Lena of her encounter with a saltwater crocodile at a little inlet a few kilometres north of their safe house. Their days were slow and quiet, perhaps boring to some but not to them as they revelled in their freedom, playing Scrabble and cards, watching old movies, cooking with a cassette tape playing in the background.

     

                They had to dye their hair every month, holed up in the tiny bathroom as they covered each other’s roots in it and carefully trimmed bangs back into shape, an ache in Lena’s chest every time she had to cover the blonde showing through. She was still her Kara though, so full of life, so carefree and adaptable to this new life outside of the prison that Lena felt like she was broken in some way, unable to brush everything that happened aside as she struggled with nightmares and the tight panic in her chest at so much water on their doorstep, each time Kara was out of their sight. She had a scar on her abdomen and her rehealed leg ached sometimes where it had been broken. She drank too much and felt lost, trying to sort through things without any guidance. As much as she’d always detested therapy, especially since the prison, Lena really could have used it then. 

     

                There were days where she sat and let her memories and thoughts utterly consume her, while Kara seemed so unbothered by it all, as if eighteen years of her life hadn’t been spent in a concrete box. Feeling as if she wasn’t adjusting well, Lena just kept going, day by day, until enough time had passed for her to sleep through the night without waking in a cold sweat, until she stopped scanning the skies and horizon for military or naval craft, knowing that even if they arrived, the searing sun of north-western Australia had saturated Kara so fully that nothing would ever be able to reach them before she dealt with it. And that was majorly why they stayed, Lena knowing that the frequent overcast or rainy days of Ireland would not irradiate the Kryptonian to quite the same level.

     

                But no one came, and no one glanced twice at them, not even on the rare moments of indulgence Lena afforded them, double scoops of ice cream on Cable Beach at sunset every month, her hand in Kara’s, seagulls wheeling about them and the tourists that thronged about on the golden sand in the warmer months. They visited the library a couple of times, parked at computers as Lena made good use of the wi-fi for updates while Kara lounged in the seat beside her, watching YouTube videos on birdwatching and sneaking jellybeans from the packet hidden in her pocket. Lena would check the news, Google searches for the trials of anyone involved in Fort Rozz in any capacity, for arrests of aliens and any insight into hers and Kara’s search effort, or whether her mother had been arrested yet. She purchased a newspaper every time they were at a store, whether it was in Broome or to the other distant stores scattered throughout the region, looking for international news on the case when she couldn’t get to a computer.

     

                That was how they found out about the dates for the trials of Alex, Kelly and Eliza, scheduled for within a week of each other in three months’ time, and Lena deliberated between letting Kara know or keeping it to herself. They were honest with each other about everything though, and Lena waited until they were safely back at their home before gently breaking the news to her. It was a long wait to find out their fates but that time together only brought them closer. There were moments where Lena felt that pull towards her, caught in the tiny kitchen together with the warm presence of Kara standing behind her, or waking up in the middle of the night with a nightmare to find her pressed up against her, face pressed into the back of her neck, warm breath fanning across her skin. 

     

                The tension was palpable and Kara wasn’t shy with her touches, her quick kisses on cheeks, holding Lena’s hand whenever she could. It was all so innocent, except for the way their gazes lingered on each other, all coming to a head three months after they’d hidden themselves away there. The weather had warmed considerably by September and Lena was content with it, knowing it would get blisteringly hot soon enough and already dreading the heat, although knowing it was preferable to the sub-zero temperatures of the Arctic. But for now, it was pleasantly hot and Kara was floating on her back in the gentle current as the sun started to set, a sky of brilliant orange stretching across the horizon. 

     

                Lena was watching her from the shade of the gazebo they’d set up on the beach, sitting in a folding camp chair with a book and a beer, pressing the cool can against her neck as she watched her come out of the water. They had a small fire going, the smell of smoke mingling with the salty tang of the wind, and Kara smiled as she crossed over to Lena, dripping water on her lap as she braced herself on the arms of the camp chair and leaned down to kiss her cheek. Overbalancing and too strong for her own good, Kara crumpled the arms of the chair in her grasp and tipped them both over, Lena going backwards as she let out a yelp of surprise, beer and book flung from her hands. Kara lay sprawled on top of her, both of them laughing at the clumsiness of the Kryptonian.

     

                It had happened sporadically, setting a cup down too hard and shattering it on the countertop, gripping cutlery too tightly in her hands, until they were warped pieces of metal, sneezing and sending herself shooting backwards into a tree, snapping the trunk as she sent it crashing to the ground. The moments were always quite funny, Kara’s sheepishness stoking the tenderness in Lena’s heart as she was always quick to reassure her it was fine, but she could still sense Kara’s unease with her strength, her speed, her abilities, not knowing if she would hurt Lena whenever she touched her. She took to the water instead, cutting through the waves as she burned off some energy, trying to mitigate the risk, even though Lena knew she was always so careful around her, every touch like Kara was handling glass.

     

                “Sorry,” Kara said as her face reddened, pushing herself up.

     

                With the weight of her on top, Lena couldn’t help the way her body responded, the desire that swept through her as she cradled Kara’s waist, knowing that for all her talk of finding out how they would fit in each other’s lives after prison, the caution of taking things slow and sifting through the traumatic events that had happened, she truly loved Kara. It had been a little secret she’d harboured for three months, each day bringing them closer, each touch setting her heart racing as her mouth went dry. And yet, she’d held back at every opportunity, wanting to give Kara the space to make sure she was making the right choice.

     

                “You’re alright,” Lena murmured, smiling as her eyes creased behind her sunglasses, reaching up to brush back a damp lock of hair plastered to Kara’s cheek. “I was just thinking about heading back for a shower, so perfect timing, really.”

     

                Kara laughed loudly as she sat up, the sound doing funny things to Lena’s chest, and her stomach too, feeling Kara’s body shake with it. Eyelids shuttering, she smiled slightly and pushed herself up too, Kara standing the rest of the way and then carefully helping her up. Gathering her near-empty beer and her book, Lena drained the remaining mouthful as Kara blew out the fire and they traipsed back up to the demountable, climbing the short steps to the front door, shedding sandy shoes outside.

     

                Inside, Lena hesitated, setting her book down on the little table and leaving the empty beer can on the unit to be tossed in with the recycling, and then moved towards the little bathroom as she shed her tank top. The glance over her shoulder was heavy-lidded and meaningful, the slight arch of an eyebrow a silent invitation as Kara stood inside the doorway in her swimsuit, hair damp, patches of skin coated in sand where she’d sprawled on top of Lena. Slipping into the bathroom, Lena turned on the water and shed the rest of her clothes before stepping into the shower stall and letting it run over flushed skin, rinsing away the grease of sun lotion and sand.

     

                It took all but a minute for the shower door to open, and she turned as Kara stepped inside, backing up so they could both fit. She didn’t have a chance to say anything before Kara was holding her face in her palms and kissing her, her mild surprise giving way to the thrill of it as she wrapped her arms around Kara’s slick body and kissed her back, tasting salt and feeling the grit of sand beneath her fingertips. Breaking it off a moment later, Lena rested her forehead against Kara’s as she breathed heavily, loosening her embrace as she swallowed thickly.

     

                “Are you sure this is what you want?”

     

                “Yes,” Kara whispered, her lips ghosting over Lena’s again before she drew back, an apprehensive look on her face as she faltered for a moment. “I know how this works, I just- I don’t know- I’ve never- just … tell me what to do.”

     

                Running her hands down Kara’s spine, Lena nodded. “It’s okay, just- if it’s too much, if you don’t want to- you tell me to stop, okay? At any point we can stop.”

     

                “Okay,” Kara murmured, her hands nervously fluttering around Lena as if she didn’t know where to put them, where it was okay to touch.

     

                “Here,” Lena softly said as she reached for the body wash and squeezed some into Kara’s hands and then her own.

     

                Slowly, she rubbed some into Kara’s shoulder, lathering it up, and repeated on the other side, touching her gently, going slow as she washed her back and her arms, trailed her fingers over Kara’s stomach. Kara copied her, her touch featherlight as she washed the day off Lena, face strained with unease as she gingerly worked the soap into suds on her skin. Trying to get her out of her head, away from the concern of hurting her, Lena leaned in and kissed her, her hands tangling in Kara’s hair as she propelled her back into the wall of the shower stall, feeling Kara respond instinctively as she held Lena closer, hands splayed over her back, her ass, mouth parting beneath her lips.

     

                After a few minutes of letting the water sluice down their bodies, sure they were rinsed off well enough but not caring if they weren’t, Lena shut the water off and pulled away, wiping water off her face as she stepped out. Foregoing a towel, she left a trail of water in her wake as she went straight to the bedroom and sank onto the covers, patting the spot beside her as Kara followed. Kissing her again, Lena eased her down onto the covers and cupped the side of her neck, breaking off to skim her nose over Kara’s cheek before kissing the underside of her jaw, mumbling against her skin as she reminded her that they could stop at any time.

     

                Breathlessly urging her not to, Kara ran her hands over Lena’s skin as Lena let her touch her wherever she’d like, fingers reflexively curling before she caught herself each time, trying not to dig them in, trying not to bruise - or worse - Lena as she writhed beneath her, her frustration growing. Taking it slow, Lena tried her best to make it meaningful, memorable, and as she kissed Kara and touched her, she smiled at the soft sound of surprise in her mouth and didn’t stop until she was sure Kara was well and truly satisfied, clammy and flushed as she lay limply on the covers of the bed with an arm across her face as she tried to slow her ragged breaths. Stretched out on her side, Lena studied her with a faintly anxious expression on her face.

     

                “Was it alright?”

     

                Letting out a shuddering laugh, Kara dropped her arm, blue eyes shining brightly as she tried to hide a smile. “That’s an understatement. That was … and you do that all the time?”

     

                With a quick laugh, Lena’s eyelids shuttered. “It depends. And how good it is also depends.”

     

                “Oh, so it won’t always-”

     

                “Oh, no, it will,”  Lena said with a slightly cocky smile. “I’ll make sure of that, don’t worry. I mean, if you wanted me to.”

     

                Choking on a laugh, Kara’s cheeks flushed a deeper pink as a shy smile curled her lips. “Yeah, yeah, I do.”

     

                Smiling, Lena brushed the backs of her fingers over Kara’s flushed cheek. “Good.”

     

                “And thank you.”

     

                Reaching for her hand, Lena kissed her knuckles and Kara pushed herself up slightly to kiss her cheek before lowering herself back down as she breathed slowly for a few moments. Then she looked at Lena with a gleam in her eyes, and Lena smiled as she raised her eyebrows. 

     

                “Will you teach me how to do that to you?”

     

                With a huff of laughter, pressing her face into Kara’s chest, Lena smiled and trailed off with a soft sigh. “I will, but not tonight. Tonight is for you.”

     

                “Oh. Well, in that case … can you do it again?”

     

                Laughing again, enjoying the ease of it after the rarity of laughter for so long, Lena responded by kissing a path down Kara’s chest and abdomen. And the following night, she held to her promise and showed Kara what to do, finding bliss in the touch of her, finding it possible to allow herself to enjoy sex, despite it all, taking comfort in someone else and deepening her relationship with Kara in a way she hadn’t been sure would survive outside of a prison. They were in love, more than they’d believed they’d loved each other even before they’d run off together, a thing that slowly made itself known as time went by.

     

                It didn’t mean it was all good, that there weren’t rough patches or that their trauma was forgotten about, but for someone who had always lived alone, it was shockingly easy for Lena to live alongside Kara in the smallest of homes. And for someone who hadn’t lived without the noise of a hundred other people in the vicinity or with any freedom, Kara adjusted well to the peaceful solitude of just the two of them to fulfil their needs themselves. 

     

                The worst of it was possibly December, the day of Alex’s trial - the last of the three - taking the bumpy road into Broome in the boiling hot car as the vents struggled to pump out air cold enough to make a difference. It was early in the morning, the time difference with the east coast of America making it so that the three trials would have already taken place, and any sentencing already in effect. Lena had thought it better that way, for Kara to know the fate of them all in one fell swoop instead of dragging it out over the course of the week, They were still yet to know the fate of anyone else from the DEO, whose trials were months away yet, but Kara didn’t care about those on a personal level, and Lena could wait for justice, so long as it came.

     

                They went grocery shopping first, loading up the car with as much food as they could fit before parked outside the library. Tucked away in the building, empty at that hour, Lena looked up the names of the three women with a taut expression on her face. She absorbed the information impassively and then powered down the computer, climbing to her feet and heading back outside to the car as she towed Kara along by the hand. Waiting until they were buckled in and on the road home, Lena cleared her throat.

     

                “Eliza and Kelly,” she started before faltering, clearing her throat again. “They’ve both had their licences to practise stripped and … they’ve been sentenced for five years.”

     

                She heard the sharp inhale and felt like a knife was being twisted in her chest. From the corner of her eye, she watched as Kara curled in on herself, the heels of her palms digging into her eyes, and a ripple of anguish crossed Lena’s face to see her so upset. It was awkward, with her thinking they were where they deserved to be and Kara wishing they were all together, free. She knew any comfort she could provide would sound hollow, Kara knowing her true feelings on the matter.

     

                “And Alex,” she rasped, wincing as she gripped the steering wheel tightly. “They pinned the whistleblowing on her as well. Had to with the Espionage Act. Um … they mitigated the death penalty. She’s been given nine.”

     

                Kara choked on a sob and Lena floundered for a moment before reaching over to squeeze her shoulder. There seemed little else she could do for her, and she swallowed past the tightness in her throat. “I’m sorry.”

     

                Opening the car door then, Kara unbuckled her seatbelt, her cheeks blotchy and red, as Lena let out a panicked sound, braking and steering the car onto the side of the road. By the time they came to a bumpy stop, Kara was out of the car and gone, streaking away on foot as nothing more than a blur, Lena’s pleading shout answered with silence. Sitting there for a moment with the engine idling, Lena sighed heavily and unbuckled herself, climbing across the centre console to shut the open door and then buckling herself back in and driving home alone. She kept hoping Kara would appear on the road and flag her down, right up to the moment she pulled off the road and down the private track to the demountable.

     

                She wasn’t there when Lena made it inside, panic making her chest feel tight, but there wasn’t much else she could do, save to unpack the car and put everything away. Kara was grieving, that was all, and Lena could at least give her the space to do that. She had so rarely been afforded privacy to any display of emotion in her life, but Lena could be the one who gave her that. 

     

                It wasn’t until lunchtime that Lena heard her footsteps on the stairs, rising from the kitchen table, abandoning her third drink to calm her nerves, and wringing her hands as Kara came inside. Red-eyed and stooped with sadness, she went straight into Lena’s arms to cry some more. She didn’t seem like herself for weeks following that, moping around the place, not eating as much as usual, not stepping foot into the water and sleeping too much, but she slowly came to terms with it and Lena gave her space throughout, and life went on as always.

     

                There was Christmas and New Year, a little less paranoid and strict as Lena indulged Kara in a late night walk through Broome to look at the Christmas lights, to look at the decorated trees in the shopping centres and stores, to pick out a gift for each other - she found a book on birds for Kara, and Kara bought her a book of crossword puzzles - more ice cream on the beach and fireworks at midnight on New Year’s as Lena kissed her on the sand. It was boring and peaceful and they loved every minute of it as summer breezed by, Lena teaching Kara to drive, Kara slowly coaxing Lena into the balmy ocean, first letting the surf rush over her toes, then sinking to her ankles, until Lena paddled in the shadows by spring, trying to let go of her old fear of the water, renewed by diving in the Arctic on her rescue mission. But this water was warm and Kara’s arms were around her, laughing and encouraging, taking Lena right back to days in the lake with her mother before she’d drowned.

     

                The trials for DEO staff were staggered quite regularly, and it was satisfying for Lena to look up the sentences whenever they were in town. Sixteen years for Deputy Lucy Lane, twenty for Warden Lauren Haley, and twenty-six for Director Hank Henshaw. There were countless others - guards who made up the majority of the sentences, and parole for administrators, technicians, chefs, janitors and any others who had been sent to the prison but hadn’t directly dealt with the wrongfully imprisoned - but for Lena, it was those three that were the most vindicating. It felt like the justice she’d been hoping for, and almost like closure. But it wasn't quite enough for her though.

    Chapter 32

                The cases dragged on for so long, that a year rolled around quickly, and then another and another, and Lena bought them a silver ring each, simple bands they wore on their ring fingers, nothing fancy, no vows, but a lifelong promise nonetheless. It was quick and unnecessary, nothing legal about it, but it was another moment of indulgence, both of them knowing to not take things for granted and knowing how quickly things could change. Their lives were small, tucked away and relatively isolated, but they had no plans to leave, even after three years. It was around that time that Lena’s occasional library usage revealed that Kelly and Eliza had both been released on parole for good behaviour, their five year sentences cut down to three years, spitting them back out into the world without the threat of imprisonment hanging over their heads - if they behaved - making them free in a way that Kara and Lena weren’t. 

     

                She didn’t keep it from her - how could she? - and tracked them down to Eliza’s hometown, a small place called Midvale in northern California. Part of her had expected Kara to take off, to go looking for them by herself the moment Lena had sat her down and told her they were out, but she hadn’t and that gave Lena the time she needed to find them and talk herself into letting Kara seek them out. Three years was a long time without seeing people you loved; Lena knew that from three months away from the person she loved, and she grimly resigned herself to divulging what she’d uncovered. Three years was a long time without going home, and Lena’s stomach swooped low with worry as she sat Kara down, holding her hands tightly as she told her where to find them.

     

                They went that very day, all the way to Midvale, and Kara touched down on golden sand, baking in the mid-June sun, setting Lena on her feet and holding her hand tightly as she looked around. Her expression was grave, posture taut and alert, and she studied the white clapboard house perched on the beachfront with palpable tension. At the sight of a blonde woman on the back porch, with more grey in her hair these days, Kara dropped Lena’s hand and moved a little too fast for a human as her shout split the lazy quiet of the day.

     

                “Eliza!”

     

                Lena watched from the beach, hugging her arms to herself, as Kara barrelled into the closest thing to a mother she’d ever known on Earth, hugging her tightly as Eliza’s exclamations of disbelief and surprise drifted towards Lena, indecipherable over the sound of the waves. Lillian had never been the best mother to Lena, had neglected her, belittled her, used her so often that Lena had cause for little trust - even their recent, if brief, reunion had taken the familiar path of her past encounters with her mother - so she found it hard to blame Kara for seeking comfort in one who had loved her badly. 

     

                Still, she hung back, nothing but indifference for the ex-doctor left within her now. There was no anger, no hatred, knowing that she’d at least served some time for her part in it all, had any future as a doctor stripped away. And as Lena watched, Kelly appeared, running barefoot across the back lawn to throw her arms around Kara, laughing, and she felt that same indifference towards the psychologist as well. All that was missing was Alex, still behind bars, still serving out her sentence, not yet halfway through it, and Lena knew that if she was there, she would feel the exact same way towards her as well. She’d hated them all before, and then she’d been grateful afterwards, for the help, for the sacrifice, and somewhere along the way, those conflicted feelings had evened out into nothing. It had all been stamped down, a necessary act so that she could enjoy the sliver of peace she’d hard-won.

     

                They noticed her when they came apart, two hands raised in tentative waves, returned somewhat reluctantly by Lena, who hunched her shoulders, eyebrows furrowed together as the wind ruffled her red hair. Lowering her hand, she abruptly turned and sank onto the sand, warm beneath her as a cool wind blew in off the coast. It was sunny and she was glad she’d brought a hat, her shoulders covered, and she was patient enough to give Kara the time she needed to reassure herself they were okay.

     

                A while later, her shadow cast across Lena and she sank to the sand at her side, holding out a cone with a scoop of vanilla ice cream, already melting. A double-scoop of chocolate was in Kara’s other hand and her eyes creased at the corners as she smiled unevenly at Lena.

     

                “They’re okay.”

     

                “Good,” Lena whispered, her lips twitching slightly.

     

                “And … are we okay?”

     

                Quickly glancing at Kara, her eyebrows rose in surprise. “Of course. Yeah, of course we are. Why?”

     

                Gesturing behind her to the big white house, Kara cringed slightly. Letting out a huff of laughter, Lena kissed her shoulder and let out a resigned sigh. “It’s fine. I- well, I knew you’d want to see them if I told you, so …”

     

                Teeth worrying at her lower lip, Kara nodded, but her eyes were wide and her expression was anxious. Staring at her, Lena gave her a long, searching look as the wind filled the silence that stretched between them. Setting a hand on her knee, Lena squeezed gently.

     

                “What’s wrong?” Giving her a doleful look, Kara grimaced and Lena blinked, leaning back slightly as understanding dawned on her face. “You don’t want to leave.”

     

                Expression crumpling, Kara ran a hand over her face and licked the melting ice cream dripping over her fingers. It was a long minute before she spoke, sheepish and apologetic. “If I had it my way, you know that I wouldn’t. But … I know that we can’t, it’s just- it makes me sad, the way it all turned out.”

     

                Stroking Kara’s dark hair, Lena kissed her forehead but had no words of comfort for her. They ate their ice cream in silence and there was a heaviness to Kara as she climbed to her feet, brushing off sand, and stared longingly at the white house. Lena was grateful the other women had left them out there alone but she hated to see Kara torn in half, that anguish lingering even when she was swept up in her arms and flown across the world, back to their home. Washing the melted ice cream from her hands, Lena stared down at the ring on her left hand as her mouth thinned, understanding what Kara meant about how it had all turned out. She would have loved a wedding, something real and binding, she would have loved to live somewhere bigger than a shoebox, without the paranoia, without worrying about money as she sold off stocks to keep them fed, the cash running a little thin now that a few years had passed. It was never a long-term solution, but this was the thing that kicked Lena into gear, to give up the peaceful solitude of her well-earned sabbatical and find a more permanent resolution to their circumstances.

     

                When Kara murmured she was going for a swim, kissing Lena before she stripped off her clothes and went straight to the sea without pause, Lena lingered at the sink a while longer before ferreting out the satellite phone hidden in the trunk beneath their bed. Hoping her mother still had the same number for her to reach her on in emergencies, years gone by since they’d spoken on the phone, Lena dialled it and paced back and forth in the slim gap between the bed and the wall.

     

                “Hello?”

     

                “Mom.”

     

                “Lena?” Lillian said with surprise, and some warmth if Lena wasn’t mistaken. “Oh. It’s good to hear your voice.”

     

                Smiling, Lena closed her eyes. “It’s good to hear yours too. How- how are you?”

     

                “Fine. Sunning myself in Saint-Tropez. And you? I’m assuming you’re still with her?”

     

                “Yes. We’re, uh, we’re good. We’re actually married now. Um, well, it’s not official or anything, but … you know, when you’re a fugitive …”

     

                “Oh. Should I offer my congratulations or would you prefer my honesty?”

     

                Letting out a quick laugh, Lena shook her head, face pinched with amusement. “I’ll take the congratulations. Haven’t heard that from you often.”

     

                “Well, congratulations, then.”

     

                There was an awkward pause and Lena didn’t know what to say next, a flicker of guilt running through her at how exploitative it was to only ever speak to her mother when she needed something. Lena wasn’t sure they had ever been different, that there had ever been a time they’d spoken out of a desire for conversation, but it had been years and she didn’t know if it was asking too much of Lillian to help her again. Her mother let out a withering sigh as the silence dragged on.

     

                “Just tell me why you’re calling. It’s obviously not a social call, and I hardly think you’d call just to tell me of your nuptials, so if you can cut to the chase, I’d like to get back to enjoying my wine.”

     

                “You didn’t go to ground for long,” Lena noted.

     

                “You know me, I can weasel my way out of any situation once I’ve greased enough palms.”

     

                “How do you think you’d manage, greasing some palms for a couple of pardons?”

     

                “Ah. I’m not sure that’s still on the table for you.”

     

                “But you could ask.”

     

                “I could, yes. And what terms are you looking for this time?”

     

                Staring down at the ring, toying with it as she swallowed thickly, Lena drew in a shuddering breath. “Any.”

     

                Lillian paused a moment. “Any?”

     

                “An NDA, I’ll- I’ll publicly endorse President Brayden, whatever needs to be done. I just … I need pardons - for both of us. And the truth about her cousin.”

     

                “You freed a bunch of aliens and metahumans into the US.”

     

                “I’m well aware of why I’m a fugitive. Now … I just want to know what I need to do to fix that. Not for me, for her. I need … some guarantee of her safety.”

     

                “Alright. Alright, let me make a few calls. Give me your number and I’ll call you back.”

     

                Hesitating, Lena knew it was an exercise in trust to give her mother the number to the satellite phone but she relented, knowing that if she couldn’t trust Lillian to help with this, no one on Earth would be able to pull the necessary strings to give her what she wanted. Rattling off a list of numbers, Lena pressed her mouth into a flat line.

     

                “Australia?” Lillian said after a moment.

     

                “Mhm. Had to get away from the cold afterwards.”

     

                “Right. Well, I’ll let you know how I get on.”

     

                “Thank you,” Lena murmured, pausing as she bit her lip. “It really is nice to speak to you.”

     

                “Yes, it is. Talk soon.”

     

                The line went dead and she kept the phone out so she would hear any incoming calls. The weather was quite cool and she made herself a cup of coffee and spent the morning trying to think of what to do next. She’d buy a house for them as soon as she had access to her funds again - something on the beach, in Midvale if she could bear to be so close to the people who had hurt her - maybe she’d move the L-Corp office out west, have some involvement in the business again, try to piece together a life and career for herself after this dragged out mess, or maybe she’d start a non-profit for aliens. She’d dye her hair back to its natural colour and Kara could go back to being a blonde, and they’d finally be able to be themselves. Almost certainly she’d give therapy another go, and wed Kara properly, give her a comfortable life with people she cared about. 

     

                As well as she could manage, Kara wasn’t built for isolation, that much Lena knew, and she didn’t want to stop her from having friends and a family, from finding out how she fit in the real world. They couldn’t hide forever, and Lena knew that forever was a more real prospect for Kara than anyone else, and wanted to make sure that - hopefully a long way down the track - when she passed, she left her wife behind in a world that cherished her, instead of feared her so much they shut her away.

     

                She kept her phone call from her mother a secret from Kara, and it took weeks of back and forth, Lillian once more the middle man between the President and her daughter. Lena had to concede to a few demands - she wouldn’t try to sue the government, an effective gag order that prohibited her from any book deals or interviews on anything related to Fort Rozz - but she willingly agreed this time and the family lawyers combed through it for any nasty surprises hidden within the agreement, before sending it through for her to sign. Part of her felt morally against it, but the overwhelming part of her was tired . She’d been away from home and comfort for a long time with no one to talk to, except for her wife, so what difference did it make if she agreed not to divulge the gritty details of her imprisonment? She was already silenced by being a fugitive, at least she could be silenced in a big home, with her money and resources, with her wife, who she’d promised to take care of, and would do that by any means. 

     

                Printing off the agreement at the library, Lena signed it and scanned it back through to her mother. It felt nerve-wracking and she wasn’t sure if her hope was misplaced, but she had to try. At the very least, she could try her hardest to buy their freedom, and she didn’t want to talk about what had happened anyway. The people who had done it to her were all in jail, her fellow inmates, who’d been wrongfully imprisoned were freed by her over a year ago, and that was all that she and Kara had wanted between them. That, and the news of Kara’s cousin, Kal-El. 

     

                Classified documents came through days after she’d sent back the signed agreement, along with a call from her mother with the confirmation that official pardons had been made for her and Kara, as well as another piece of news. Lena waited until Kara was back from her kayaking, smiling as she told her about her rare sighting of a Square-tailed Kite, before she suggested they go into Broome. They went to the library and Lena paid to print off the classified documents, rolling the pages up to hide the front page as she held Kara’s hand and led them back out not ten minutes after they’d arrived. She drove them to the beach and bought them ice cream, the sunset just starting, and they sat side by side on the sand as Lena fought to swallow. She hadn’t read the documents, hadn’t thought it was any right of hers to know before Kara did, but she faltered now at the reveal.

     

                “What’s wrong?” Kara asked, giving her a searching look.

     

                Drawing in a shuddering breath, Lena picked up the folded document and roughly cleared her throat as she spoke softly. “I’ve been speaking to my mother. She’s helped strike a deal with the government. Um … they sent this through. The report for your- your cousin.”

     

                Gently setting it in Kara’s lap, Lena moved to climb to her feet, giving her a bit of privacy to get through it. Kara reached out and grabbed her hand though, pulling her back down. She toyed with the corner of the pages and Lena could see her pulse racing at her throat, swallowing thickly as her half-eaten ice cream slowly melted.

     

                “Um … I don’t think I can-” Kara said as her voice cracked. “Can you-”

     

                Nodding, Lena’s face rippled with pain as she took the document back, hesitating before throwing her ice cream to the seagulls to fight over and then smoothing out the pages. It was silent for ten minutes as she read each page, a tightness in her chest, sadness weighing heavily on her as she got through it all and then set the document aside, pinned beneath her leg. The silence was heavy and she drew in a shaky breath, staring out at the sea as she gently summarised what she’d read.

     

                “Your cousin made it here before you. He crashed onto a farm out in the Midwest of America, out in Kansas, um … there was a lot of damage to his pod when it crashed. The filters that converted the carbon dioxide into oxygen broke. He … suffocated inside the pod before a farmer found him.”

     

                The breath was forced from Kara’s lungs and she ducked her head, cheeks wet as a pitifully small oh escaped her. Lena wrapped her arms around her, squeezing tightly, and Kara was silent for a moment, trying to process the fact that she'd been sent worlds away to raise a baby who'd never had a fighting chance at living.

     

                “They didn’t- they didn’t … kill him?”

     

                “No,” Lena wearily sighed, eyes closed. “No, it was an accident. The reason they know so much about your kind is because the DEO ... took his body for research.”

     

                Wiping her wet cheeks, Kara cleared her throat as she nodded. “Okay. Okay, that’s- I’m glad I know. Thank you for finding out for me.”

     

                Tears were swimming in the corners of Lena’s eyes and she drew in a shuddering breath as she tipped her head back, staring up at the sky. “There’s something else I need to tell you.”

     

                She met Kara’s gaze, her expression tender as she held her hands. Kara didn’t speak as she gave Lena a searching look, concern clouding her tanned face, blue eyes intense and anxious. Clearing her throat, Lena gave her a thin smile. “Alex was released yesterday.”

     

                This time, Kara sucked in a sharp breath of surprise, her eyes widening a fraction. “I- what- how? It’s only been … three months.”

     

                “It was one of my conditions.”

     

                “Conditions? For what?”

     

                Eyes creasing at the corners, Lena smiled, “for our pardons.”

     

                “I … don’t understand. We- but we’re fugitives. We didn’t-”

     

                Shaking her head, Lena let out a choked laugh, one hand cupping Kara’s cheek as the other still tightly clutched her hand. “It’s finally over, we don’t have to hide anymore.”

     

                A pretty sunset of pinks and oranges filled the horizon as waves gently broke over the shore, and Kara stared at Lena with bewildered surprise as the chocolate ice cream melted over her fingers, mouth opening and closing in disbelief. Laughing, Lena leaned in and kissed her, a warmth in her chest as a weight was lifted off her shoulders. Settling back down beside her, she leaned her head on Kara’s shoulder and let out a relieved sigh, knowing that the worst of it was truly behind them now. It was only the beginning of their future together though - together as free women - and Lena was nervous to see where it would take them, but had no doubt it would be together, no matter what.

     

                “Eat your ice cream,” Lena murmured as she smiled, feeling Kara’s warm arm around her waist. “Enjoy the sunset and the beach and the birds, and then let’s go home.”
